# netherite-v2 DEVLOG

## 2026-11-23 lane/audit-feat: the scalar features are the run's choice; one build runs any set

The audit's last item. Three commits on the lane, each droppable on its own (the first two are lane/audit-feat's
7593d497 and c217b600, cherry-picked): 69bf8770, 8fba6493 and 19ab72b3. Dropped, the feature words are build-time
again and the entry below holds as written. The comparison is against 3ad3f120's compile-time builds of the same
trainer (lane `audit-feat-base`), one working directory, on the dev host; the logs are the lane's `out/audit/`.

**What changed.**

- *The row's count is a run-time value* (69bf8770). The six feature words (`.ls .hs .dk .or .gv .tk`) each passed a
  `-D` that fixed the scalar row's width, so a model of any other subset needed its own build of every variant.
  net.h holds the run's set as a process-wide mask (`neth_net_fs`: mask, count, fixed). Host code reads
  `NETH_NET_NS` from it, device code a `__constant__` copy that each `.cu` file uploads where it makes its state
  (`neth_net_dsync`), and `loop.cu`'s two staging kernels take the count as an argument.
  - The kernels that need fc1's K at compile time (`k_fcrow`, the fc1 GEMM, `k_afused`) are templates on the count
    padded to 64. The 40 reachable rows pad to four widths (192, 320, 896, 1024), and every build's K is the one its
    compile-time build used, so the arithmetic is the same.
- *ntloop and ntinit take the set* (8fba6493). `--features WORDS` (ls hs dk or gv tk, or none; spaces, commas or
  dots between) and the run file's `policy.net.features`. With neither, an NTW2 `--init` file's header decides; an
  NTW1 file or no `--init` gets the build's default, which is all the words in a variant's name mean now. A named set
  must hold every feature the file has, or the run is refused naming both; a flag and a run key that differ are
  refused too.
  - **The checkpoint rule is not the entry below's.** A build no longer refuses a file of another set, because the
    file's header decides: `s1`, `s1.ls` and `s1.dk.or` run an `s1.ls` file as ls, with one digest. Refused: a set
    that lacks a feature the file has, and an NTW1 file of more than 155 scalars (migrate it, as below).
  - A file with fewer features than the run loads with zero weights on the rest: a trained ls net given
    `--features ls,hs` has the ls run's digest.
  - ntinit takes `--features` for a fresh net and with `--from`. `make train-loop-v` does not build `V/ntinit`, so a
    worktree's ntinit from before these commits keeps the old rules until it is built by hand
    (`make -C csrc/runtime $PWD/out/runtime/train/V/ntinit`).
- *A migrated file's header names the build* (19ab72b3). `ntinit --migrate` wrote `variant unnamed` whenever the
  stated set was not the build's own; it now writes the build's word, as a model a run saves does.

**Measured.**

- Trajectory digests, the compile-time build against this tree, one weights file and one command (64 envs, 60 group
  steps, learning off): equal for the production set fresh (a3ad6eadfa930f8f), for none, ls and dk or fresh (all three
  6f4e8cedc27eadf6: a fresh net's first 60 steps do not tell the sets apart), and for `ckpt-060` migrated as ls
  (3d745b18fc812a0f).
- So two nets were trained 19 updates by the compile-time builds (their scalar columns' largest weight then 0.042
  against 0.029 fresh) and run on both trees: ls 5ff5cdee55aa7709, dk or f4bf40ced72f08fd, equal. With fc1's scalar
  columns set to 0 the two digests are others (d28dea638fcecb16, 99c0d37c59766ab9), equal again: the digest reads
  those columns. `ckpt-060`'s scalar columns average 0.17 where a fresh net's do 0.015.
- The first learner row with learning on, the same trained nets: the same loss on both trees in 5 runs of 6 to the
  last digit, and in the sixth each tree one of the two values of the third epoch (below). Fresh nets, 15 interleaved
  runs a tree: the same values for none, the recurrent build, ls, dk or and the production set; `ckpt-060` four
  values within 1.1e-8.
- ntinit: the same tensors as the compile-time builds' for a fresh ls, dk or and none net, for `--from` and for
  `--migrate`. The refusals name their reason: a flag lacking the file's feature; `--features xx`; two `--features`;
  a migration whose features make 171 scalars of a 169-scalar file.
- Throughput, the production variant (`nether ab`, learning on, 256 envs in 8 groups, about a minute a run,
  alternating order, card 3), the compile-time build's env-steps a second against this tree's: three sets of 5, 5
  and 8 rounds give 0.9970, 0.9988 and 0.9894; the 18 paired rounds together 0.9941, from 0.9845 to 1.0037 at 95%.
  A run's own spread is 2 to 6%. No slowdown is shown; one of about 1% can be neither shown nor ruled out.
- Size: `ntloop` 2,868,008 against 3,033,712 bytes for `s1`, 3,119,592 against 3,313,232 for the production
  variant; the five trainer objects 1,625,432 against 1,764,864 and 1,895,744 against 2,063,240 bytes; `w1.af`'s 1.84
  against 2.69 MB. A cold compile of the five: `s1` 7.0 against 7.2 s, `w1.af` 8.0 against 11.2 s (the worker's).
- The checks at 19ab72b3: `train-actor-v-check`, `train-wire-check` (the GAE case, 6 PASS), `train-loop-check`
  (df2a60c5's digests), `nether gate --quick` 6 of 6, the export check 5 of 5, and the live list of the entry below
  again, its digests and learner rows alike.

**On the way.**

- The worker's one odd row is not explained. Of 77 runs of `s1 --features ls` one first learner row gave
  -0.021496661, 1.7% from the usual value; the compile-time build showed no such value in 77. In 480 more runs on
  each tree it did not come again (120 side by side on a quiet host; 360 with each run pinned to two cores, 120 of
  those with a second job of this lane's sharing the card): 570 a tree in all, the one odd row on this tree's side.
- The learner's first update does not repeat bit for bit on either tree. The run has one update of 3 epochs; the
  first two are equal in every run, and the third's loss is -0.02187241055071354 or -0.021872462704777718 (561 and
  390 of 960 runs; a third value, -0.02187246084213257, in 9). The two differ by 5.2e-8 in the loss, 2.8e-4 in `pg`,
  1.2e-6 in the gradient norm.
- `neth_net_dsync` does not look at `cudaMemcpyToSymbol`'s result. The four-width switches have no default case (the
  mask is 6 bits, so they are complete). The critic's tensor-core path loops to a run-time bound now (only with
  `--critic`; not measured).

## 2026-11-23 lane/audit-fixes: checkpoints name their inputs, the draw and the bootstrap are flags, the guide is slim

An audit of the code's naive spots; its list was settled the same day. The commits on df2a60c5 each carry one change.
Everything below was measured on the dev host at the lane's head; the logs are the lane's `out/audit/` (not
committed).

**What changed.**

- *Checkpoints say which inputs they were built for* (a6dd740a). An `.ntw` file starts `NTW2`, a header length and
  `variant V\nfeatures F\nscalars N\n`; the tensor records follow as they were. One parser and one writer serve every
  reader (`neth_checkpoint.c`, built with `-DNETH_NTW_ONLY` where net.h is all there is). Before, an `s1.ls` model and
  an `s1.dk.or` model have the same tensor shapes (169 scalars) and loaded into each other without a word.
  - A file built for a feature the build lacks is refused, both named. One with fewer features than the run loads
    with zero weights on the rest, as a prefix file did.
  - An NTW1 file with features is refused with the command that migrates it:
    `ntinit --migrate IN.ntw OUT.ntw --features ls`. Three on the dev host have 169 scalars and need it: `ckpt-060.ntw`,
    `curric2-R100-s3.ntw`, `s64big-final.ntw` (their Adam files too; the file cannot say which 14, the command asks).
    An NTW1 file of 155 scalars loads as before.
- *Run files read lines of any length* (8b3b1fc1): `getline` in `neth_runconf.c` and `worldconf.c`. A 3,271-byte
  `starts.seeds` line (300 seeds) runs; df2a60c5 refused it with "not KEY: VALUE".
- *The draw's temperature and greedy choice are flags* (46bdddaa, 3f65d6ce): `--temp T`, `--greedy keys|cam|both`, on
  any build, in place of the words `.t3 .t5 .t7 .gk .gc .gkc`. A frozen policy only: refused with `--learn 1`, with
  `--teacher`, and on a fused `.af` build. `actor_check [--temp T] [--greedy ...]`, raweval `-T`, rawpix `RP_DRAW`.
  A word that is none of actor.mk's stops make (it compiled as the variant without it before).
- *A timed-out episode is not a death* (3c6684fb, 4a3685db, 3ad3f120). `terminations` beside `truncations` in the
  vector env's buffers: the task's own end against the clock's. The learner bootstraps a terminated row from zero, as
  before, and a timed-out one from its own value: `--trunc-boot on|off` (run file `ppo.trunc_boot`, default on).
  `--check-learn` pins the GAE on a hand-made segment, both ways.
  - The value is one step stale: the critic never sees the timed-out episode's last observation (the next row is the
    new episode's first).
  - A run is no longer bit for bit a df2a60c5 run once a timeout falls inside a segment. `--trunc-boot off` is the
    learner as it was.
  - `struct neth_vec_bufs` gained a member, the last. A trainer built before the change runs against the new
    `libneth.so` as it did: df2a60c5's `s1` trainer gives its own trajectory digest, and its `s1.r1.m4.b.f` its own
    first learner row, on this tree's library. In the middle of the struct (3c6684fb) they failed on the
    observation's shape.
- *Wood-punch grades on its win rate* (08d34a0c, 2400d576): the episode record keeps `win`, `episodes.jsonl` has
  `"win": 0|1` under `ms`, `nether eval` prints `win k/n` with its Wilson interval and pairs it (McNemar), and
  `configs/envs/wood-punch.yaml` has `primary_metric: win`.
  - Recordings are version 4 (312 bytes an episode). A reader from an older tree refuses them.
  - The models trained on wood-punch so far win 0 of 512, 0 of 128 and 0 of 64 scored episodes, so a flywheel step
    there can only KEEP once a candidate wins.
- *The guide* (95e7b194): `AGENTS.md` from 91,446 bytes to 16,890: the rules and the method, its Rules section 3,425
  bytes. The command ledger it carried is `git show df2a60c5:AGENTS.md`; `docs/scripts.md` says so.
- *The engine* (12098790): `ai.c` resolves `blocks_movement`'s class once per block id, into `ai_move_class[4096]`,
  instead of up to 11 `strcmp` calls on each navigation clearance check. The 3,925 unregistered ids have no class
  name, which the old chain read past.
- *The index* (69a7a371): `RegionFile.java`'s record cited `read_whole`, which `region.c` no longer has.
- *Two leftovers* (0242601d): the pipe releases the terminations buffer it pinned, and the `truncations` comment says
  what sets it.

**Measured.**

- The checks on the merged tree: `train-actor-v-check`, `train-wire-check` (with the GAE case: 6 PASS),
  `train-loop-check` and `nether gate --quick` (6 of 6) all pass. `train-loop-check`'s trajectory digests are
  df2a60c5's: 440c72b7dfc3dd9f and 486fdf7386b0ea68.
- The rules through `ntloop` itself: an `s1.dk.or` build refuses an `s1.ls` file and the other way round; a 155-scalar
  file loads in both; the migrated `ckpt-060` loads in `s1.ls` and is refused by `s1.dk.or`. (At 35db84ac. The entry
  above gives the say to the file's header instead.)
- The old draws by flag, one weights file and one command, the old binaries df2a60c5's run on this tree's files: no
  flag gives 6f4e8cedc27eadf6 (the plain build's), `--temp 0.5` 0f7b4d9215041c4a (`.t5`'s), `--greedy both`
  ac444ceb1fa8b080 (`.gkc`'s), also with `--graph 1`.
- The learner, `s1.r1.m4.b.f`, its first row with an update: `--trunc-boot off` gives a df2a60c5 first update field for
  field (loss -0.024073058739304543 or -0.024320514872670174 at ep-len 40: the two orders the groups finish in);
  `on` gives -0.024233540520071983 or -0.024046944454312325, its value loss 3.1e-7 where `off` has 1.15e-4; at
  ep-len 100, where the first segment has no end, both give -0.02423546463251114, a df2a60c5 row.
- `nether eval` on dirt-punch with a trained model: win 511 of 512 and 512 of 512 on two evals; live on the merged
  tree, 64 of 64.
- The engine: 170,131,456 cases of the old chain against the table, 0 differ (2,260,800 of them where the old chain
  met a NULL name). A whole replay of `gold-g1-s42` takes 0.17% fewer instructions (2,955,543,001 against
  2,950,607,491); the micro-measurement 1,100,865,098 against 139,385,044 for 3,420,000 calls, 7.9 times fewer.
- The native test suite fails the same 52 jobs at the base commit and at the lane's head, each for a missing
  recording directory (this host has `gold-g1-s42` only); 11 pass.

**On the way.**

- This host has no `hud_mixed` recording (`out/java/render` holds `forest-fast`), so `make -C csrc` leaves
  `items.rgba` and `mobs/mushroom_red.rgba` out of `out/assets` (75 of 77), and `train-loop-check` and every live
  trainer run stop on them. The lane records the scene into its own `out/audit/scenes/hud_mixed` (the oracle's
  `script` target, 9 s) and remakes the assets from it (`make -C csrc assets HUDSCENE=...`): then `digest-128x2` and
  `digest-128x2-f32` are as `gates.tsv` pins. A tree makes its own with `make -C oracle render-scenes`.
- `hostfixed.yaml` and `host16.yaml` are not made by `train-loop-cfg`, so two of the four `digest-128x2` pins do not
  run here.
- A lane links `out/java` to the canonical tree's. The lane's first `make -C oracle build` (the recording needs it)
  made its `oracle/src` from the cache and the patch (identical to the canonical tree's: 0 of 1,287 files differ) and
  rebuilt the shared `out/java/classes` (2,089 classes, 5 s), so that stamp moved. Nothing was running against them.
- Left for later: `curric.h` reads `index.tsv` through `char line[8192]`; `strcmp` on a `class_name` that may be NULL
  in `seedworld.c`, `survival.c`, `enchant.c`, `tileticks.c`, `randomtick.c`; `wood-logs3.yaml` and `ore-mine.yaml`
  still grade on `ret`; `ai.c` and `pathfind.c` keep a block-class table each; `learn_io.h`'s fixture reader reads
  NTW1 only; `neth_vec_bufs.terminals` is never set or read; a chain's forced end counts as a timeout; the learner's
  books after the first update do not repeat run to run (the actor's refresh timing), so long comparisons need a
  deterministic refresh.

## 2026-11-23 lane/configs-nw-clean: the S6 pass is tickpass; configs/ holds only the registry files and folders

**What changed.**

- `csrc/cuda/tick/nwpass.cpp` is `tickpass.cpp` (`out/native/cuda/tick/tickpass.so`). The passes are
  `tick-rename`, `tick-roots`, `tick-stub` and `tick-dev`, the option `-tick-callbacks`. The device runtime's
  `nwdev_*` names and `NWDEV_*` macros are `tickdev_*` and `TICKDEV_*`, `mirror.tsv`'s kept list is
  `tick-roots.kept`. No `nwpass`, `nwdev`, `nw-rename`, `nw-roots`, `nw-stub` or `nw-dev` is left in `csrc/`.
- `configs/` at its root holds `gates.yaml`, `fidelity.yaml` and `checkpoints.tsv`, and the folders `envs`, `sim`,
  `algo`, `gyms` and `tests`.
  - `configs/tests`: the 31 run files a Makefile, `gates.tsv`, `macrodig.tsv`, a case binary or the raw tools
    (`raw*.mk`, `raweval.sh`) read, moved as they were, with every caller's path. Also `pgo-devcast.yaml` (the former
    `workstation-scalable.yaml`, kept whole for `pgo.mk`'s `PGO_DEV_CFG` so the profile's workload stays the same).
  - New: `configs/sim/rtx3090.yaml` (128 worlds in 16 groups of 8, 32 workers) and `configs/sim/blackwell.yaml`
    (256 in 8 of 32, 48 workers), both the 64x64 device cast at FP32 and one tick a step. Also
    `configs/envs/wood-logs3.yaml` (three logs, the hint, 30 s, from spawn starts) and `configs/envs/ore-mine.yaml`
    (iron ore with a stone pickaxe, 20 s, rawstarts' dev starts).
  - Deleted: eval-van32, gold, ladder, ppoac, ppoac-eval, s64boot, speedrun-grpo, stronghold-vanilla, t1-overworld,
    the t2 and t3 files, workstation-ladder, workstation-scalable-tps2, desktop3090-scalable and rawskill-pot64.
    They are still in git history (`git show 50eeb8f3:configs/NAME.yaml`).
- A config in a folder of `configs/` resolves a relative `pipeline.start` against the tree, as one in `configs/`
  does. This holds in `wconf_start_path`, `cr_start_abs` and `WorldConf.root`. `worldconf_check` reads
  `configs/*.yaml` (minus gates.yaml and fidelity.yaml, which are not world files) and `configs/tests/*.yaml`, and
  checks that `configs/tests/x.yaml` resolves to `/r/out/s`.

**Why the raw run files and the PGO file stayed.** `raw*.mk`, `raweval.sh` and `ntloop --config` read a run file.
An env or sim layer is not one: `wconf_load` refuses its `description:` line. So pointing those tools at
`configs/envs` or `configs/sim` would have broken them.

**Receipts (CPU only).** `worldconf_check` on this tree's configs, with a recording tree's `out/` linked in: ok, 32
named configs. Every moved file that matched its start before still matches from `configs/tests`. `nether list`
shows 6 envs, 5 sims and 2 algos. `nether train --env wood-logs3 --sim rtx3090|blackwell --algo ppo-wood` composes.
`nether harvest --env ore-mine|wood-logs3 --dry-run` prints the rawstarts commands. `tickpass.so` builds with
clang 21, and `opt -passes=tick-roots -tick-callbacks=` loads it.

## 2026-11-23 lane/nether-polish: `nether` is the binary; env/sim/algo layers composed in C; harvest makes verified split banks in seconds; the quick gate passes on a fresh checkout in 2.7 s

**What changed.**

- `csrc/cli/netherite.c` is `nether.c`. `make` and `make cli` build `out/bin/nether`, `make install` installs
  `$(PREFIX)/bin/nether`, and every banner, prefix and document says `nether`.
- New layer directories: `configs/envs` (wood-punch, iron-mine, end-crystal-bow, dragon-finish), `configs/sim`
  (fast-64, exact-64, cpu-debug) and `configs/algo` (ppo-raw, ppo-wood). `train`, `eval`, `flywheel` and
  `harvest` take `--env`, `--sim` and `--algo` (a name or a path).
- `csrc/cli/cli_compose.c` merges them in this order: the run file given, sim, algo, env, then `--set`. The result
  goes to `out/compose/LABEL-HASH.{run,gym,bank}.yaml`.
  - An env's `episode.seconds` becomes `sim.pipeline.episode_seconds`.
  - Its `reward` becomes `policy.task`, and `actions.keys` becomes `policy.task.keys`.
  - Its `eval`, `harvest`, `train` and `flywheel` keys are the verbs' own.
  - A key no table line takes is refused.
  - `nether list` prints the registry in 0.47 ms (median of 30).
- `nether harvest` gained:
  - `--seeds A..B`;
  - `harvest.prepare` (run once);
  - `source` (library rows cut at a stage);
  - `steps`;
  - `reject` (a regex; a rejected seed is done, not failed);
  - `verify` once per `{start}`;
  - merged `DIR/train/index.tsv` and `DIR/eval/index.tsv`, each row's seed checked against the SHA-256 split.
- `rawstarts` gained `--near-block ID:DIST` and `--biome NAME`. `--logs` and the placement mode are byte-identical
  to before.
- `--profile` (or `NETHER_PROFILE=1`) prints ms per phase.
- `nether gate` gained `--no-build` (it skips checks marked `build: yes`) and an `ms` field per check.

**Measured** (64-core box, hyperfine, at least 3 runs, medians; `docs/benchmarks.md` has every table):

- `--help` 0.58 ms and `list` 0.47 ms.
- Offline End eval compare 4.09 ms (dragon 137/256 against 0/256, McNemar p 1.15e-41, as the overnight report
  says).
- Quick gate 2.73 s with `--no-build` and 3.31 s with builds. The pinned 128x2 digest is 2.55 s of that. The
  globals check went from 0.86 s to 0.11 s.
- `nether ab`: 1.13, 2.28 and 4.52 s for 1, 2 and 4 rounds, linear, one digest.
- `harvest --env wood-punch`, 1 thread: 2.17 s for 8 seeds and 3.96 s for 16, with byte-identical indexes at 1
  and 8 threads and overlap 0.
- Live flywheel step on the RTX 3090 box (composed wood-punch + fast-64 + ppo-wood, 300,000 env-steps, 16-episode
  exact eval): 10.2 to 10.3 s of work, 3 of 3 BASELINE, 0 NaN skips.

**Fixed on the way.**

- *`gates.tsv` observation pins.* Every observation pin matched the canonical trees' `out/assets/items.rgba`,
  which was cut from a `hud_mixed` scene recorded 2026-09-24. Today's oracle records that scene differently, and
  identically on both machines. All 8 recomputable observation digests were repinned; every trajectory digest
  held.
  - A tree with the old `out/assets` needs `make -C oracle render-scenes && make -C csrc assets` (after moving
    the old directory aside).
  - `digest-pearl-walk` was not repinned (its dev start is not on this host).
- *Derived run files.* Every derived run file (`out/compose`, `out/flywheel/RUN/run.yaml`, `out/train/...`) now
  carries an absolute `pipeline.start` (`cr_start_abs`, resolved as `wconf_start_path` resolves it for the
  source file). Before, a relative start resolved next to the derived file, and the cast found no atlas there.
- *`train-prep`* takes a root-relative start path such as a seed set's `s1`.
- *`cy_dump`* writes `-0.5` plain, because ntloop's reader takes no quotes.
- *Flywheel rate.* The flywheel reports a run shorter than one log interval at its overall rate instead of NaN.
- *Scripts.* Five dead scripts deleted (`docs/scripts.md`).
- *Privacy.* The privacy sweep gave every config, comment and DEVLOG host mention a generic label.

**Next.** Harvest the real banks with `--env` (wood-punch over the 1,000-seed set; iron-mine over the statebank),
then run flywheel steps from them. A tree whose `out/assets` predates today should remake it before trusting the
quick gate.

## 2026-11-23 lane/overnight-2026-11-23-unified: Wave 1's four lanes merged; the recurrent net's graph; r1 trains fastest at 160 worlds in 5 groups of 32 (2.04x base with learning on)

**Merged** onto 2e329bc3: lane/hill-straggler (--graph's copy-node front, the side-stream cast, configs/desktop3090-scalable.yaml),
lane/hill-raycast-sparse (RCF_FLAT), lane/hill-train-fidelity (the device-cast PGO profile with keep-text-section-prefix,
--train-skip-ambient, --distant-tick-radius, client.cast_radius, REC_FID_*) and lane/hill-rnn-hotbar
(s1.ls.hb.hs.dk.r1.m4.b.f.sb). Two conflicts: DEVLOG (both entries kept) and neth_record_hook.c's record_start call (the
fidelity lane's new runconf argument with the RNN lane's o->macros). csrc/mods/macros untouched.

**The profile after the merge** (desktop-3090, RTX 3090, the r1 variant, --learn 1, dist64, the run file's 128 worlds in 16 groups
of 8): 89,057 env-steps/s with the main thread busy 95.4% of the window and 16.2 of 32 workers stepping: the sim was no
longer the limit, the main thread was, and --graph 1 was off for a recurrent net (neth_pipe.c: launch 0.061 of a 0.090 ms
group step). Two answers, both measured:

- Group size. r1 at learn 1, dist64, 3 rounds: 128 in 8x16 106,443; 128 in 4x32 115,855; 96 in 6x16 113,424; 96 in 3x32
  99,625; 160 in 5x32 122,050; 192 in 6x32 119,333. Bigger groups also give the recurrent learner bigger updates (a
  segment an update: 1,024 samples at groups of 8, 4,096 at 32).
- The recurrent net under --graph (this lane, loop.cu neth_grnn_h0, neth_pipe.c graph_capture): the actor's state is
  already at a fixed place a group (hst); its episode starts are the staging block's done bytes (zero before the group's
  first outcome, where the launch without the graph passes NULL), and one kernel in the graph writes the segment's start
  state h0 into the slot's half at its step 0. Parity: --learn 0 digests equal with and without the graph (7be027a01210877b
  fresh net; 2fd859bf511ab0e7 on a briefly trained net with 960 resets), and every segment's h0 hashed at the end equal
  (565935cc56c19fb7; a fresh net's h stays 0, so that check needs the trained one). Learn-on digests are not reproducible
  even without the graph (two runs: 77fe5b065cd85483, 3d0d6fb29246fcef), so they are not a parity check. Speed, learn 1,
  3 rounds: 128 in 8x16 106,135 to 110,548 (1.042x, apart); 160 in 5x32 123,299 to 121,949 (0.989x, apart). It helps
  where the main thread binds and not at the best shape: Phase 2's r1 runs take 160 in 5x32 without the graph.

## 2026-11-22 lane/hill-straggler: on desktop-3090 the shape is the lever, not the barrier: 128 worlds in groups of 8 run 1.52x the 256-in-32 shape (steady) and 1.54x (reset-heavy), every digest equal to base; configs/desktop3090-scalable.yaml

The brief: kill the 20% per-group barrier loss (a group is received only when its slowest env is done, vecenv.c
vec_recv), first by smaller groups on lane/cuda-graph's --graph (fbdb488a), then by a dynamic ready-queue batcher.
Measured on desktop-3090 (Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 16 cores, 32 threads, 2 L3s; RTX 3090), workstation-scalable.yaml without its library
of starts (desktop-3090's cache lacks statebank-2026-11-19/lib: the bench copy drops starts.library, curriculum, floor and
spawn_min), --init s64-it42 --critic 128 --threads 32 --learn 0 --digest, the cast fast32, served (no --depth).

- At the config's shape (256 worlds, 8 groups of 32) the workers are not idle: 31.2 of 32 stepping on average (the
  pool's own step time, tick_ns), so the barrier costs desktop-3090 about 2%, not 20% (the 20% was gpu-workstation's 64 workers at
  4 envs a worker). The pool already steals across L3s (pipeline.c: layout doms sets steal 1).
- What moves desktop-3090 is the number of worlds: an env-step costs 0.49 ms of a worker at 256 worlds and 0.30 ms at 128
  (steady; 0.64 and 0.42 ms reset-heavy), the same code and trajectory kind, so the world count's memory against the
  L3s is the likely cause (not profiled). Groups of 8 rather than 16 add about 4% at 128 worlds; --graph about 1%,
  but it is what keeps 16 groups' main thread off its limit (busy 89.0% of the window at base, 53.7% with the graph).
- Receipts: 4 rounds each, interleaved (out/native/abrun), base 2e329bc3 against fbdb488a, load 19 to 36 from the
  other Wave 1 lanes on the host. Env-steps/s medians (min to max):

  | variant | steady (6000 steps) | reset-heavy (6000, ep-len 2000) | digest steady / reset |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | base, 256 in 8 of 32 | 63,967 (60,469 to 64,103) | 45,640 (38,157 to 47,331) | e3afa35c767cb1e1 / 273791170ec9d957 |
  | fbdb488a --graph 1, 256 in 8 | 63,568 (60,909 to 63,767), 0.99 | 47,070 (45,351 to 47,206), 1.03, overlap | the same |
  | base, 128 in 16 of 8 | 96,427 (96,212 to 96,934), 1.51 | 69,132 (68,916 to 69,539), 1.51 | fa45675da1ff4b13 / b13f9781ce21ca75 |
  | fbdb488a --graph 1, 128 in 16 | 97,461 (97,089 to 98,953), 1.52 | 70,144 (69,842 to 70,322), 1.54 | the same |
  | fbdb488a --graph 1 --depth 15 | 92,785 (92,529 to 93,847), 1.45 | 68,157 (67,746 to 68,351), 1.49 | the same |

  Every run of a shape printed one digest, base and candidate alike: --graph and served against depth change no
  trajectory. A shape's digest is its own (another grouping draws other samples), so 128 against 256 is a
  throughput comparison of two trajectories, not a byte-for-byte one.
- The world count around it (3 rounds, steady, --graph 1, groups of 8): 64 worlds 88,072, 96 worlds 100,772, 128
  worlds 96,780, 160 worlds 88,415. 96 is 4% past 128 (apart); the run file keeps 128 (4 envs a worker, the full
  receipt, a quarter more episodes in parallel); 96 is the next thing to try in a training run.
- Learning on (--learn 1, ppo.mb 8192: at groups of 8 that is 8 segments of 128 x 8 an update, the same batch):
  256 in 32 at 54,102 (one run) against 128 in 8 at 73,358 and 72,967, about 1.35x, rough; 39 updates at 21.3 ms
  of the device each, no NaN. Fewer worlds is fewer episodes in parallel for the same samples: a training run's
  curve, not this lane's numbers, says whether 128 learns as well as 256.
- Not built: the dynamic ready-queue batcher. With groups of 8 the workers step 29.6 of 32 on average, so it could
  win back at most about 7% here, and it moves every per-group structure (the vec env's groups, a graph captured per
  group, the segments [T][gs], the casts by group) to per-env slots. It is worth building only where the workers
  idle more: gpu-workstation's 64 workers. The idle there should be measured again at gpu-workstation's best world count first.

configs/desktop3090-scalable.yaml: workstation-scalable.yaml with worlds 128, groups 16, group 8, batch 128, depth 16 and
workers 32 (the run needs the library of starts on the host). Gates: make -C csrc globals PASS (612 writable
symbols, all allowed), make -C csrc/runtime train-wire-check PASS (check-actor fp32 0 of 4,096 actions differ); no
code changed, csrc/mods/macros untouched.

## 2026-11-23 lane/hill-raycast-sparse: the fast casts' air loop with one back edge; fast32 1.77x a launch, every frame byte-equal; registers and air bricks not the lever

**What changed.** cast_fast.cu's DDA air loop (RCF_FLAT, default 1): its `continue`s inside branches became if/else
chains that all end at the loop's foot, so a warp's lanes reconverge every step. The same steps, loads and decisions in
the same order; RCF_FLAT 0 keeps the old form. `make -C csrc gpu-raycast-bench VARIANT=NAME NVXFLAGS=...` now compiles
cast_fast.cu with the flags too (it linked the default's object), so RCF_BS, RCF_MINB and RCF_FLAT sweep there.

**Why.** On the 3090, fast32 was 2x slower than the strict FP32 cast (0.5691 against 0.2895 ms a launch on the same
dump, 2 bytes of 1.5 MB apart). ncu: fast32 issued 164.5M warp instructions against 85.2M, 7.6 lanes active an
instruction against 16.8, and its air loop 5 lanes of 32 (FP32's structured loop 13 to 14; cast.cu's lane/rcsplit note
is the same bug). After: 76 registers as before, no spills.

**Receipts** (desktop-3090 RTX 3090, abrun 4 rounds, shared GPU lock). rcbench on a fresh 128-env 64x64 workstation-scalable dump
(ntloop --dump-cast 600): 0.5701 -> 0.3225 ms a launch (apart), frames and seen records equal to the dump's. ntloop
s1.ls.m4.b.f.sb, workstation-scalable's sim, s64-it42, --ns 256 --warm 200 --steps 2000 --learn 0: steady 29,158 -> 30,128
env-steps/s (+3.3%, apart), frame digest 6cd983567272cbfa and trajectory digest 9cdfb73875e76b6c on all 8 runs;
--ep-len 2000 (256 resets a run) 27,323 -> 28,214 (+3.3%, overlap: base spread 5.2%), 9f59173bf3a5cf37 /
8e066e611996be19 on all 8. desktop-3090 is CPU-bound (30 of 32 workers stepping), so the kernel's gain is small end to end
here. Nether (gold nether, seed 42) and End (gold end) at 64x64 fast32, 64 envs, 600 steps: frame digests
34a4be6466121e4d and cfbffecd0d7f9871, trajectory digests eeb7e07e1dd7937e and dd85eaf6553d1b83, equal before and
after (one run each: 27.4k -> 32.3k and 30.2k -> 38.4k env-steps/s, rough). globals PASS, train-wire-check PASS,
csrc/mods/macros untouched.

**Not the lever.** Registers: the kernel is 76 (not 128) on sm_86, 50% theoretical occupancy; before the fix 64
registers (RCF_MINB 8, no spills) measured 0.5719 against 0.5687 ms (overlap) and 64-thread blocks 2% slower. After
it, MINB 8 is 0.3132 against 0.3217 ms (2.6%, apart, frames equal): not taken, too small to show end to end on desktop-3090;
a candidate where the GPU bounds. A 4x4x4 air-brick skip: cast.cu has it (RC_BRICKJ, off: lane/raycast measured it
costing more than it saved), these rays average 12.7 air steps, and a jump recomputes t where fast32's loop adds dtx,
so its frames would move. The entity cull in rc_head_get was not reached.

## 2026-11-21 lane/ticks-per-step: tps 2 and 4 Java-exact through the recorder (rec v3); 1.54x game-ticks/s at tps 2 on a contended gpu-workstation but 1.10x on a quieter one; tps 2 keeps depth on 256 held-out worlds, tps 4 halves it; configs/workstation-scalable-tps2.yaml

made (`neth_vec_bufs.tick_acts`, `tick_macro`; NULL at T 1), the recorder writes them as rec version 3 subs
(`rec_chunk.nsub`, `REC_SUB_BYTES`), `ntrec tape` writes T lines a step (the act, then the sub or the hold-only act),
`ntrec end` counts T ticks a step. A reset step, which recv runs before the recorder reads the episode's last step,
no longer clears the buffers (it wiped the last step's macro ticks: 3 lines of a tps 4 script differed).
`rec-gate REC_TPS=T` runs its vanilla case at T. (2) 66c29600: `--score`'s quota was ep_len + 1 decisions with ep_len
in ticks, so a tps T eval played T episodes and scored the first (656 s for 168 s of work at tps 4); now

## 2026-11-19 lane/gpu-workstation-roofline: ppoac's trainer on gpu-workstation GPU 0, 1.78x over whole episodes by layout (64 workers, the FP32 cast; configs/workstation-scalable.yaml); the env's CPU tick bounds it, the GPU 37 to 86% busy; 16 groups won only on short windows; a start's resident zero pages given back (12 MB a start, digests equal)

**Setup.** gpu-workstation (Threadripper PRO 9985WX, 64 cores in eight 32 MB L3s; RTX PRO 6000, sm_120), GPU 0 only, RSS cap
20 GB. ntloop s1.ls built with CUDA_ARCH=sm_120. gpu-workstation has neither library-kills nor ppo-ac's seed set, so the
starts are 64 state-bank library starts (six of each overworld stage, ten Nether; ~/.cache/netherite-native/
workstation-scalable/lib64, symlinks into statebank-2026-11-19/lib) and 16 state-bank spawns. Everything else is
configs/ppoac.yaml (vanilla, easy, rd 4, 12 macro families, 107 options, s64-it42, --critic 128). The host was shared
the whole time: the sibling lanes' 5 to 20 chain processes, a 38-thread ntloop (chooser-ppo, GPU 3) and python jobs,
load 57 to 130 on 128 threads. Only abrun's interleaved rounds compare. Numbers from separate runs are labelled rough.

**Where an env-step goes** (perf record, 60 workers, N 256, by source object): the engine's tick 72% (vanilla mob
spawning and random ticks 7.1 of it; the mobs' living, entity, combat, ai and pathfind most of the rest), the
macros, views and hooks 14.5% (state_hook's census 3.6, obsview_block 3.3: called per block), pool scheduling 6.7%,
libc and kernel 4.3%, the host side of the cast 2.2%. Flat: no function over 4.1%. 1.84 to 1.91 M instructions
an env-step at every env count.

**The env count** (no library, so 320 envs fit; 64 workers, 32 envs a group; perf stat 8 s mid-run; one run each):

        envs   env-steps/s  stepping  IPC   DRAM fills an env-step  RSS
        128       80,203     29.0    1.26        3,089             7.5 GB
        192      104,677     40.6    1.18        4,313            10.2 GB
        256      117,881     52.1    1.02        5,892            12.9 GB
        320      123,639     57.0    1.00        6,663            15.6 GB

The L3 cliff (lane/envcpu's) is there: more envs raise throughput only by giving the workers more to step, while each
worker's step takes 28% longer (0.361 to 0.461 ms). DRAM traffic at 320 is about 53 GB/s (6,663 x 64 B x 123,639), far under the host's
bandwidth: latency, not bandwidth. 512 and 1,024 envs were not run: about 47 MB an env puts them at 25 and 37 GB (the
cap is 20).

**The levers, abrun, 3 rounds, medians** (out/ab in the lane): 64 workers against 30 at 8 groups 1.73x (108,821
against 62,770, apart); 96 workers 0.93x of 64 and the learner off 1.08x. 16 groups against 8 at 64 workers 1.13x
(125,913 against 111,450, apart; the main thread 74% busy against 49%) on 6,000-step windows, but 0.92x on
30,000-step ones (56,363 against 61,481, overlap; the main thread 84 to 89% busy against 56 to 68%): not kept; 4 groups 0.78x; 32 groups 1.03x (the main
thread 94% busy, the next bound). 288 envs in 18 groups 1.015x of 16 groups at 256 (1.5 GB more). The FP32 cast
against FP64 at 16 groups 1.04x (130,062 against 124,792, apart); fixed 1.03x. Vanilla against fast fidelity
(spawning, random ticks and weather off), one pair each, rough: 67,909 against 142,220 at 30 workers (2.1x), 120,685
against 161,841 at 60. The library: 67,494 env-steps/s without it against 67,909 with it, so no step cost, but 4.9 GB
of RSS for 64 starts. ppoac's macros cut to recipe,strip: 60,707, slower (other behaviour, not comparable).

**The GPU** (nsys 3 s at 16 groups; ncu serialized): with the FP64 cast the kernels' union is 86.3% busy and
rc_cast<double> 46% of kernel time; with workstation-scalable (FP32) 37.2%. ncu: rc_cast is latency bound in either
precision: 51 ns a block FP64, 34 to 58 FP32, occupancy 27 to 30% (128 registers a thread, 33% theoretical), SM
throughput 42% (FP64) and 13% (FP32), DRAM under 4%. The actor's GEMMs (gemm_mma, k_cf) launch 13 to 16 blocks on
188 SMs and reach 1 to 5% of throughput: the net is too small for the bf16 roofline (548 TFLOPS) to matter. The main
thread issues every CUDA call (one thread, 127k launches and 78k copies in 3 s, about 5.4 kernels and 3.4 copies a
group step); its own laps at 16 groups: 0.12 ms a group step, launch 0.065 of it, 71 to 78% busy.

**Why desktop-3090's ppoac ran 56,174 against README's 148,028.** README's 64x64 number is s64boot's shape: fast fidelity,
two macro families, one spawn start, 4 groups. Fast against vanilla is 2.1x here at 30 workers (rough), which takes 56k
to about 118k. desktop-3090's 30 workers share 16 cores: 27.3 stepping at 56,174 is 0.49 ms a worker's env-step, against
0.33 ms on gpu-workstation's unshared cores at load 5. The library costs RAM, not steps (43 GB on desktop-3090: about 77 MB a held
start, 274 of them). The remaining 1.25x (118k to 148k) was not measured: s64boot's 5-minute spawn episodes against
ppoac's late-stage starts and 10-minute episodes are the likely difference.

**Ceiling on gpu-workstation** (projections from the counters, not runs): 64 cores at 4.1 GHz (the stepping workers' measured
clock) and 1.84 M instructions an env-step give 145k env-steps/s at IPC 1.0 (256+ envs) and 177k at IPC 1.26 (128 envs),
plus SMT's 6 to 13% (lane/rlbind) on an idle host. workstation-scalable's whole-episode runs reached 99,794 to 131,951 on the shared host. The
GPU would carry about 2.7x more casts and updates before it bounds (37% busy).

**Kept.**
- configs/workstation-scalable.yaml: ppoac.yaml with performance.workers 0 (one a physical core), client.cast_precision 32
  and the state-bank starts; groups stay 8 (4,096 samples an update, ppoac's). Against ppoac's layout on the same
  starts, 30,000 steps an env (about 2.5 episodes, 512 resets a run), abrun 4 rounds: 111,676 against 62,752
  env-steps/s, 1.78x, apart (after 99,794 to 124,541, before 59,306 to 64,659; load 55 to 103). An earlier 3-round
  window of the same pair read 68,646 against 55,891 (1.23x, apart) with the main thread's send (it waits on the
  group's cast) at 0.19 to 0.24 ms a group step in both builds against 0.05 to 0.07 in the 4-round one: something on
  the host or GPU slowed both then, not found. The 16-group version on 13,000-step windows read 124,630 against 60,036
  (2.08x), which is the short-window effect above. A lone 30,000-step run of the final config: 131,951. A 9-minute run
  held RSS at 18.4 to 18.9 GB.
- pool.c start_drop_zero: once a start is scanned, each resident all-zero page of its image below the used top goes
  back (image_give_pages). The state bank's images held 49 MB resident against 36 MB nonzero. Steady RSS at 256 envs,
  79 starts, 16 groups, 2 runs each: 17.78 against 16.84 GB (11.9 MB a start; 274 starts would save 3.3 GB);
  throughput the same (129,334 and 130,134 against 129,167 and 131,069). ntloop --digest (standin policy, 64 envs, 300-step
  episodes, resets onto library starts) 1d8a99348d56e23f on both builds, twice each; macro-digests 16 of 16 runnable
  rows PASS (6 rows' starts are not on gpu-workstation: obs-g5-3600, pearl-night-s42, out/java/try/s1sh). -DPOOL_KEEP_ZERO
  builds the before.

**Not done.** 512 and 1,024 envs (RAM cap). A quiet-host measurement (the siblings ran all day). The main thread's
launches as a CUDA graph and the cast's wait out of send (the bound of 16 groups over whole episodes). The census's
48-block height scan, rewritten with one chunk lookup a 16-block run, was exact (1.8 M calls compared, 0 differ) but no
faster (13 to 22 us a call either way: misses on about 49 chunk heightmaps); reverted. Fast fidelity or a fidelity ladder for training (2.1x, but
fast episodes do not replay on Java). Report: the lane's out/report.md.

## 2026-11-18 lane/pground: the pearl hunt priced by its ground, then by a prebuilt floor; the supply is capped by monsters that never tick

The pearl leg (11 or 12 pearls and eyes in 110,000 ticks from the four library pearl starts) had 0 of 256. This lane
asked whether another ground, or a built one, gives the bot endermen it can see. It does not reach the bar on either.
The one change kept for the bot is `threat_ender=low`. The structural finding is that at render distance 4 and 8 the
monster cap is held by monsters that never tick, so they never despawn. Every count below is the server's state or is
labelled as the macro's own books. Every WHAT-IF (a dev start, a changed render distance, a privileged read used to
choose) says so and is never a benchmark row. Rates are 64 attempts × 110,000 ticks at sampler seeds 180000+ unless
named, with one sigma beside them.

**Built (all opt-in or read only; macro-digests unchanged with each off; chain-alone-gate passed before rows were read):**
- `nwrl_ground` and chain `--dig-log`'s G, E, Q, P, O and R rows (69b1d2ed, af0e493b, 5ceab490, f521514c): read only,
  PRIVILEGED. They record the ground a night was spent on, the supply's accounting, enderman-steps by sky, the caves'
  air, and the loaded and watched chunks with the spawner's own count.
- `tools/groundmap.c` (2b614d3c): the grounds within 1,500 blocks from the world generator (a model, `pshare`).
  `tools/vshare.c` (5ceab490): visible spawn cells within 64 of a standing eye.
- `pearl_march` (99546f9e, 448522de; off by default): a surface march at night. It did not beat standing (below).
- `threat_ender` (5208ce92 `reach`, 730efdad `low`; off by default): a screaming enderman within reach of the eye is
  fought. `low` aims 0.4 over its feet, out of the stare cone. Kept (below).
- chain `--kill-trace` and the death trace's target columns (cf38fa75): read only.
- `pearl_floor=watch` (b7482aaa, d3d200e2, 19b705f5, 7a378abf; off by default; a WHAT-IF's fixed rule, never a
  benchmark macro): the bot holds the shelter cell a dev start built round it, stares at an enderman in view, fights
  in reach, fetches a kill's drop, and eats. Its sampler part is the start's walk out (2 steps a yaw bin) and the
  sweep's phase and noise. Without the walk, 64 attempts were one trajectory (the fourth rule).
- chain `--floor-log FILE --floor-box BOX` (eddaf006, bbd3dd1e, 98e83512; read only, PRIVILEGED) with `nwrl_floor`:
  - F rows, per attempt and half day: the box's monsters born and inside, the box's light, and the spawner's count
    against the cap.
  - C rows: the overworld's monsters by kind, ticking or frozen, by chunk band from the player, and how many left or
    came.
  - The gate books, read at find_chunks' cap test (`struct spawner` mon_tests, mon_open, mon_walks, mon_made, books
    only): ticks the monster gate was reached and open, and the pack walks and records made on the open ticks.
- The ledger row pground-rd8-bolt-t99743 was fixed by lane/divfix's 50745f38 (pin divfix-bolt-rd8-s42) and set fixed
  in 50f1b798. On the merged build the s42-bp rd 8 known answer passes, and attempt 3's script is byte-identical to
  before the fix. The other rd 8 legs were not re-run.

**Items 1 to 3, the ground (benchmark where library starts, else WHAT-IF):**
- **Supply map (b1, the kept set).** Pearls a night alive were s2-bp 0.005, s42-bp 0.032, s2-eye 0.101 and s42-eye
  0.045. By the night's ground the open nights were not better than the underground ones (0.037 against 0.052). By the
  night's clear lines within 64, 0, 1 and 2 or more lines gave 0.001, 0.151 and 0.468 pearls a night: a line of sight
  decides it, and the ground does not explain the spread between legs.
- **Grounds within reach (groundmap; a model, not a measurement).** No land within 1,500 blocks is predicted past 2.1x
  its start's share of sky spawns, apart from s2-bp's own cell under the sea.
- **WHAT-IF s2-bp moved to land (Extreme Hills, 399 blocks away).** It gave 0.026 pearls a night (sigma 0.015) against
  the control's 0, a quarter of the model's figure, and it died faster. "Where" is closed.
- **pearl_march (benchmark).** s2-eye 0.073 against 0.101, s42-eye 0.039 against 0.045. It adds path, not distance

- **WHAT-IF render distance (rd 8, 12).** Pearls moved up at rd 12 (s42-eye pooled over two blocks 0.084 against 0.036

  kill-trace cause: the fight lock looked at the enderman's middle within 4, which provokes a fresh stare.
- **threat_ender=low (benchmark, the four rd 4 pearl starts pooled by nights).**
  - Pearls a night 0.045 against 0.043 (+0.2 sigma).
  - Ender deaths about 2 nights against 14.
  - Screamers killed 0.70 against 0.48 (+4.1 sigma).
  - At rd 8 and 12 (WHAT-IF) ender deaths fell to a quarter or a third, and s42-eye's pearls rose (rd 8 0.054 to 0.136,

**The prebuilt floor (orders 1:49 PM to 3:41 PM; every number a WHAT-IF).** The design:

- **The cause, in source.** The spawner counts the cap over a window of ±8 chunks (SpawnerAnimals). A monster ticks
  only with every chunk within 32 blocks of it loaded (World.updateEntityWithOptionalForce), and the server loads
  ±(render distance) chunks (PlayerManager). So at rd 4 and 8 the outer rings of the window hold monsters that never
  tick and never despawn, and they fill the cap: the gate opens on 0.1 to 0.6% of ticks. rd 10 is the least render
  distance that ticks the whole window. There the frozen share falls to 11 to 16%, all in chunks 9 to 16, counted but
  outside the window. The gate opens on 0.7 to 1.5% of ticks, but the count stays at 82 to 84 against 79, with 55 to 57
  ticking monsters within 4 chunks.
- **An inference, not measured.** Those 55 to 57 may be walkers the trench holds, since it lies within the 32 blocks
  where a monster never despawns. The check (q-trench) was cancelled by the 4:56 PM order.
- **Where the encounters went.** At rd 4 and 8 the floor's skeletons shot into the shelter's open face from 8 to 15
  blocks: every rd 4 death on s2 and 37 of 46 at rd 8 had a skeleton in line of sight. The trench removed that (0
  skeleton deaths at rd 10).
- **Verdict.** The rd 10 floor raised distinct endermen seen to 0.709 and 1.149 per 24,000 launched ticks (7.5x and 12x
  Astra's 0.094 at rd 4). Retained pearls are 37x to 74x under the bar, the second block was cancelled, and the sham on
  s42, with no spawnable floor, retained more than the floor (0.0341 against 0.0136, about 1.7 sigma): what the floor
  adds is sightings, not pearls. The Astra review's ceiling is an expected yield at 0.5 pearl a kill on these fixed
  paths, not a bound (a single drop or a changed trajectory can exceed it). At perfect kills and pickup it gives 0.355
  (s42) and 0.574 (s2) per launched cycle, so this floor cannot reach 1.0 on supply alone, and no construction macro was
  built.
- **The loss after supply is delivery to melee range, not aim.** 208 seen and 26 ever within 4 on s42; 337 and 68 on
  s2. (dmin is the eye to the box middle, not the attack check.) This is a lead for a later lane.

## 2026-11-18 lane/choice: the first decision point between macros; the armour-versus-pickaxe choice is real (24 conflicts in 14 of 24 earned launches) and does not matter (diamond pickaxe 20 against 20 of 48)

Result first. The armour craft slot (macros.c's mac_start, after furnace_kit=carry's take) is now one decision with
two options: the next armour piece, or a replacement iron pickaxe. The pickaxe is offered only on a conflict: the one
iron pickaxe held is damaged, no other iron or diamond pickaxe is held, the craft could make an iron pickaxe now, and
the ingots cannot pay for both. Under the default the choice is today's, bit for bit.

On earned states the conflict is common. The forward panel's 24 iron-pickaxe launches met 24 conflicts in 14 launches
(14 worlds, 14 parent states). Forked from identical live memory, the pickaxe changed every conflict launch's
trajectory, but not its outcome. Pooled over two sampler blocks (48 launches), the diamond pickaxe came 20 against 20,
obsidian 6 against 6, the Nether 2 against 2 and deaths 25 against 24. The paired diamond-pickaxe flips were 4 against
the pickaxe in block a and 4 for it in block b (exact McNemar p = 1). So this slot is a genuine choice but not a useful
first one to learn. dispatcher.md's next boundary (gather replacement wood against continue mining) is the next
candidate.

**Where the design came from.** An outside review by GPT 6.2 Astra (~/dev/nv2-lanes/astra/out/dispatcher.md, read
only) found that the macros are a hand-ordered state machine with nothing for a learner to choose between: the policy
chose on 180,613 of 3,609,705 ticks, and a chooser matched random. This lane takes the review's "First commit" (one
choice at the armour-craft slot, with a read-only query and one commit) and its Acceptance items 1 to 3. The measure is
the forward panel's earned states, not a fixture.

**The code (all opt-in).**
- armor.c: `arm_choice_query` is read only and returns the offers as a mask. `arm_craft_commit` holds the armour's
  bookkeeping (cf_had, cf_retry, cf_starts) and runs once, on the armour commit only. `arm_choose` is the slot.
- The offers are ephemeral. The winner is M_CRAFT plus cplan, as before; there is no saved field and no format bump.
- The selector is one run-level option, `armor_choice`:
  - armor (the default);
  - ipick (the pickaxe on a conflict);
  - check (armor, with the query run twice and every env byte and the offers compared);
  - invalid (a test's: a selection never offered; the default is committed and counted).
- The books are `struct arm_choice`, at the end of struct vec_env past lvl, outside every saved range and the RNG.
  nwrl_vec_kit's ch_* fields read them.
- chain: `--choice-log FILE` (a C row a conflict, an E row an attempt), `--replay-reseed S` (a crossing's live part
  drawn from sampler S: a second block from one crossing) and `--mem-at N:FILE` (the raw memory at any step).
- The inputs are the 36-slot inventory with its damage (the server's) and the macros' table memory, the armour's own
  reads. For a pixels-only student this is PRIVILEGED.

**The routing proof.** The fixture is a dev start (a panel spawn start with dev slot ops: 8 ingots, 2 sticks, an iron
pickaxe at damage 200, a table; no chestplate). The scripts are in ~/.cache/netherite-native/choice-stagetable:
fixture.sh, fix.sh and fixtures/.
- armor crafts the chestplate: 8 ingots debited, 6 points worn, 1 iron pickaxe held.
- ipick crafts the pickaxe: 3 ingots and 2 sticks debited, 2 iron pickaxes held, 0 points worn.
- One craft start per commit (queries = commits).
- invalid commits the armour, counted with its reason.
- check: 0 of 2 double queries moved a byte or an offer.
- The rollout and stage rows of armor, check and invalid are byte-equal. Across the 24 earned launches, check ran 101
  double queries and 0 moved a byte or an offer.
- In both arms the fixture's first start (env step 9, the dev slots two ticks old) crafted nothing. The second (step
  1,410) crafted, with no second debit.
- A death or abort mid-craft and a saved mid-craft continuation were not run as separate cases. The crossing restores
  below continue running controllers, and no restore shows a double craft.

**The legacy proof.**
- macro-digests PASS. gates-env's nine CPU digests PASS (GATES-ENV PASS).
- rlbind MACROS=0 builds.
- chain-alone-gate PASS on the fixture under armor_choice=ipick and under armor (600 steps, attempts 3, 17 and 40
  alone and in batches of 4 and 32).
- chain-ka, one per alternative, on library-kills s42-s42k20-iron_pickaxe attempt 14, bound 9,000 ticks, at the start's
  own difficulty (easy). A scan of 64 attempts by 30,000 ticks found conflicts from 4 of 5 library iron-pickaxe starts:
  142 in all; s1cont150 had none. Both arms meet the conflict at step 7,599: the helmet offered, 7 ingots, pickaxe
  damage 120.
  - armor: helmet; ends with 15 points worn and 1 iron pickaxe.
  - ipick: pickaxe; ends with 13 points worn, 2 iron pickaxes, and another place.
  - Both are KA PASS: 9,001 rows, 0 field mismatches, END EQUAL with the place exact.
- From spawn on panel worlds w26 and w45 to 30,000 ticks: master 490fe013's chain, this tree without the option and
  with armor_choice=armor give byte-equal rollout, stage, supply, end, census and death-trace rows.
- The 24 remade panel attempts below equal lane/fwd's archived rows in every log (rollout, stages, end, deaths,
  census, death trace, ladder), so the frozen configuration plays the same on this build.

**Crossings are build-bound.** lane/fwd's raw memory crossings (fwd-stagetable/crossings) do not load on master or
here ("another build's": lane/armed grew the controllers after d9a1e66a). Later lanes rebuild them by the steps prefix:
replay the attempt from spawn on their own build with --crossings, check its rows equal lane/fwd's (scripts/cmpfwd.sh),
then restore. This lane's remade crossings, for the 24 iron-pickaxe worlds, are choice-stagetable/cross/wK (68 MB, this
build only). Their restore check covers the armour arm launched from each conflict world's crossing, against the
uninterrupted attempt. In 14 of 14 the rollout row, end log and death log are byte-equal, and so are every stage row
after the crossing and every conflict row (step, plan, ingots, damage, choice). What differs is only books that build
up over the replayed prefix: the census's owners, the supply log's r_furnace rung step, the slot's cumulative query
count, and the prefix's stage rows (kind and mbit 0, the replay's own).

**How often (item 3).**
- Iron-pickaxe launches: 24 conflicts in 14 of 24. Bucket launches: 7 conflicts in 3 of 21 (most conflicts come before
  the bucket).
- The offered piece: the helmet 14 times (5 to 7 ingots), the leggings 5 (8 to 9), the boots 4 (5 to 6), the chestplate
  once. The iron pickaxe's damage was 134 to 236 of 250.
- lane/wood's pickaxe-bit rows were still running (its dev128 cohort) and are not counted.

**Does it matter (item 4).** Each fork starts from the remade iron-pickaxe crossing: identical live memory and the same
720,000-tick deadline from spawn. Block a draws the live part from the crossing's own sampler (the armour arm is then
the uninterrupted attempt). Block b reseeds it (`--replay-reseed`). A launch with no conflict plays the same in both
arms and is counted once with its arm's rows; deaths and no-conflict launches are in the denominators.

| per original launch, of 24 | block a armour | block a pickaxe | block b armour | block b pickaxe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| launches with a conflict | 14 | 14 | 10 | 10 |
| diamond pickaxe | 12 | 8 | 8 | 12 |
| obsidian | 5 | 2 | 1 | 4 |
| the Nether | 1 | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| blaze rod | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| deaths | 11 | 10 | 14 | 14 |

The blocks disagree in sign on every row. That is the noise of two blocks, not an effect.

A lead from block a, from the books only and not a proven cause: on 6 of 8 conflict launches checked, the pickaxe arm's
armour mine dug 2 to 5 more ores and ran 400 to 1,900 more steps. armor_kit=full rebuys the 3 ingots, so the spare
pickaxe's uses go back into the armour's ore.

Not measured: pickaxe durability at the portal (only 2 Nether entries a block, and no damage column in the logs), and
wood at the portal.

Rows: choice-stagetable/runs/sa (the remade panel), fa, fb (the forks) and score-a.txt, score-b.txt (scripts/score.sh).

## 2026-11-18 lane/armed: armour as its own stage; 28 armoured and 20 Nether-entry starts earned through Java

Result first. The armour stage now ends in real library starts: 28 armoured starts (two for each of library-kills'
14 iron_pickaxe and bucket starts) and 20 Nether-entry starts made from them. Each one was played by the bot, ran on
the Java client with KA PASS, and replays in C with 0 mismatches. None is a dev start.

From the armoured starts to the Nether (nether:10), the armour base reaches 123 of 1,792, against the bench's 100 of
896 on the unarmoured starts: worse, past noise. The gap is in the starts, not the options: the armour stage spends
the iron pickaxe and the wood. wood_bare=climb (new, opt-in) recovers part of it, 163 of 1,792. Adding the existing
obsidian_flint=later gives 178, which is level with the bench (89 a 896 against 100) within noise.

From the 20 Nether-entry starts the rod leg reaches 95 to 104 of 1,280 (7.4 to 8.1%). The library's own unarmoured
Nether starts reach 10 of 448 (2.2%) at the same bounds. Three library starts carry the gain; three stay at zero.

Method. One stage leg at a time, 64 random attempts a start, sampler seeds 180000+. One sigma is about 4 of 64. Two
starts made from one library start are pooled as one pair and also reported per library start. ALONE-GATE ran before
every set's rows were read, and chain-ka ran on every new option and every new start.

- **Earned starts: train/earn.sh** (`make -C csrc/runtime chain-earn`, 3f4c44c5, 49605ed4). The steps:
  - The leg's attempt runs alone; it must reach.
  - The same attempt plays past its arrival on the Java client, toward a target it does not reach (ka.sh, KA PASS).
    Its script is held equal to the leg's through the arrival.
  - The save is the first quiet row (`ntstarts quiet`, with the script's screens).
  - `ntstarts cut` makes the checkpoint, and the oracle saves it.
  - If the manifest's quiescence is not all true, it saves again 20 ticks on, at most 4 times. The rows carry no portal
    state, so 2 of the first 5 Nether earns were saved still in the portal.
  - The join's Snapshot is the start, and C replays it with 0 mismatches.

  next attempt with a different arrival step. The 28 armoured starts are in

## 2026-11-18 lane/divfix: two engine divergences the stage lanes found, a lightning bolt's lava test and a jockey rider's walking block

Both repros now replay with 0 field mismatches: pground-rd8-bolt-t99743 (110,001 rows) and armed-ka27-jockey (43,513
rows). Each has its own commit and a short pin that fails on master 320fc0ce. No pinned digest moved.

**pground-rd8-bolt-t99743 (lane/pground), commit 50745f38.** This is the seed 42 blaze_powder start rejoined at render
distance 8. At row 99,743 a thunderstorm bolt struck at (-1030, 63, -1632), which is column z = 0 of chunk (-65,-102),
the last row of the active set. EntityLightningBolt.onUpdate calls super.onUpdate, so Entity.onEntityUpdate runs on the
bolt's 0.6 x 1.8 box on the tick it is made (updateEntities runs after the chunk loop). Its handleLavaMovement is
World.isMaterialInBB, which reads through getBlock with no chunk-exists test. So the read at z = -1633 loaded chunk
(-65,-103) through provideChunk, and that load moved the overworld's World.rand: the row's d.sw. csrc/engine/lightning.c
lightning_tick modelled neither the water test nor the lava test (its comment said no Random is drawn in air). The new
bolt_entity_update runs both:
- handle_water_movement, with the splash's draws on the bolt's own Random after the first update (width 0.6: 13
  bubbles and 13 splashes);
- ie_material_in_bb over the box shrunk 0.1 sideways and 0.4 at the bottom, which loads a chunk as getBlock does.

The bolt's own fire from lava is not kept, because no world state reads it. The bolt struct gains in_water,
first_update and the motion the flow push adds to, and phase.c's bolt digest folds in the two flags. A bolt has to
strike on an edge column at the edge of the loaded square for this to matter; the finder's rd-4 runs of the same length
passed. Pin `out/java/snapshots/divfix-bolt-rd8-s42`: Java's plain snapshot at tick 99,700 (`make -C oracle replay
SNAPAT=99700 SNAPPLAIN=1 CACHE=0 POOL=0`) and the repro's rows 99,700 to 99,800 (101 rows, 0.33 s; 19 MB). On master it
fails first at row 99,743 on d.sw (230 mismatches); with the fix it is OK.

**armed-ka27-jockey (lane/armed), commit 050536ae.** This is the armoured seed 1 iron_pickaxe start. A spider jockey's
skeleton (7886), riding spider 7887 in water in a cave, had Motion[1] 0.012 in Java against -0.02 in C at row 34,590.
The finder's lead, the 32-block loaded test, is not the cause: C runs the vehicle's and the rider's tests where Java
does. I compared Java snapshots at ticks 34,588 to 34,592 with a C trace of the rider's Random. The mount's Random was
equal on every tick. The rider's Random was equal through its EntityAISwimming roll of row 34,588; then C drew two more
floats, the swim sound's pitch in Entity.moveEntity's walking block. Java runs that block only while ridingEntity ==
null. entity.c tests e->riding, and only the player ever set it, so a mob rider walked. From then on C's rider was two
draws ahead, and the swim roll of row 34,590 landed above 0.8: no jump in C, a jump in Java
((0 + 0.04) x 0.8 - 0.02 = 0.012). The fix is in csrc/engine/living.c: living_move sets e.riding from riding_entity
before entity_move_memo. Only the swim sound draws in that block, so this shows only for a mob rider in water that
passes its next step distance on its own moveEntity. A rider's motion is zeroed every tick and it moves only by its
own drag or gravity. I have not checked which stored recordings hold a mob rider in water.

Pin `out/java/snapshots/divfix-jockey-swim-s1`: Java's plain snapshot at tick 34,150, before the jockey spawns, and
rows 34,150 to 34,620 (471 rows, 0.27 s; 11 MB). On master it fails first at row 34,590 on d.ents (10 mismatches); with
the fix it is OK. A cut at tick 34,500 does not pin it. The snapshot hands C Java's rider, whose step distance is 0
because it never walked, so master's C does not reach a step within 120 rows.

Both pins use the keyframe-cut tape form of lane/divs4: the header, `{"t":N}` placeholders before the snapshot's tick,
then the original rows. The ledger rows belong to the finders (pground.tsv and armed.tsv), so this lane adds none; it
met no third divergence. Checks on 050536ae: `make -s -C csrc test TESTJ=6` exits 0, and both pins round-trip and replay
OK. `make -C csrc/runtime macro-digests` gives MACRO-DIGESTS PASS. The nine CPU digests of gates-env (GT_J=1, under the
lock) give GATES-ENV PASS, each equal to its pin. index-check reports 64 records with errors: the Java records' missing
render evidence, none of them a record this lane changed (lightning.c, lightning.h, living.c). Copies of both pins and
this lane's logs are in ~/.cache/netherite-native/divfix-stagetable. The repros stay in the finders' stagetables
(pground-stagetable/repro, armed-stagetable/repro).

Before the armour leg, on flint's leg (fxcg, kept on its own failure modes): armor_giveup=all (81c005d8: given-up ores

14 -> 0). armor_timing=now alone cost flint's leg 70 -> 51 of 448 with 0 supplied entries: the armour macro drove
8,454 steps an attempt, most of it the walker standing still before ores the planner found no way to.

What the rows showed, in order of size:

- The armour got no turn. armor_kit's start is last in macros.c MACROS, and from the iron starts the strip mine, the
  iron plans and the craft drive the attempt to the next stage: 259 of 320 attempts on the five iron starts never gave
  it a step. armor_turn=station puts it ahead of the strip mines once a furnace and a table are held or in reach; 13 of
  the 14 armour starts begin with no furnace, so armor_turn=make also takes the turn when the station can be made from
  what is held (carry_gate's test: a table from planks or a log, a furnace from 8 cobblestone with a table).
- The mine dug by hand. c150 iron_pickaxe's 64 attempts all stopped with the iron pickaxe in the main inventory and none
  in the hotbar (the wooden and stone ones worn out): the dig walker's tool (common.c best_tool) reads the hotbar only.
  armor_pick=fetch swaps it in (snow's sn_fetch slot rule).
- The craft waited behind the mine. 123 of 185 attempts stopped at 24 ingots with no boots had a piece craftable while
  another macro owned (the armour mine's want counts the sword's, bucket's and flint's ingots past 24) and walked off
  from a table nobody carried. armor_craft=first starts the craft with that piece's plan ahead of every other start and
  ends the mine's run on its scan step for it.
- A bot in a screen is deaf to threat_interrupt: deaths whose first hit landed in the furnace's screen (the smelt's

The divergence (kaudit-skelfire-rainend, mob-other, fixed at 4e80608f). pdig's ka-ohfd-s42eye-a20 (seed 42, easy)
held every row to 13465. At 13466, the tick a rain ended (the strength 0.20 to 0.19), two skeletons under the sky 41
and 67 blocks from the player held Fire 160 on Java and -1 in C, everything else equal. No difficulty is read on that
path. C set the fire in the skeleton's daylight burn as Java does, with equal draws. Then the same update's moveEntity
put it out ("wet and burning: fizz"), because entity_is_wet read nw_env->entity.raining, which sr_world_begin set
before servertick_tick's updateWeather. So at a rain's start and end, moveEntity's World.isRaining was the previous
tick's. The fix sets it in sr_pass_begin, after the weather update.

The neighbours already read the current tick:
- the server's lightning test (is_raining, live);
- the living pass (anw.raining, set in sr_pass_begin);
- the fire block and farmland (fire_set_weather, after the update);
- the player's weather (after serverreplay_tick).

The client world's entities never burn (isRemote). Its one entity_raining reader is the playable client's
clientents.c, off the recordings' path.

After the fix:
- ohfd passes (30001 rows, END EQUAL, exact).
- The whole suite passes.
- macro-digests: 22 of 22.
- The CPU vec_bench digests: 9 of 9, nothing to repin.

## 2026-11-17 lane/ghast: the ghast's player search lacked the sneak range (rods-ghastyaw-s2a5 fixed)

The divergence lane/rods found on 2026-11-16 (seed 2's s2stock10 blaze_rod library start, chain attempt sampler seed
180005: rows equal to 5325, then Nether ghast 1128's Rotation[0] 179.12 on Java, 71.02 in C, 6 field mismatches over
5505 rows) is fixed (2ca84f38) and pinned (out/java/snapshots/rods-ghastyaw-s2a5, the oracle's recording of the
attempt, made with CACHE=0 POOL=0).

The cause. World.getClosestVulnerablePlayer shrinks the range for a sneaking player:
`if (var13.isSneaking()) var16 = p_72846_7_ * 0.800000011920929D;`. Every mob but the ghast searches through
slimes.c an_closest_vulnerable_player, which has that line; the ghast has its own copy, ghasts.c
gh_closest_vulnerable_player, whose comment assumed the player never sneaks, and tested the plain 100 blocks. Ghast
1128 spawned 80.58 blocks from the bot while it sneaked: Java's 80-block search found nobody for 70 ticks (searching
again every tick), C's 100 found the player at once, so the 21-tick aggroCooldown cycle ran on another phase from then
on. That was invisible while the player lived: both sides re-acquire a living target whatever the phase, so the yaw
(aimed at the target) agreed. The player died at row 5321; at 5326 C's cooldown ran out first, the search returned
nothing for a dead player and the yaw fell back to the motion heading (71.02), while Java's cooldown had 5 ticks left
and kept aiming at the body (179.12). Found by printing the C ghast's target and aggroCooldown each tick against the
oracle snapshot's runtime fields (aggroCooldown 5, targetedEntity the player, at t5327).

The fix: gh_player gets `sneaking`, set from the server player in serverreplay.c sr_pass_begin beside health and
is_dead, and gh_closest_vulnerable_player takes `range * 0.800000011920929` when it is set, with Java's
`range < 0.0 ||` test kept. The repro's recording replays with 0 field mismatches (6 before), and the native ghast's
state equals the oracle's runtime fields at t5327.

Checks: `make -s -C csrc test TESTJ=6` rc 0, 907 recordings OK, the 33 whose start holds a ghast among them; smoke 235
of 235; clangcheck ok; macro-digests PASS (22 rows, no digest moved); the alone gate on the s2stock10 blaze_rod Nether
start (attempts 3, 17, 40 alone and in batches of 4 and 32, every step's --nether-trace) ALONE-GATE PASS. The alone
gate takes `-T nether` now (alone_gate.sh): its stronghold trace writes no row in the Nether.

Siblings, by reading: the blaze, pigman, enderman, silverfish, spider and slime all go through
an_closest_vulnerable_player (which has the sneak line); the bat has no target, and the dragon picks from
playerEntities with no range in Java too. One gap all of them share, not fixed: the isInvisible branch (the range times
0.7F * getArmorVisibility, floored at 0.1F) is not ported; no recording reaches it, brewing is off and no drop, trade or
chest gives the potion. The index lists it missing (World.java.json).

What it reaches: a Nether row of an earlier bench or stage table can differ where a ghast was 80 to 100 blocks from a
sneaking bot (the C engine targeted it early); the same attempt rerun now follows Java.

attempts each, sampler seeds 180000+, 110,000 ticks, about five nights, `--start-latched 1`) measured per night: alive
after nights 1 to 5, deaths by first-hit class, pearls, sightings and kills a night alive. Two options kept, both opt-in
and off by default: threat_skeleton=hit (arrow first hits 87 -> 24, alive after night 5 98 -> 138 of 256) and
pearl_reach_aim=on (the oracle's blind swings 1,022 -> 0). Pearls a night alive did not move: 0.005 to 0.07, against
the kills' 1.04, which is a selected number (this lane's own nights: 29 of 900 gained one). The loss is the search,
and the search's endermen are mostly buried: on s2-eye's nights with no sighting 67 in 100 of the enderman-steps within
64 are 6 or more blocks under the eye and none has a clear line from any height tried. Every option and trace was
checked on Java on a moved attempt (`--tape-attempt`, the Java client from the start's checkpoint, CACHE=0 POOL=0, 0
field mismatches) and chain-alone-gate passed with it on. One sigma is about 4 of 64; a difference under 12 is noise
unless pooled past two sigma. Rows, tables, scripts, the bench set (`bench-mopts.txt`, a line a setting with its commit
and number), the archived patches and `notes-next-lane.txt` are in ~/.cache/netherite-native/pnight-stagetable
(README).

only): each enderman's first sighting by the hunt's phase and its distance, the oracle walk's books, the census's near

### The arrows: threat_skeleton=hit (aaace808)

Of 87 arrow deaths (b1) 82 neither closed nor fled; the skeleton was in view in 86, within 6 blocks at the hit in 60;
42 of s42-eye's 45 were under the random driver's mine lock. No controller fought a skeleton in view (threat_interrupt
took zombies and spiders; the fight lock walked only within 10). threat_skeleton=hit (with threat_interrupt): a
skeleton in view within 16 after a hit taken in the last 100 steps starts the fight lock, which walks to it however
far. Arrow first hits 11/13/18/45 -> 5/7/9/3; alive after night 5 31/37/21/9 -> 36/37/25/40 (98 -> 138; s42-eye's 31
past 12); the melee first hits rose 15 -> 30 (more attempts alive at night, enderman first hits 6 -> 14). Kept by the
rule.

### The unlabelled deaths named, and the long falls (the edge guard, archived)

The 36 deaths with no entity killer (the combat tracker's killing hit, read at death: nwrl_combat): 20 falls (11 long
ones of 14.6 to 34 blocks, the food controller 6 and the pearl hunt 5; 9 short ones finishing a player already low), 6
drownings (all under the surface swim, under a roof, y 47 to 60), 6 lava (3 of the hunt underground), 3 suffocations
(under the strip), 1 with no entry. Of the 11 long falls 10 walked off a brink under the walker's own forward at a
walking pace, none knocked; 1 was the mine lock digging its own floor. edge_guard (opt-in): a macro's or provision's
walk heading into a cell over 4 open cells takes sneak. on: long falls 11 -> 5; its misses (the hold column): the
guard held sneak to the brink, then let go once the player's middle was over the drop with its box still on the edge
(the cell ahead was the feet's own) and the walk went on; and s42-bp's fights paid for the sneak (37 -> 27 alive).
fall (the one revision): the feet's own column, the fall over the next two cells, no guard in the fight lock or 40
steps after a hit: long falls 3, alive after night 5 138 -> 144, s42-bp's cost gone. Not zero, so archived
(archive/edge_guard.*). Its three leftover modes: the mine macro digging its own floor; the food walk down ledges 3
apart; sneak held 400 steps at a brink, then a step with no move key (the guard needs one).
