## 2026-11-10 A privileged path search between ticks left stale keys in the livings' pathfinder table (pearlsee-oracle-t15960); the env's pathfinder arrays now know their owner, and a finder that is not it starts its table afresh: the episode equal to the Java client at every tick; and the C client world kept entities of an unloaded client chunk in its lists, where vanilla's blankChunk drops them from the mouse-over pick (chain-pighit-t5942): client_entity.in_blank (lane/divpearl)

The divergence lane/pearlsee found: the frozen s64-it42 from golden-g9's blaze_rod start, `--mopt pearl_oracle=on`,
eval seed 1000, env 21's first 24,000-tick episode, whose vec env rows left the Java client's at t 15,960 (d.ents; the
player's rows at t 21,023, an ender pearl the sim's player holds and Java's never gets). Copies of its files are in
this lane's out/rec8 and out/replay/rec8-21.

**Not the engine against Java.** `out/native/test_snapshots out/replay/rec8-21` (the C engine on the Java client's tape
of that episode) replays all 24,000 rows with 0 field mismatches. So the C engine equals Java on those inputs, and the
vec env differs from the C engine on the same inputs: code outside the tick changes state the tick reads. Reproduced
here (pearlsee's rec8.sh as out/rep.sh, gpuq): the sim's rows equal rec8's row for row, d.ents at t 15,960
6eecefd889b1fe36 against Java's f96c84fcd64b00ff. Ruled out with instrumentation (not committed): the census and the
path ask never change d.ents, d.sw or d.blk where they run; the shared block bounds (env collide: stairs octant,
ladder, fence, pane, chest) never move between ticks in the whole 900k env-step run. The oracle's snapshot at the head
of t 15,960 (make -C oracle replay SNAPAT=15960) against the sim's state there, through the engine's statediff_run
called from the pool for env 21: 0 differences (entities 155 and 155, chunks 333 and 333, scalars). Equal saved state
and a different tick: the difference is state no snapshot holds.

**The cause.** runtime/walkto.c (lane/pearlsee's walk_to, PRIVILEGED: pearl_oracle, lane/rod's and lane/chain's
walks) searches with its own `struct pf` over the env's pathfinder arrays (arena.h pf_store: points, the key table,
the heap). The livings' finder (ai.c nav_shared.f) lives across searches, keeps its table's size, and clears the
table only at the slots its last search's points name (pathfind.c pf_clear_map walks pts[0..npts)). A walkto search
between two ticks overwrote both the points and the keys, so the livings' next search began with walkto's keys
standing in the table and its own old keys uncleared: a lookup of a cell walkto had opened returned walkto's point,
and a mob's path differed with no draw from any Random (d.sw equal at t 15,960 and 15,961). The engine's own searches
all go through nav_shared.f, which is why no recording ever showed it.

**The fix** (csrc/engine/pathfind.h, pathfind.c setup): pf_store.owner, the finder whose search last used the arrays;
a finder that is not the owner starts its table afresh (mcap 0: pf_lookup clears its first 1024 slots, growth clears
the rest). A search's answer is the same with a fresh table or a kept one (the table only maps a PathPoint.makeHash
key to its point), so every vanilla run is unchanged.

**Checks.** The repro again with the fix (out/rep4): the sim's rows equal the old Java tape to t 18,735 (15,959
before), then the policy's later acts are its own on the corrected state. That episode replayed on the Java client
(`netherite replay out/rep4/episodes.nrec 21:0 --every 0`): END EQUAL, and every d.* digest of the sim's 23,999 rows
equal to the Java client's (out/cmprows.sh, 0 differing ticks). A gate for the class: vec_bench `--walk-ask` (every env
asks a path every step to a cell up to 12 blocks across from its feet, nwrl_walkto_ask_rel; the answer unread) and
gates-env's digest-pearl-walk: macrodig.tsv's pearl-all start (night, endermen and zombies) with the asks, held to the
digests the same run has without them, trajectory 95bf5a9161d271a6 (pearl-all's pin) and observation
ce700f2838601c16. A library built without the pathfind.c change (VARIANT=nofix) gives 694b7848ba824d84 and
8578326232f9fc0f there, so the gate fails on the bug. The default start does not show it: digest-128x2's shape with the
asks kept a9d498ac53a83ba3 both with and without the fix (its animals rarely path where the player's search did), and
spawn-all's d8aa160b1d3bd011 the same; that line was not kept.

**Seen, not fixed (not this divergence).** The runtime's ray casts (vis_scan, the census, shview, obsview, netherview,
endview, itemuse_look_liquid in the step hook) run the engine's raytrace_blocks, which writes vanilla's shared block
bounds (the stairs object's octant for good, the ladder's bounds, a fence's, a pane's, a chest's; a portal's axis into a
server world). The Java client never made those casts. No change was seen in this episode's 900k env-steps, so it is
untested as a cause. The guard, not landed: an env flag the pool holds at 1 outside session_tick, under which
collide.c's setters (collide_ladder_bounds' store, collide_chest_bounds_set, collide_fence_bounds_set,
collide_pane_bounds_set, collide_stairs_traced, the stairs reset and the frame's item_bounds) and raytrace.c's End
portal item_bounds and portal axis write skip their stores.

**The second divergence, chain-pighit-t5942 (lane/chain's, a true engine against Java one).** lane/chain's chain tape
from spawn (seed 42 at normal difficulty, the meat rung's hunt, 7,725 ticks) was replayed by test_snapshots, and the
replay of the Java client's own recording differed first at row 5942, d.sstat. An attack press hit pig 54 at (-150.30,
66.00, -243.50) in C (health 10 to 6, hurt, knockback, 2 more sword damage, 0.3 more exhaustion) and nothing in Java.
The cause is the client's chunk unload. At t 4401 an S21 unload of client chunk (-10,-16) left pig 54's live copy in
it. In vanilla, Chunk.onChunkUnload, WorldClient.onEntityRemoved and the entitySpawnQueue hand that copy to
spawnEntityInWorld, and ChunkProviderClient's blankChunk takes it there (its chunkExists is always true, its addEntity
does nothing). So the copy keeps its old chunkCoordX/Y/Z, sits in no chunk's entity list (the reloaded chunk never
takes it back), and getEntitiesWithinAABBExcludingEntity misses it. That call is EntityRenderer.getMouseOver's
entity pick and the client's collision box search, and the miss lasts until the copy's position leaves those
coordinates while the chunk it enters is loaded. The C client world (clientworld.c) kept it in the lists, so C's pick
found the pig 1,541 ticks later. A second part: a client living whose (int)posX,(int)posZ chunk is not loaded gets
moveEntityWithHeading's isRemote branch (motionY -0.1, no gravity).

**The fix** (csrc/engine/clientworld.{c,h}, combat.{c,h}, serverreplay.c): client_entity.in_blank. It is set on an S21
unload of the copy's chunk (combat_client_chunk_unloaded from serverreplay's chunk drop) and when the copy moves into a
chunk the client lacks (client_entity_chunk_add keeps the old coordinates there, as blankChunk does). It is cleared
when the copy enters a loaded chunk, and read from a snapshot's addedToChunk 1 with cidx -1. The pick and the client's
box search skip a copy with in_blank set. The client living's move takes the -0.1 sink in an unloaded chunk. Checks:
the chain tape (`out/native/test_snapshots`) went from 23,050 field mismatches from row 5942 to 0 in 7,725 rows. It is
kept as a recording, out/java/snapshots/chain-pighit-s42 (the Java client's tape and snapshot from the repro command
in csrc/tests/divergences/divpearl.tsv's row), and the suite replays it. The play that reached it: walking away from
pigs past the view distance, coming back, and attacking one that had not moved out of its chunk.

**What the tables say** (s64-it42 unless named; "link" = from the library's start of the stage; counts are runs):

- The funnel from seed 42's spawn ends at the diamond pickaxe: 26 of 256 (0.10, median minute 21.8; 22 of 256 for s64big-final)
  and nothing after it. Its conversions: 0.98, 0.97, 0.82, 0.87, 0.67 (iron ingot to iron pickaxe), 0.86, 0.88, then 0.20
  (flint and steel to the diamond pickaxe) and 0.00 (to obsidian, 0 of 26).
- Seeds it never saw (101-164): 90 of 256 get a wooden pickaxe (s64big-final 163), the diamond pickaxe 6 (10), obsidian 0
  (1). Of the 122 runs that neither died nor got wood, 82 had a log in view and they moved a median of 9 blocks in 2 hours
  (p90 26): the policy stands still where seed 42's spawn taught it a route. No macro fails here (the net's own keys drive
  89% of those steps); this is the gap distillation to raw inputs will meet first.
- Deaths from spawn: 0.85 a run for s64-it42 (0.72 for s64big-final), 40% of runs die; killed by hunger 27% (52% for
  s64big-final), zombies 26%, skeletons 14%, drowning 11%; all in the overworld; 51% on the net's own keys, 15% under the
  strip. At normal difficulty health drains to half a heart at food 0 and 92 to 96% of runs sit at food 0 at the end (the
  first minute at food 0 is 14 to 28 by milestone): the food macro does not keep a run fed over 2 hours.
- The library links (rate of the next milestone within the stage's length, 128 runs; spawn, wooden, stone, furnace, iron
  ingot, iron pickaxe, bucket, flint and steel | diamond pickaxe | obsidian | Nether | blaze rod | pearl | eye | room): s64-it42
  0.91 0.88 0.81 0.77 0.41 0.56 0.22 0.07 | 0 | 0.34 | 0 | 0 | 0.99 | 0.17, then the room to the End 3 of 22 and the End to
  the dragon 16 of 128 (0.125); s64big-final 0.93 0.80 0.64 0.53 0.38 0.49 0.39 0.08 | 0 | 0.60 | 0 | 0 | 0.99 | 0.17, 2 of 22,
  20 of 128 (0.16). The early links are not near 1 either: 0.41 and 0.38 for the iron pickaxe.

**Where the runs stop, the three worst links** (the generated text per link is in the dragon-bench.txt of each model).
A flaw found by lane/rod and lane/obsid after the first tables, now in the tool (every link row carries the distinct
trajectories behind its runs, the largest identical group, the starts played of the library's, and the flag NOT A RATE
under 8 distinct or with one trajectory over half the runs): a frozen policy whose macro drives every step does not
diverge from a library start, so 128 runs are not 128 samples. s64-it42: the Nether start is **9 distinct trajectories, 118 of
128 runs one of them, from 1 start (not a rate)**, the diamond pickaxe start **11 distinct, 67 in the largest group, from 2 starts
(not a rate)**; every other link is 109 to 128 distinct (blaze rod to pearl 109, largest group 9, from 3 starts: a rate),
and the from-spawn sets 256 of 256 distinct (seed 42's from one start, the sampler diverging them; seeds 101-164 from 63).
So the first two "0 of 128" below are one or two trajectories each; their causes (the fall under the strip, the
drowning of one start) are real but their rates are not measured.

1. *Diamond pickaxe to obsidian: 0 of 128 from the library's starts (both models), 0 of 26 from spawn (0 of 22).* From the
   library's two diamond-pickaxe starts (NOT A RATE: 11 distinct trajectories) 123 of 128 die: 67 are one trajectory, a
   drowning at step 2,643 with the surface macro driving (s13-h36-diamond_pickaxe), and the other start's deaths are
   three skeleton kills at steps 16,507, 16,635 and 16,330 to 16,436 (about 50) with the strip driving. From spawn the
   cause is another: 24 of the 26 runs hold the kit (the obsidian macro's books) and none gets obsidian: the macro's lava search
   (OW_SEARCH) drove 814k steps and its strip 138k, no run mined an obsidian, the bucket portal began in 4 runs, chose a
   site in none, and no run holds a lava bucket. Lava the camera can reach is the limit (lane/obsidian5: within 256 blocks
   of 61% of spawns, seed 42's nearest at 282). 12 of the 26 die (8 of hunger).
2. *The Nether to a blaze rod: 0 of 128 (both); NOT A RATE for s64-it42: one start, 118 of the 128 runs are one trajectory, all
   dead at step 14,543 (lane/rod's finding, reproduced).* 118 of 128 die in the Nether by a landing over 3.5 blocks, every one with
   the strip macro as the driver of the step before (s64big-final: 20 die so, 108 spend 2.58M steps in the nether macro
   without a rod; s64-it42's other 10 spend 240k). That the strip drives in the Nether is the finding; why it digs a step
   there is not isolated (a trace of the first fall is the lane's first job). Where the nether macro drives, no run
   finds the spawner: lane/pearlhunt's DEVLOG measured the fortress found in 512 of 512 and the spawner seen in none, a
   lavafall over the bridge (a dev start, nether_under_guard on).
3. *A blaze rod to a pearl: 0 of 128 (both).* 22 die (8 by a blaze with the nether macro driving, 5 by fire or lava with the
   strip). Of the 106 that live the pearl macro drove a step in 3 (the drivers' steps) and the strip drove 52% of their steps, the
   nether macro 32% (the Nether start never leaves: 34 of 42 stay); 34 of the 106 hold a rod at the end, 19 of the 86 overworld
   runs a bucket. The want is overworld, night, a rod or powder held, and a start (macro_start runs only between macros;
   the strip's climb latch and pearl_yield also hold it): the macro did not start in 103 of 106 runs over a 20-minute day
   that has a night, and the books do not say which condition held it. lane/pearlhunt's branch (pearl_walk straight, the
   lava guard, pearl_keep and craft_return, climb_way pillar, all off by default, measured from a later stage: the
   golden-g13 kit, 3 pearls and 6 rods) is what the hunt needs once it starts; what this link needs first is the start condition,
   a counted books line per condition (night, rod or powder held, between macros, pearl_busy) which this lane did not add.

Other links under 0.5, from the same runs: bucket to flint and steel 0.22 (s64big-final 0.39), of its 27 deaths 18
drowned with the surface macro driving; flint and steel to the diamond pickaxe 0.07 (0.08), of 17 deaths 9 drowned with
the surface macro, and the 102 survivors had the strip drive 56% of their steps and 1 holds a diamond; iron ingot to iron
pickaxe 0.41: all 11 deaths drowned (surface), and the craft or iron macro drove no step in 40 of the other 64; the eye to
the stronghold's room 0.17: 46 of 106 failures die (zombie 14, skeleton 9, with the stronghold macro driving), 60 live
2.0M stronghold steps without finding the room; the room to the End 3 of 22 (silverfish 6, fire or lava 6 of 12
deaths); the End to the dragon 0.125: of 102 deaths 59 "the End, no mob" and 38 the void, the dragon macro driving every one.

## 2026-11-09 An eval at 1,000 episodes (standard error 0.015 to 0.021, paired start by start) re-reads the raw-skill table: lr 3e-4 costs 0.10 on search teachers against the survivors and nothing once the collapse is counted, memory does not help hard ore (minGRU minus feed-forward -0.003, 95% -0.06 to +0.06), the pixels-only student is level with its teacher on plain ore and 0.17 to 0.42 under it on hard ore and any-spawn logs, the 0.59 / 0.33 seed gap is one collapsed run, and telling two recipes 0.05 apart takes 18 to 49 runs each whatever the eval's size (lane/eval1k)

The brief: every number on the raw-skill route was an eval of 64 to 128 episodes (standard error 0.057 at 64 and 0.7) and
conclusions were drawn from differences of 0.03 to 0.14. This lane trains nothing: it builds the eval and re-scores
the models on disk (~/.cache/netherite-native/models/rawpix, rawtree, rawsearch).

**The eval** (`make -C csrc/runtime raweval RE_W=MODEL.ntw RE_TASK=ore|orecave|hard|hardcave|logview|logany|lognear|logs3near|logs3view
[RE_KIND=student|teacher] [RE_ARM=strip|van]`, train/raweval.sh and raweval.mk; inside `gpuq.sh check --mem 8000 --`):
- `ntloop --start-cycle on` (off by default; nwrl_vec_opts.start_cycle, vecenv.c draw_start_mix): env i's episode j plays library
  start (i + j n) mod starts, in index order, no draw. A model meets the same starts and, with `--seed`, the same sampler
  stream whatever it is, so two evals compare start by start. The default digests are unchanged (the option is read only
  when set; gates-env below).
- 1,024 episodes a model: the first 512 starts of the task's held-out library, each played twice (a library of 500 is
  played whole twice; one of 70 or 307 would be played 15 or 4 times). More distinct starts beat more plays of a start:
  the intraclass correlation (between-start variance over the total) is 0.46 to 0.83, so a start's two plays are not
  two independent episodes. Processes of 48 starts (96 envs, 9.3 to 11.1 GB resident each, one at a time).
- `train/rawstat.c` (out/runtime/train/rawstat; `one`, `pair`, `table MANIFEST`): success; its standard error with a
  start as the cluster (and the binomial one beside it); deaths; the standard deviation between starts and within a start
  (one-way ANOVA); for a pair the difference of the two evals' per-start means, its 95% interval (t over the shared
  starts) and the starts A won, lost and tied; for a recipe's runs the spread of the run means, the eval noise taken
  out of it and the share of the old evals' spread that was eval noise.
- Held-out libraries (world seeds 501 to 1000, never trained on; out/runtime/eval1k, made by `make -C csrc/runtime
  raweval-starts` with rawstarts, placement seed 2): plain ore 923 starts (462 world seeds), dark-cave ore 998 (499),
  hard ore 868 (435), hard ore in caves 998 (499); rawtree-logs' held-out logs: every spawn 500, a log within 16 blocks
  307, a log in view 70. The lanes' evals drew 128 envs from 32 starts (16 world seeds, two placements) for the ore
  tasks. Here 512 of each are used; the log libraries cannot grow past 500 without capturing more seeds, so the 70 in
  view stay 70 (not run in this batch).

**What a 1,000-episode eval resolves.** Start-cluster standard error of one eval: 0.014 to 0.015 on plain ore (0.82),
0.017 to 0.019 on hard ore (0.4 to 0.7), 0.020 on the any-spawn log (0.4 to 0.7). That is 0.015 for plain ore and 0.02
for the rest, not 0.015 everywhere, because a start is nearly decided for the log task (between-start sd 0.42, within
0.20, intraclass 0.83) while it is half luck on plain ore (0.27 and 0.27, 0.52). A replicate: the same teacher on the
same 500 starts with a different sampler seed scored 0.693 and 0.685. Against the old evals (n 64 to 128 on 32 starts): 8 to 16 times
the episodes and 16 times the starts on the ore tasks (the log tasks drew from the same 500 spawns: 4 to 5 times the starts a 128-env eval touched).

**Where the lanes' levels moved.** The absolute levels on the ore tasks were high on the 32-start libraries: hard-ore
teachers 0.797 there (six runs), 0.636 here (the same six, 512 starts); hard-ore feed-forward students 0.550 / 0.466 there
(seeds 6 / 7), 0.408 / 0.363 here; plain-ore students 0.808 / 0.826 there, 0.824 / 0.825 here (the plain library was
representative). Any-spawn search students 0.589 / 0.331, 0.544 / 0.320 here.

**Time.** On a quiet host a 1,000-episode eval of a 60-second task took 70 s (search teacher p1 seed 6: starts loaded 15.5
s, 1.2M env-steps in 49.2 s = 24.4k env-steps/s, the rest 5.3 s), a plain-ore one about 30 s (a 256-start test: four
processes of 5.7 to 9.1 s). The batch ran with
lane/acrl training and later lane/dbench on the same 32 cores and the 3090, so its own numbers are not env-steps/s
measurements: per task, mean wall, starts loaded, env steps: any-spawn log (20 evals) 126 s, 25 s, 90 s (13.3k env-steps/s);
hard ore (28) 55 s, 24 s, 20 s; hard ore in caves (12) 49 s, 23 s, 15 s; plain ore (4) 65 s, 25 s, 29 s. Where it goes:
the loading of the 512 starts is 45 to 50% of an ore eval (about 47 ms a start, once per start per eval) and 20% of a
log eval; the rest is the engine's tick on the workers (1.14 ms an env-step), which a 3090 does not shorten. Not done:
several models in one process to load the starts once (it would take an ntloop that plays N models in turn) and a

**How much of the spread between runs of a recipe is the eval's noise.** For the six-run recipes with no collapse, the
share of the old evals' spread (variance of six run means at n episodes) that was the eval's own within-start noise
(the runs share their starts, so the start sampling is common to all of them) / the binomial p (1 - p) / n the lanes
quoted: at n = 64 and 128 episodes, hard ore teachers lr 1e-3 38% / 23% (binomial 57% / 40%) with the training runs' sd
0.052; lr 3e-4 7% / 4% (sd 0.154); search teachers lr 3e-4 17% / 9% (sd 0.061); hard ore feed-forward plain 44% / 28%
(sd 0.046), minGRU plain 49% / 32% (sd 0.040), feed-forward caves 15% / 8% (sd 0.091), minGRU caves 9% / 5% (sd 0.107).
At the 1,000-episode eval the eval's share of the spread is 0% to 6%. A recipe with a collapsed run has a training sd of
0.28 (search lr 1e-3, 0.278) and the eval is 0% of it. So the old spread of "0.53 to 0.75" was the training runs'
(sd 0.04 to 0.15) with the eval adding 5% to 50% of its variance at 64 to 128 episodes; the binomial 0.057 overstated the
eval's noise on the logs (intraclass 0.8: it is mostly start luck, common to the runs) and was closer on hard ore
(57% against 38% at 64 episodes for the lr 1e-3 teachers).

- *memory does not help hard ore*: **holds.** minGRU minus feed-forward on the same six teachers: plain -0.003 (-0.060

  (plain) or +0.11 (caves) is excluded and a loss of that size is not.
- *the any-spawn log is 0.59 on seed 6 and 0.33 on seed 7*: **the levels hold within 0.05, the gap does not.** Search

  without it seed 7 is 0.480 and the gap +0.064 (-0.25 to +0.38) with three and two runs: not a seed effect at this size.

  +0.25), reversed on plain ore, where they are level (+0.04 and -0.03).** Table above.

**Runs and episodes to tell two recipes 0.05 apart** (95% two-sided, power 80%, one eval a run, recipes on the same
starts): k = 2 (s_train^2 + s_eval^2) (1.96 + 0.84)^2 / 0.05^2. With the typical six-run recipe's training sd 0.052 and
the eval's within-start variance 0.09 / n: 18 runs of each at n = 1,000 and 25 at n = 64; with the pooled sd of seven
clean recipes (0.087): 49 runs each at 1,000 and 57 at 64. The eval size moves it 15% to 30%; the runs are the
cost. Three runs a recipe tells 0.05 apart only if the training sd is under about 0.02 (none of the recipes here is under
0.04). So: pool recipes by many seeds, or lower the run-to-run spread (a validation-picked checkpoint, a collapse guard
as the three-log teacher's anchor was), before another recipe is compared by a difference under 0.1.

## 2026-11-09 A privileged critic does not make pixels-only PPO learn from scratch (plain ore 0.33 / 0.22 held-out with it, 0.22 / 0.21 without, against the DAgger student's 0.84 / 0.79, three trainer seeds, 512 episodes each); on top of the DAgger student it keeps hard ore at the student's level (0.50 / 0.34 against 0.50 / 0.40) where PPO without it erodes it (0.36 / 0.23), and PPO lifts the search student with or without it (every spawn 0.67 and 0.68 against 0.56, two seeds); the KL early stop at 0.015 to 0.02 keeps 40% of the steps and helps nothing; the multi-task net not measured (lane/acrl)

Parked at 3:25 pm by the route change (macros back, the dragon from spawn first); what was run is below, what was not is at the end.

**Built** (all off by default; gates-env and train-loop-check at the end of this section):
- `ntloop --critic H` (train/critic.cuh, learn.h ntc_*): the privileged critic. Two relu layers of H over the whole
  scalar row as the env wrote it, before `--zero-sc` (the .or seen-ore and seen-log slots, task.hint's nearest block,
  the dig, the player's own state), its output added to the trunk's value head. The split: the shared stem and trunk
  as before (the actor's heads and the trunk's value head read them), the privileged inputs in a second value branch
  joined after the trunk, so the actor's logits never depend on them and the value loss still trains the trunk
  through its own head; the branch's last layer starts at 0 (a fresh critic changes nothing), its own Adam (the
  learner's lr and norm clip), stepped with every learner step and the value warm-up's, its actor copy
  double-buffered as the actor's weights are. OUT/critic.ntc; `--critic-init`. 15,105 parameters at H 64 over 169
  scalars. It lowers the value loss 10 to 20 times on plain ore (0.0007 to 0.0013 against 0.015 to 0.019 at 400k).
  Cost: 44.2k against 44.8k env-steps/s in the one uncontended pair (400k, 256 envs); in the 1.2M pairs, run beside
  my own builds and other jobs, 27.7k to 29.1k against 31.3k to 43.4k: rough, not resolved.
- `--kl-stop X`: an update's epochs stopped at the first minibatch whose approx KL (the kl book, before its step)
  passes X, that step and every later one skipped on the device (a flag k_adam reads, no host sync); rows get
  kl_steps and kl_stops. `--vclip X`: PPO2's clipped value term.
- `--task-hint-shape off` (nwrl_vec_opts.task_hint_noshape): task.hint fills the seen-object slot (the critic's
  input) and leaves the potential's cell the last one drawn, so the reward is the one without the hint.
- `--task-item2 N --task-from2 K` (nwrl_vec_opts.task_item2): a second task for the envs whose start is K or later,
  and the .tk builds (net.h NT_TASK, late_scalars bit 5): the task one-hot in the policy's scalars.

**Method.** Every number is a frozen eval at temperature 0.5 (.t5), each env's first episode, 4 sampler seeds (7 to
10) x 128 envs = 512 episodes on fixed held-out starts; "se" is the standard error over trainer seeds (a run's own
binomial se is about 0.02). Search evals play 48-spawn chunks of the held-out libraries, one a sampler seed (192
spawns; the full 500-spawn library peaked at 32 GB), so they are not rawsearch's numbers; the students were
re-scored on the same episodes, so every comparison here is paired. Training at 256 envs (rawskill's recipe; 15.6 to
18 GB), the actor's ore scalars zeroed (`--zero-sc ore`, pixels, the dig and the player's own state), auto exposure.

lower (0.601 against 0.745 for the five that survived lr 1e-3); for a fresh net the KL hardly moves and the spread
stays (0.516 to 0.938). At entropy 0.003 the entropy falls instead of rising and the KL an update does not move
(0.025 against 0.028 to
0.034): the bonus is not what makes the step large. What it does is keep the search: four of six fresh ore teachers
never found the ore in training (0 of their last 200k env-steps' episodes), and one warm search teacher won 86% of its
training spawns and 0 of the held-out ones. So the step is set by the update itself (the advantages normalised to unit
scale over the rollout, 4 epochs of minibatches at that rate), and no single knob tried here holds the levels and the
region together. What held both here: the KL anchor to the start at lr 3e-4 and entropy 0.01 for the three-log
teacher, which starts from a trained net (0.870, KL 0.003, none of six collapsed; the same anchor at entropy 0.003 on
the search teacher held the region and lost the level, 0.476); a fresh net at lr 1e-3, entropy 0.01 (none of six
collapsed). The
remaining candidate is an early stop of the epochs at a KL target, which needs the per-minibatch KL back on the host
(the updates are queued on the device); not built.

## 2026-11-05 Iron ore from pixels alone: a seen-ore teacher distilled by DAgger into a pixels-only 64x64 student through an auto exposure, held-out 0.77 to 0.84 plain and 0.71 to 0.94 in dark caves (means 0.81 to 0.90 over three runs on each of two seeds, temperature 0.5), about a minute a run; pixels-only PPO stays at 0.19 to 0.50 (lane/rawpix)

The task is lane/rawskill's: a stone pickaxe in hand, iron ore 2 to 4 blocks away in view, the drop picked up within
10 s, raw controls only. The goal: a policy that sees pixels, the crack scalar and its own state, but not the
seen-ore scalars, at held-out success 0.8 on plain starts (seeds 501 to 516) and in dark caves with no torch (the same
seeds, rawstarts --cave --no-torch), on two seeds, with a run under a minute. Every number is a frozen eval: each
env's first 10 s episode on a held-out start, 64 or 128 envs, eval seed 7, on the dev host's 3090 beside other lanes'
jobs. With 128 envs a success rate near 0.8 has a standard error of 0.035.

**The command**: `make -C csrc/runtime rawpix RP_SEED=K` (train/rawpix.mk; inside `gpuq.sh check --mem 20000 --`).
1. It makes the starts where missing (`rawpix-starts`): rawskill's plain libraries, dark caves from seeds 1-16 and
   501-516, seeds 1-100 plain and caves, and their mixes (the 16 seeds' 58 starts, the 100 seeds' 374, the 50 seeds'
   186).
2. The teacher: PPO for 400k env-steps on the 16 seeds' plain starts with the seen-ore scalars (s1.dk.or, through
   make rawskill), about 15 s. Its held-out plain success is 0.83 to 0.95 (64 envs).
3. The student: a fresh net of the same build with zero weights on the 12 seen-ore scalars (the s1.dk init, widened).
   It learns the teacher's actions for 800k env-steps on the 100 seeds' mix, driving 90% of the episodes itself
   (DAgger, `--beta 0.9`) while the teacher labels every step, about 30 s at 34k to 40k env-steps/s.
4. The evals: the frozen student on the held-out plain and dark-cave starts, 128 envs, the scalars zeroed, in the
   `.t5` build (keys and camera drawn at temperature 0.5) and sampled.

It prints RAWPIX-TIME and RAWPIX lines. RP_CURVE=N adds the student's held-out checkpoints. Every new ntloop option is
off by default (gates-env PASS):
- `--obs-tone auto|gamma:G`: a kernel on the segment's bytes before the actor and learner read them. auto is each
  frame times 255 over its brightest byte, a camera's auto exposure.
- `--zero-sc LO:N|ore`: the scalars read 0 by actor and learner.
- `--student-zero LO:N|ore`: the student's loss reads them as 0, so their weights get no gradient. Checked on the
  blob: fc1's 12 ore columns stay exactly 0, so the student is pixels-only by construction.
- `--student-prev env|label`.
- The `.t3 .t5 .t7` builds (net.h NTA_TEMP): evals only, refused with learning or a teacher.
- rawskill's RS_HELD2.

**Why pixels failed** (measured first):
- At 16x16 the cast takes the nearest texel. Iron ore is stone plus 37 of 256 tan texels (14.5%); its mean is within
  10 levels of stone's grey. At 2 to 4 blocks a face covers 3 to 6 pixels a side (64x64: 13 to 26), so on the surface
  the ore reads plainly as a speckled grey block among grass. At 8 blocks and beyond (0.4 tan pixels a face at 16x16)
  and against stone it does not.
- Dark caves: a frame's brightest byte is 10 to 12 of 255 (the lightmap's floor 0.059 at Moody, 0.14 at Bright).
  Scaled by its own maximum, the same frame shows the ore and its specks: the information is in the bytes, 1 to 3
  levels apart.
- Pixels-only PPO turns its camera off the ore, drifts down and digs grass, and never recenters. The seen-ore
  scalars hand the .or policy the look's offset to the ore.
- Scalars at train time, zeroed at test (or64-s6): 16 and 14 of 64. A policy never given them: 19 and 20 of 64. The
  policy leans on the scalars, so having had them does not help without them.

## 2026-11-05 The macros as mods: csrc/mods/macros, a file a macro and one registration table; the env core (vecenv.c, 5,542 lines to 2,764) calls them only through a dispatcher; MACROS=0 builds libnwrl without them, raw controls only; every trajectory unchanged (18 macro digest rows and gates-env equal at every step) (lane/macromod)

The brief: make the macros a mod extension (GOAL.md "Actions: macros are mods on top ... easy to add"): one struct a
macro fills, one registration table, the core calling only the hooks; every macro in its own file under one folder; a
build without the folder running raw controls only. A refactor: every trajectory unchanged, no macro added or changed.

**The proof first** (10b5bff1). gates-env's digests run the macros only at their defaults, so a move that broke an
option, a ladder level, a labeller or a late family would pass it. `make -C csrc/runtime macro-digests`
(csrc/runtime/macrodig.sh, macrodig.tsv): 18 rows of vec_bench under random actions from a start where each family
runs (spawn with every macro and with the teacher's set, the L4g, L5a and L4f levels with their labellers, keys off,
the picks, the iron and g5 starts, the kit start with and without options, pearl night, the Nether, the End, the
stronghold's eyes), each with four digests: the trajectory, the labels and acts (vec_bench --label-digest), the
episodes' records, and the books (gui, the stronghold's and the craft labeller's). Pinned at 754f27f9 (master), the
same in two runs. vec_bench gained --mopts, --late, --level BITS[:LABELLER], --dev and an action
nwrl_vec_action_width wide.

**The steps**, each held to the 18 rows:
- f7220f63, the move, no line changed: vecenv.c's macro code cut by line ranges (a partition: every line in exactly
  one range) into csrc/mods/macros/{common, craft, portal, loot, fight, food, seek, strip, surface}.c and macros.c,
  the vecenv_*.c and .h files moved by git mv (nether, stronghold, pearl, obsidian, bportal, strip2 for vecenv_strip.c,
  shadow). macros.c includes the folder into vecenv.c's translation unit, as the macros always were (every function
  static; nothing crosses a library boundary, nothing inlines differently). gates-env PASS at this commit.
- 21fb4596, the API: `struct vec_macro` (macro.h) with a hook a phase (observe, cand, aid, policy, interrupt,
  start, drive, label, half, after, end, abort, reset), macros.c's MACROS table with each macro's rank in each ordered
  phase, and the dispatcher's mac_*. macro_start's, macro_drive's, mbit_of's, macro_end's, env_reset's and decode's
  per-macro blocks moved unchanged into hooks in each macro's file (new files screen.c, mine.c, end.c, dragon.c,
  aids.c). The orders are data because the code's were not one order: the start is a priority; the candidate test
  is ordered (the stronghold latches its start as it tests); the strip's lava check reads the Nether's state before
  the Nether's books move it; the label names the strip while the seek it handed off to drives.
- 6dbd970c, the rest of the core's calls (the books at the result, the deaths, a decision step and the gui cursor; the
  label's fits, chance, envpick and mask; the make's settings) as hooks, the options table to csrc/runtime/vecopts.c
  (the core reads MOPT; its indices are nwrl_vec_opts.macro_opts' layout), and `make -C csrc/runtime rlbind MACROS=0`:
  out/var/nomacros/libnwrl.so, vecenv.c against csrc/runtime/nomacros.c (no macro registered; every macro API call
  -1). At `--macros 0` both libraries give the same trajectory, label, episode and books digests (l4gcase, 32 envs,
  300 steps: 2a91e2f9cede0fde).
- 1d5e0245, each macro's run-file names in its own file (`.sw`: the craft macro lists craft, table-anywhere, iron,
  late, liquid, portal, carry, notable, norecipe, recipekey, tablekey; pearl pearlcave; seek seekkey; screen noscreen),
  read through vecenv.h's nwrl_vec_macro_switch: train/loop.c's MACRO_BITS and brutetab.c's copy are gone. The 29
  names and bits equal the old table's. Comments naming the moved files name their new paths.

Adding a macro is now its file, its `#include` and table line in macros.c, and its bit in vecenv.h (SPEC.md "The
macros as mods"). What stays in the core: struct vec_env's fields of the macros' state (the macros' own structs where
they have them), the options table, the End's books (vecdragon.c: the End and the dragon's death are milestones with
the macros off), and nwrl_vec_opts' bit layout.

on the student's own; distil as l5aseek.yaml one seed to 256M, a second if it holds; the 20-minute eval with the kept

mining episode at L6b on the Java client. Every eval is ladder16's: 256 runs of 20 minutes from seed 42's spawn, the

at seed 7, ladder16's stored number.

  `actions.seek_walk` and `actions.seek_dig`, macro|policy, default macro). The int32 macros have no free bit (SEEKKEY
  took bit 30), so these are options, effective only where the env's macros hold NWRL_VEC_SEEKKEY: the level's episodes
  and the frozen eval at the level split the seek, the teacher's 16383 keeps it whole. The halves, by the seek's cell
  (SEEK_DIG_REACH 4.0 blocks, eye to the cell's centre, the seek's own dig reach): the walk half, nothing dug and the
  cell farther than 4 (the walk, and any block dug in the line on the way); the dig half, the cell within 4 or dug (the

  **L6b's start and end** (seek_walk policy at 2113933306): key 13 down, no macro running, seek_want holding on a cell
  within 4 blocks of the eye: the seek begins there and ends as the seek ends (the item picked up, dug and not picked up
  in 60 steps, given up, a death or the lava escape) or when its cell is farther than 4 with nothing dug; it hands back

## 2026-11-05 Mining iron ore on the raw controls, learned from a fresh net in 247k to 360k env-steps (3.6 to 6.9 s), held-out 0.92 to 0.95, the whole command 13 to 14 s, on the 16x16 cast with the seen-ore scalars (pixels alone 0.13 to 0.33); its episodes replay END EQUAL on the Java client (lane/rawskill)

The task (Elliot's raw-controls skill): a stone pickaxe in hand, iron ore placed 2 to 4 blocks in view, success the
ore's drop picked up within 10 s; forward, back, left, right, jump, attack and the two camera bins, no macro; the
16x16 ray cast with the dig and seen-ore scalars (w1.dk.or). All of it is options, off by default (gates-env PASS):

- **The task** (the run file's `task` section, csrc/runtime/vecenv_task.c): the pickup ends the episode (win 1), a
  death too (-0.5), the keys masked to `task.keys`, shaping `once` (each term paid once a unit) or `potential` (the
  look's angle to the last seen ore, the eye's distance to it and the crack stage as one potential, paid as its
  change). `task.sticky on|block` latches the attack on the crosshair's block (any, or the ore only). `actions.macros
  none`.
- **The starts** (`make -C csrc/runtime rawstarts`, train/rawstarts.c): dev starts from the seed set's spawns (a give,
  a setblock, a tp; the oracle's script takes the same lines, so episodes replay), the distance, the turn
  (`--turn`, `--turn-min`: out of view) and `--cave` (the player in a cave near the spawn, a torch at the feet unless
  `--no-torch`). Training starts from seeds 1 to 16 (26), held-out seeds 501 to 516 (32), never trained on.
- **The loop** (`make -C csrc/runtime rawskill [RS_SEED=K] [RS_STEPS=N]`): builds its variant (0.8 s when nothing
  changed), a fresh net, PPO for RS_STEPS, the frozen policy on the held-out starts, and RAWSKILL-TIME (process and
  CUDA start, the starts' loading, the env steps with the learner, the eval) and RAWSKILL (held-out success, steps
  to the pickup, deaths). RS_CURVE=N adds held-out checkpoint evals during training (ntloop `--eval-extra`).

  seconds, the sweep's table (`-g`), episodes as the Java client's frames beside the policy's own 16x16 view
  (ntloop `--obs-dump`); `netherite replay` replays a dev start's episode (ntrec tape writes its setup lines, DEV=1).

What moved the time, in order (256 envs on the dev host's 3090 beside other lanes' jobs; every rate is rough):

| step | env-steps/s | the command | held-out |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 envs, horizon 64, lr 3e-4 (pot-or-s1, s2) | 5.7k to 6.1k | 260 to 270 s at 1.5M | 0.828, 0.828 |
| 128 envs (pot-or-n128-s3) | 10.9k | 196 s at 2M | 0.906 |
| 256 envs, 4 groups, 30 workers (s3, s4) | 16.7k, 23.1k | 130, 99 s at 2M | 0.812, 0.922 |
| + `starts.pin` (s3, s4) | 34.9k, 32.5k | 66, 69 s at 2M | 0.875, 0.891 |
| + PPO horizon 8, 4 epochs, lr 1e-3 (s4, s5) | 43.9k, 48.7k | 14.0, 13.1 s at 400k | 0.922, 0.938 |

- **Resets were the limit** (POOL_RESET_COUNT, 128 envs, stand-in, 50-step episodes): with the starts drawn at every
  reset about half the resets switch start and copy the whole image (89 to 91 ms) and the rest 36 to 38 ms; to the
  env's own start 12 to 17 ms. `starts.pin` (vecenv.h start_pin: each env keeps the start the make drew for it)
  took the stand-in from 19.2k-19.7k to 48.5k-49.4k env-steps/s (two rounds each, alternating). The kernel fix that
  made a same-start reset cheap at all is the section below.
- **Why it needed 2M env-steps** (the orchestrator's question): every run sat at 0 until about 0.8M, then rose to 0.85
  in about 0.3M. Breaking the ore takes about 23 ticks of attack on one block. The sweep (seed 3, then 4 and 5 for
  the best; env-steps to training success 0.85 over the last 1000 episodes; the table in out/demo/rawskill.html):
  horizon 64 to 32 with 4 epochs 857k; horizon 16, 4 epochs 536k; lr 1e-3 with horizon 16: 336k, 355k, 452k; with
  horizon 8: 247k, 360k, 257k. The gain is PPO's updates an env-step and the learning rate. What did not carry it:
  the sticky attack (on any block: digs dirt, stalls near 0.35, held-out 0.156; on the ore only: learns earliest,
  0.03 at 0.18M, but stalls near 0.35, held-out 0.28 to 0.75 in every combination), the crack weight 0.05 to 0.3
  (slower: 420k against 336k), the action repeat (2: 925k decisions, 40 s; 4: 574k decisions, 57 s, since a decision
  costs its ticks), lr 2e-3 and 8 epochs (no better than lr 1e-3, 4 epochs).
- **16x16 against 64x64** (s1.dk.or, configs/rawskill-pot64.yaml, 256 envs, pinned off, 2M, seeds 3 and 4): 64x64
  learned at the same env-steps (held-out 0.84 and 0.80, past 0.8 at about 1.26M) at 13.9k and 13.8k env-steps/s
  against 16.7k and 23.1k, 157 to 159 s against 99 to 130 s: 16x16 learns faster per wall second.
- **Harder starts** (held-out, the near-start model then a mix of near, wide 2 to 12 blocks turned up to 180 degrees,
  and cave starts, pinned, 3M): ore 5 to 12 blocks away 0.45-0.53 then 0.63-0.75; turned away 90 to 180 degrees
  0-0.05 then 0.20-0.36. Caves were 0 until the setup's order was fixed: it gave the pickaxe before the tp, the item
  stayed at the spawn and every cave episode was bare-handed (0 of 1,919 won; the tp now comes first). Then, the
  near starts plus 19 cave starts, the winner's PPO, 1M env-steps, seed 3: with a torch at the feet, cave training
  episodes 0.715 won and held-out caves 0.844 lit and 0.844 dark; without the torch 0.731, and 0.797 on both. The
  torch (a change to the task) does not matter to this policy: the 16x16 cast of an unlit cave is near black, but the
  w1.dk.or build's seen-ore scalars come from the cast's geometry, not its light, and the seeded eval sampled the
  same episodes lit and dark. A policy on pixels alone would need the light.
- **How much rests on the seen-ore scalars** (the orchestrator's arm; a compass the raw-pixel end goal will not
  have): the default without them (RS_V=w1.dk: the 16x16 pixels and the crack scalar), seeds 6 and 7, held-out 0.328
  and 0.125 at 400k env-steps and 0.281 and 0.172 at 1M, against 0.891 and 0.812 with them; on dark caves (never
  trained on) 0.172 and 0.125 (400k), 0.109 and 0.031 (1M), against 0.797 and 0.750. Most of the success is the
  scalars, and the pixels-only policy gains nothing from 400k to 1M at these settings: the next lever for the raw
  end goal is the observation (64x64, or 16x16 with the ore's colour kept), not PPO.
- **Java**: the learned episodes (2M pinned model; the 600k horizon-8 model) and an untrained one on held-out seed 513

## 2026-11-05 A reset to the same start 942 ms to 29 ms on Linux 7.0: the write tracker's scan lists holes as written there, and the reset zeroed the whole 6.5 GB arena (lane/rawskill)

Found by lane/rawskill's 10-second episodes: ntloop's stand-in at 256 envs on one start ran 21,146 to 22,429
env-steps/s with no reset in the window and 5,009 to 6,625 with one reset an env every 200 steps, every reset about
2.1 million minor faults (546 M over 256), a plain seed-set start and a dev start alike. The dev host runs kernel
7.0.0-42 since its 2026-11-04 freeze; lane/resetcopy (2026-10-30) measured a reset at 100 to 200-step episodes at 1.3
to 1.9 ms on the kernel before.

- **Where** (POOL_RESET_COUNT, `make -C csrc/runtime rlbind VARIANT=rc XFLAGS=-DPOOL_RESET_COUNT`, 128 envs, one
  start, 10 s episodes): a reset to the same start (the delta path) 942.2 ms, of it zero 894.2 ms over 2,120,300
  pages, 2,118,695 faults. The whole copy before it had handed back (madvise DONTNEED) 1,712,848 pages: the image's
  arena between the start's runs, never written. pool.c reset_written zeroes every page image_wtrack_scan lists
  that the start's runs do not cover, and image.h's contract is that a hole is never listed; on 7.0 PAGEMAP_SCAN
  lists the holes of a write-protected range as PAGE_IS_WRITTEN (the protect walk leaves them no marker), so
  zero_lines read every hole and faulted it in.
- **The fix** (csrc/engine/image.c image_wtrack_scan): the return mask adds PAGE_IS_SWAPPED and a run neither
  present nor swapped is dropped (a hole reads zero; a swapped or migrating page holds bytes and stays listed).
- **After**, the same run: the delta reset 29.1 ms (zero 3.1 ms over 1,607 pages), 4 faults; 11,771 env-steps/s
  against 5,248. POOL_RESET_VERIFY (every reset's image against its start's, page by page, non-resident pages read):
  256 resets on a seed-set start (192 by the pages written) and 256 on 27 dev starts (63 by the pages written), 0
  pages differ.
- What it cost any run on this kernel before the fix (a projection, not measured on the other lanes' runs): about
  0.9 s of a worker at every reset by the pages written, beside about 0.6 s of stepping in a 5-minute episode at
  brute16fast's 0.1 ms of a worker an env-step.

policy's key: the policy decides when, the macro still executes. Then the key's execution is the next rung's to take
away. Removed outright, each craft half cost about 2.3 depth (L4c 0.611, L4d 0.596; L4f 0.456 for both). As one key
each it costs nothing (L4e 3.10 and 3.06, L4g 3.49 and 3.47), once two things are labelled. The step after the key must
be labelled if the execution reads the key (recipe_hold, ladder13). The windows the key leaves the student in must be
labelled too, or the student sits in them (window_label level, ladder14; here 1.36 without it). The mine lock (the
attack starts it) and the fight macro were already this shape. Next candidates, from the teacher's census at 16383

with the level kept L4e, two training seeds, ingots against L4a's 169; (2) L4f = L4e without the table half
(NWRL_VEC_NOTABLE on top of 436215802: 503324666), distilled with (1)'s fix and whatever teaches the table's hotbar

crafting episode at the lowest rung that holds replayed on the Java client, and the ladder's table so far.

training. Every arm: the s1.hb.dk.gv build, a fresh net (ntinit 1 with --seed 1000, or ntinit 2 with --seed 2000), the
teacher s64-it42 at --macros 16383, 256M env-steps, l4ekey.yaml's recipe otherwise (gui cursor, press_label key, beta
0.5, hold weight 10 in the dig scope).

- **What the books say** (new: `score recipe`, vecenv.h nwrl_vec_gui_books [8] to [17]: the recipe's first steps by
  window, NWRL_VEC_NORECIPE's hand-offs at the recipe's start and after it, the smelt's ingots taken by the macro, the

  (2.629, as ladder12): a run starts 8.18 2x2 recipes, 10.36 3x3 and 0.953 smelts; 9.52 recipes a run are handed back
  after they started, 0.941 of them smelts; the macro takes the smelt's ingots 0.004 times a run (1 run in 256).
- **The cause.** craft() checks the hand-off (`NWRL_VEC_NORECIPE && plan_gui && !(NWRL_VEC_RECIPEKEY && rjump)`) at
  every call of the recipe half, not only at its first: a step without the policy's jump hands the window back. A 3x3
  recipe is about three such calls (its ops four to a call, one a step); the smelt's wait is one a step for 200 ticks an
  ore. The distiller labels the recipe's first step as the jump (label half 3) and masks the rest as the level's macro's
  (w 0), so the student was never taught to keep the jump held; a sampled jump let go once loses the smelt, and
  craft_plan names no smelt with the ore already in the furnace, so it never restarts (a 2x2 or 3x3 recipe restarts:
  closing the window gives the grid back). The label count the brief asked about is also lowest at the furnace (over
  256M the recipe's first step 95,056 times under the inventory, 69,275 under a table, 19,995 under a furnace:
  distill.jsonl `rscr`), but the count is not what loses the smelt.
- **The fix: distill.recipe_hold on** (--recipe-hold; distill.h ntd_recipe_hold; NWRL_VEC_RECIPEKEY levels, .gv
  builds): the recipe's later steps (label half 2) under a container screen labelled as the jump key alone, weight 1.

## 2026-11-03 The craft rung split in two: neither half alone holds L4a (L4c without the recipe half 0.611 pooled, L4d without the table half 0.596, against 2.93); L4c stops at the 3x3 clicks in the window the macro opens, L4d at placing the table (half of it the hotbar slot: 1.07 with policy_place); with the recipe as the policy's one key (NWRL_VEC_RECIPEKEY: its jump under the window starts the recipe macro) L4e holds near L4a, 2.68 and 2.50 on two training seeds, level with L4a through the furnace and short only at the smelt (lane/ladder12)

The brief: (1) the craft macro split into two switches, both on by default: (a) the table, a crafting table or furnace
placed and its window open when a plan needs it; (b) the recipe, the clicks under the open window, the result, the close;
the code shared. (2) L4c = L4a without (b), L4d = L4a without (a), each distilled as l4bdistill.yaml with actions.gui
cursor and press_label key from the start, one training seed to 256M, the 20-minute eval at eval seeds 7 and 8 with the
kept checkpoint; whichever holds near L4a a second seed and the next rung. (3) If neither holds: the half and the click
or state it stops at, the cheapest isolating change once (the 3x3 recipe as a policy's pick); a crafting episode on the
Java client.

Every eval is ladder10's and ladder11's: 256 runs of 20 minutes from seed 42's spawn, the sampled actor, `ntloop --score
--clock raw`, eval seeds 7 and 8, the dev host's 3090 through gpuq; checkpoint evals are 128 runs at seed 1000 beside the
training. Every arm is a fresh net with L4a's init and seed (ntinit 1, --seed 1000), the s1.hb.dk.gv build, the teacher
s64-it42 at --macros 16383, 256M env-steps (31 to 45 minutes each). L4a re-run in this tree as the baseline (ladder10's
L4aT-s1-best, its s1.hb.dk build): 2.824 (.106) / 3.039 (.114), pooled 2.93 (ladder10: 2.86 / 3.05).

- **Where the split falls** (vecenv.c craft(), vecenv.h NWRL_VEC_NOTABLE 67108864 and NWRL_VEC_NORECIPE 134217728, each
  a switch that turns its half off, as NOSCREEN): the craft macro's phase. CP_OPEN is the table half: for a 2x2 plan the
  inventory key; for a 3x3 plan open_bench (the remembered table looked at and used; else the table selected in the
  hotbar, the look 60 degrees down, place_item trying each side and digging the floor if none takes it, the use on the
  placed block; fetch_item first when the table is only in the main inventory: the inventory opened, the number-key swap
  to the hotbar, the close); for the smelt open_furnace, the same with the furnace. CP_CLICKS on is the recipe half:
  recipe_ops (each part's stack picked up, a right click into each grid slot, put back; the result shift clicked) or
  smelt_ops (ore and fuel in), CP_WAIT (the smelt's wait, the ingots taken), CP_CLOSE. Only the crafting plans split
  (plan_gui: the 2x2 and 3x3 recipes and the smelt); the bucket, portal, frame, throw and take plans stay the craft
  macro's whole under either bit. One code path: NORECIPE returns from craft() where CP_CLICKS would start and that step
  is the policy's (decode restores the policy's act: no wasted step); NOTABLE starts no crafting plan with no screen
  open, and under a tidy inventory, crafting or furnace window the policy opened, recipe_start (craft_begin, macro_start's
  start, factored out) begins the plan craft_plan names where plan_fits (shared with ladder11's labeller) says it fits
  the window, from CP_CLICKS, remembering the table or furnace under the crosshair.
- **Labels say the half** (nwrl_vec_label.half, in what was padding; the struct's size and offsets unchanged): 1 table,
  2 recipe, 3 the recipe's first step, 0 neither. The distiller counts a craft label in the level unless the level turns

The brief: (1) the screen macro as a switch, on by default; L4a = 8186 without it, distilled as l3bdistill.yaml,
compared against L3b's kept. (2) Craft as the policy's clicks: the action gains what the craft macro's plans emit
under a screen, the labels the macro's own ops; L4b = L4a without craft, distilled and evaluated, its gap named by
cause; a crafting episode replays on the Java client. (3) If (2) is too big, land (1) and the click heads with their
labels and gate.

Every eval is ladder9's: 256 runs of 20 minutes from seed 42's spawn, the sampled actor, `ntloop --score --clock raw`,
eval seeds 7 and 8, the dev host's 3090 through gpuq; checkpoint evals are 128 runs at seed 1000 beside the training.
The default path reproduces ladder9 exactly: L3bT-s1-best at 8186, seed 7, 2.957 (theirs 2.96).

- **The screen switch** is NWRL_VEC_NOSCREEN (33554432, `noscreen` in the macro names): a bit that turns the screen macro
  off, so it stays on by default and every level number means what it meant. The screen macro starts whenever a screen
  other than the death screen is open and no macro runs (the policy's use on a table, furnace or chest, an inventory a
  macro left open), throws the cursor's stack out (a click at -999) and closes it. With the bit, no macro starts under an
  open screen and the policy must close it (the credits' respawn stays). The distiller counts the screen macro in a
  level unless the level has the bit. L4a is 8186 + 33554432 = **33562618**.
- **Clicks in the 16-wide action** (`actions.gui: off | cursor`, off by default; vecenv.c MOPTS, gui_policy, gui_label).
  Under a container screen (inventory, crafting table, furnace, chest) the camera's two bins are the mouse on a 9x8
  cursor grid (vecenv.h NWRL_VEC_GUI_*: rows 0-2 the screen's own slots, the crafting grid at columns 0-2, the result at
  1,4; rows 3-5 the main inventory, row 6 the hotbar, 7,0 outside the window), mine is a left click, place a right one,
  sneak with mine a shift click, the hotbar element a number key's swap; key 12 (swap_item, unused before) is the
  inventory key, pressed on the step it goes down (a held key presses once): it opens the inventory and closes a
  container screen. A raw mouse and keyboard at a window, with the cursor's position absolute rather than moved. A
  macro's GUI ops go one a step (the rest queued), so each step's op is one the action can say, and its label says it
  (NWRL_VEC_LBL_GUI clear). No net change: the student's action is still 16 (17 with the hotbar) wide.
  - The open window's slots as scalars (late_scalars bit 4; net.h NT_GV, the `.gv` build): the screen's kind, then for
    each of the grid's 63 cells and the cursor the stack's count over 64 at its class of 11 (log, planks, stick,
    cobblestone, coal, iron ore, iron ingot, diamond, table, flint, other), 708 scalars. A player at the window sees
    which slot holds what; the 32 counts do not say.

The brief: L3 (4091, L2 without the seek) stalls at 2.59 to 2.61, and the whole gap is the seek's walk to ore in view.
One untested cause: the walk takes many steps and the student is feed-forward, so ore that leaves the 64x64 view is
forgotten. The pilot distils L3 as configs/l3distill.yaml does, on the minGRU variant (lane/ntgru's NT_RNN) with the
.hb.dk build L3 uses, one training seed, to 64M with the kept checkpoint. The second seed and 256M were conditional on
either of two bars:
- iron ore got above ladder5's .355 by more than its spread (about .03 at 256 runs);
- depth above 2.61 by more than about 0.15, so above about 2.76.

**Neither bar is met.** Every number below is the 20-minute eval (256 runs from seed 42's spawn, one 20-minute episode
each, macros 4091, policy_tool on, `ntloop --score --clock raw`, eval seed 7 unless it says 8) unless it says checkpoint
eval (128 runs, seed 1000, run beside the training).

- **Built** (the default builds unchanged: only NT_RNN builds and ntinit's .r1 output change):
  - `.hb` with `.r1` (`make -C csrc/runtime train-loop-v NT_V=s1.hb.dk.r1`). net.h refused the pair because "both take
    the blob's last two places". In fact NT_ORDER already puts the hotbar's two tensors first and the minGRU's after
    them, but learn.h's layout and actor.cu's place() indexed the minGRU at I0 + 16, the hotbar's slot. Both now
    index it at I0 + 16 + 2 NT_HOTBAR, and the #error is gone. No fastppo fixture holds the two together, so
    actor_check and learn_check do not cover the pair.
  - In distillation with --beta, the teacher and the student actor shared one state buffer, each stepping it in
    place. The teacher stepped first, so the student read a state the teacher had already changed. The teacher now
    gets its own (ntd's th, zeroed), and the loop's buffer, which the segments store as h0, is the student's alone.
  - ntd_widen loads a teacher without the minGRU (and without the hotbar before it) into a .r1 build with the
    minGRU's tensors zero, so its h stays 0 and it acts as it did. Before, it took only a missing hotbar.
  - ntinit for a .r1 variant zeroes the candidate's half (rnn_w rows D..2D-1, rnn_b D..2D-1). That is net.h's fresh
    start: h stays 0 and the net is the feed-forward one until training moves it.
- **The equivalence check.** ladder5's kept L3T-s1 was widened into the .hb.dk.r1 build (ntinit --from: the 20
  tensors copied, the minGRU's candidate zero). It scores ladder5's numbers exactly: 2.590 (SE 0.086), deaths .172,

whole gap is the seek's own work on states no label reached (DAgger's student drove at the teacher's macros, so the
seek took over there too). Build a student-level DAgger with the removed macro as the labeller: the student drives at
L3, the seek runs beside it on the student's state, its act the label where it would act, the teacher's label
elsewhere; a distill option, defaults unchanged; the same 20-minute eval and kept checkpoint as l3distill.yaml, two
training seeds to 256M; above 2.61 kept on two seeds by more than the eval's spread.

Every number is the 20-minute eval (256 runs, one episode each, eval seed 7, macros 4091, `ntloop --score --clock raw`,
out/l/ev.sh's command in l3label.yaml's header) unless it says the checkpoint eval (128 runs, seed 1000, beside the
training). That eval reproduces ladder5's kept L3T-s1 exactly: 2.590 (0.086), iron ore seen .805, got .355.
Fresh nets: out/runtime/train/s1.hb/ntinit seed 1 and 2 (the cache's fresh-s1.ntw is another variant's blob).

- **Built** (all off by default; GATES-ENV, TRAIN-HSEE-CHECK and TRAIN-WIDTH-CHECK PASS in a fresh worktree of
  77e03803, the eight pinned digests unchanged):
  - A per-env macro level: `nwrl_vec_level(v, level, labeller)` makes two shallow copies of `struct nwrl_vec` that
    differ only in `macros` (the level; the level and the labeller); `nwrl_vec_env_level(v, id, on)` has env id decode
    and drive its macros through the level's copy from its next decision (called at an episode's start). Nothing in
    decode's call tree writes `v`, so the copies share every pointer safely.
  - The labeller (csrc/runtime/vecenv_shadow.c): the seek's state machine run beside such an env on the same state,
    with its own copy of the seek's fields, kind, age and memo of cells given up (`struct vec_shd`, swapped in and out
    around the call), started and driven as macro_start and macro_drive would at the level plus the seek (8187, L2's
    seek: any reach, no crouch), never stepped. Where it would drive, the step's label is its act (mbit SEEK,
    `NWRL_VEC_LBL_SHADOW`); a step a level macro drives ends its run.
  - The trainer (loop.c, distill.cu; run-file keys under distill): `--labeller seek` (with `--beta`);
    `--level-share F` (of the student's episodes, the share at the level with the labeller, the rest at the teacher's
    macros as before; default 1); `--student-labels teacher|shadow|none` (on the level's episodes the teacher labels
    the student's other steps, nothing else trains, or nothing trains: the control); `--labeller-align DEG` (the
    seek's attack kept in a label only with the student's look within DEG of its aim, or on its cell);
    `--labeller-reach B` (a run starts only on a cell within B blocks). The labeller's label trains as a removed
    macro's act does, the student's own action the next step's previous action. distill.jsonl: lsteps, shadow (by
    stage), lmasked.

- **What it means for the ladder**: the removed macro as the labeller is not yet the ladder's general tool. A macro's
  act is a good label only on the states its own previous acts produce (the seek's look already on its line, its
  walk already under way); on the student's states the same act is a different instruction, and DAgger's loop
  amplifies whatever the student learns from it. What could make it one: label a macro's intent rather than its act
  (where the cell is, as ladder5's .or scalars, with the turn alone as the label), cap the labelled share of the
  student's own steps, or label only steps where the student's action already agrees with the macro's except for the
  keys. The control's kept 2.75 suggests the 40/40/20 mix is free to keep while trying these.

tool in hand and an unbroken attack. At play, without retraining, the tool pick (policy_tool=on) and greedy keys (.gk)
took the two 1024M students to 2.71 and 3.00. Train L2 that way at two seeds to 256M, with the held attack trained
rather than decoded; take a winner to 1024M; make it the run file's default.

Every number is lane/ntbc's 20-minute eval (256 envs, one episode each, eval seed 7 unless said, level 8187) on the dev
host's 3090. The recipe is the GPU host's night chain dagL2h-b50 exactly (its lib.sh chain(), read from the GPU host):

+192M from the 64M model and its Adam state. Each arm is evaluated with the option it was trained with.

- **Built** (all off by default; the default digests unchanged):
  - policy_tool now also drops the slot labels it would make itself (vecenv.c vec_label). A removed macro's slot
    change to the hotbar's best tool for the crosshair's block, with the attack held, is no longer a label. The 64M
    run trained 660 slot labels against the night's 14,744: only the mine lock's switches the env's pick would not
    make.
  - ntloop `--hold-weight W --hold-scope all|lock|dig` (distill.cu k_bc): the attack key's BCE gradient times W on a
    removed macro's label that holds the attack. The scopes are all (every removed macro, the strip's tunnels
    included), lock (the mine lock's only) and dig (the mine lock's, where the step before held the attack too).
  - Run-file keys `distill.teacher, level, beta, hot_weight, hold_weight, hold_scope` (loop.c), and
    configs/l2distill.yaml: L2 distillation and its eval as one run file, with policy_tool on and the hold weight 1.
- **Why a weight and not .gk** (the brief's choice): the distiller's loss has no entropy term (k_bc: the cameras' CE,
  the keys' BCE, the hotbar's CE). So the student's attack probability is the labels' frequency in what it sees. The
  dig's labels hold attack every tick, but the teacher's own steps around them do not, and the student cannot tell
  them apart: p about 0.95, so a 23-tick stone dig survives 31% of the time. .gk decodes the argmax at play, and ntloop
  refuses it with --teacher, so it cannot be trained. A weight W moves the trained optimum's odds W times toward the
  dig's labels, so the sampled policy itself would hold. Training greedy keys is not a separate thing from this.

The long run (configs/s64big.yaml) sat at a next-milestone rate of exactly 0 on eight stages. The brief's reading was the
5-minute episode. This lane built per-stage lengths, traced the obsidian start's deaths, and split length from the
pearl macro.

- **Built** (each off by default; gates-env PASS in fresh worktrees of the code and of the merge with master):
  - `starts.episode_seconds: STAGE/SECONDS,...` (ntloop `--stage-seconds`). Each start of the mix plays its stage's
    length; stages not named play `pipeline.episode_seconds`.
    - vecenv: `nwrl_vec_opts.start_ep_len`, the env's length taken at each reset's draw.
    - A group's envs now end apart, so `group_done` resets only the ended envs, with a step of those ids alone.
      Without the key the whole group ends together, as before.
    - Refused with a start window. `--score` drops it (one length, its `--minutes`).
  - `starts.share: resets|steps`: `steps` divides each start's draw by its length, so the curriculum's weights are
    shares of env-steps and spawn_min holds spawn's share of training.
  - `starts.clock: played|left`: `left` makes o[7] the share of the last five minutes gone (0 before them). It
    equals `played` at 5 minutes, so the value function reads the time left at any length.
  - The return-scale books zero each ended env, not only a group that ended together (the same order when it does).
  - episodes.jsonl's `len`.
  - Run files: configs/s64stagelen.yaml (s64big plus the lengths: iron pickaxe and bucket 10 minutes; flint and steel,
    the diamond pickaxe, obsidian and the Nether 20; the eye and the End 30), and configs/s64big2.yaml.

  | keys and camera greedy (.gkc) | 1.02 | 1.25 | .016 .211 | 0 .020 | 0 .012 |

  The lock's value at L2 is two things, both of which the student must now do itself: the tool in hand when it
  attacks a block (the slot: +0.43 and +0.57 alone), and the attack held with no break while the block cracks (+0.28
  and +0.33 from drawing the keys greedily: in 1.7.10 one tick without attack drops the block's damage to 0,
  survival.c's resetBlockRemoving, so a sampled key at p 0.95 keeps a 23-tick stone dig with a wooden pickaxe 31% of
  the time). Together 2.71 and 3.00: the whole lock (2.84, 2.82) and the L1 students (3.32) within reach. The lock's
  aim and hold without the tool pick are worth nothing (1.78, 1.80): stone by hand gives no cobblestone. Greedy
  camera bins break it (1.02, 1.25: the argmax look never turns).
- **Why the student cannot pick the slot**: its scalars hold each item's count over the whole inventory, the selected
  slot and the held item's index, never which slot holds which item (vecenv.c scalars); the slot-change labels name
  a number key whose meaning changes each episode. The student's argmax on them: 2.0% and 6.2% at 64M, 16.7% at
  256M, 21.2% at 1024M (b50-s1): it switches by sampling.
- **The change tested: the hotbar's tools as scalars** (net.h NT_HSEE, the `.hs` builds; nwrl_vec_opts.late_scalars
  bit 1, NWRL_VEC_HSEE_N 27: per slot the pickaxe's, axe's and shovel's tier over 4, what the HUD's hotbar shows).
  Trained as lane/ntbc's L2 chain (fresh-s1.hb, --beta 0.5, 64M then +192M, the 3090), against the .hb runs at the
  same env-steps (the GPU host's: 64M 2.28, 0.82, 1.91; 256M 2.08, 1.68, 1.81):

  | .hs student | 64M | 256M | slot labels' argmax at 256M | + tool pick at play | + greedy keys | + both |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | seed 1 | 2.07 | 1.62 | 0.291 (.hb 0.167) | 2.47 | 1.82 | 2.86 |
  | seed 2 | 2.00 | 1.77 | 0.359 | 2.13 | 2.23 | 2.82 |

  Both seeds at 256M (1.62, 1.77; mean 1.69) sit inside the .hb runs' 1.68 to 2.08. The student reads its slot labels
  better (argmax 0.29 and 0.36 against 0.17) and still does not switch in play: the tool pick at play adds +0.85 and
  +0.36 to it, as it adds +0.43 and +0.57 to the .hb students. Seeing what each slot holds is not enough: what it
  lacks is when, since the block under the crosshair reaches the scalars only as mo_hit (hit or not; its kind is in
  the pixels alone), and a switch label is 3 decisions in 10,000. Not the change that moves L2; off by default.
- **Built** (all off by default): `policy_tool` and `mine_tool` (policy.actions options, vecenv.c MOPTS); NT_HSEE
  (`.hs`; a blob of 155 or 169 scalars loads into the wider fc1 with zero weights, loop.c ntw_flat and ntd_widen);
  NTA_GREEDY (`.gk`, `.gc`, `.gkc`: the actor's keys, camera or both drawn greedily, the hotbar sampled; ntloop
  refuses learning or a teacher with it); distill.jsonl's `stages`; k_ssc (the student's scalars) kept the scalars
  past the 14 previous keys as zeros (the keys' shift ran past them): any NT_LATE (.ls) distillation trained on zeroed
  late scalars; now the env's values. One teardown segfault seen once after a refused `--init` (s1.hb.hs under
  gpuq, two others the same command exited cleanly), not traced.
- **Gates** (a fresh worktree of 0e995ba1, master merged): GATES-ENV PASS (13 gates: the eight pinned digests equal,
  pool-gate 133,280 rows, raycast-gate 31,660, native-test, train-loop-check, livguard); TRAIN-WIDTH-CHECK PASS;
  TRAIN-HSEE-CHECK PASS (new, train/loop.mk: a fresh s1.hb net in the s1.hb and s1.hb.hs builds, and with
  policy_tool=off given: one trajectory digest, 4431a555c98c37b5).

The change that moves L2 today, measured: the tool pick kept as its own small macro (policy_tool=on, the one act of
the mine lock the student cannot learn yet) and the keys drawn greedily (.gk) at play: 1.89 and 1.71 to 2.71 and
3.00 on the two 1024M students (1.62 and 1.77 to 2.86 and 2.82 on the .hs ones at 256M), no retraining; the L1
students 3.32.

Next: train L2 with policy_tool on (the level becomes 8187 plus the tool pick: the student no longer needs the
switch labels) at two seeds, and train the held attack instead of decoding it greedily (the keys' entropy term or a
lower temperature on attack alone; greedy camera bins break the walk, 1.02 and 1.25); for the switch itself, the
crosshair's block kind in the scalars (what F3 shows) beside .hs, then --hot-weight again (lane/nthotbar's 30 made
false switches when nothing said which slot held what).

## 2026-11-02 Observation parity, the C client world: at 16x16 and at 64x64 39 of 40 pool-gate recordings now cast row for row as the Java client does (34 and 32 before; 133,279 of 133,280 rows each), from five fixes to the client world's light, chunk set and copies; the one row left (s1chain-S23 row 3124) is an arrow copy's client hit that teleports an enderman's copy on its own Random, which C does not model (lane/parity2)

Continues lane/parity (the section below): the cast's inputs that no row field sees, by cause.

| | 16x16 | 64x64 |
|---|---|---|
| lane/parity's start (3aede81c) | 34 of 40 | 32 of 40 |
| this lane (5c060461) | 39 of 40 | 39 of 40 |

Measured by `bash csrc/runtime/rcparity.sh -j 6 DIR` over pool_gate.list, the oracle replayed fresh (POOL=0) both
times (out/parity/base, out/parity/final); every C check in between ran against those oracle digests (`-k`).

- **The client's sections (parity-skylight, parity-blocklight).** A ground-up chunk packet (S26PacketMapChunkBulk and
  a ground-up S21) leaves out every section with no block, and Chunk.fillChunk nulls it; a light write into a null
  section makes a fresh one (Chunk.setLightValue). C's client copy shared the server's empty sections, light and all,
  so its relight went on from the server's values (respawn-loop-s1's chunk (11, 14) section 5, gold-g15-s42's sky).
  world.c chunk_drop_empty_secs drops them on both send paths (the S26 bulk's copy, the S21 share).
- **The leaves' marks (parity-blocklight).** BlockLeaves.breakBlock and BlockLog's mark the leaves around with
  setBlockMetadataWithNotify(.., 4): no markBlockForUpdate, so no packet. C wrote them with flag 2, an S23 each, and
  the client's relight of one carried the lava's block light into a chunk Java's never lit (respawn-loop-s1 at 64x64).
  The write is the store alone now (world_set_meta's notify branch, never taken at flag 4, had closed a call-graph
  cycle through the block worklist).
- **An older snapshot's active set.** A snapshot without WorldClient.previousActiveChunkSet: the Java client had walked
  the set once a row from row 2 of its join (the oracle's --cw-prev), so C's first walk started two rows ahead and
  relit respawn-loop-s1's lava at row 25 against Java's 27; session.c rebuilds the set from the walks (cw_walks_before).
- **The bulk's queue (parity-chunkgone).** The S26 path drains sr->send_queue, set at a login or respawn; a walk off
  the square had PlayerInstance.removePlayer take chunk (10, 20) out of EntityPlayerMP.loadedChunks (its S21 found no
  chunk on the client), but the queue kept it and its bulk went out 4 ticks later (chat-deaths-s1). The bulk path skips
  a chunk the player manager no longer holds for the player (chunkload.c cl_player_holds); bulks and S21s also reach
  the client in the order sent (sr_sent_chunk.at, serverreplay_sync_client_chunks).
- **The dragon's phase (parity-endjoin).** cp-end-s1's checkpoint dragon was isAirBorne (its runtime fields), which runs
  its tracker entry's update block off the every-third-tick phase; endfight_snapshot_dragon dropped it, so C skipped the
  tick-2 move and the copy ran a move behind for rows 3 to 6. pickobj_bind also resumes each bound entry's recorded
  tracker state, as combat_bind does for the livings.
- **The last sent motion (parity-copypos).** EntityTrackerEntry.tryStartWachingThis takes the entity's motion as the
  entry's last sent; combat.c's try_start_watching kept the S12 the entry made before anyone watched, so enderman
  1012's S12 at gold-g30-s42 tick 6487 (a change under 0.02 from the stale value) never went out and its copy stood
  0.03 off at row 6488. gold-g30-s42 and s1chain-S23's row 1159 are equal now.
- **Open, with the cause (csrc/tests/divergences/parity.tsv):**
  - parity-teleport: s1chain-S23 row 3124. Both servers teleport enderman 267 in tick 3124 and send the same S18, but
    the Java client's copy had already jumped in its own tick: the arrow copy beside it hit it, and
    EntityEnderman.attackEntityFrom has no isRemote guard, so the indirect damage ran teleportRandomly on the copy's own
    Random. C's client arrows make no hit and its living copies keep no Random (an enderman's also draws two portal
    particles a tick). A port, not a fix.
  - parity-poollight (the oracle's warm pool): not reached; Pool.java restores every static's graph, so the leak is
    outside it. rcparity replays fresh.
- **Tools.** test_snapshots `--cw-cells T:CX:CZ:SEC,...` prints C's client sections (light, block, the server's beside
  them, each chunk's relight cursor and the section masks); the oracle's `--cw-cells` prints the Java client's the same
  way (CwDiff's CWMASK, CWQ lines), `--cw-prev` the active set each tick, and `--cw-pkts ID,...` each tick's packets for
  those entities with their client copies' state (position, box, dead, wet, burning). Each is diagnostic only and
  refused by the warm pool.
- **Gates at 5c060461:** the native suite PASS (3,889 jobs); gates-env PASS in a fresh worktree (13 gates, every
  digest the pinned one); `make -C oracle gate` 5 of 5; globals, stack clean; index-check 64 records with errors, as
  master; callgraph's one cycle outside worldgen (the zombie jockey's) is master's.

## 2026-11-01 The macros were never the cost (every chain macro ran at 94% of recipe + strip, vanilla against vanilla); vanilla's engine was. Four macro scans read only what can match, the pearl rows are made only when the macro may drive, the random ticks run only the draws that hit a ticking block, and a pathless creature's repeated path search is answered from the world's memo: every digest master's, instructions an env-step -21% at the blaze-rod start with every macro, -4.6% at spawn; env-steps/s +5.8% and +1.4% there (lane/macroperf)

The brief set a target of every macro at 75% of the recipe-only run (57,637 against 246k to 261k env-steps/s). Those
two numbers were measured at different fidelities: the recipe run was at fast (s64boot: no spawning, random ticks or
weather) and the chain run at vanilla. Vanilla against vanilla, the frozen s64-it42 with recipe + strip scored 61,335
(out/runs/night/s64van/score.log), so the chain was already at 94%. On the CPU bench at spawn (recipe, host cast),
vanilla is 4.27M user instructions an env-step and fast 2.96M; every chain macro together added about 220k. The
orchestrator retargeted the lane at 11:55 pm: keep the macro cuts, then cut vanilla's engine cost (csrc/engine), the
entity pass first. Every change below keeps master's trajectory and observation digests:

- **obsview.c** (the obsidian and portal macros' view) reads only the sections the chunk holds. It tests each 16-cell
  (x, z) column's two 8-byte words for water, lava and obsidian with a SWAR byte compare, then walks the matching
  cells in the original y, z, x order: the same candidates, the same per-cell body. **netherview.c** and **shview.c**
  skip a band that holds none of their ids. Before the reference hooks were taken out, the obsview and shview
  rewrites ran beside the original functions in VARIANT builds at five starts: every call equal.
- **The pearl macro's far-depth rows** (rlbind.c's state hook) were made in every env every step. Now they are made
  only on a step the macro may drive (`pearl_depth_due`), through `nwrl_far_depth_now`. A `-DPEARL_DEPTH_POISON`
  build, which fills rows not made with junk, gives pearl_check books equal to master's.
- **servertick.c, the random ticks.** `rtick_prefetch` replays the chunk's LCG draws, keeps only those whose
  4,096-cell group holds a random-ticking block, and prefetches their cells. The tick runs those draws with the LCG
  set to each one's value. A write to the chunk or an LCG a tick moved hands control back to the original loop at
  the next draw.
- **pathfind.c, World.getPathEntityToEntity's answers kept in the world** (`struct pf_memo`, 16 slots, paths up to 48
  points). An old-AI creature with no path searches again every tick. A probe build at gold-g9 (every macro, 64 envs
  x 1,100 steps) counted 70,012 entity searches, 44,271 of them exact repeats.
  - The key: the searcher's fields byte for byte, the end cell, max_dist, the four flags, and the world's map_ver
    and bseq when the search began.
  - When an answer is kept: only if the search loaded nothing and bseq was at most wseq then. Any later block or
    metadata write takes a bseq past that wseq, and a chunk joining or leaving moves map_ver.
  - A search that reads two worlds is not kept.
