## 2026-11-01 The brute-force table with every macro, from seed 42's spawn and seeds 1-1000's, on CPUs alone: in 2-hour runs random play reaches the iron pickaxe (1.6% at seed 42, 6.3% over the seeds), an ender pearl (4.3%, 1.6%) and once a diamond pickaxe (1 of 256, +strip2), and nothing past it in 3,840 chain runs; the pearl step's nights triple the deaths, and pearl with pearlcave takes every step from spawn (lane/brutetab)

GOAL.md "Done means" 1 again. DEVLOG 2026-10-27 lane/intent made the first rows with a scratch Python script, before
the chain's macros existed. Now it is all in C: `out/runtime/train/brutetab` (csrc/runtime/train/brutetab.c, its rule
in train/brutetab.mk) runs a random policy over the vector env with the host ray cast and no device
(CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=, device_mesh 0, raycast host, render none). It reads a run file: configs/brutetab-early.yaml
(180 s episodes, 512 envs) or configs/brutetab-chain.yaml (2-hour episodes, 128 envs), both with s64chain-strip2's
world and 64x64 observation at vanilla fidelity (natural spawning on). Each env plays R episodes. Per milestone (a log;
stages.h's chain, wooden pickaxe to the End; then the dragon) it prints the count, the share of episodes and the CPU
wall a success, ep_len / (rate x env-steps/s), with the 95% bound (rate < 3 / E) where none was seen; `--json` writes
a line a row. The policy is lane/intent's better row: each step the camera's two bins uniform over 20 +- 5 of the 41,
each of the 14 keys held with p 0.5. `--seeds 1-1000` takes the seed set of the run's world (seedset-d989661987,
lane/seeds), shuffled by `--seed`; seed 42 is the run's own start, drawn at one seed's share. Short episodes use
`--window W:S` (W loaded, S more a round), long ones `--sample K` (K loaded, about 135 MB a start). The tool raises
its open files to the hard limit: on the GPU host a window of starts plus the region spill's files ran out of the soft
1024 at a 512-env row's 4th round ("the snapshot does not load"); those rows were run again. `make -C csrc/runtime
brutetab-names-check` holds its macro names to train/loop.c's MACRO_BITS (23, equal). A preset is macro_set's spec
plus `all`.

**Where and how.** The GPU host's CPUs, 2026-11-01 11:29 pm to 2026-11-02 1:57 am MT: cores 32-55 and their siblings
96-119, as two streams of 12 cores and 24 threads (32-43,96-107 and 44-55,108-119), each row in its own scope capped at
36 GB (the peak was 17.3 GB). 40 rows, 24,320 episodes, 626.7M env-steps in 2 h 28 min, 70.6k env-steps/s over the
24 cores together. No GPU touched: a watcher read every brutetab process's fds and maps once a minute, 149 samples, all
"nvidia fds 0, nvidia maps 0"; the GPUs' processes were another project's.

Samples. The early rows: 2,048 episodes of 180 s each. From seed 42 that is 512 envs x 4; from the seeds 128 envs x 16
with `--window 32:32`, 503 distinct seeds. The chain rows: 2-hour episodes, 128 envs x 1. From seed 42, sampler seeds
1 and 2 are pooled (256 a row); they agree, e.g. recipe,strip,food gives iron ingots 18 and 18, iron pickaxes 2 and 2,
flint and steel 5 and 11. From the seeds, `--sample 128` once, 86 distinct seeds.

A cell is the count (the share) and the wall a success at the row's env-steps/s on 12 of the GPU host's cores; a 0
is under the "a 0 means" column's bound. The chain rows add each macro to the row above: recipe, then strip and food,
then obsidian, nether, pearl, stronghold, dragon, bportal and strip2 in turn. `all` is every MACRO_BITS bit (+strip2's
and pearlcave). Rows of equal counts are the same trajectories; their env-steps/s (seed 42: 35.0k to 37.0k for
+pearl through +bportal) is this host's timing noise.

What the table says:
- The raw keys never get a log: 0 of 4,096 runs from both starts. The mine lock gets the log (73% of 180 s runs at
  seed 42's spawn, 42% over the seeds), the craft macro the wooden pickaxe (6%), and table-anywhere with iron triple
  that (20.7% at seed 42, 14.5% over the seeds) and add the stone pickaxe (1.2%). lane/intent's row at 32x32 and fast
  fidelity had 20.3% and 1.26%.
- In 2 hours, recipe alone goes to the furnace (5.1% at seed 42, 1.6% over the seeds) and an iron ingot (2.0%, 0).
  Adding strip and food reaches the iron pickaxe (1.6%, 6.3%), flint and steel (6.3%, 1.6%) and a bucket (0.8% at
  seed 42). Through the chain rows only +strip2 got a diamond pickaxe: 1 of 256 from seed 42, 16.9 min a success on 12
  cores. Nothing reached obsidian, the Nether, blaze rods or powder, an eye, the End or the dragon in 3,840 chain runs.
- A chain macro whose entry needs an item random play never makes does nothing from spawn. +obsidian (it wants a
  diamond pickaxe) gives the same counts and deaths as the row before it; so do +stronghold (12 eyes), +dragon (the
  End) and +bportal (flint and steel and two buckets). +nether changes overworld play through the craft macro's sword
  plan (an iron sword from 2 spare ingots, else a stone one): at seed 42 the iron ingot falls from 36 to 11 of 256 and
  the iron pickaxe from 4 to 1. +strip2 changes it back up: iron ingots 13 to 29 of 256, a diamond pickaxe once.
- +pearl is the first chain step random play reaches: an ender pearl in 4.3% (seed 42) and 1.6% (the seeds) of
  2-hour runs, 92.6 s a pearl on 12 cores. But its want is only "the overworld at night, pearls and eyes under 12"
  (vecenv_pearl.c pearl_want: no sword, no armour, no food), so every night of every run becomes the enderman hunt.
  Deaths go from 1.91 to 6.07 a run at seed 42 (90% of runs die at least once) and from 1.41 to 4.28 over the seeds.
  keep_inventory is off, so each death drops the kit.
- `all` is +strip2 with pearlcave, and pearl with pearlcave takes every step from spawn. pearlcave makes the pearl
  step's want hold by day too (vecenv_pearl.c:142), and with nothing held its cave stair makes nothing: 0 logs in 256
  (seed 42) and 128 (seeds) 2-hour runs, almost no deaths, the env 3.2x faster (118k env-steps/s, the player not
  playing). Checked on the dev host, 16 envs x 120 s: recipe,strip,food with pearl got 8 logs, with pearlcave 8,
  with both 0.
- Deaths at 180 s are mostly the surface macro's absence: with mine alone 38% of seed 42's runs die, with base 8%
  (18% and 2% over the seeds). In 2 hours 74% of seed 42's recipe runs and 64% of the seeds' die at least once before
  any chain macro.

**Wall time** (one success expected: 1 / (rate x episodes an hour)). The cells are 12 of the GPU host's cores, at each
stream's own env-steps/s. The lane's 24 cores ran two streams at once at those rates, so the whole set did about twice
a cell's throughput (70.6k env-steps/s over the sweep). The 3090 host (the dev host, a Ryzen 9 9950X3D: 16 Zen 5 cores,
32 threads, the trainer's 30 workers) was not measured. It sat at load 34 to 96 from seven lanes and a trainer
tonight, and a lane may take 8 of its threads, so a full-host run was not this lane's to make. Its figure is a
projection by worker threads, 30 against a stream's 24 on the same Zen 5 generation: 1.25x a cell's env-steps/s, so
every wall above times 0.8, and the whole sweep (4.63 stream-hours of 12 cores) about 3.7 hours there. Projected on
the 3090 host, from seed 42 with recipe,strip,food: a wooden pickaxe in 3 s, a stone pickaxe 6.5 s, an iron ingot
18 s, flint and steel 40 s, an iron pickaxe 2.6 min (seeds 1-1000: 50 s). An ender pearl with +pearl takes 74 s, the
diamond pickaxe with +strip2 13.5 min (one success seen: a rate, not an estimate). Obsidian and everything after it
is over 3.5 min a success at recipe,strip,food's 95% bound (4.4 min on 12 cores), which is only a bound: random play
may never get there.

Next. The rows past the iron pickaxe need a policy, not more samples: the same run files meet the frozen s64-it42
(`make -C csrc/runtime train-score RUN=configs/brutetab-chain.yaml ...`). For the chain from spawn, pearl's want
should ask for the kit it was planned with (a sword, food), and pearl with pearlcave should not start without a
pickaxe. A quiet-hour dev-host measurement should replace the projection.
## 2026-11-01 The strip's 3-diamond envs were out of wood, because the strip wears every pickaxe out on stone: NWRL_VEC_STRIP2 now climbs to the surface for wood (a reserve for the next pickaxes), leaves the depth when its want ends, guards against a mob behind, and the surface macro closes a screen before it swims; in the case 70 of 71 three-diamond envs make the diamond pickaxe (strip2 62 of 109) and 80 envs die (108); in the chain the diamond pickaxe 48 to 70 of 512 and depth +0.6, but deaths 0.60 to 0.73 a run (lane/strip3)

strip_case's books now hold what the last step held and the step the diamond pickaxe was first held. They show what
stopped strip2's 3-diamond envs. gold-g5 starts with 12 planks' worth of wood and s9 with 11. By 30 minutes the strip
has dug 900 to 2,100 cobblestone an env; a stone pickaxe lasts 131 blocks, iron 250 and diamond 1,561, and each one
takes 2 sticks. From gold-g5 the live envs ended at tier 0, the iron pickaxe worn out with ingots unused, and diamond
pickaxes made at steps 10,000 to 23,000 were worn out by 36,000. The 3-diamond envs held 0 to 2 planks and no table.

What it does (csrc/runtime/vecenv_strip.c; hooks in vecenv.c's strip_want (strip_want0 is the old one), strip(),
seek_want(), seek() and the surface macro; constants at vecenv_strip.c's top; no new bit):

- The climb: the strip's own sets in a mode that prefers up. A set tries a stair up, then flat, then a step down, and
  only then the quarter turn, with the strip's floor, lava and liquid rules all the way. Underground that is a
  staircase; at the surface it follows the ground.
- The wood errand: while the strip has digging to do and a pickaxe is held, it starts when the wood held (planks, a
  log at 4, two sticks at 1) is short of a table (none held or in reach) plus 2 for sticks. It runs until 12 more are
  held: up to the surface and along it until seek_want's wood want takes a log in view. The craft makes the rest
  where the player stands.
- Out of the depth: with the strip's own want over and the feet under y 40, it climbs until the feet reach y 56.
- The guard: the strip's "other" first deaths (traced: s9 seed 1, env 3) were a mob hitting from behind in a clear
  tunnel, 3 every 12 steps, with nothing in view. A hostile in view within 5 (not a creeper, an enderman or a pigman)
  gets the fight lock. A hurt with nothing in view turns the look back.
- Drowning under the crafting screen (traced: s9 seed 1, env 9): the craft opened a table placed with its head in
  water, and the surface macro then held jump under the open screen, which no key passes, until the env drowned. The
  surface macro now closes a screen first, behind the bit.
- A set that dug gravel or sand waits 20 steps and judges its cells again. A stair up turns from sand, gravel or clay
  over the head (the floors of lakes and seas, which a2's climbs dug up under and drowned). The wood seek walks
  crouched.
- ST3_KEEP6 and ST3_NOGUARD: VARIANT builds, measurement only (no trip with the wood kept; the guard off).

## 2026-11-02 Observation parity: the Java client draws the policy's ray cast from its own world (RayCast.java, raycast.c's FP64 reference), each row's frame digest in the tape; at 16x16 34 of 40 pool-gate recordings equal row for row (133,134 of 133,280 rows), at 64x64 32 of 40 (132,972); the rest are named C client-world divergences (two fixed here) and one oracle pool leak (lane/parity)

GOAL.md "Done means" 4, SPEC.md "The environment as configuration" 5. The policy's observation, csrc/runtime/raycast.c's
FP64 reference instance (the one the gates pin), is now computed by the oracle from the Java client's own state, so a
policy can play the real client live and its frames can be held to C's.

- **The port** (oracle/harness/netherite/oracle/RayCast.java, 1,678 lines; no oracle/src edit). raycast_ref in
  raycast.c's operation order: the pinhole rays, the DDA (ties x, y, z), blocks by kind (cube, box, cross, the double
  plants, water and lava with their surface heights), the tints from the table's biomes and colormaps, the light of
  the cell the ray left with chunk_light's semantics on the client chunks' storage arrays, rc_light_port's lightmap,
  sky and fog (build_rs's inputs: the client world's clock, the server world's prevRainingStrength and
  prevThunderingStrength, the biome temperature with BiomeGenBase's noise), the entity boxes (the client world's living
  copies and fireballs, then the dragon, then the player's dimension's server items, orbs and arrows), the End sky and
  the underwater overlay. It reads the tables C loads (out/java/render/forest-fast, out/assets). Rows are split over
  8 walker threads with a chunk cache each (a 64x64 replay costs what a 16x16 one does: end-dragon-s1 55 s either
  way at load ~110).
- **The switch.** `client.camera raycast` with `client.observation WxH` (and client.channels, client.graphics,
  client.gamma) in WorldConf.java (worldconf.c already had the key), or Main's `--raycast WxH[xCH][:fancy]` on any
  replay. Each row gets `d.rc`, the frame's FNV-1a 64 (pool_gate --raycast-rows' digest), and the header
  `options.raycast`; off otherwise, so no existing tape changes (Check.diff skips d.rc where either side lacks it, as
  d.px). `--raycast-dump DIR:@T` (oracle) and pool_gate `--raycast-dump DIR:WxH:@T` write one row's frame and its
  trace (the setup's reals as bits, the entity boxes, each pixel's walk, its light and biome), so a divergence names
  its pixel and cause.
- **The check:** `make -C csrc/runtime raycast-parity` (csrc/runtime/rcparity.sh): every pool_gate.list recording
  replayed by the oracle with --raycast and by pool_gate with --raycast-rows, row for row, the first differing row of
  each traced on both sides; `-k DIR` reuses an earlier run's oracle digests (a C change checked in C's time), `-n`
  skips the traces, `-d SIZE DIR NAME:ROW` traces given rows.
- **Fixed on the way:**
  - The cast never drew the ender dragon: the C client keeps it as a pick object (pickobj.c PK_DRAGON), not a living
    copy, so every End frame lacked it (end-dragon-s1 387 of 1,221 rows). raycast.c's entities() now adds it after the
    living copies (3dc45dce; only End casts change).
  - A killing blow's S19 status 3 (onDeath's setEntityState) goes out in the network tick with the blow; C sent it at
    the next tick's tracker pass, so the client copy's deathTime ran a tick behind and the corpse stayed a tick past
    the Java client's (combat-mobs-s1 row 2322's cow, night-s1, gold-g15-s42, s1chain-S8: 11 rows).
    combat_server_attack sends it now (afd3a1b9); the suite passes on it.
- **Open** (csrc/tests/divergences/parity.tsv, each with its repro). None is in a row: the client world's light, its
  chunk set and its copies' positions are only seen by the cast.
  - parity-skylight: the C client world's sky light after a respawn and far from the player (respawn-loop-s1 row 25:

## 2026-11-01 Macro options: every either/or in the chain macros is a run-file option (23 of them, each default today's behaviour), lava sensed only by sight (lava_sense view, the new default: the old rule rested on lava's sound), no macro reads a sound; stronghold_locate snap reaches the End in 8 of 64 envs on 12 eyes, pair 0, follow 0 (lane/macroopts)

Elliot, 2026-11-02 (GOAL.md "Macro options"): where a macro could work one way or another, every way is a configurable
option, and no macro uses sound. The orchestrator's reading of "the easiest the default": easiest for the policy
distilled from the macro, the way that reaches the step most often, so every default is today's behaviour, except
where today's rested on sound.

- **The plumbing.** `nwrl_vec_opts.macro_opts` (API 14, NWRL_VERSION 11 to 14; 12 and 13 had not bumped it): a string
  "name=word,...". vecenv.c's MOPTS table holds each option's name, its words in value order, its default and a line
  on what it does; `nwrl_vec_make` parses the string into `v->mo[]` and refuses an unknown name or word.
  `nwrl_vec_mopt_check` and `nwrl_vec_mopt_list` are public. The run file sets an option as `policy.actions.NAME:
  WORD` beside `actions.macros` (train/loop.c read_run: any actions key but macros and picks; an unknown one fails the
  read: `policy.actions.stronghold_method: no macro option stronghold_method`). `ntloop --mopt NAME=WORD` overrides it,
  and `ntloop --mopts` lists them all. sh_check, obsidian_case and nether_case take `--opt NAME=WORD`.
- **stronghold_locate** follow | pair | snap (snap). snap is lane/stronghold2's method: one far throw, its heading
  matched to the ring's chunk grid, with the pair as fallback. pair is two throws 24 blocks apart, their lines crossed.
  follow is new: walk 200 blocks along each eye's line and throw again; a line that points back past the last one
  halves the stride, down to 24; over the room the eye flies down and the dig starts there. "Heading plus
  deceleration" is not a separate method. EntityEnderEye.moveTowards aims 12 blocks ahead and 8 up whenever the
  stronghold is farther than 12, so the deceleration gives the distance to that point, not to the stronghold. Within
  12 blocks the eye flies down onto the room's column, and every method already uses that (sh_estimate's est 2).
  The case: sh_check, 32 envs, 36,000 steps, train-fast, the random policy, on the GPU host's CPUs. 12-eye and 16-eye
  kits (lane/stronghold2's starts, ~/dev/nw/.tmp/chain-inputs/stronghold2), sampler seeds 1 and 2, totals over 64 envs:

  | method | eyes | room | the End | throws an env | eyes lost | deaths while it ran |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | follow | 12 | 12 | 0 | 6.9, 8.3 | 260 | 4 |
  | pair | 12 | 40 | 0 | 3.8, 3.2 | 130 | 7 |
  | snap | 12 | 31 | **8** | 2.4, 2.1 | 43 | 5 |
  | follow | 16 | 12 | 3 | 6.9, 9.5 | 280 | 5 |
  | pair | 16 | 40 | **21** | 3.8, 3.2 | 130 | 6 |
  | snap | 16 | 31 | 17 | 2.4, 2.1 | 43 | 4 |

  snap at 12 eyes gives lane/stronghold2's numbers exactly (rooms 15 and 16, Ends 2 and 6, 78 and 68 throws), so the
  default path is unchanged. pair reaches the room most often but spends the eyes the frames need, so on 12 eyes

## 2026-11-01 After the exit portal: the credits pause the server's tick counter, so the autosave's unloads and the time packet come later than C ran them; both of lane/dragon3's kill tapes equal on the Java client to their last row, and the fixed vec env's kill episode too (lane/exitdiv)

One cause for both tapes (ledger `exitdiv-pausesave`, 4604dd42; `dg3-exit-overworld-t18900` fixed by it).

- **The cause.** GuiWinGame pauses the game, and IntegratedServer.tick skips `super.tick()` while paused, so
  MinecraftServer's `tickCounter` stands still for the credits' rows (two here: the overworld's time froze at 271,605
  for t 18,695 and 18,696). C modelled the pause (the first paused tick's save, the frozen world) but ran the
  `tickCounter % 900` autosave on the row tick, `(t + 1) % 900`. saveAllChunks queues every loaded chunk without a
  player instance outside the spawn box, so after the credits C unloaded the overworld's chunks the player had walked
  away from two rows before Java. Seed 1 env 16: row 18,900, Java 289 chunks against C's 256, 18 entities in the 33
  chunks (sheep 2365 to 2367 and 2410), Java unloading them at 18,902. Seed 2 env 24: row 21,600, w.ents 162 against
  149. `session_tick_counter` (the row, plus the snapshot's offset, less the paused rows) now drives the save and the
  `% 20` S03 time packet, which reads the same counter.
- **The S03 half, checked on Java's client clock.** Rows equal either way, but the frame judge's `dragon-s1chain-S23`
  shot at t 16,785 moved (a 6-row credits pause at 16,772 to 16,777). Java's own client clock there (the oracle's
  render-state probe at ticks 16,768 to 16,791): level with the server from the respawn through 16,785, one behind
  from 16,786, so the S03 is sent in row 16,785, the paused counter's. C with the old timing: `FAIL play check ...
  row 16780 client world time want 190917 got 190916`; with the new: 24 of 24 frames agree, 16,790 rows. The shot's
  budget (a ratchet measured on the wrong clock) is re-accepted at its new numbers: 629 px against 631, 478 against
  480, channel means up 0.0004 to 0.001 (the sky a tick later); pxdiff's survey finds three registration clusters at
  leaf edges, nothing else.
- **The respawn click Java refused (t 19,310) is not a second cause, and not the vec env's.** The vec env's own world
  split at 18,900 and its player died there at t 19,307 (hp 1.36 to 0, GuiGameOver), so it clicked respawn; Java's
  player lived. On the fixed engine nothing in csrc/runtime needed a change.
- Every one of the 868 recordings has its snapshot's tickCounter equal to its tick mod 900, so the change moves a save
  only after a pause.

## 2026-11-01 The strip mine stopped because the iron pickaxe was not in the hotbar and the staircase's floor check failed at every level: NWRL_VEC_STRIP2 (16777216, off by default) fixes both; from gold-g5 15x the cells and 12 iron ore and 4 to 5 diamonds an hour where it dug none, but 2 to 10 of 32 envs are still mining at 30 minutes (target 28); the chain's diamond pickaxe 12 to 30 of 256, deaths 0.49 to 0.61 a run (lane/strip2)

lane/eyetrade measured the strip from gold-g5-s42: it stopped after about 6,000 ticks, and 28 of 32 envs ended on the
same 123 cobblestone. The causes, traced one env at a time (-DST_TRACE=ENV, a VARIANT build):

- gold-g5's iron pickaxe is in main-inventory slot 16. The craft's shift-click fills from the hotbar's end, and that
  hotbar was full. `best_tool` reads only the hotbar, so the strip dug with the stone pickaxe until it broke (step
  ~2,100), then the wooden one (~4,100), then with the hand: stone by hand is 150 ticks and drops nothing, and the
  60-step progress rule turned the strip first. `strip_want` counts all 36 slots, so the strip kept the step (98.8%
  of steps) and walked no cell after ~4,000.
- Going down, the floor check aims at the next step's floor centre. From where the walk stops, that ray clips the
  block under the feet: the floor reads bad, the strip turns a quarter at every level (a 2x2 spiral, 160 steps a

  the tunnel behind; a spare stone pickaxe crafted into the main inventory while the iron one wore.

What `strip2` does (csrc/runtime/vecenv_strip.c, new, included by vecenv.c before the seek; one-line hooks in strip(),
seek(), the mine lock, dig_under(), strip_want() and craft_plan(); constants at its top; only with NWRL_VEC_STRIP on):

- The strip, the seek and the mine lock dig with the cheapest pickaxe that mines the block (stone, wood, then iron and
  diamond, kept for the ores that need them). A better-ranked pickaxe in the main inventory is moved to the hotbar
  under the inventory screen with a number key's click, at most one errand every 40 steps. A stone pickaxe is made
  beside an iron one while a table is at hand. The spare never makes a table: a rule that did (d50766c6) spent the
  diamond pickaxe's planks (0 made, envs ending on 3 to 5 diamonds) and was reverted.
- The floor is judged on the far part of its top face. With the feet under y 12, the strip stairs back up with a
  jump. Below y 16, nothing digs two or more under the feet.
- Lava in view (obsview OV_HOT, never through a wall), every 5 strip steps: within 4 across, from one under to three
  over, the strip heads the cardinal way most away from it; ahead within 8 at the head or under, a quarter turn; on
  the liquid ray within 3, back along the tunnel.
- strip_want: 4 planks for a table, or none with an iron pickaxe held; a table made again for the diamond pickaxe.
  Under 3 free slots, the surplus (cobblestone past 128, dirt, gravel, saplings) is thrown behind.

  strip's steps. `out/runtime/strip_case` (csrc/runtime/strip_case.c) prints them per env with deaths by cause and

What was wrong. On lane/enddiv's fixed engine, lane/dragon2's macro killed nothing because the crystals healed back what
it did. The books now read the server's own healing crystal (`dragon_state.healing_crystal_index`, endview's books
only; the macro never reads it). With the lob off (`-DDG_LOB=0 -DDG_HUNT_R=80 -DDG_RELEASE=12` reproduces lane/dragon2's

ran hurt with a healing crystal on 37,173 to 42,497 ticks a seed. That is 3,700 to 4,250 health over 32 envs, about
what they dealt. Three causes:
- A crystal on a pillar is hidden from below by the pillar's own top edge, and a low arc rises into that edge.
- An entity moves only while the chunks within 32 blocks of it are loaded (World.updateEntityWithOptionalForce). At
  render distance 4 the server loads 4 chunks around the player's, so an arrow at a crystal more than 2 chunks from
  the player's chunk stops in the air. The crystals shot 9 times without a kill sat 38 to 40 blocks out on z.

  blocks out on 56% of the healing ticks (seed 1, partway through).

  89.7 degrees down, the arrow comes down 9 to 17 blocks a block across and clears the edge). ItemBow's spread moves
  the landing about 1.3 blocks each way after its 90-tick flight, so about 0.47 of lobs should land in the crystal's

  from the crystal toward the centre, a lob between 12 and 30 blocks.
- The hunt out to 110 blocks (`DG_HUNT_R`). Lobs from wherever a kept crystal is in reach (in the hole, and from the
  snipe tower after a look around).
- Hunts back to back: lane/dragon2 walked back to the centre and dug a hole between two hunts, so its pit phase took
  33% of the first ten minutes. The hole now comes after the last hunt.

## 2026-11-01 Eyes of ender from a priest, measured: the trade ladder, not the game time, stops it. A village pays 1.7 emeralds for coal (5.4 for coal and wheat) before every path stalls, and 12 eyes come in 0 and 1 of 8,000 village draws. Seed 42's nearest priest is 1,449 blocks away. The macro was not built (lane/eyetrade)

The brief: measure the priest route (one eye for 7 to 10 emeralds) against pearls and rods, and build a trade macro only
if it is cheaper. It is not, so this lane built measurement tools only.

- **The rule** (EntityVillager, and csrc/engine/villagers.c and trades.c, every member at index status exact,
  trade-full-s1 and trade-prof-s1):
  - Using the list's LAST recipe unlocks: 40 ticks with nobody trading, then every disabled recipe +2..12 uses (only
    when the list holds more than one), and one new recipe from the profession's table at p + sqrt(size) * 0.2.
  - The priest's table: eye 0.3, bottle o' enchanting, redstone, glowstone, and eight enchanted-tool trades at 0.05
    each, which take the tool and 2 to 4 emeralds. An empty draw gives 8 to 9 gold ingots for an emerald.
  - No gap in C.
- **Villages in reach** (`out/runtime/trade_census --census`: the engine's own structure_walk; a measurement of the
  world, never something a macro reads; it matches cov-villagerep-s42's village at 692, -331):
  - Seed 42: the nearest village is 964 blocks off with no priest; the nearest priest is 1,449.
  - Seed 191: a librarian and a blacksmith 71 blocks off; the nearest priest is 884.
  - The 999-seed set: a priest within 256 blocks on 54 seeds, within 128 on 21.
  - The library's 25 seeds: within 256 on 2 (seed 20 at 167, seed 67 at 252).
- **The ladder** (`trade_census --econ`: trades_add_default and trades_unlock_boost with the unlock rule; 4,000
  villages a row; sampler seeds 1 and 2 agree within 5%). The trader buys an eye when it can, else unlocks the
  priest's last offer, and sells goods only when short of emeralds.
  - A priest's first offer is an eye in 16% of draws.
  - One priest with unlimited emeralds reaches 12 eyes in 9% of draws, 23% if iron tools are handed over for its
    enchanted-tool trades, 84% with diamond ones too, at 101 to 119 emeralds.
  - A full village (4 farmers, a librarian, a priest, a blacksmith, a butcher) starting from no emeralds:
    - coal only: 1.7 emeralds before it stalls, 0.07 eyes;
    - coal and wheat: 5.4 emeralds, 0.34 eyes, 12 eyes in 1 of 8,000 draws;
    - every good villagers buy, plus iron and diamond tools: 59 emeralds, 12 eyes in 18%.
  - The stall: a buy offer allows 7 sales and comes back only through an unlock, and an unlock is buying that
    villager's last offer, with emeralds.
  - Every seed-set priest village within 512 blocks, with its real professions (coal and wheat): 0.51 eyes, 12 in
    0.02% of draws.
- **The goods an hour** (`out/runtime/trade_case`, configs/s64trade.yaml: gold-g5-s42's iron pickaxe, the recipe,
  strip and food macros, the random policy, natural spawning, the host ray cast, 32 envs, sampler seeds 1 and 2):
  - Coal 101 and 89, all within the first 3,000 ticks: about 70 an hour while the strip digs about 870 cells an hour.
  - Over 30 minutes, 6.3 and 5.6 coal an hour (0.32 and 0.29 emeralds), no deaths.

## 2026-11-01 The dragon kill's divergence: three C engine causes (the End's crystal slots, a reloaded arrow's pickup, the crystal's client fire); lane/dragon's kill tape replays equal on the Java client for all 24,000 rows, and the fixed vec env's episodes equal Java's row for row (lane/enddiv)

lane/dragon's split at t=8081 compared the vec env's rows with `test_snapshots --row-dump` of the Java run, which
are C's rows of Java's tape: C against C. C against Java first split at row 5747 (the ledger row's last clause).
Pin: Java's run of the kill tape as `out/java/snapshots/end-kill-g30-s42` (24,000 rows from 42/G29's tick 2, the kill
and the exit portal at 21,353), in the suite.

- **Row 5747, w.ents 134/132** (ad3e43d7, `enddiv-crystalslots`). dragon.h's 64 crystal slots were append-only:
  every chunk reload of a spike constructs a new EntityEnderCrystal and took a new slot while the unloaded one
  stayed. Fighting around the island reloads the spikes every few hundred ticks, so by row 5747 the slots were gone
  and two saved crystals of a reloaded chunk were never built (every later id two lower). `dragon_crystal_slot`
  reuses a slot whose crystal left the world, except the dragon's healing crystal (vanilla's dragon keeps that
  reference across the unload). The slot users that depend on order pick a strict minimum (the healing crystal)
  or sort by chunk stamp (the blast and projectile queries).
- **Row 5995, the player's arrows 30 against Java's 31** (34193695, `enddiv-arrowreload`). An arrow a chunk reload
  rebuilt (`sr_arrow_adopt`) joined only the living world's chunk lists: `ie_added_to_world` adds nothing while the
  chunk being read is not in the world yet, and the pickup walk (`collide_with_player_pool`) reads the item world's.
  It now joins the chunk as `Chunk.addEntity` does (`ie_add_to_chunk`, as `sr_restore_tnt` already did).
- **Row 11251 of the fixed vec env's tape, d.cw** (13d8a86f, `enddiv-crystalfire`). `d.cw` is the client Random's
  seed×31 + its LCG, so two rows give a tick's step count: Java 6,891, C 6,893. Over 11240 to 11400, with C's
  Random resynced to Java's every row, 6 ticks disagreed, and on 5 of them Java's count equalled C's count for 999
  iterations of the void fog loop. That is what one cell read solid in Java and air in C does to the fog's sample
  stream (it falls a draw behind and usually realigns an iteration late). Forcing each of C's sampled air cells solid
  singled out (23, 88, 16), the top of a spike whose crystal died at tick 4,413, on all 6 ticks. The oracle's
  `--cw-cells` showed fire (id 51, block light 15) there in Java's client from then on; the server and both C worlds
  had air. Vanilla: the blast's S27 clears the client's fire and the next flush's S23 sends the server's air. The
  client crystal (`EntityEnderCrystal.onUpdate` runs on the client, and in the End writes fire into its cell) is still
  there, because its S13 comes a tick later (World.updateEntities removes a dead entity in the next pass, and only
  then does the tracker let go). So it puts the fire back, and the client keeps it. C untracked a crystal at setDead
  (pickobj `view_of`), a tick early, and its client copy wrote no fire. This was the open "client-only fire" line in

## 2026-11-01 Ender pearls, round two: the census puts the endermen in caves, so x10 is out of reach from the surface; the pearl macro's pillar, flee, hide and walk changes take first deaths 85 to 64 and pearls 7 to 8 in 192 env-nights (lane/pearl2)

The brief: pearls a night x10 and deaths a night /3 on lane/pearl's case, measured first. Neither target was reached.

The measurement. `pearl_check --census` (rlbind.h nwrl_census; measurement only, privileged, never read by the macro)
books every step the server's endermen by horizontal distance band (distance, height against the eye, under the sky,
tracked, in the cone, the line from the eye clear, and from 2 and 4 blocks higher), the hostiles within 16, the
player's biome, and every death's phase, pillar, cover, height and health ten steps before. On lane/pearl's macro, 32
envs, seeds 1 and 2: 1.7 to 1.9 endermen alive within 128 blocks a step, about 0.55 within 64; of those 16 to 64 blocks
off, 5 to 20% under the sky, 42 to 93% more than 6 blocks below the eye, the line clear for 2%; in view 0.025 a step
(0.0019 with the bit off). The player is on open ground already (ice plains 51 to 63% of steps, frozen river 18 to 28%).
Lines from 2 blocks higher clear 1.2 to 1.5x as many, from 4 higher 1.4 to 3.4x. 42 kills in 192 env-nights and a drop
of 0 or 1 pearl (nextInt(2)) cap the pearls at about 0.11 a night even with every drop picked up: 3x, not 10x. First
deaths (28 of 64): 19 on the pillar, skeleton 11, enderman 6, spider 4, zombie 4, creeper 2, drowning 1, most at 1 to 3
HP ten steps before (arrows from out of view while held up the pillar to heal; a zombie behind the player on the walk;
at 10 HP a pillar built beside a zombie whose knockback stalls it).

What changed in vecenv_pearl.c (NWRL_VEC_PEARL, still off by default; every constant at the top of the file):
rlbind.h nwrl_far gains the frame's depth (14 rays inside the 64x64 frame's view to the first block or liquid within
64, on only with the bit) and the stats screen's endermen killed (the kill is now stat.killEntity.Enderman, not
stat.mobKills). The macro keeps 16 yaw sectors of the depth: the walk steers to the longest dry view (water, lava and
ice wet), a pillar goes up only where the view is long, a scan with a short view ends at 48 steps unless an enderman
showed in the last 200. The scan pillar is 5 high with nothing about, 3 with an enderman in view, dug down to 3 when a
provoked one is within 8. A hit from out of view is turned to (the knockback's reverse); a pillar with no enderman for
200 steps is left away from the hit. At 10 HP or under a skeleton (or a hit with nothing in view) is fled, sprinting,
turning from water and creepers; zombies and spiders are fought (fled, they kept pace and hit). At 8 HP and 30 quiet
steps the hide: centred, 3 blocks dug down, a cobblestone put against the rim's inner face over the head, sealed when
the look straight up meets it, held to 18 HP, then mined and climbed. No pillar dug down with a creeper within 8; only a
screaming enderman keeps the player up, the height by floor (fighting from a 2-high pillar mid-dig killed 3 of 16 arena
envs); a provoked target lost is swept for; drops are fetched from the walk too; no pillar from water.

## 2026-11-01 A library of starts at every stage on 25 seeds, every one a Java-made snapshot whose episodes replay on the Java client; the native trainer draws from it through a curriculum, with the seed set natively and the late game's scalars behind a switch; under the KL anchor the curriculum and spawn alone stay level on every stage, and without it spawn alone saturates the beginning (wooden 0.29 to 0.52-0.55) while the curriculum loses the middle (stone 0.89 to 0.32-0.39, bucket 0.53 to 0.09-0.16), two seeds each (lane/starts)

Elliot asked for checkpoints the player spawns at, holding different items, on many seeds, harvested from good
episodes, with a curriculum so training never starts from scratch and never only from the end.

- **The library** (`out/library` of the lane: 150 starts, 1.11 GB, `index.tsv`: id, seed, stage, milestones,
  dimension, items, provenance, bytes, path; `csrc/runtime/train/harvest.sh`, `out/runtime/train/ntstarts`).
  - Each of the 116 harvested starts goes through four steps: the episode's tape (`ntrec tape`) is replayed by the
    oracle; `ntstarts stages` reads its rows for the first quiet tick (no screen open, on the ground) after each new
    stage; the script cut there plus a `save` makes a vanilla Save and Quit checkpoint (`LIB/ID/cp`); and the
    oracle's Snapshot of that checkpoint's join is the start (`LIB/ID/start`).
  - The other 34 are references to stored snapshots: golden g1 to g30 (seed 42, every stage to the End) and the
    human's sessions. `cp-nether-s1` and `cp-end-s1` are dev starts, which the product refuses; the index skips
    dev starts.
  - Stages (`train/stages.h`) come from the milestone mask and the dimension in chain order: spawn, wooden and
    stone pickaxe, furnace, iron ingot, iron pickaxe, bucket, flint and steel, diamond pickaxe, obsidian, nether,
    blaze rod, blaze powder, ender pearl, ender eye, end. A milestone bit added to vecenv.h fails the build at a
    static assert until its chain entry is written (lane/dragon's).
  - About 8.9 MB a harvested start: the snapshot 4.9 MB plus the checkpoint's save, with its pre/ snapshot and
    copied tape dropped. `-1` caps the library at one start per (seed, stage).
  - Seeds: seed 42 from the night's four 8-milestone vanilla tapes (32 starts, 6 minutes). Then 24 more seeds from
    the frozen s64-it42 at vanilla on seeds 1-24 and 65-88 (`configs/s64van.yaml`, 128 envs, 30-minute episodes,
    the best episode per seed): 84 starts in 37 minutes at load 50 to 100, the oracle's first pass 1.5 to 2.5
    minutes per episode.
  - By stage: spawn 3, wooden 30, stone 25, furnace 19, iron ingot 14, iron pickaxe 11, bucket 6, flint and steel
    8, diamond pickaxe 8, obsidian 1, nether 1, blaze rod 3, pearl 13, eye 6, end 2. The frozen policy never gets
    past the diamond pickaxe, so every later stage is the golden chain's or the human's (seed 42).
- **The trainer draws from it** (`train/curric.h`; run file `starts.seeds`, `seed_set`, `library`, `stages`,
  `library_seeds`, `curriculum`, `floor`, `spawn_min`, `min_eps`; `configs/s64starts.yaml`).
  - `starts.seeds` is native now. Each seed's start is found in the seed set whose world.yaml is the sim's world
    with a different seed, and every start is loaded at the make (no window yet).
  - `nwrl_vec_start_weights` (vecenv.c, reset path only) moves the shares between resets.
  - Each reset draws a stage, then one of its starts. Adaptive weights score each stage (1 - r) + 2|r - r0| on its
    next milestone's rate since the last row, with a floor of 0.04 a stage and spawn at least 0.25; they go in
    iters.jsonl's `curriculum`.
  - The recording's header names the mix's starts (`mix_K`), so `ntrec tape` and `netherite replay` replay an
    episode from any of them. `start_from` resolves the snapshot's own start: a fresh world of its seed, or its
    checkpoint, falling back to out/java/checkpoints/SEED/NAME when the recorded path is gone. It also resolves the
    config's start by name.
- **The late game's scalars** (net.h `NT_LATE`, build word `.ls`; `nwrl_vec_opts.late_scalars`, off by default):
  - 14 more inputs: log1p counts of obsidian, the iron and diamond pickaxes and swords, blaze rods and powder,
    pearls, eyes, the water and lava buckets and food, then the Nether and the End.
  - A 155-scalar blob loads with zero fc1 columns on them. s1 and s1.ls give the same trajectory digest
    (cc357b9a4f73b681) over 32 envs and 160 group steps from the late-stage starts, where the new inputs are
    nonzero. The digest hashes the 155 base scalars and every step's reward and driver, so equal digests mean
    equal actions.
  - There is no PyTorch fixture for .ls, so its learner with nonzero late weights is held by nothing beyond
    training without NaN.
- **Replays on the Java client**, every one END EQUAL:
  - 5-minute episodes from harvested starts on seed 13 (the iron-pickaxe start, gaining a diamond pickaxe and a
    bucket) and seed 2;
  - 40-step episodes from a seed-42 library start and a seed-3 spawn;
  - lane/nether's episode from gold-g8-s42 through `netherite replay`, FROM resolved to checkpoint 42/G7.
  - A dev start is refused with its reason.
- **The A/B** (s64-it42 widened on s1.ls, configs/s64starts.yaml: train-fast, 5-minute episodes, lr 5e-6, ref_kl
  1.0; 128 envs, 12M env-steps an arm, trainer seeds 1 and 2).

    library starts of those seeds (at most 3 a stage).
  - The eval is held-out where it can be: the spawns and harvested starts of seeds 65-88, plus the late stages,

- **Without the anchor** (`--ref-kl 0 --lr 1e-5`, 30M env-steps an arm, trainer seeds 3 and 4, the same paired

  | stage (next) | start | spawn alone s3 | s4 | curriculum s3 | s4 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | spawn (wooden) | 0.286 | 0.548 | 0.524 | 0.214 | 0.262 |
  | wooden (stone) | 0.893 | 0.893 | 0.821 | 0.393 | 0.321 |

  | depth, 512 runs (SE 0.1) | 5.39 | 5.42 | 5.33 | 5.02 | 4.94 |

  - Spawn alone did what Elliot predicted, on both seeds: it saturates the beginning and loses the later stages.
  - The curriculum as built hurts, on both seeds: spawn does not gain, the middle of the chain falls, and only the
    deaths where the late starts are fall.
  - Its training return fell from about 9.7 to 2.7 while deaths a row rose from 30 to 160.
  - The likely cause (a hypothesis, not tested): a death from a late start costs the death term plus the value of
    everything held, and the shared running reward scale then shrinks every early stage's signal. The policy

## 2026-11-01 The End fight as a macro: the End and the dragon as milestones, one kill and exit in 64 random-policy episodes, a C-against-Java divergence at t=8081 of the fight (lane/dragon)

What it adds. `NWRL_VEC_DRAGON` (2097152, `dragon` in MACRO_BITS) is the End fight, from the arrival platform to the
exit portal, in csrc/runtime/vecdragon.c (every tuned constant a `DG_*` at its top). It reads only the End as the
player sees it, from csrc/runtime/endview.c (called from rlbind.c's state hook in the End; kept beside nwrl_state so
mcsr-speedrun's ctypes layouts stay as they are): the crystals in view (within 75 degrees of the look, the line from
the eye to the middle or the top clear), the dragon's head and body and the boss bar's health, and the endermen in
view. The End entered (`NWRL_VEC_MS_END`, bit 14) and the dragon killed (`NWRL_VEC_MS_DRAGON`, bit 15) are
milestones in the record, the save mask (archive names `end`, `dragon`), episodes.jsonl, iters.jsonl, the score
table and train-score-sweep's columns. `reward.end` and `reward.dragon` (or `--end-weight`, `--dragon-weight`) are 0
unless named, so default digests do not move.

Composition. The macro starts in the End, alive, with no screen open, holding a sword in the hotbar or a bow with
arrows (macro_start, after eating, before the hunt). It ends when the dimension changes, the player dies, or a screen
other than its own fetch's inventory opens. It writes the whole act every step and nothing on the step it ends, so
nothing stays held. The credits after the exit are the screen macro's (PG_RESPAWN with the bit).

The fight:
- The climb out of the platform's pit.
- A snipe tower while the dragon sleeps. At render distance 4 its chunks are not loaded from the platform, so it does
  not fly.
- Crystals shot by bow on a solved arc (full draw 3.0 a tick, gravity 0.05, drag 0.99). Melee was not measured
  against it: it needs a tower up each obsidian pillar, up to 40 blocks, inside the dragon's circle.
- The walk in to the island's centre, and a cobblestone box there against the wing push. It ducks into a box on the
  way when the dragon comes.
- A snipe again when the boss bar shows healing and no crystal is in view: a pillar's own top edge hides its crystal
  from below.
- Arrows at the dragon's head led by its motion, and the stone sword within 9 blocks.
- The exit: wait 210 steps, then walk to the portal under the death. The portal is at y 64 whatever the ground, so
  when stuck under its bedrock rim it backs out, towers to the rim's top and walks in.

Beds were not used, from 1.7.10's formula (not measured): a bed blast near enough to hurt the dragon's head hurts the
player about as much, and the chain has no wool.

The case: `out/runtime/dragon_case --config configs/dragon.yaml` (`make -C csrc/runtime dragon-case`). Seed 42's
golden End arrival (configs/checkpoints.tsv `end`, gold-g30-s42, the Java checkpoint 42/G29) has the golden kit
(stone sword, bow, 51 arrows, about 306 cobblestone, iron armor, food). 32 envs, 24,000 steps, a random policy under
the macros, sampler seeds 1 and 2:

| | seed 1 | seed 2 | without the bit, seed 1 / 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| the dragon killed | 0 | 1 (step 20,995) | 0 / 0 |
| the exit portal | 0 | 1 (step 21,353) | 0 / 0 |
| End deaths: void, dragon, enderman, other | 4, 5, 2, 18 | 4, 7, 5, 12 | 27, 1, 1, 3 / 27, 0, 1, 4 |
| the dragon's lowest health seen, mean | 158.5 | 144.5 | 199.4 / 199.4 |

The bit cuts void deaths from 27 of 32 to 4, but 28 to 29 envs still die in the End (median step 10,886 to 12,956);
12 to 18 of those deaths are unattributed (not the void, the dragon's head or an enderman near). The frozen s64-it42
from the same start (configs/dragon64.yaml, 256 runs, 20 minutes, eval seed 1000, the 3090 through gpuq), with the
bit against without (`--macros 16383`, the model's own set):

| | with | without |
|---|---|---|
| deaths a run | 0.80 | 3.63 |
| kills | 0 | 0 |
| depth (SE) | 5.38 (0.052) | 6.02 (0.072) |

Without the bit the model walks off the island and collects overworld milestones after respawning, which is why its
depth is higher.

The Java replay is not equal. dragon_case `--tape DIR --rows ID` runs each episode twice with the sampler restarted
and tapes the second; seed 2's env 2 ends identically both times. Its tape on the Java client from 42/G29 gives rows
equal to the vec env's own for 8,079 rows. At t=8081 the entity digest differs and the player's motion y is +0.333
in C against -0.078 on the ground in Java. The divergence is ledger row `dragon-endfight-t8081` (open; the wing push
or an enderman's hit are the candidates). Out/report.md has the details, the episode's path and stages for
lane/starts, and what is left.

- Gates: GATES-ENV PASS in fresh worktrees of 9fd01d6b and of 56a1484e (master merged at ad574797, lane/pearl:
  both macros kept; seed 2's kill and exit reproduce after it at the same steps), master's recordings linked,

  unchanged (512x4 090cb0a8007a184d a12bbde7e7e8b15d, 128x2 a9d498ac53a83ba3 fbe418a4838cb318, and the f32, fx and

## 2026-11-01 Ender pearls hunted at night from a pillar: no deaths in the arena, 0.08 pearls a night in the wild, about 150 nights for 12 (lane/pearl)

NWRL_VEC_PEARL (524288, "pearl"; csrc/runtime/vecenv_pearl.c, included by vecenv.c; off by default). In the overworld at
night (the day's time 13000 to 23000) with pearls and eyes under 12, it builds a 3-high cobblestone pillar and fights from
the top. EntityMob.attackEntity hits only with the feet within 2.0 blocks and the boxes level in height, and the creeper's
fuse lights within 3.0, so nothing on the ground reaches the top, while an enderman's 2.9-high box beside the pillar is
still in the player's 3-block reach. From the pillar it turns to find an enderman (rlbind.h nwrl_far: endermen in view
out to 64 blocks, vis's rule, never through a wall, with the scream the screen shows). It stares at the box middle until
the enderman screams, which is the vanilla provocation (shouldAttackPlayer: the look within acos(1 - 0.025/d) of the box
middle). After that it watches the enderman by the top of its box, because an angry one stared at within 4 blocks teleports
away, and by a point under its feet when it is farther than 10 blocks, so that it keeps teleporting toward the player. It
hits with the hotbar's best weapon whenever the crosshair is on the target. A kill is booked when stat.mobKills moves within
4 steps of the target leaving view. The drops are picked up once no enderman has shown for 100 steps: the pillar is dug
back (the cobblestone comes back) and each drop is walked to. With no enderman in view it scans for 360 steps, digs down,
and walks 300 steps along a heading the policy's camera steers. On the walk it turns away from water and lava (the
bucket's ray), swims at the surface, walks away from skeletons in view, flees creepers within 7 blocks, and fights other
hostiles within 10 blocks with the fight lock. When hurt to 10 HP or less it goes up the pillar instead of fighting. It
gives the step back by day (after coming down), at 12 pearls and eyes, to eating (NWRL_VEC_FOOD) and to drowning (the
surface macro). It leaves held the pearls and every cobblestone not still in a pillar.

The case: pearl_check (csrc/runtime/pearl_check.c, `make -C csrc/runtime pearl_check`; the macro's books through
nwrl_vec_pearl). The start is oracle/tests/pearl-night-s42.jsonl, recorded on the oracle: seed 42's spawn, then an iron

## 2026-11-01 The step label's macro is 32 bits wide, so the chain's macros (switches from 1 << 17) label their own steps (lane/mbit32)

lane/pearl found it: `nwrl_vec_label.mbit` (lane/ntbc's label of the macro that drove a step, by its switch, read by
distillation's census and its level test) was a uint16_t, and the five chain macros being built today (obsidian 1 << 17,
nether, pearl, stronghold, dragon up to 1 << 21) would label as 0, the policy's own step, so a student would learn
their acts as the teacher's policy. mbit is uint32_t now (the struct 20 to 24 bytes; vecenv.c's write the only writer,
train/distill.cu the only reader, which reads it as an int already, and `--level` is an int); NWRL_VEC_LBL_SCREEN stays
0x8000. Nothing stores labels: the recording's per-step macro is bufs.kind.

- gates-env PASS (default digests unchanged).
- The distillation smoke (s64-it42 teaching itself at level 8191, 256 envs, --steps 400, about 102k env-steps, the
  3090 through gpuq), this build against master's twice: every class's counts within master's own run-to-run spread
  (the async pipeline steps 102,400 to 102,592 env-steps a run, so no two runs are equal): mine 74.60% of steps
  against 74.56% and 74.63%, none 16.92% against 16.97% and 16.93%, craft 8.23% against 8.21% and 8.19%, screen 2 in
  each. No macro on master has a switch past 0x8000, so the label's values are the same at either width.

  (the rate to 0 over 2 hours; same seed, init and recipe; out/runs/night/scratch16-anneal-s1, 1.70B env-steps at
  236,488 env-steps/s) passed 1.64B with its entropy near 9 throughout and peaked higher (from spawn at 93 minutes:
  97% wooden, 84% stone pickaxe, 18% furnace, 9.9% iron ingot, 1.0% iron pickaxe, about G3's 80-90 minutes), then its
  deep milestones slid as the rate reached 0 (furnace 5.5%, iron pickaxe 0.24% at 120 minutes). A controlled test on
  the GPU host (out/runs/night/resume): the first run's checkpoint at 130 minutes (1.48B, before its slide) resumed
  30 minutes, two trainer seeds an arm, Adam afresh: rate held, the entropy fell to 0.7 in both and the stone pickaxe
  from spawn from 51-57% to 17-35%; annealed, the entropy held (2.4, 4.0), one seed climbed (stone 69% to 86%) and the
  other lost skills at high entropy (58% to 27%). The anneal stops the entropy collapse; it does not yet make the late
  run hold its deep milestones.
- **minGRU** (lane/ntgru): built and held to its reference, 1 to 3% of env-steps/s, but it collapsed on 4 of 6 seeds
  at the feed-forward recipe (feed-forward 0 of 6): off by default.

Flywheel fixes the night needed (out/flywheel, untracked): testmap.sh checks its hold every round (a loop started
before the hold ran a full strace suite beside bench windows); gpuq.sh never pauses a window's own process group (a
window opened inside a yield job stopped itself and held the queue for 8 minutes); `ntloop --run` honours --warm and
--steps over the run file's hours (master bd576cca; three lanes' short checks had run for hours). The GPU host's base

## 2026-11-01 PPO that holds a good start: ppo.ref_kl (the policy's KL to the start's frozen weights) turns erosion into a hold on both starts at both trainer seeds (the L1 student 0.00 to 0.37 under today's defaults, 3.54 to 3.65 with the anchor, start 3.46; s64-it42 4.23 to 4.60, 4.73 to 4.80, start 4.73); the value warm-up and the annealed rate alone do not hold the student; 250M of the combination plateaus at 3.62 to 3.74 and ends at 3.55, no climb past the 64M arms (lane/ntppo)

The brief: lane/ntboot and lane/ntbc found the native trainer's PPO erodes every good policy it starts from. Make a KL
anchor, a value warm-up and an annealed rate native (run-file keys and flags, off by default), held to fastppo's, then
test them at 64M env-steps from two starts with two trainer seeds an arm. Base 03455f88. Every arm trained and every
score ran on the GPU host's GPU 2 (RTX PRO 6000, shared with lane/ntbc's distillation until about 9:00 am), except four
cross-checks on the 3090. out/report.md has every score.

- **What landed** (defaults unchanged; the books, rows and digests of a run without the keys are as before):
  - `ppo.ref_kl X` / `--ref-kl X`, fastppo's --ref-kl. loss += X * sum(KL(pi || ref) m) / nm over the policy's
    steps, with ref the --init weights frozen on the device. KL is fastppo's policy_kl: the camera heads'
    categoricals plus the 14 keys' Bernoullis. k_loss computes it and its gradient (d/dlc = p (lc - rc + 1) before
    log_softmax's backward; p(1-p)(x - rx) for a key). The reference's logits are computed once per segment
    (ntl_ref_forward, in chunks of the minibatch), not once per minibatch per epoch as in fastppo: one extra forward
    per update. The `ref_kl` book (iters.jsonl already had the column) is its mean.
    `ppo.ref_kl_schedule const|linear` takes the coefficient to 0 over the run (not tested in an arm).
  - `ppo.value_warmup N` / `--value-warmup N`: the first N updates train v.weight and v.bias alone. k_loss's pol 0
    gives no policy gradient. ntl_adam_value clips over the head's gradient and runs Adam on the two tensors with
    their own count. Every other weight and moment is untouched. With a fresh Adam, the head's moments are zeroed at
    the warm-up's end. `ppo.value_warmup_lr` / `--value-warmup-lr` sets the warm-up's own rate: s64boot's 5e-6
    would barely move a head in 150 steps, so the arms used 3e-4.
  - `ppo.anneal on` / `--anneal on`, fastppo's --anneal: lr0 times (1 - share done), set before each update. The
    share done is the larger of env-steps over --env-steps and hours over --hours.
  - configs/l1ppo.yaml: the L1 student's run file. It is s64boot.yaml's sim with 20-minute episodes, macros recipe
    (8191), and ntloop's default PPO and reward (lane/ntbc's eroding arms).
- **Held to fastppo.** out/fix_refkl.py (uv inside mcsr-ntwidth, not in the tree) runs ntref.py's learner with
  fastppo's Learner at --ref-kl 0.5. The reference is the fixture's start weights plus noise (0.5 sd on fc.2 and the
  heads), so the KL and its gradient act from step 1 (ref_kl book 2.37). It writes learn-refkl-w1 and learn-refkl-s1
  in ~/.cache/netherite-native. learn_check reads the manifest's ref_kl and ref.ntw. fp32 and bf16 PASS on both, the
  ref_kl book within 2e-5 relative (fp32). The value warm-up's check runs on every fixture: the value head's gradient
  equals the fixture's (fp32 err 2e-7), the policy heads' gradients are exactly 0, and after the update every entry
  outside the head and both moments are bit for bit unchanged. A first w1 fixture (seed 5) missed GAE's tolerance by
  0.3% and bf16's after1 class by conv3's 64-entry bias: the seed dependence learn_check's header documents. It was
  replaced by seed 6.
- **The arms** (64M env-steps from fresh Adam, trainer seeds 1 and 2): today's recipe (the control), then each fix
  alone (ref_kl 1.0, fastppo's pareto value; warm-up 50 updates at 3e-4; anneal), then all three.
  - (a) s64-it42 with configs/s64boot.yaml (lr 5e-6, ent 0.01, the pareto reward and archive).
  - (b) lane/ntbc's L1 student (out/d/L1w1/256.ntw, sha256 23176c5f...) with configs/l1ppo.yaml (lr 3e-4, ent 0.003).

  Scores are train-score, 256 runs x 60 minutes from spawn, eval seeds 1000 and 1001. The table gives the pooled
  mean (the two eval seeds in brackets); one score's SE is 0.07 to 0.10 for L1 and 0.12 to 0.14 for s64.

  | arm | s64-it42, seed 1 | seed 2 | L1, seed 1 | seed 2 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | the start (frozen) | 4.73 (4.76, 4.70) | | 3.46 (3.44, 3.48) | |
  | control | 4.23 (4.38, 4.08) | 4.60 (4.51, 4.68) | 0.00 (0.00, 0.00) | 0.37 (0.33, 0.40) |
  | ref_kl 1.0 | 4.78 (4.87, 4.68) | 4.80 (4.78, 4.82) | 3.54 (3.50, 3.59) | 3.56 (3.55, 3.57) |
  | value warm-up | 4.90 (4.92, 4.88) | 4.56 (4.52, 4.60) | 1.19 (1.18, 1.20) | 0.27 (0.22, 0.32) |
  | anneal | 4.65 (4.57, 4.72) | 4.75 (4.70, 4.80) | 1.65 (1.62, 1.67) | 2.19 (2.15, 2.22) |
  | all three | 4.75 (4.69, 4.81) | 4.73 (4.79, 4.68) | 3.65 (3.74, 3.56) | 3.62 (3.68, 3.57) |

  - The L1 student: only the anchor holds. The control, the warm-up and anneal collapse its entropy from about 10.5

    model at this rate does not separate them at 64M.

- **250M of the combination on the L1 student** (trainer seed 1, the anneal over 250M, a checkpoint every 3 minutes;
  250M env-steps in 1,770 s, 141k env-steps/s). Pooled depth by env-steps: 22M 3.37, 58M 3.51, 87M 3.45, 114M 3.44,

- **Cross-check, the 3090 against the GPU host:** s64-it42 scored 4.81 and 4.71 on the 3090 against 4.76 and 4.70,

- **Gates** (a fresh worktree of 1059ed8d, the recordings linked): GATES-ENV PASS (13 of 13: the eight pinned
