## 2026-11-01 The hotbar as the policy's own action (NT_HOTBAR, .hb builds): a student without the strip macro and the mine lock reaches the stone pickaxe (30.9% and 25.8% of episodes at 64M env-steps against 0.4% and 2.7% without the head), depth 1.18 and 1.37 against 0.86 and 0.93, 1.73 at 256M against 0.98; at L1 level (3.08, 3.35 against 2.85, 3.37) (lane/nthotbar)

lane/ntbc's L2 student (no strip, no mine lock) learned to mine wood and never passed it: the mine lock's tool pick
was the one act its 16-wide action had no key for. This lane gives the policy the hotbar.

- **NT_HOTBAR** (net.h, default 0; build word `.hb`, `make -C csrc/runtime train-loop-v NT_V=s1.hb`): a 10-way head
  (keep, slot 1 to 9), the blob's last two tensors hot_w [10][D] and hot_b [10]; NT_ACTION 17. The actor draws it by
  Gumbel-max on lanes 16..25 of the keys' warp from its own Philox elements (96..105, so the camera's and keys' draws
  are the default's), logp ((cam0 + cam1) + keys) + hot; the learner's k_loss adds its log-softmax, entropy and
  gradient (the heads one [107][D] matrix, the heads' row stride 112). The fused actor (NTA_FUSE) and learner MLP
  (NTL_FC) are off in a .hb build.
- **The vector env**: `NWRL_VEC_HOTBAR` (65536) is a bit of nwrl_vec_opts.macros, not a new field (mcsr's ctypes
  mirror of the opts would read past its end). With it bufs.actions is [n][17] and the last element 1..9 presses that
  number key on a step no macro drives; `nwrl_vec_action_width()` lets ntloop refuse a library of the wrong width.
- **Labels**: nwrl_vec_label gains `hotbar`; a removed macro's slot change is now the student's label (the teacher's
  own steps label keep). distill.jsonl adds ce_hot, acc_hot, switch, acc_switch and a `hotlab` census. A teacher
  without the head is widened with one that always keeps (weights 0, keep bias 0, slots -1e4): its actions unchanged.
  `--hot-weight W` scales the gradient on slot-change labels (default 1). ntinit's `--from BASE.ntw` adds the head to
  a net that lacks it (weights x0.01, keep bias 4: 86% keep).
- **The reference**: mcsr-speedrun branch nthotbar (af41920), scripts/ntref.py `fresh:...,hot=1` (Small plus the
  head; the Learner's term). Fixtures actor-fresh-{w1,s1}.hb and learn-fresh-{w1,s1}.hb in ~/.cache/netherite-native;
  train-width-check runs them (43 checks, 10 new). learn-fresh-w1.hb is from model seed 2: seed 0's failed
  element-wise through one fc2 unit sitting on relu's kink (kept as learn-fresh-w1.hb-relu174).
- **Bugs found in the new code**: a warp sum inside `hl ? ... : 0` (k_loss, k_bc's --soft target) deadlocked the warp
  (lanes 10..31 skipped a full-mask shuffle); the device uniform reaches 1.0f once in 2^24 elements and -log(-log 1)
  is +inf, so the teacher (slots at -1e4) switched twice in 4M steps: the hotbar's uniforms are clamped under 1. **The
  camera heads have the same corner** (about 5e-6 forced bins a step), left because the fix moves every pinned digest.
- **Results** (the GPU host's GPU 2, shared; ntbc's recipe: s64-it42 at L0 teaching, 256 envs, hard labels, a 7M
  env-step eval at the level, seed 7; ntbc's columns its own runs, "no head s2" run here on the default build):

  | L2 depth  | head s1 | head s2 | no head s1 (ntbc) | no head s2 | head, --hot-weight 30, s1 |
  |----------:|--------:|--------:|------------------:|-----------:|--------------------------:|
  | 4M        | 0.59    | 0.00    | 0.62              | 0.35       | 0.16                      |
  | 16M       | 1.04    | 1.14    | 0.68              | 0.76       | 0.39                      |
  | 64M       | 1.18    | 1.37    | 0.86              | 0.93       | 1.03                      |
  | 256M      | 1.73    |         | 0.98              |            |                           |

  Stone pickaxe at 64M 30.9% and 25.8% with the head, 0.4% and 2.7% without; at 256M 48.8% (0), iron pickaxe 4.7%.
  L1 at 64M: 3.08 and 3.35 with the head against ntbc's 2.85 and 3.37 (means 3.21, 3.11: inside the seed spread). The
  slot-change labels are 3 in 10,000 decisions; the student's argmax on them is right 0 to 4% through 64M (27% at
  256M), so it switches by sampling. --hot-weight 30 (one seed) learns them sooner (31% at 64M) but makes false
  switches (keep accuracy 99.89% against 99.97%) and lost depth (1.03 against 1.18): the default stays 1.
- **Default unchanged**: in a fresh worktree at the lane's last code commit GATES-ENV PASS (13 gates: the eight pinned
  digests, train-loop-check, native-test, pool-gate 133,280 rows, raycast-gate 31,660) and TRAIN-WIDTH-CHECK PASS;
  against the base commit's build, actor and distillation trajectory digests equal (aaf616ed9c902c2f) and
  learn_check's printout byte-equal in fp32 and bf16.
- **Found outside the lane**: mcsr-speedrun's VecBufs ends at `mask`, and lane/ntbc's `label` made the C struct one
  pointer longer: nwrl_vec_buffers (`*b = v->b`) writes 8 bytes past a Python caller's ctypes object. The fix is one
  field in mcsr/vecenv.py.

Next: L2 with the head to 1B env-steps on two seeds (it climbs: 1.28 at 64M, 1.73 at 256M, against L1's 3.59; the
rest of what the mine lock did, its aim and persistence, is the likely rest of the gap, not measured here); PPO on top once ntbc's collapse is fixed, now that the policy can act on the slot.

## 2026-11-01 A minGRU in the native trainer (net.h NT_RNN): actor and learner held to fastppo's Small(gru=1) in fp32 and bf16, 1 to 3% of the trainer's env-steps/s; at the feed-forward recipe four of six seeds collapse (lane/ntgru)

Elliot, 2026-11-01: the route steps the policy down to lower macro levels and the raw keyboard and mouse, where the
policy needs memory; the only Pareto arm past the 0.46M net had an LSTM. minGRU (Feng et al. 2024): both gates from
the input alone, so T steps train as one GEMM and an elementwise scan. Base 1eae76cc. out/report.md has every table.

- **The net** (net.h NT_RNN 1, default 0): after fc2, not in its place: G = rnn(z2) [2D], h' = h + sigmoid(G_z) (G_h -
  h), the heads read z2 + h'. The feed-forward net stays a sub-function: at a fresh start the candidate's half is zero,
  h stays 0 and the net is NT_RNN 0's to the bit on the shared tensors (ntref.py's rnn=1 draws every other layer as
  without it), so the two arms differ by the layer alone; replacing fc2 would change the trunk too. Its two tensors go
  last in the blob and the learner's layout. Variants V.r1 (w1.r1, s1.r1; actor.mk's nt_vrnn).
- **The state.** Each env's state [n][D] fp32 on the device (loop.c's hst), stepped in place by the actor; an episode
  start (the last action's truncation, the step's first flag) zeroes it before the step. A segment stores the state at
  its start, already zeroed where its first step starts an episode (nt_rnn_h0), not every step's: the learner's scan
  recomputes the rest from it with the update's weights, as fastppo's Learner does for its LSTM (D floats an env a
  segment, against T D); first[t] is done[t-1] of the segment itself. PPO's minibatches are whole env columns: the
  loop shuffles envs, not samples (mb / T envs a minibatch, mb rounded to a multiple of T, ntl_cols's T-major order),
  and ntl_seq hands the learner the segment's start states and ends. ntloop --check-actor refuses NT_RNN (its fixture
  has no state; actor_check's recurrent mode covers the actor).
- **Kernels.** Learner (train/rnn.cuh; learn.cu gets one include and three dispatch lines, its convolutions and fc
  code untouched): the gates' GEMM over the minibatch (cuBLAS, G in the 16-bit type as fastppo's autocast rounds it),
  the scan (a thread a column and unit over its T steps, keeping each step's state in fp32), its reverse (dG and the
  carry dh (1 - g), cut at an episode start, each column's bias gradient summed in fp32 on the way, the columns in
  order after), the weight's GEMM, and dG W added into d2 by the GEMM's beta before fc2's relu'. Actor
  (train/rnn_actor.cuh): the gates' GEMM with the state update in its epilogue, one kernel: 8 samples and 32 units a
  block, 8 k-slices of a warp each, the slices' partials summed in order in shared memory.
- **The reference** (mcsr branch ntgru, worktree ~/dev/mcsr-ntgru): fastppo.Small(gru=1) and the Learner's recurrent
  paths on any Small.H; ntref.py MODEL fresh:...,rnn=1[,hzero=0]: the recurrent actor fixture (8 steps of 512 envs
  from a random state, about 10% first flags, the final state) and the learner fixtures (the start states, env orders).
- **Checks** (train-width-check runs NT_RVARIANTS w1.r1 s1.r1 beside the 30 feed-forward checks; TRAIN-WIDTH-CHECK
  PASS). Actor, fp32: the state after 8 steps max|d| 3.7e-8 (w1.r1) and 3.0e-8 (s1.r1), 0 of 4,096 actions differ;
  bf16: the state normwise 2.07e-3 against fastppo's own bf16 2.78e-3 (w1.r1), 1.55e-3 against 2.43e-3 (s1.r1).
  Learner: fp32 and bf16 PASS on learn-fresh-{w1,s1}.r1 and their -s1 fixtures. Two bounds moved in learn_check: the
  pg book's floor is 1e-3 of pg's absolute mass (2e-7 relative logp noise moves pg by up to 9.5e-8 on a book of 1e-4;
  an f64 recompute showed it), and a bf16 tensor where fastppo's own bf16 equals its fp32 exactly (s1.r1's v.bias
  after Adam's +-lr steps) is held to the fp32 gate's normwise 2e-3.
- **Speed** (the 3090, abrun 3 rounds alternating, bf16). learn_bench an update (8,192 samples, 3 epochs): w1 4.506 ms
  feed-forward, 5.396 recurrent (+19.8%; the first learner 5.520), s1 25.78 and 26.66 (+3.4%; first 26.79), spreads
  under 0.4%, apart. nsys on the first learner: the layer's 1.0 ms an update was its three GEMMs 0.53, the reverse scan
  0.22 and the scan 0.17; the three cuts (G in 16 bits, the bias in the scan, d2 by beta) took 0.12 ms of it. Scans
  chunked over T (8 steps a thread block's pass, NTR_CH) measured level (5.475 against 5.474 ms) and were dropped.
  actor_bench, a group of 128 a call: w1 32.74 us feed-forward, 41.15 recurrent (the first kernel, one thread a unit
  over all k, 57.76), s1 98.89 and 108.7 (144.8). Trainer env-steps/s (ntloop --policy actor, learner on, 4 groups,
  100 warm and 1,000 steps; the k-sliced actor, the first learner): w1 at 512 envs 228,254 against 223,290 (-2.2%,
  overlap: spreads 3.6 and 2.2%), s1 at 256 envs 135,417 against 131,152 (-3.2%, apart: spreads 0.2 and 0.8%); with
  the final learner, w1 in longer runs (300 warm, 4,000 steps, 5 rounds) 275,257 against 271,473 (-1.4%, overlap:
  spreads 5.2 and 7.0%), s1 132,258 against 130,252 (-1.5%, overlap: 1.9 and 2.4%). The layer costs 1 to 3% of
  env-steps/s at both sizes. The learner's scan is not fused into its GEMM: the scan is 0.17 ms of a 5.40 ms w1
  update, so a fused kernel saves at most that and G's round trip (a projection, not measured: under 1% of the
  trainer's step); the actor's is fused (the layer adds 8.4 us to a 32.7 us w1 call).
- **Learning** (the GPU host's GPU 2: brute16 at 16x16, fast fidelity, the milestone archive off, 512 envs, 28M
  env-steps a run, trainer seeds 1 to 6 an arm, run one at a time interleaved; both arms from the same function; the
  frozen eval: vanilla fidelity, seed 1000, 1,024 episodes). The arms are not inside each other's spread. Feed-forward:
  returns 27.72, 28.52, 28.31, 27.88, 23.37, 27.49 (mean 27.22), the stone pickaxe in 0.5, 5.1, 3.9, 10.4, 4.2, 5.5%
  of episodes (mean 4.93), the wooden pickaxe in 94.5 to 100%. minGRU: returns 29.79, 0.40, 27.00, 0.06, 0.35, 0.15
  (mean 9.63), stone 2.3, 0, 4.3, 0, 0, 0% (mean 1.10): four of six seeds collapsed (the wooden pickaxe in 0 to 0.1%;
  Fisher exact against 0 of 6: p 0.03 one-sided, 0.06 two-sided), the two that did not land inside the feed-forward
  range. Return SEs 0.2 to 0.35 an eval, stone 0.2 to 1.0 points. Every run dips after a few million env-steps (return
  4.6 at random to under 1); the feed-forward runs climb back with entropy near 7 to 8 (one at 1.1), the collapsed
  minGRU runs lose it to 0.002 to 0.5 and settle on a policy that neither acts nor dies (seed 4 at 13.7M: deaths 0,
  the no-macro share 0.94). Not a state bug: the trained models under PPO at lr 0 (frozen weights, 1.5M env-steps on
  the 3090: kl and clipfrac are the actor against the learner alone) give kl 4e-7 to 1.4e-5 in bf16 for both nets,
  1e-10 to 3e-9 in fp32, clipfrac 0. So the minGRU does not train reliably at the feed-forward recipe (lr 3e-4, ent
  0.003); the levers next, each over the same six seeds: the recurrent layer's own lr, the gate's bias started
  negative, ent for the recurrent arm, a bounded candidate (h~ = W_h z2 + b_h is unbounded today and the heads read
  z2 + h).
- **Gates**, in this tree and a fresh worktree of 01b1a050 (master's recordings linked, every build from the caches):
  train-width-check PASS (default and recurrent variants), GATES-ENV PASS (the eight digest pins as pinned, pool-gate
  133,280 rows, raycast-gate 31,660 rows, livguard, native-test, train-loop-check PASS in 154 s). The default build's
  learner and actor include rnn.cuh and rnn_actor.cuh only as stubs (NT_RNN 0).

## 2026-11-01 Distillation to fewer macros in ntloop (--teacher): the s64 teacher's strip mine learned from its acts, a 256M-step student without the strip macro at depth 3.59 against the teacher's own net's 2.97 there (78% of the teacher with every macro, 4.61), still climbing with data but bending; without the mine lock too the 16-wide action cannot pick a tool and no student passes the wooden pickaxe; PPO on top at ntloop's defaults collapses the student, as it degrades the teacher (lane/ntbc)

GOAL.md's route (Elliot, 2026-10-29): a policy with high-level macros makes data whose action-level labels come free,
and a model learns to act from it at a lower macro level. The teacher is mcsr pareto's s64 iteration 42 (64x64 RGB,
stem, wm 1), exported to net.h's blob; every number below is this tree's own 20-minute eval from spawn (256 envs, one
episode each, ntloop --policy actor --learn 0, eval seed 7 unless said), on the GPU host's shared card (its env-steps/s
are not speeds). The teacher scores higher here than in the python eval of Oct 19 (4.73 against 3.41 at 20 minutes:
the macros have improved since that library), so every comparison is inside this eval.

- **The path** (csrc/runtime/train/distill.{h,cu}; one hook each in loop.c, learn.cu's ntl_grad and vecenv.c's
  vec_act; `ntloop --teacher T.ntw --init S.ntw --level L [--soft 1] [--beta B]`): the teacher is the actor at the
  env's macros, the learner the student. vecenv.c labels every decision step with the act the engine stepped in the
  16-wide action (vecenv.h struct nwrl_vec_label: the nearest of the 41 mu-law bins to the look's change, an absolute
  look less the yaw and pitch the act was made from; the keys from the holds; the macro that drove it by its switch,
  strip, seek, fight and hunt told apart from the mine lock; flags for GUI ops, a hotbar change, a press without a
  hold). A step the policy drove, or that started a macro the student keeps (Macros.chosen), is labelled with the
  teacher's action; a step a kept macro drove is masked; a step a removed macro drove is labelled with its act. The
  loss (k_bc, through a new ntl_hyper.loss hook: PPO's kernel otherwise) is cross-entropy on both camera bins and the
  keys over the labelled steps plus the value's squared error to the teacher's value. The student's scalars are
  rewritten from the labels: the previous macro kind only for a kept macro, the previous bins and keys what the
  student would have sent. Held by a check on every policy-driven step (the rewrite against the env's own fields):
  97.7M steps over the L1 wm 1 chain, 0 different. A teacher narrower than the build is widened exactly (zero
  channels): the s1 and s2 builds drive the same fp32 trajectory digest, 317a27958af760ec.
- **What the action cannot say** (the census over 48M teacher steps at every macro): macros drove 61.4% of the steps
  (strip 34.9%, mine lock 12.6%, craft 9.2%, seek 3.9%). Of those 29.5M macro steps 78.7% are exactly the action's
  bins and keys; 19.9% look between two bins and go to the nearest (mean miss 0.23 degrees on the strip's, 0.38 on
  the mine lock's; 0.48% of all macro steps are past half a bin's gap); 0.75% have GUI ops (masked: craft's and the screen's, macros
  every level keeps); 0.48% change the hotbar (dropped from the label: no key of the 14 selects a slot); 0.21% press
  a key without holding it. On the macros that move (mine, strip, seek, surface) a hotbar change is 0.07%: rare, and
  the one step a student without the mine lock cannot do.
- **Levels** (switch bits): L0 16383 the teacher's (the recipe and strip), L1 8191 without strip, L2 8187 without
  strip and the mine lock. The teacher's own net at each: L0 4.73 and 4.50 (eval seeds 7, 8), L1 2.92 and 3.02, L2
  0.08 (8% reach a wooden pickaxe).
- **The scaling curve** (depth, milestones an episode of 13; hard labels; out/report.md has every milestone):

  | env-steps | L1 wm 1, seed 1 | L1 wm 1, seed 2 | L1 wm 2 | L2 wm 1 |
  |----------:|----------------:|----------------:|--------:|--------:|
  | 4M        | 0.96            | 0.64            | 0.75    | 0.62    |
  | 16M       | 1.88            | 1.15            | 1.83    | 0.68    |
  | 64M       | 2.85            | 3.37            | 3.35    | 0.86    |
  | 256M      | 3.66 (3.52 at eval seed 8) | 3.51 | 3.54    | 0.98    |

  Two training seeds at L1 wm 1 differ by up to 0.73 at 16M and 0.52 at 64M (the eval itself by 0.14 between eval
  seeds), so wm 2's 64M lead (3.35 against a 3.11 mean) is inside one run's spread and at 256M the widths are level:
  data, not capacity, moved the student over these points. At 256M the wm 1 student (3.59 over two seeds) passes
  the teacher's own net at L1 (2.97 over two eval seeds) by 0.62 and reaches 78% of the teacher with every macro
  (4.61); each milestone as means of the two runs (the teacher's of its two eval seeds at L1, then at L0): stone
  pickaxe 92% (92%, 92%), iron ingot 54% (34%, 68%), iron pickaxe 36% (24%, 50%), bucket 12% (4%, 28%), flint and
  steel 3% (0%, 39%). The last 4x of data bought 0.48 against 1.59 for the one before: the curve is bending. At L2 the student learns to mine without the lock (a wooden pickaxe in 98% of
  episodes at 256M, the teacher's own net there 8%) and never passes it (stone pickaxe 0 at every point): stone needs
  the pickaxe in hand, and the mine lock's tool pick is the one act the action has no key for.
- **Soft targets** (--soft 1: the teacher's forward on the minibatch, its softmax and sigmoids the target where its
  action is the label; seed 1): 1.12, 1.02, 2.62, 3.04 at 4, 16, 64, 256M against hard's two-run means 0.80, 1.52,
  3.11, 3.59: no gain (at 256M 0.55 under, below both hard runs), so the default stays hard.
- **DAgger** (--beta B: the student a second actor driving that share of the episodes, the teacher labelling every
  state, the macros still the teacher's) is built and checked (the rewrite check 0 different at beta 0.25 and 0.5)
  and not yet measured.
- **PPO on top** (part 4; L1, 64M env-steps, fresh Adam, ntloop's defaults: lr 3e-4, ent 0.003, clip 0.2, 3 epochs
  of 8192): from the 256M student (frozen 3.59) seed 1 0.00 (its entropy 6.4 to 0.23, the training episodes' stone
  pickaxe 89% to 47%), seed 2 2.18, at lr 5e-5 1.73. The control, the teacher's own net at L1 under the same PPO:
  2.92 frozen to 1.53 (stone pickaxe in training 89% to 30% at 20M, back to 86% at 64M). The recipe degrades even
  a policy PPO trained, so this is no verdict on the distilled start: PPO at a new level needs a value warm-up and
  an anchor to the start (ppo.ref_kl) first.
- **Gates**: GATES-ENV PASS in a fresh worktree of eba478df (master merged; the eight pinned digests, pool-gate 40
  recordings 133,280 rows, raycast-gate 31,660 rows, train-loop-check, livguard, native-test), and before the merge
  at aa473a0a; the label's work in vec_act moves no digest.

Next: the L2 wall is the action space, not the data: a hotbar head (or the mine lock's tool pick kept as its own
small macro) before L2 can be learned; DAgger at L1 against the hard-label curve at the same env-steps; PPO from the
student with a value warm-up and a KL to the student (ppo.ref_kl, refused as not implemented today) once ntloop's PPO
holds the teacher itself at L1.

## 2026-11-01 The repo for a PufferLib-style run: netherite train, score and replay on the native trainer, a fresh clone trains from setup alone, the front page, configs/ swept (lane/polish)

Elliot, 2026-11-01: "a polished Netherite repo", "get this ready for a pufferlib style huge run with all our macros",
and "Tools, not scripts". Base bd576cca.

- **The CLI is the way in, no Python on it** (csrc/cli/netherite.c). `netherite train RUN.yaml [NTLOOP ARGS]` runs
  `make -C csrc/runtime train-prep RUN=...`, then `out/runtime/train/[s1/]ntloop --run RUN.yaml --out
  out/train/NAME-DATE-TIME`, with the build picked by the run file's observation (16x16 the default, 64x64 s1) and
  ntloop's flags after it. Without `--init` it starts from a fresh net (below). The external trainer's directive stays
  only behind `--trainer DIR`. `demo` is gone (replay is the demo). `netherite score RUN.yaml W.ntw [RUNS MIN SEED]`
  is lane/ntboot's `make train-score`. `netherite replay EPISODES.nrec EPISODE [--every N] [--force]` turns
  out/demo/jr.sh and cmp.py's recipe into a tool. It runs `ntrec tape` (the script and the world), the oracle's
  `make script` on that world with client.gamma 1.0 (frames only) and frames every N ticks, then `ntrec end` (new,
  below), then ffmpeg's mp4 at 30 frames a second, all into out/replay/RUN-EPISODE. `netherite help` and each verb's
  `--help` give one line and one example.
- **What a fresh host lacked, now made by the rules.** train-prep (csrc/runtime/train/run.mk) checks for each piece
  and makes it where missing: the trainer, libnwrl, ntrec and ntinit; out/assets (`make -C csrc assets`);
  out/java/render/forest-fast, the cast's atlas (the oracle's render-scenes, which `netherite setup` already ran);
  and the run file's start. A configs/checkpoints.tsv name whose script starts from a fresh world is recorded by the
  oracle: spawn is gold-g1-s42, 684 rows. A scratch clone's recording equals the stored one in all 683 rows past
  the header, s02 chat aside, as gold-chain.sh compares. The trainer's gate configs moved from
  ~/.cache/netherite-native into configs/brute16.yaml and configs/brute16dev.yaml (loop.mk NTCONF, NTCONF_DEV; the
  same keys byte for byte, a new header). The client jar comes from setup's `--mc DIR`: this host has no launcher
  install in ~/.minecraft, so setup needs `--mc` pointed at a launcher-layout directory.
- **A fresh net without Python** (csrc/runtime/train/ntinit.c, out/runtime/train/[V/]ntinit OUT.ntw [SEED]). The
  native trainer refused to run without `--init`, and the only fresh weights came from mcsr's scripts/ntref.py.
  ntinit uses fastppo Small's initialisation: torch's default uniform bounds (1/sqrt(fan_in) for weight and bias),
  then the calm start (the heads' weights times 0.01, the camera's bias -0.5 |bin - 20|, the keys' bias forward 1,
  jump -2, sprint -1, mine -1, hit -3, the rest -4). It draws with splitmix64, so the distribution is torch's but the
  bytes are not. `--stats` prints each tensor's spread. Against ~/.cache/netherite-native/actor-fresh-w1 (ntref.py
  fresh, calm=0), the trunk's bounds agree to the 4th decimal (conv1 0.1443, fc2 0.0625). The heads' weights are 100x
  smaller, which is calm=0 against Small's own start: a fastppo run from scratch starts calm, so ntinit does too.
- **ntrec end FILE I [TAPE]** (recread.c): the record's end (the 40 items it counts) against the Java client's last
  row (sp.inv summed by id). It prints END EQUAL, DIFF or INCOMPLETE; complete means the last row is the last act's
  tick, steps + 1.
- **Proved in a scratch clone** (git clone of lane/polish into ~/dev/nw/.tmp/polish-fresh, `make`, `netherite setup
  --mc DIR`): `netherite train configs/brute16.yaml --hours 0.01` through gpuq built everything and recorded the start
  from nothing. ntinit wrote seed 1's net, and ntloop trained it: 5,916,037 env-steps in 34.17 s (173,142
  env-steps/s, one run beside the other lanes, not a benchmark), 722 updates, model.ntw. The brief's
  `netherite train configs/brute16fast.yaml --hours 0.01`, with lane/envcpu's file copied in untracked before it
  landed, ran 4,689,660 env-steps in 34.72 s (135,075 env-steps/s, the same caveat), 1,280 episodes, model.ntw. After
  merging master at a093d472 (envcpu landed, brute16fast.yaml tracked), the same command from a pulled scratch clone
  ran 3,684,209 env-steps in 34.56 s beside the night's 3-hour run on the 3090, and `netherite score
  configs/brute16fast.yaml` on that model (64 one-minute runs, lane/ntboot 1787d241 merged in a throwaway branch)
  printed TRAIN-SCORE OK, depth 0.156 (0.046). Then `netherite train
  configs/ladder.yaml --init that model.ntw --ns 32 --groups 2 --ep-len 600 --env-steps 40000 --rec on --rec-keep
  all` produced 64 episodes; the first 32 are the make's, at vanilla. `netherite replay ... 9` played env 25's
  episode (it made a wooden pickaxe) on the Java client: END EQUAL (7 planks, 2 sticks, the pickaxe; last row t 601,
  600 acts), 300 frames, a 1.99 MB mp4. The last frame shows the table and the hotbar the record holds. `netherite
  gate --quick` passed: the oracle's gates, then fresh-play-s1, fresh-s42 and break-place-s1. `tools/export.sh --mc
  DIR` passes all 8 checks (tracked, jar, language, decompiled, private, then build, setup and the quick gate in its
  own clean clone). The first run failed language and private on master's text: loop.c's JSON "Infinity", now
  justified in tools/lang_allow.tsv, and 22 DEVLOG lines that used the two machines' names as hosts, now written as
  the dev host and the GPU host. The night's entries will bring the names back unless written that way.
- **score** ran against lane/ntboot merged into the scratch clone (a clean merge). ntboot's `--score` refused any run
  file with starts.archive, which brute, brute16 and brute16fast all have. Relayed to the orchestrator; since ntboot
  7a6693b7 --score drops the file's archive and refuses only a --save-starts flag, and the verb runs on brute16fast.
  Until ntboot lands, `netherite score` stops at make's missing train-score target.
- **README.md** is the front page: what it is, the quickstart (setup, gate, train, score, replay), a run file's keys
  by what they configure (seeds and starts, envs, observation, actions and macros, fidelity, precision, recipe,
  data), and "Measured on one RTX 3090", each number with its DEVLOG entry.
- **configs/**: 37 files at the base. Deleted the five that nothing names: explore, library, speedrun-curriculum,
  speedrun-loot-grpo and speedrun-grpo-logs2. The search covered this tree, DEVLOG's last 10 days and the code of
  every ~/dev/mcsr-* checkout. speedrun-s2 to s17 stay: mcsr/rl/curriculum.py builds their names. Added brute16 and
  brute16dev; 34 now. Every search is in the lane's report.

## 2026-11-01 The learner's MLP, heads and loss as one kernel and the actor's 16x16 step as one kernel, both compile-time variants (off by default): the trainer +2.8 to +3.2% at 16x16 (10 of 10 paired rounds faster) and +1.5 to +1.6% at 64x64 (15 of 15 at 256 and 512 envs), the fused chain's DRAM bytes 44 to 48% fewer, every width check passing once k_fcrow rounds as the per-layer path does; fusing the actor's MLP alone was slower at every size the trainer calls (lane/ntfc)

The brief: chain C (the learner's fc1, fc2, the three heads, the loss and their backward to dz0) and chain G (the actor's
step) in as few kernels as the sizes allow, against today's cuBLAS path. Base 1eae76cc; every GPU number in gpuq
windows on the 3090 beside other lanes' and the nightly's co-tenants (comparisons interleaved in one window). The GPU
host's cards were taken by another project all night: no sm_120 numbers. out/report.md has every table.

- **Where chain C stood** (nsys on learn_bench, bf16, one minibatch of 8192): k_flat to k_unflat is 27 kernels, 406 us
  of 1,542 at w1 (26%), 703 of about 8,580 at s1 (8%), 896 of about 4,290 at w2 (21%). Its FLOPs are 0.14 to 0.5 ms of
  the 71 TFLOPS roof; the rest was launches, k_flat/k_unflat/bias/relu passes over z0 (19 MB at s1) and small GEMMs.
- **k_fcrow** (train/fc.cuh, `NTL_FC 1`; the variant word `.fc`: `make -C csrc/runtime train-learn-v NT_V=s1.fc`):
  FC_BM samples of a minibatch from x3 to dx3 in one block, every activation in shared memory: z0 gathered from
  relu(x3 + b3) and the scalars (k_flat's job) in chunks of 64 columns, fc1, fc2, the heads, k_loss's arithmetic a warp
  a sample, dH (times NT_LSCALE), d2 = dH Wh relu'(z2), d1 = d2 W2 relu'(z1), dz0 = d1 W1 written as dx3 times relu'(x3
  + b3) (k_unflat's). z0 is channels last (x3's own layout: 16-byte loads), fc1's weights permuted to match and
  k_gunperm takes fc1's gradient back (its new zp argument). Every product is prec.cuh's mma16816 (so every NT_MMA mode
  builds) with A by ldmatrix and B from fragment-packed 16-bit weight copies (k_fcpack each minibatch, 0.8 to 3 M
  halves, L2-resident; one 16-byte load a lane a 16x16 tile, 4 k-steps in flight, the ring carried across fc1's
  chunks). relu'(z1) and relu'(x3 + b3) are kept as bits. The weights' gradients stay cuBLAS (three GEMMs on the z0,
  z1, z2, dH, d2, d1 it writes); the biases' are its column sums a block, summed in block order by k_fcfin
  (deterministic). k_nm, k_books and the loss scale as before. Off past D 512 (wm 4, 8: the rows do not fit 99 KB).
- **How it got there** (learn_bench ms an update, abrun 3 rounds a window, all apart unless said): the first version
  (64 rows, 8 warps) 4.50 to 4.33 at w1, 25.55 to 25.41 at s1, w2 overlap; ncu on it: 35% long scoreboard (dz0's
  epilogue read x3 from global per element, fc1's gather converted each load right after issuing it), 31% tensor math,
  occupancy 16.7%. Loads issued a chunk ahead and converted after the products, relu'(x3) as bits: 4.31 (w1), 25.41
  (s1), 12.82 to 12.61 (w2). 16 warps in two row groups (`.fc16`): 4.20, 25.31. 32 rows a block, two blocks an SM
  (the default now; `.bm64`/`.fc16` keep the others): w1 4.524 to 4.126 (-8.8%), s1 at the trainer's 256-env
  minibatch of 4,096 (`learn_bench --mb 4096`, new) 26.69 to 26.12 (-2.1%), at 8,192 25.29 against 25.34 for `.fc16`.
- **DRAM bytes** (ncu, L2 flushed before each kernel, the first minibatch's chain C): w1 140.6 to 73.1 MB (27 to 11
  kernels), s1 235.0 to 128.8 MB (26 to 10), w2 284.2 to 159.0 MB; ncu's serialized time 420 to 268 us, 699 to 508,
  898 to 827.
- **k_afused** (train/actorfused.cuh, `NTA_FUSE 1`, `.af`; 16x16 wm 1 only, elsewhere the per-layer actor): the whole
  bf16 step for 8, 4 or 2 samples a block (by the call's size: 128 samples fill 64 SMs) from the cast's bytes to the
  draw: conv1's A fragments built in registers from the bytes, conv2 and conv3 by ldmatrix over unpadded swizzled maps
  in shared memory, fc1, fc2 and the heads as k_fcrow's products, heads_draw's sampler. The device RNG's counter:
  every block reads it and draws at counter + 1, the last block (a ticket in the workspace's rng[2]) stores it, so the
  noise is the per-layer path's. actor_bench, bf16, graph replay median: B 512 80.9 to 43.0 us (0.53x), B 128 (the
  trainer's group at 512 envs) 36.9 to 33.9 (-8%; 41.0 with 8 samples a block, 16 SMs busy). fc1, fc2, the heads and
  the draw alone after the per-layer convolutions (16 samples a block, every variant) was slower at every size the
  trainer calls (s1 B 64 65.5 to 79.9 us, B 128 100.4 to 110.6; w1 B 128 36.9 to 42.0): 4 to 8 blocks carry the whole
  MLP where the per-layer GEMMs spread N over the SMs. Dropped. The 64x64 convolutions were not fused.
- **The trainer** (ntloop, the learner on, device cast served, 4 groups, 32 threads, 2,000 group steps after 200,
  abrun in bench windows; medians, paired by round): 16x16 at 512 envs, two windows: 324,367 (per-layer) against
  333,737 (`.fc16.af`, +2.9%, apart), and 319,630 against 328,568 (`.fc.af`, +2.8%, overlap; `.af` alone +2.4%,
  overlap); the fused build faster in all 7 paired rounds (+1.6 to +4.1%). 64x64 s1 at 256 envs: 147,063 against
  150,162 (`.fc16`, +2.1%, overlap), 147,892 against 150,135 (`.fc`, +1.5%, overlap), faster in all 7 paired rounds
  (+0.5 to +2.7%); at 512 envs 152,896 against 155,241 (`.fc16`, +1.5%, apart) and 152,928 against 155,354 (`.fc`,
  +1.6%, apart). Those builds rounded fc1 and fc2 once (Quality below); after the fix, one window each, 3 rounds: 16x16
  at 512 envs 321,712 against 331,986 (`.fc.af`, +3.2%, apart, spreads 1.4% and 1.8%), 64x64 at 256 envs 148,028
  against 150,361 (`.fc`, +1.6%, apart, spreads 0.3% and 2.0%), the fused build faster in every round. (A first try at
  those two windows ran beside this lane's own fresh-worktree gates, load 21 to 42, per-layer runs 122k to 234k:
  discarded.) The defaults are unchanged (the brief); turning `.fc` (and `.af` at 16x16) on is the next step.
- **Quality.** train-width-check NT_WFUSE=.fc.af first failed 1 of 33: a05-learn-bf16 (round 10's trained weights),
  conv.0's gradient 1.48x fastppo's own bf16 error (the class bound 1.25x; the per-layer path 0.86x), on every k_fcrow
  shape. A debug build comparing k_fcrow's z1, z2, dH, d2, d1 and dx3 with the per-layer path's on that fixture
  (out/l/fcdbg.patch, not committed): z1 and z2 differed by 0.3% (bf16 rounding) and rows near the PPO clip's edges
  took the other side (a row's keys gradient changed sign), and those rows carry the convolutions' gradients. k_fcrow
  rounded fc1's and fc2's sum plus bias once; the per-layer path rounds the GEMM's sum to bf16, then adds the bias and
  rounds again. Rounding as it does (now the default; `-DFC_RND1` keeps the single rounding) makes z1 differ in 5 of
  2,097,152 entries, dH in none, and a05 passes at 0.86x. train-width-check NT_WFUSE=.fc.af: 33 of 33 PASS, each
  learner fixture's worst bf16 gradient error equal to the default build's to three digits (w1 3.99e-2, s1 3.56e-2, w2
  1.93e-2, s2 4.61e-2, a05 1.28e-1; w4 and w8 build the per-layer path). The extra rounding costs nothing measurable:
  learn_bench at mb 8192, 3 rounds, w1 4.508 to 4.107 ms (-8.9%, apart), s1 25.66 to 25.20 (-1.8%, apart). The fp32
  path is untouched. actor_check passes on `.af` (bf16 normwise camera
  2.1e-5, value 6.2e-3 against fastppo's own bf16 7.3e-3); its new bf16 device-RNG check (a seed repeats, the next call
  draws anew, the seed's draws fp32's but at near ties) passes on both paths with 4,095 of 4,096 samples equal.
- **Gates** (a fresh worktree of the branch at 52542846, the defaults): gates-env PASS (13 gates, train-loop-check
  among them), train-width-check PASS (33 of 33); and in the lane, train-width-check NT_WFUSE=.fc.af 33 of 33.
- **Not done.** sm_120: the GPU host's cards were another project's all night. The 64x64 actor's convolutions were not fused
  (the MLP alone lost, so a fused 64x64 actor would have to win on the convolutions). k_fcrow runs at about half the
  tensor roof (fc1's chunk barriers, B fragments arriving late; more prefetch needs registers or shared memory it lacks
  at two blocks an SM).
## 2026-11-01 s64-it42 in the native trainer: it plays as well as fastppo scores it on today's env (depth 4.51 to 4.82 natively, 4.76 and 4.83 in fastppo's scorer); the frozen eval and its sweep as make targets; every native fine-tune from it lost iron pickaxe within 10 to 40M env-steps, as fastppo's own did, so the big run is its episodes as data; SPEC 6c 1 of 3 seeds inside fastppo's (lane/ntboot)

The night's big run starts from the best model measured, mcsr pareto's s64 iteration 42 (fastppo Small, 64x64 RGB through
the stem, wm 1: net.h's s1 variant). Exported by `ntref.py export` to ~/.cache/netherite-native/models/s64-it42.ntw.
Scores are 60 minutes from seed 42's spawn with the strip, 512 runs; out/report.md has every table.

- **Natively as in fastppo.** ntloop --score at eval seeds 1000, 1001 and 1002 gave depth 4.82, 4.57 and 4.51 (SE
  0.09 each), iron pickaxe 54.9, 51.8 and 50.4%, deaths 0.30, 0.27 and 0.31. fastppo's own scorer (fromspawn.py) on
  this tree's libnwrl, 2 x 256 runs, gave 4.76 and 4.83 (iron pickaxe 59.0 and 54.7%). Both sit far above DEVLOG "The
  frontier"'s 3.39 (31% iron pickaxe): that gap is the env's macro work since 2026-10-19 (lane/flint, stripsafe,
  lavaesc, craftfix, the strip from a stall), not the native macros API, observation or sampler. The eval's own
  spread is wider than one score's SE: one model's eval seeds moved depth by 0.31. Rank on pooled seeds, and on iron
  pickaxe, which moved 4.5 points.
- **The eval as a tool.** `make -C csrc/runtime train-score RUN=FILE W=W.ntw [V=s1] [RUNS MIN SEED CLOCK]` (ntloop
  --score) prints fromspawn's table and a JSON line: 512 x 60 min in 141 s on the 3090 (260.7k env-steps/s).
  `train-score-sweep WS="..." | WDIR=DIR [SEEDS="1000 1001"]` scores several models at several seeds, one table, seeds
  pooled; WDIR takes a run's --save-every checkpoints. --score drops the run file's starts.archive (lane/polish's
  `netherite score` on brute16fast.yaml needed it) and refuses only a --save-starts flag.
- **The reward.** The first fine-tune arms ran on ntloop's default reward (every milestone 1, logs uncapped): the
  first s64boot.yaml carried none of the pareto recipe's. ntloop now takes fastppo's --values, --caps and --nether
  beside --log-cap and --ms-weights, and the run file's policy.reward.log_cap, ms_weights, values, caps and nether
  (pairs NAME/W: the grammar holds no '='). configs/s64boot.yaml carries mcsr runs/pareto/recipe's reward and its

## 2026-11-01 The 64x64 learner's stem and conv1 in two kernels that keep h0 and dx0 on chip (NTL_S1B, NTL_S1F; off by default): the stem path's DRAM traffic 2.31 GB to 0.48 GB a minibatch, the learner's update 24% faster in bf16 and 35% with fp16 accumulation, every error the same to four digits; the 64x64 trainer +0.8 to 1.6% (inside its noise: it waits on the env now); FLOPs at fp32 accumulation are not free (lane/ntbytes)

Elliot, 2026-11-01: "FP16 inputs, FP32 accumulate, and potentially FP16 outputs or even FP32 outputs ... double the
memory throughput." The learner already stored 16-bit in and out with FP32 accumulation, so the brief was the bytes
left, at s1 (64x64 with the stem, where the trainer was learner-bound). Base e3605a36, master merged at 1eae76cc
(lane/nth16's acc4 and NT_MMA). The 3090 had co-tenants all lane (the nightly's tick_batch and render_check, other
lanes' windows); one kernel's nsys time swung 906 to 1,805 us. So the kernel numbers are ncu's (each kernel replayed
alone, caches flushed) and every A/B is abrun's interleaved rounds. out/report.md has every table.

- **Where the bytes were** (ncu, every kernel of one update, a minibatch of 8192): 8,806 us and 5.14 GB of DRAM traffic.
  The stem path took 4,009 us and 2.31 GB: k_stem_mma, conv1's k_igemm over h0, its k_cwgrad, k_c1dx, k_stem_dw_mma and
  their sums. h0 (relu of the stem, 268 MB) went to DRAM once and was read back three times; dx0 (268 MB) went out and
  back once.
- **k_s1b (NTL_S1B)**: conv1's whole backward and the stem's gradients in one kernel, a sample at a time in shared
  memory (87 KB, a block of 16 warps an SM):
  - h0 recomputed from the bytes by s1_stem, k_stem_mma's tiles and arithmetic, so the same bits;
  - conv1's weight gradient, and its bias from column sums;
  - conv1's input gradient transposed (dx0^T = W1^T dy^T), so its accumulator, masked by relu', is packed straight into
    the A operand of the stem's weight gradient (the FlashAttention trick);
  - the next sample's bytes load during this one's GEMMs, its dx1 during its stem; the blocks' sums are added in block
    order (deterministic);
  - h0 laid out by x parity with the 8-channel halves swapped on bit 2 of x / 2 (ldmatrix's eight rows on eight bank
    groups).

  DRAM sees the bytes and dx1 only. No dx0 buffer.
- **k_s1f (NTL_S1F, needs NTL_S1B)**: the stem into shared memory, then conv1's implicit GEMM from it, h1 out as conv_o
  wrote it (learn_check's forward rows equal the default's). No h0 buffer.
- **Builds**: V.b and V.b.f, beside nth16's V.mP (actor.mk's nt_vflags: `make -C csrc/runtime train-learn-v
  NT_V=s1.b.f`, `train-loop-v NT_V=s1.m2.b.f`). `train-width-check NT_WX=b.f` runs s1's learner checks on it. The
  default build's code is master's.
- **Grids.** Wave quantization decided them, not occupancy:
  - k_s1b: 2,392 us at 16 samples a block (6.2 waves), 2,713 at 32 (3.1), 2,122 at one wave;
  - a persistent one-wave grid stretched to 5.2 ms beside the co-tenant;
  - now S1_WAVES (2) waves of the device's SMs: k_s1b 2,098 / 2,104 / 2,113 us at 1 / 2 / 4 waves, k_s1f 870 to 881.
- **After** (ncu, a minibatch): k_s1f 872 us (100.8 MB read, 131.5 written, 266 GB/s, 28.5% of 936), k_s1b 2,105 us
  (235.0 and 3.1 MB, 113 GB/s, 12.1%), k_s1bsum 10 us. The stem path is 2,987 us (−25.5%) and 476 MB (−79.4%); the
  minibatch 7,438 us (−15.5%) and 3.08 GB (−40%). With fp16 accumulation: s1.m2 8,254 us, s1.m2.b.f 6,296 (k_s1f 586
  us, k_s1b 1,612).
- **FLOPs at fp32 accumulation are not free.** ncu's tensor % has the 142 TFLOPS fp16-accumulate rate as its 100%;
  fp32 accumulation peaks at 71. In those terms the old kernels ran at 41 to 57 TFLOPS of 71 (k_c1dx 42, conv1's
  k_cwgrad 41, conv2's 57). k_s1b does 11.8 MFLOP a sample, 13% of it the stem's recompute, and runs at 45 TFLOPS. Its
  top stalls are math-pipe throttle and MIO (the bytes' 1-byte shared loads for the stem's operands); DRAM 12%. So the
  bytes fell 79% and the time 25%, and the fusions gain more at fp16 accumulation.
- **Item 2, fewer bits: not built, by the counts.**
  - k_cwgrad's fp32 partials are 11.5 MB written plus 10.8 MB read back a minibatch (0.4% of 5.1 GB): at most 12 us.
  - 8-bit activations: no stem-path kernel is DRAM-bound after item 1, and an INT8 mma needs both operands 8-bit.
  - What is left DRAM-bound is conv3's im2col route through a3 (151 MB): k_im2col 260 us (89.5% of 936), the three
    cuBLAS GEMMs over a3 (626 us, 84 to 91%) and k_col2im 302 us (92.5%). That is 1,188 us and about 1.06 GB a
    minibatch: conv3 as an implicit GEMM is the next byte target.

## 2026-11-01 The FP16 ray cast two rays a thread in half2: every device cast the host's, its air step 52 instructions a ray against 85, and the kernel still 1.5 to 1.8x the scalar FP16's (2x FP32's): the walks it cannot pack run back to back at lower occupancy with a longer tail; a frozen policy at FP16 casts level with FP32 over 8,192 episodes (lane/cxh2)

- **The variant** (cast.cu RC_H2 1; off by default): `rc_cast<h16, false, true>`, 64 threads a block, two pixels a
  thread (RC_PAIR 1: i and i + 8 of the 16 x 8 tile; 0, neighbours, measured 3 to 14% slower). walk2 steps both rays'
  first air loop together: the compares by HSET2 masks (`__hle2_mask`), the chosen axis' t, boundary and next t by
  `__hadd2_rn` / `__hsub2_rn` / `__hmul2_rn` (each lane rounded as the scalar `__hadd_rn`, so no operation of raycast.h's
  order changed), the masks as LOP3 selects; the integers two to a register (16-bit lanes: the cell from the eye's cell,
  the Morton index, a section crossing as its carry or borrow, the top by a lane compare); a step where both cells are air
  and neither lane meets an edge, the top or its limit has no branch but the loop's. A jump is dda_jump on one lane at a
  time; each lane's end goes to a local record (struct rc_res) and the unchanged scalar walk goes on from it (the hit's
  shading, transparent texels, water, later segments). The shared code (rc_dir, walk's rs) leaves FP64's and FP32's
  kernels the same size (6,376 and 5,472 SASS instructions before and after; fixed and scalar FP16 8 fewer).

## 2026-10-31 The fidelity ladder in ntloop: rungs, a schedule and a fade from the run file, each episode's rung recorded, fast 3.8x and stripped 6.1x vanilla in the trainer, three arms (flat fast, flat vanilla, fast then vanilla) inside each other's spread on two seeds (lane/ladder)

Elliot, 2026-10-24: "the training recipe is a fidelity ladder"; 2026-10-31: "all these levers should be added and
tested". The engine kept a rung per env and changed it only at a reset; ntloop had no ladder. Base 7d1917ff.

- **The run file's policy.ladder** (configs/ladder.yaml, loop.c "the fidelity ladder"): `rungs` low to high
  (vanilla; fast, train-fast's spawning, random ticks and weather off; stripped, fast and mobs none; or a '+' list of
  the switches a rung turns off), `schedule` env_steps | minutes | milestone (`milestone` NAME reached in a share
  `at` of the top rung's last `window` episodes opens the next) | fixed (`shares`), `at` (one boundary a rung past
  the first), `fade` (the units cross one after another over that span), `unit` group (the default: a group stays
  rung-homogeneous, so its step waits only for its own envs) or env. The sim runs at vanilla with fidelity.rung
  exact (ntloop refuses anything else with a ladder: a rung goes on over the start's image at a reset); a rung is
  put on at a received group's resets through pool_rung_set and pool_rung_fid (new, one entry point: the stripped
  path's fidelity per env, NULL for stripped's own), never mid-episode; the actor and learner are unchanged. Each
  env's first episode (the vector env's make, before ntloop can set a rung) runs at the sim's fidelity, booked as
  rung -1. The milestone archive (saved starts) is refused with a ladder: a saved start carries its episode's rung.
- **Books and records.** episodes.jsonl gets each episode's `rung`, iters.jsonl `ladder_envs` (the envs whose next

## 2026-10-31 The FP16 cast finished and measured: half instructions on the device (9 to 14% over float-and-round with its launch bound, still 14 to 25% behind FP32), 2.1 to 3.0x FP32's host cycles, 2.5% of pixels off FP64's at every size against FP32's 0.001 to 0.05%; not worth keeping (lane/cxf16)

Base: lane/castexact's WIP (93af52d7) and its 8f299bd0 (the wrappers raycast_f16.c and raycast_fx.c, the one
renderstate lock), cherry-picked. castexact's first measurements (out/cx on its tree) are the starting rows.

- **The device in half instructions.** cast.cu's h16 did each + - * and compare as float's, rounded back
  (castexact's). RC_H16 1 (the default): __hadd_rn, __hsub_rn, __hmul_rn (never contracted to an HFMA, as
  --fmad=false), __hneg and the half compares; / and sqrt stay float's rounded once (__hdiv and hsqrt are not promised
  correctly rounded). Either way the same bits (IEEE half's correctly rounded result; 24 >= 2 x 11 + 2), and every
  device cast stayed equal to the host's. Alone 6 to 8% faster a launch (0.1961 to 0.1797 ms at 16x16, 0.3369 to
  0.3107 at 128x128, one window). RC_MINB16 (the FP16 kernel's own __launch_bounds__, 4 before) ranked 4 to 8
  in two gpu windows: 6 the best at every size (1.3 to 6.3% ahead of 4), the new default. half2 is not used: a DDA
  step updates one axis after a three-way compare, so there are no pairs of the same half operation in a ray, and
  two rays a thread would split at their first different step; GA102 issues scalar HADD and HMUL at FP32's rate, so
  only the conversions were left to save.
- **A bug the 128x128 size found** (FP16 alone). A unit direction's component under 1/65504 (a ray within about 1.5e-5
  of parallel to an axis plane) has a reciprocal that overflows a half: id = inf, and with the eye's offset exactly on a boundary its
  first t is 0 x inf = NaN. The reference's `!(t <= range)` ended the ray as a miss there, the fast path's runs'
  `t >= tlim` went on walking: nether-trip-s1 row 125, 128x128, pixel (31, 44), reference 23 3 3 (the Nether fog), fast
  38 17 13 (netherrack). Found by bisecting the fast path with throwaway knobs (the runs off: equal; empty_run swapped
  for dda_jump: unequal), then one pixel's walks printed. The fix is in the instance's definition (raycast.h): such a
  component is 0, the ray not moving on that axis, as d +-0 already is (raycast.c rays_row, cast.cu rc_cast). FP32
  and FP64 cannot meet it (their reciprocals overflow only under 3e-39 and 6e-309). castexact gated FP16 at 16x16 and
  32x32 only; raycast-gate and raycast-device-gate (gpu-raycast-check) now have a fourth run, RCSPECS16 = 64x64:f16
  128x128:f16 (pool_gate takes four specs a run). The pinned 16x16 digests (gates.tsv *-f16) did not
  move; on the gate recordings only nether-trip-s1's 128x128 digest did (576b06083427cab3 to 743dd251f3ab5acb).
- **The device against the host**, pool_gate_rcd --raycast-device on semcam-gate's six recordings at 16x16, 32x32,
  64x64 and 128x128 FP16 (48 episodes): OK, 63,320 rows, every device cast equal to the host's, the reference equal to
  the fast path.

Where they land (pxdiff survey --min-px 3 --thresh 1, sr-speedrun-s1's 20 frames at 64x64, FP64 against FP16): 3,408 of
81,920 pixels differ; the clusters texel-selection 32 (388 pixels), unresolved 30 (303), edge 5 (30), cutout-sky 2
(7), content 1 (5), shading-offset 1 (3). Speckle a few pixels wide across textured faces: the texel each ray picks
(u 16 on a half's coordinates: past 16 blocks the ulp is 1/64 of a block, a quarter of a texel) and cell edges.

Is FP16 worth keeping: no. FP32 beats it on both axes at every size. On the host it costs 2.1 to 3.0x FP32's cycles and
cannot do better: Zen 5 computes each operation in FP32 and converts both ways, so even a lane path would be FP32's
lanes plus a round trip an operation. On the device it runs 14 to 25% slower than FP32: the walk has nothing for half2,
and the scalar half instructions issue at FP32's rate. Its error is 2.5% of pixels, 54 to 2,600 times FP32's, and flat
across sizes, because the ray's own coordinates carry it. Its one win is over FP64 on the device (0.43x at 128x128),
and FP32 already has that. The code stays because it is gated and its column is measured; retiring the config value
is Elliot's call.

## 2026-10-31 Skipping air by 4x4x4 bricks costs the ray cast more than it saves on both chips (host +5.5 to 9.0%, device +17 to 40%), so it ships off; every variant byte-equal; one renderstate lock for all instances (lane/castexact)

The brief (Elliot, 2026-10-31: "is there a faster way to do this with fewer bits and how much we actually need to
accumulate?"): skip air by a 64-bit occupancy mask per 4x4x4 brick on the host and the device with the same bytes; a
fixed-point instance; the bits each part needs. Base 7d1917ff. After the dev host's 7:26 pm crash (not this lane's
code: the orchestrator traced it to another lane's library) the orchestrator split the work at 8:20 pm: this lane kept
the bricks and the walks; lane/cxfix the fixed instance, lane/cxf16 FP16, lane/cxmatrix the instance-by-size timing
tool. Their code came from this lane's commits (93af52d7, 8f299bd0); their numbers are theirs. The notebook is out/cx.

What the lane made (csrc/runtime/raycast.c; cuda/raycast/cast.cu; knobs on the cast's objects, RCXFLAGS / NVXFLAGS):
- sec_bricks: a section's 64-bit mask, bit (x >> 2) * 16 + (z >> 2) * 4 + (y >> 2) set where the brick holds a
  nonzero id (AVX-512: a section's 4,096 ids in 64-byte loads), kept beside each lsec entry of the cast's window
  (rcwin.bm). When the window moves, a column whose chunk has the same address and write sequence keeps its masks
  (rccarry), so only new or written columns are scanned.
- RC_BRICK 1: the dry air walk's lanes load a cell's id only where the lane's brick bit is set (rp_bocc, then one load
  a lane under the mask); RC_BRICK 2: a masked dword gather instead. A lane in a clear brick reads 0, the same value.
- RC_BRICKJ 1 (brick_jump): a lane that read air in a clear brick goes straight to the brick's last cell on its path.
  On each axis: the steps to the brick's far side n (3 - (i & 3) going up, i & 3 going down); the next boundaries'
  t, T_2 .. T_4, from the step's own expression ((u - o) id, with u advanced by the same additions), so the bits are
  the same; the exit step is the least far-side t under the step's order (ties x, then y, then z); each other axis
  takes the boundaries ordered before it (t <= te for an axis before the exit axis, t < te for one after). The jump is
  taken only when te is under the ray's limit. The fixed instance keeps its steps, because its near-tie order comes
  from the integers (rc_fx_cmp). The device's own RC_BRICKJ (cast.cu, scalar per thread) loads the brick's 64 bytes
  on entering it and jumps with dda_jump.
- The fix the gates found: renderstate_compute keeps a static, and each instance's unit had its own t_rs_lock around
  it, so two instances' reference casts raced. raycast-gate's run with fixed and FP16 specs together failed at random
  rows on 16 threads, while each instance alone passed. Now there is one hidden raycast_rs_lock, defined by the FP64
  unit and extern in the others; the same run is 63,320 rows equal. lane/cxfix and lane/cxf16 took this commit.

Bytes: every variant gives the pinned digests at 512x4 (FP32 090cb0a8007a184d e730535a6cf703b3, FP64 a12bbde7e7e8b15d);
RC_BRICKJ 1's pool_gate passes raycast-gate's FP64 run (47,490 rows) and FP32 run (63,320 rows) fast against
reference; the device's RC_BRICKJ 1 rcbench has frames and seen equal on all 16 stored casts (4 sizes x 4 instances).

FP64's walk: 71.5k, 65.4k with masked loads (-8.6%), 73.9k with the jump (+3.4%: eight lanes of doubles pay for
the jump's arithmetic in full). The masks do take the ids' read down by 16 to 44% (a counting build: 66% of the lanes'
id reads fall in clear bricks), but the walk is held by its dependent chain of steps rather than by any one load. The
saving moves into the edge lookup (each new section's mask gathered beside its ids) and into the jump's own
arithmetic, so the walk falls at most 9.4% (5.6k cycles), less than the 9.4k it costs to make the masks. Why so
little is skipped: the walk's id loads already hit L1 97.4% of the time (lane/hostf32's IBS), so the walk waits on
loads completing, not on misses. A mask adds a load and a test to every step to save a load that was cheap already,
and the steps stay in the same dependent chain. The process's top-down at fixed work (perf stat -M PipelineL1, the
same shape, one window, 3 rounds, spreads 0.4 to 2.5%; dispatch slots an env-step, medians): without bricks 1,188.7k

act from it and is matched against lower levels down to the raw keyboard and mouse. ntloop kept weights, not the
episodes. Now `ntloop --rec DIR` (or the run file's policy.record.episodes on; off by default) writes

  look and its mode, the hotbar, the gui ops), with the step's reward. No observation: the episode's tape replays it.

  the ops apart, any step a column cannot hold kept whole as an exception: none in today's heads), zstd over the
  episode. On 3,072 episodes of the brute recipe's trainer (512 envs, 16x16, the a05-070 actor learning): the env's
  buffers 316 bytes an env-step, packed 29.3, compressed 5.73 (zstd 3; 5.84 with the chunk headers); zstd 1 5.93 at
  1.2 GB/s, zstd 9 5.23 at 0.17 GB/s. Byte planes for the multi-byte columns measured worse (7.04 against 5.92 on the
  same 2,048 episodes: the look's floats take few values and repeat whole). The bytes are in the keys (1.22, the
  policy's sampled bits), the two look floats (0.96 and 1.00), hold (0.47) and the bins (0.42, 0.44): ntrec stats.

  80,896 episodes) reach the wooden pickaxe in 23 to 94% of episodes and the stone pickaxe in 10 to 85%, the furnace
  and later milestones in 0 to 20%, so "every episode that gains a milestone" keeps nearly all of them. The default:
  keep every episode that gains a milestone past the stone pickaxe (record.milestones; from a saved start, more
  milestones at the end than its level and one of the set among them), and 2% of the rest (a hash of the seed, env
  and episode number). `ntrec keep` on the 3,072 kept-all episodes: 10.3% kept by gain, 1.8% sampled, 12.0% of the
  env-steps; 0.44, 0.62 and 0.87 GB an hour at 180k, 250k and 350k env-steps/s (all of them 3.8, 5.3 and 7.4 GB;

## 2026-10-31 The FP32 host cast's air walk at sixteen lanes: its cycles 18% fewer, the cast's 7.6%, the env's 0.9% at fixed work; the 16x16 trainer +0.3%, inside its noise; every byte the same (lane/hostf32)

The brief: the FP32 instance of the host cast at 16 floats a register on AVX-512 (lane/castf32's "Left"), byte-equal to
the FP32 device cast and its pinned digests, FP64 untouched; by stall category; variants as compile-time knobs ranked
as a grid in one window. Base bb3a326b. Every number below is from vec_bench at the trainer's shape (16x16, 512 envs
in 4 groups, 32 threads, random actions, 1,500 steps after 100: fixed work, equal trajectory and observation digests
in every run) unless it says ntloop; the notebook is out/hf (scripts, logs, the windows' abrun logs).

What changed (raycast.c, one source):
- The lanes are RC_W wide: FP64 eight (a zmm of doubles, as before), FP32 RC_W32, 16 by default (a zmm of floats; 8 is
  the ymm of AVX-512VL's forms, lane/castf32's). Beside RV, the lane macros gained RI (the int32 lanes: a ymm for
  eight, a zmm for 16), RM and RK_* (the masks), and RP with rp_* (each lane's section address: one zmm of eight
  pointers, two for 16). rays_air_body, rays_on, hand_back and ents_lanes are written on them; each lane's operations
  are the scalar's, so the lane count changes no byte.
- FP64's machine code is master's instruction for instruction (objdump of raycast.o: 0 lines differ); FP32 built with
  -DRC_W32=8 is master's raycast_f32.o instruction for instruction, so that variant is master's cast in this tree.
- Knobs, each -D on the cast's objects: RC_W32 (8, 16), RC_BLOCK (steps before a refill), RC_EGATHER (0: a load a
  lane crossing into a section instead of the qword gathers; 2: so when two or fewer cross), RC_IDGATHER (1: the ids
  by gathers of the dword each ends), RC_IDPACK (1, 2: the addresses read back from memory, the bytes packed by shifts
  or through memory; 3: packed by shifts; 4: two eight-lane halves), RC_HBSCATTER (hand_back by scatters), RC_NO_SIMD
  (a build without x86's lanes, the Mac's path, on this host). The defaults are the kept build. raycast.mk's RCXFLAGS puts flags on the
  cast's objects alone, so `make -C csrc/runtime rlbind VARIANT=NAME RCXFLAGS='-DRC_W32=8'` builds a variant library
  whose engine is the default's from ccache: lane/hostf32's 17-variant grid built in 29 s.
- gates.tsv pins the FP32 host cast's own digests (digest-512x4-f32 090cb0a8007a184d e730535a6cf703b3,
  digest-128x2-f32 a9d498ac53a83ba3 d4f720c9d22f328f, made from master's code), gates-env runs them (gates.mk's
  hostf32.yaml: host.yaml with cast_precision 32). exp_neg32 is marked unused for clang's FP64 instance.

## 2026-10-31 The repeated lane jobs became abrun, ncustall, gate sets, and VARIANT builds (lane/tooling)

Elliot's rule: "simplify everything and instill that into being a general rule". The lane inventory found 699 scripts (15,009 lines), including 148 timing scripts, 179 digest comparisons, 125 profiler wrappers, 35 gate bundles, and 45 variant builds. AGENTS.md now points lanes to the shared commands. Proof logs and the limits of their comparisons are in out/report.md.

- `out/native/abrun` runs variants in alternating order for multiple rounds, extracts a metric and trajectory digest, rejects failed runs, missing metrics, and unequal digests, and prints median, range, spread, ratio, and bars. On a fresh worktree, 512x4 layout `any` and `doms` ran three times each on the same fixed work with digest `0b080aec71c4103a`: medians 245,130 and 270,625 env-steps/s, with nonoverlapping ranges. `--lower` and `--require` checked the stored cast comparison; the final kernel was faster on all three dumps, although these dumps and absolute timings do not reproduce lane/casthot's earlier 64x64 128-env spread.
- `out/native/ncustall` reads Nsight Compute's SASS source export and reports stall samples by instruction, source line, reason, and opcode, with a before/after comparison. On the two supplied reports it counted 38,570 and 27,872 samples, including long scoreboard 5,009 and 2,229 and branch resolving 3,299 and 1,375. The earlier lane/casthot DEVLOG gives 40,841 and 29,202, 5,432 and 2,278, 3,471 and 1,431. The supplied reports' own SASS rows support this tool's counts; those earlier figures cannot be reproduced from these reports. A different profiling pass or aggregation could explain the mismatch.
- `make -C csrc/runtime gates-env` and `gates-cast` build once, run independent gates up to `GT_J` at a time, and print a line per gate plus a final PASS or FAIL. `gates.tsv` pins the 512x4 and 128x2 digests from master. Pool and oracle references run under `setsid -w`; GPU checks use the queue after waiting for free device memory. The native suite also takes a check slot for its frame judges. In a fresh worktree both sets passed, and a planted wrong 512x4 digest failed at `digest-512x4`.
- `make -C csrc/runtime rlbind VARIANT=NAME XFLAGS=...` builds an isolated `out/var/NAME/libnwrl.so` with parallel compilation. `make -C csrc gpu-raycast-bench VARIANT=NAME NVXFLAGS=...` builds an isolated `out/var/NAME/rcbench`. The default builds remain untouched. `abrun` timed `-fno-plt` against the default at 512x4 (244,073 against 241,637 env-steps/s, overlapping ranges and equal digests) and `-Xptxas -dlcm=cg` against the default cast on a stored dump (0.4531 against 0.4025 ms, nonoverlapping ranges).

## 2026-10-30 The pick's block ray traced every tick again: round 10's memo skipped the trace's writes to the blocks' shared bounds, so a cracked stair's dig particles spawned over the full cube; pix-crack-s1's frames back to their budgets, the speed unchanged (lane/pickfix)

The brief: `make -s -C csrc test` failed in one job on lane/resetfix, pix-crack-s1's frame judge at both sizes
(t=50, 1298 px against 225; 85 against 2 at 128x128), bisected by the orchestrator to 00531593 (lane/clienttick, the
pick's ray memo). The task was to find the input the memo's key missed and fix it exactly. On lane/resetfix
(9b7e46e0), the dev host. out/report.md has every attempt and every gate's last lines.

- **The cause.** raytrace_blocks is not a pure function of the ray and the cells. Like vanilla's
  setBlockBoundsBasedOnState on the Block singletons, it writes the shared bounds in `nw_env->collide` (a stair's
  octant 7, the chest, ladder, fence, pane and End portal bounds) and reads others (the portal frame, the brewing
  stand, a ladder's last bounds). A memo hit skipped the writes. In pix-crack-s1 the player's collision query resets
  the cracked stair's octant (collide.c) between two picks of a still ray, the memo does not set it again, and the
  dig particles (particles_live.c over collide_stairs_octant) spawn over the full cube. The rows held. A diagnostic,
  the memo re-marking the stair on a hit, gave t=50 exactly its budget values.
- **Why the verify build passed.** -DCP_PICK_VERIFY ran the full trace on every ray and compared only the returned
  answer, so in that build nothing was ever skipped and it behaved like the memo-free engine. Its gates were digest
  runs with no frames. The frame judges in `make -s -C csrc test` see it, and were already in the suite. Lesson: a
  memo's verify mode compares the env state the skipped call writes, not only its result, and a round that touches
  the client's pick runs the native suite.
- **The fix.** The memo is out (survival.c, survival.h, player.c). An exact one needs a touch flag inside raytrace.c
  for six writes and three reads and would save less than the commit's -0.15% instructions. At 512x4 in bench
  windows, five rounds each with the order alternated, the tip ran 87,175 env-steps/s and the fix 87,286 (each side
  spans 1.4%), instructions within 0.04%, digests equal.
- **Gates.** The native suite with no FAIL, pool-gate 40 recordings OK (133,280 rows), raycast-gate OK (47,490),
  train-loop-check PASS; again in a fresh worktree. Ledger: csrc/tests/divergences/pickfix.tsv.

## 2026-10-30 A start's packed blob only for a stored chunk unwritten since the start: the park compared the region store's wseq with the live world's, so every stored chunk passed; every pool and cast gate equal again, the speed kept (lane/resetfix)

The brief: the pool gate (play-reload2-s1 row 240 w.bc 31 against 24, gold-g15-s42 row 469) and the cast gate
(sr-speedrun-s1 row 1471) failed on lane/cpubase12. The orchestrator bisected them to 18bf634f (lane/resettick,
round 5). The task was to find the cause and fix it exactly, keeping that commit's speed. On lane/ntcast
(1bfcf326), the dev host, CPU and the 3090. out/report.md has every attempt and every gate's last lines.

- **The cause.** sr_pack took the start's blob for a chunk with `c->wseq <= b->wseq` (the live world's wseq at the
  start). A parked chunk is in the region store, though, and `put_chunk` stamps an inserted chunk with the receiving
  world's sequence. Stored chunks carry the store's 101, 102, ... against the live world's 525, so every stored chunk
  passed, written or not. The park packed the start's cells over the episode's, and the chunk's next load read them.
  A probe comparing every taken blob with chunk_pack's bytes found 133 stale blobs in one play-reload2-s1 episode:
  fallen gravel in bands 0 and 1 (the start's cave-in), leaves' decay bits, some sky light. The seed-tick index and
  the region cache hit, the commit's other two kept things, were right: with the blob lookup off, all three
  recordings passed with both still kept.
- **The fix** (world.h, world.c, serverreplay.c). `struct chunk start_wseq`: every insertion clears it, and
  `sr_store_chunk` sets it to the store's stamp when the chunk leaves the live world with a wseq no later than the
  blobs'. The park takes the blob only while `wseq == start_wseq`, meaning no store write since. The probe, run over
  the full pool gate: 0 of 4,638 taken blobs differ from chunk_pack's (39,259 parks).
- **Why round 5's gates passed.** Its gates were vec_bench digest A/Bs and a TICKS_VERIFY build of the same runs. In
  vec_bench's random-action episodes the stale blobs never reach the trajectory: fixed and unfixed give the same
  digests (a9d498ac53a83ba3 at 128x2, 461fc2a45e94ed16 at 512x4) and the same instructions. Only the pool gate and
  the cast gate replay recordings that write chunks which later unload and load again. A round that changes what a
  reset keeps or skips should run `pool-gate` (about 40 s) and `raycast-gate` as gates. No list line was missing.

Gates, here and again in a fresh worktree of 9cd85731: pool-gate 40 recordings OK, 133,280 rows (master's count);
raycast-gate OK, 47,490 rows; gpu-raycast-check OK, 47,490 rows (24,198 device casts equal on sr-speedrun-s1);
train-loop-check PASS with its digests unchanged (486fdf7386b0ea68, 149019890991de49). The native suite (here):
every job but pix-crack-s1's two frame judges (t=50, 1,298 px against 225). The tip fails those two with the same
numbers, so that failure predates this lane and is still open.

| vec_bench, one bench window, interleaved, 2 runs a side | tip 1bfcf326 | fix 9cd85731 |
|---|---|---|
| 128x2, 16 threads, warm 100 + 2000, ep-len 200 | 104,344; 103,893 | 103,004; 104,141 (-0.5%) |
| 512x4, 32 threads, warm 100 + 400, ep-len 200 | 87,210; 87,028 | 87,864; 87,094 (+0.4%) |

The noise is up to 1.1% between runs of one side. instructions:u at 128x2 were 390.48G and 390.45G against 390.50G
and 390.48G. lane/resettick's gain is kept: on this corpus the blobs it took were nearly all of truly unwritten
chunks. The runs used vec_bench's defaults, not placement's pipe0.yaml (which is on the GPU host only).

## 2026-10-30 The ray cast on the device beside the native trainer: the main thread serves the env and the 3090 as either finishes, the cast's launch packs nothing, the groups' streams ahead of the learner's; 64x64 1.20 to 1.44x the host cast, 16x16 1.14x with one group of four cast on its workers, every frame the host cast's (lane/ntcast)

SPEC item 6d, Elliot (2026-10-30): the CPU env bounds the native trainer, so move the cast to the GPU and keep the
trainer and the cast there together, batched across the groups that are ready. On lane/cpubase12 with lane/ntwire
and lane/ntwidth merged, the dev host (3090 on PCIe Gen3 x8), every number from gpuq bench windows, the runs
interleaved, two each (out/perf/ntcast.tsv has all 27 rows).

What the device path was (the base, ntloop at depth 1, nsys and perf at 16x16): the main thread blocked in
`nwrl_vec_recv` while finished groups sat on the device, or in a group's event while the env had groups ready;
`rcdev_launch` packed each group's staged section records on the main thread (39 us and 33 us of API a launch of
128 envs in steady state, 250 us at a reset's window) and copied every env's 8.4 KB head whole (270 KB, 43 us on
the bus a group of 32); and the cast kernel at 16x16 is a latency chain: a launch of 32 envs takes 0.26 to 0.30 ms
alone (64 blocks, 6.7% occupancy, IPC 0.36), about what 128 envs take (rcbench on dumps: 32/64/128 envs 0.324/
0.309/0.339 ms at 16x16, 0.377/0.406/0.509 at 64x64).

What changed:

- **The loop serves both sides** (`ntloop --serve`, the default with the device cast): it sends every group whose
  event has fired, takes every group the env has finished without waiting (`nwrl_vec_try_recv`, new; pipeline.c's
  `pipe_poll_some` with min 0 now collects what the pool has done in the direct mode, where it collected nothing), and
  waits in recv only with nothing launched. Received groups not cast yet go in one launch
  (`nwrl_vec_cast_groups`, new; `--cast-max`) on the first group's stream; each group's stream waits for that cast's
  event, then its copies, its policy and its actions. One cast stream for all groups ran the casts one after another
  (90k env-steps/s against 197k at 128 envs in 4).
- **The launch packs nothing** (cuda/raycast/host.cu): the workers' stages, heads and seen records are page-locked
  and mapped. `rc_scatter` reads each env's records where its worker staged them, `rc_head_get` copies each head
  through its last entity box (about 4 KB, mostly the 3 KB lightmap), and `rc_seen_fin` writes the seen records to
  host memory. The main thread's launch went from 0.07 to 0.02 ms a group step at 512 envs, and the pack's
  RC_SLOTS x n x 246 KB of device and page-locked memory is gone.
- **The groups' streams ahead of the learner's** (`--prio`, the default served): the 64x64 trainer went from 119.5k
  and 117.6k to 128.6k and 129.3k env-steps/s. The learner then took 58 ms an update instead of 43 and was busy the
  whole window, but kept up.
- **The trainer on `nt_actor_reload`** (train/trainer.cu): no private compile of actor.cu and no layout probe. There
  are two images still, a workspace per image per group, and each group's RNG counter is carried over a switch with
  `nt_actor_ws_seed`, so a group's draws are one sequence. ntloop is built per net.h variant
  (`make -C csrc/runtime train-loop-v NT_V=s1`, out/runtime/train/V/ntloop).
- **Every frame held** (`--frame-digest`): each env's segment (frames, scalars, reward, end, driver) is hashed every
  step as the device holds it. train-loop-check now holds every run to the host cast's 149019890991de49 and to
  vec_bench's 486fdf7386b0ea68: depth 0 and 1, served, `--cast-max 1`, `--cast-hold 1` and `--stage 1`. It also
  checks 64x64 through s1 (92a51d43e464cbe1), and the native actor (fixed weights, learning off) on both casts
  (440c72b7dfc3dd9f, f36f3b661bd6fa6b). It caught one bug on the way: rc_head_get copied nent's 16 bytes only in
  its second pass. Also new: `--dump-cast N:PATH` (rcbench's input); rcbench builds again (the cast's ch argument).

- **Smoke** (150 s, the device cast with K=1 at 512x4, lane/ntwire's init7.ntw, Adam afresh, the archive off): no NaN,

  141 s. lane/ntwire's native ran kl 0.0042 to 0.0126 and clipfrac 0.049 to 0.166, so the top kl row is a little

Tried and dropped (each exact, measured in its own window):
- A sleep between looks instead of the spin (`--idle-us 5, 20`): 117.1k to 118.7k against 117.8k to 118.7k.
- Holding received groups while a cast runs, so they batch (`--cast-hold`, 1.4 to 2.5 groups a cast): -4 to -6% at

- The seen records into device memory and copied back, against the mapped writes (rc_seen_fin shows 30 us a launch
  in the split's trace): 295k and 294k against 305k and 302k at 512x4 K=1.

- A per-env ready queue: not built. The workers' idle share with the split at 512x4 is about 6%.

Gates, in a fresh worktree of the branch (out/java and out/assets linked; built in 32 s): train-wire-check,

Left: at 16x16 a launch costs its longest ray's chain (0.3 ms whatever the envs). The head's 3 KB lightmap an env
crosses PCIe Gen3 x8 every step (rc_head_get 76 us at 128 envs). So the device cast wins at 16x16 only with the

per-ray setup and the hit's general path, not in the air loop. K is a config key the run file sets: K=1 at 16x16
512x4, K=2 at 64x64 256x4 measured best here. pipeline.c is outside the brief's files (the one min-0 line).

The policy (the reference's GPU time, us a sample: the actor at a group of B, plus the learner; the GPU-bound rate in
parentheses):

| net | params | fwd MFLOP | actor B32 / B64 / B128 / B256 | learner | B64 | B128 | B256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16x16 wm1 | 0.27M | 1.9 | 4.15 / 2.14 / 1.14 / 0.63 | 1.64 | (264k) | (360k) | (440k) |
| 16x16 wm2 | 0.94M | 7.1 | 4.53 / 2.32 / 1.38 / 0.74 | 2.66 | (201k) | (247k) | (294k) |
| 16x16 wm4 | 3.5M | 27.0 | 5.88 / 3.08 / 1.99 / 1.29 | 5.72 | (114k) | (130k) | (143k) |
| 16x16 wm8 | 13.4M | 105.4 | 10.46 / 6.93 / 4.21 / 2.91 | 17.02 | (42k) | (47k) | (50k) |
| 16x16 wm16 | 52.4M | 416.2 | 30.98 / 19.41 / 13.00 / 9.59 | 59.52 | | (14k) | (14k) |
| 32x32 wm1 | 0.46M | 6.9 | 7.19 / 3.88 / 2.02 / 0.93 | 4.30 | (122k) | (158k) | (191k) |
| 32x32 wm2 | 1.7M | 25.9 | 5.34 / 3.72 / 2.20 / 1.44 | 7.88 | | (99k) | (107k) |
| 64x64 stem wm1 | 0.47M | 11.9 | 8.32 / 4.51 / 2.61 / 1.63 | 11.13 | | (73k) | (78k) |
| 64x64 stem wm2 | 1.7M | 34.3 | 6.11 / 4.43 / 2.91 / 2.19 | 15.33 | | (55k) | (57k) |
| 64x64 stem wm4 | 6.7M | 115.3 | 10.92 / 6.99 / 5.01 / 4.09 | 32.33 | | | (27k) |

The reference actor costs about 130 us a call whatever the group (launch-bound), so a group under 64 costs it 2 to
4 us a sample. The native kernels (lane/ntactor, lane/ntlearn; 16x16 wm1 only): the actor 0.28 us a sample at 128 and
0.18 at 512, the learner 0.59 (4.8 ms an update): 4.1 and 2.8 times the reference.

Together (min of the two ceilings, the native loop's env and the reference's GPU, assuming the loop overlaps them;
no end-to-end native trainer exists to confirm it): at 16x16, wm1 269k (env-bound, 512/4), wm2 247k (512/4, about
balanced), wm4 130 to 143k, wm8 47 to 50k, wm16 14k; at 64x64 with the stem, wm1 73k and wm2 55k (both GPU-bound
against the env's 92 to 107k). So with today's kernels capacity is free up to about 1M parameters at 16x16 (wm2:
3.5 times wm1's for 8% fewer samples) and costs about linearly past it. The Python trainer adds its own bound (the
main thread's 0.7 ms a group step, mem.trainer-path-levers: 91k at groups of 64, 183k at 128).

- **Runs handed on to lanes** (a3, a4; 5479c104). walk hands a ray it took into deep water from air (surface drawn, eye
  dry, 4 cells of water below) or a ray going up past a block it passed (snow layer, grass) to rays_on, AVX-512 lanes
  that pass water or air from the ray's own cell (a lane's step the fast loop's), and goes on where they hand it back
  with its colour and in_water. The fast loop's state there is changed by none of the cells passed, so walk resumed
  takes the same steps; raycast_seen's ties now go to the lower pixel (seen_add), which pixel order gave. Without the
  depth test the brief's shape paid for its 3-step runs (+1.5% paired cycles).
- **The lanes' hand-back** (a6, a7, a9; 5479c104, 7f4cbfe6). hand_back makes the dead lanes' hand-back in lanes and
  stores it without branches (a6); asks for the metadata and sky-light lines of each cell a ray is handed back onto,
  which walk reads first (a7); and takes the stopped lanes' state in registers: the lanes had kept it by masked stores
  to the stack, which a load cannot take from the store queue, so hand_back's first load waited for them (a9, 0.8% of
  the brief's cycles).
