## 2026-10-30 A reset restores by the 64-byte lines that differ and protects again only what its scan found written, and a reset to another start takes a held image that holds that start; a reset at 100-step episodes 2.10 to 1.33 ms, env-steps/s +7.8% at 100-step episodes, +6.4% at 200, +3.9% at 500, +16% on 8 seed starts, +6.4% on the seed set, the brief's bench flat, every trajectory, frame and image byte the same (lane/resetcopy)

The brief: memmove was the largest function on the 8 seed starts and grew with the thread count in the brief's long
runs, 87% of it reset_written's image copy. Count what a reset copies and why, then make it cheaper, every byte of
the image the start's. Measured CPU only on the GPU host, from lane/cpubase10 (6bad8b82), on placement's
out/pipe0.yaml. Every attempt is a row of out/perf/resetcopy.tsv; out/report.md has them all with the counts; out/rc
the scripts, logs and dropped patches.

- **Counted first** (POOL_RESET_COUNT in RL_PICDEF: 1 a reset's time by phase, pages, pointers and minor faults by
  kind and path; 2 content and residency by the image's parts; 3 the 64-byte lines of each restored page that differ
  from the start's). At the spawn start with 100-step episodes a reset was 2.10 ms (scan 0.40, copy 0.99, zero 0.39,
  protect 0.21): 1,361 pages copied (bands 693, heap 287, chunks 173) and 812 zeroed (heap 541, chunks 133), 353
  and 190 of them unchanged (the hot runs: pages written in one of the last four episodes stay unprotected). 564 of
  the copied pages differ from the start in one line, 449 of them bands: the header's sharer count (`shared`), which
  every chunk copy for the client and every unload writes; 232 in 2 to 4 lines, 16 in all 64. On 8 seed starts 593
  of 640 resets go to another start, a whole copy of 12.0 ms (copy 7.05 with 2,433 faults, madvise 4.54): 7,089
  pages copied, 3,242 resident pages handed back and 2,448 of the start's faulted in, about 80% of both heap (two
  starts' heaps sit at different pages), 36 pages the new start's already. This host hides kernel symbols; charged
  to their first user frame (out/rc/kcall.awk), seed8's kernel samples are 9.2% under madvise and 5.8% under memmove
  (the copy's faults). A page copy in place costs about 0.7 us, a cold one alone 250 to 320 ns (out/rc/pcb.c), 1 to
  1.5 us with 4 to 16 at once: memory-bound.
- **The line restore** (20f3aa51). restore_lines and zero_lines: a listed page is compared with the start's a line at
  a time (its pointers rebased in a 4 KB buffer when it has any), and only differing lines are written; a page to
  zero writes only its nonzero lines. **The protect from the scan**: every page written since the last protect is
  one the scan listed or one the zap log names, so a delta reset protects again only the scan's runs that found no
  room among the hot runs and the zap log's (image_wtrack_protect_runs, image.c, declared in a new image_wt.h that
  only image.c and pool.c include), the hot runs too every fourth reset, not a walk of the whole image (protect
  0.185 to 0.071 ms, the scan 0.33 to 0.22).
- **In AVX-512 lanes** (e77640a4): lines_page512 and zero_page512, a line a compare, the next page prefetched first
  (the stream prefetcher stops at a page's end), behind `__builtin_cpu_supports("avx512f")` and `__x86_64__`. The
  copy part 0.91 to 0.75 ms at 100-step episodes. A reset 2.10 to 1.33 ms there, 2.85 to 1.90 at 200-step episodes.
- **Held images** (01c717b5). spare_trade, in pool_reset under the pool's lock with the env idle: an env whose image
  holds another start than its new one takes a held image whose tracker is in step with the new start (a reset by
  the pages written, 4.3 ms against a 10.4 to 12 ms whole copy) and leaves its own, with the tracker state that moves
  with an image (wt_on, wt_serial, wt_prot, hot_resets); with none it takes the image held longest and copies there,
  its own staying for an env that will want its start. One held image per POOL_SPARE_DIV (4) envs, made as first
  needed; none with device generation or a view, none past the address window less 256 slots (none at 1,024 envs).
  Exact because an image's bytes after its reset are its start's whichever env it serves (RESETVERIFY), the engine's
  references are offsets from the image's base, and the cast's keep is keyed by the reset's epoch. Count builds on 8
  seed starts: n/8 72,043 env-steps/s, n/4 76,328, n/2 79,692, n 78,295 against 65,949, RSS 5.39, 5.90, 6.89, 8.65
  GB against 4.86; at n/2 and n 335 of 512 resets to another start found an image (a group's 64 envs reset together).

  cells a step through them (the ten offsets the four can sit at, selected by cmovs) and the seed comes from its

## 2026-10-30 The pool's steps through lock-free rings a domain, the poll woken once a group, the vector env's resets queued without waiting; the brief's bench +33.8% at 64 threads and +39.5% at 96, 8 seed starts +16.2%, every trajectory and frame the same, 200 stress runs with no hang (lane/balance)

The brief: at 64 threads the workers' step fell 16% on lane/cpubase9 and env-steps/s moved 1%; neither the main thread
nor the workers' mean bounded it. Count what does, then fix it. Measured CPU only on the GPU host, from lane/cpubase9
0758b102, on placement's out/pipe0.yaml. Every attempt is a row of out/perf/balance.tsv; out/report.md has the counts
and every attempt; out/bl the scripts (the trace build: trace.patch, csync.sh, an.sh, sweep.sh; the windows: ab.sh,
threads.sh, resets.sh, final.sh; stress.sh, gates.sh, fresh.sh, gs.sh).

- **Counted first: the pool's mutex, not Little's law.** perf at 64 threads after the warm-up: 29.8% of the process's
  cycles in the kernel, 22% on the futex hash bucket's spinlock, from the workers' lock and unlock of the pool's one
  mutex (rlbind's no-view layout: eight domain queues, env i on L3 i mod 8, steals, one lock). A trace build (every
  job's start and end by worker, every main thread call): the workers busy 61.4%, each 60 us step followed by 24 us
  waiting for the lock; the main thread's send held it 50 us a group of 128; a group's turnaround 762 us.
- **The rings** (7d3bd1b6). pool_step holds its envs under the lock, copies their acts and pushes outside it; a fast
  pool (no device generation; one queue or a queue a domain) publishes each step to its queue's ring, which a worker
  claims with a CAS and steals from the fullest other ring without the lock; a step's end goes to a done ring by
  sequence with the worker's own counts; a waiting consumer names how many ends it needs and only the step that
  completes them wakes it (pool_poll_min). Without a device the pipeline's poll takes the pool's results itself (no
  collector thread). 64 threads +28.8% (638k to 822k, no digest).
- **The main thread** (3d7246af, 8b8a4b1a). vec_bench --digest's FNV-1a in eight envs' chains at once, in registers
  (the same value; the byte-at-a-time chain was 72.5% of the main thread); one clock read a batch in the pipeline
  (three an env were 25% of its running cycles); the poll watches the done ring up to 100 us before it sleeps, idle
  workers try the lock-free take up to 50 us before they sleep. With --digest +13.8%, then +15.2%, then pairs 1.21 to
  1.40.
- **Async resets** (54f22831). On 8 seed starts at 16 threads the workers were busy 80%: group_done took 76 ms a group,
  one synchronous pool_reset a start (up to nine in turn, about seven envs each). pool_async_resets: pool_reset
  queues and returns, each job holding its start; a step queued behind a running reset is pushed by the reset's
  worker; vecenv turns it on (nothing in it reads an env between its reset and its reset step's result).
  group_done 60 us, the workers 99% busy; seed starts +16.5%, the seed set +10.2%.

  against its next. 128 envs in 2 groups, 500 casts each, the brief's shape: the eye and its angles equal in 56.9% of
  casts and the bytes the same in 29.7%; same-start 200-step episodes 49.6% and 16.7%; the 8 seed starts 29.4% and
  13.6%. With the macros off the random policy holds the camera in under 2% of casts: the repeats are the macros'
  (mining, crafting, the chest's waits). Of the frames with the camera still (brief's shape / same start / seed
  starts): nothing the frame read differs 30.6 / 10.6 / 12.9%; only the light, fog or sky colours 45.0 / 46.0 / 18.6%
  (the daylight cycle moves the lightmap's sky entries and the fog's colour most ticks); an entity box 8.4 / 8.6 /
  21.0%; a window chunk's write stamp 16.0 / 34.8 / 47.3%.
- **The kept frame** (raycast_seen_keep, raycast.h). The key is every input the frame's pixels read: the camera, the
  eye's cell and liquid, range, top, graphics, channels; the entity boxes with their rectangles, colours and light;
  the window's chunks by address and write sequence (world.h wseq: every block, metadata and light write, a client
  copy's cells, the insertion; rcmirror.c's device copy skips a column on the same two); of the lightmap only the
  entries lit() indexed, the fog's colour only where a pixel was fogged, the sky's only where one took the sky plane
  (struct rcuse, marked as the walk goes). A walk's path depends on no colour, so equal inputs on what the frame read
  make the same bytes. A reset puts the start's write sequences back, so the pool's epoch is part of the key:
  rlbind.c passes pool_epoch as it does for the device mirror (four lines there, outside this lane's files).
- **The frame shaded again** (keep_match 1). Each recorded cast keeps its pixels' layers as the walk lit them (the
  texel times the tint, the lightmap entry, the face's shade, the fog factor, a surface's alpha; the miss's fog, End
  sky or sky plane), and a frame whose walks are the kept frame's runs them through lit_apply, thru_add, sky_mix and
  pixel_out, the functions the walk now calls itself. 1.06 layers a pixel on the brief's shape.
- **Changed chunks and boxes** (keep_match 3, keep_rewalk). A column whose chunk changed is the same to the frame
  when no pixel's ray reaches it: each pixel's reach (its direction across x and z, the end of its walk's last cell;
  every cell a walk reads is on its ray before that or above or below such a cell) against the column's square a
  block wider, two blocks more along the ray, in AVX-512 floats sixteen rays a step. Otherwise, and when entity boxes
  changed, only the pixels a changed box's old or new rectangle holds (rays_fill tests a box only there, the first of
  equals) and the pixels whose rays reach a changed column are walked again (rays_runs), the rest shaded from their
  layers, and the seen record is made again from per-pixel notes in pixel order.
- **The record only while the camera is still.** Making it cost 19k instructions a cast (with the macros off the keep
  without it was 0.6% under the base and with it 2.3% over); a record serves only a cast with its frame's camera, so
  a cast makes it only when its camera is the kept frame's. With the macros off the head runs 661.2k instructions an
  env-step, the base 665.5k and 666.7k in two other runs (rough: about 0.7% under).

## 2026-10-29 A client flood ends once its queue holds only missing cells, none of which can push a loaded one: lt_flood_ng 8.4% of a seed-start run to 0.3%, instructions -16.5% on the 8 seed starts and -10.0% on the seed set, every trajectory and frame the same (lane/seedlight)

The brief: on seed starts the light engine was the second largest cost (lt_flood_ng 8.9%, lt_flood_block 1.8%,
world_bwl_step 1.0%); count what each episode floods and why, and make it cheaper, every light value and row the
same. Measured on the GPU host, CPU only, placement's pipe0.yaml, against lane/cpubase6 (b0b8aeee). Every row is in
out/perf/seedlight.tsv; out/report.md has the counts and every attempt, out/sl the scripts and logs.

- **Counted first** (a count build in a scratch tree, not committed: counters by world, cause and ticks since the
  start). On the 8 seed starts an episode's client floods took 782k turns, 774,753 of them cells of chunks the
  client lacks, and 774,636 of those came after the last loaded cell had left the queue; no such cell ever pushed a
  loaded one. 87 floods an episode filled the 32,768-entry queue (spawn start: 88k missing turns, 9.8 filling
  floods). These are vanilla's: near the client's loaded edge a missing cell reads 0, is air and drops its writes,
  so the cells along a loaded chunk's edge push each other until the radius or the full queue stops them. By cause
  the light is block changes (server 753 floods, client 238 an episode), sky columns and chunk light;
  enqueueRelightChecks does no pass on these starts (every cursor at 4,096), so the start's pending checks are not
  the cost.
- **The cut** (world.c lt_flood, lt_missing_quiet). Once no loaded cell is left in the queue (LP_TAIL's count nl),
  the rest writes nothing and the light is frozen; a missing cell pushes a loaded one only from a corner column
  whose two neighbors across the edges are loaded and 2 apart. lt_missing_quiet checks every such cell of the
  table within the radius; when none can push, the flood ends. Off a light capture only (the queue's tail it leaves
  is the capture's, lightcap.c), and only once the env's sticky overflow flag is set (a flood that would set it
  runs on: about one an episode).

## 2026-10-29 A reset copies back what the episode wrote: a write-protect tracker over each env's image, the start's bytes only where the env wrote since its last reset to that start; +16.8% env-steps/s at 200-step episodes, +10.1% at 500, the 512-env bench +0.8%, every trajectory, frame and image byte the same (lane/resetimg)

The brief: on lane/cpubase4 (49645225) a reset (csrc/runtime/pool.c reset_job) copied every run of the start's image
into the env's slot and handed the rest back, so it cost the start's size, not the episode's writes: the image copy
was 19.3% of cycles at 200-step episodes. Make a reset cost what the episode wrote, the image byte for byte what the
copy makes. Measured on the GPU host, CPU only, on placement's pipe0.yaml. Every row is in out/perf/resetimg.tsv;
out/report.md has every attempt.

- **Counted first.** The spawn start's image is 7,862 nonzero pages (32 MB) in 457 runs with 11,262 pointers. A
  reset took about 9.7 ms of a worker (from the step's cost at ep-len 100 against 500): the copy 4.4 ms, the gaps'
  madvise 1.2 ms, the rebase 0.07 ms, the rest what runs after the copy. An episode changes about 2,450 of the
  start's pages and writes about 1,050 outside it, the same at 200 and 500 steps: the list slab (1,178 copied, 466
  zeroed), the bands (731), the chunks, the heap, written in every episode's first ticks.
- **The tracker** (image.h, image.c `image_wtrack_*`). One userfaultfd a pool in asynchronous write-protect mode
  over every env's image: a write to a protected page lifts the protection in the kernel without a handler, and
  PAGEMAP_SCAN lists the pages written since and protects a range again in one walk (its holes left holes). A page
  the engine hands back while tracked is a hole the scan cannot see; image_give_pages already logs those (the zap
  log, imgxfer's tracker's), 10.5 entries an episode here, never full. The scan lists every written entry, present
  or not: a written page swapped out or under migration is not present for a while (this host swaps and compacts),
  and a present-only scan would never restore it. One run before that fix spun 6 minutes in set_pop_first; it did
  not reproduce, and this is the likely cause, not a proven one.
- **The reset** (pool.c reset_written, restore_range). A reset to the start the env was last reset to (a serial a
  start, pool_start.serial against pool_env.wt_serial) copies the start's bytes back over the pages written since,
  rebasing the start's pointers on those pages only, zeroes the written pages outside the start in place (they stay
  resident: the next episode writes them again, no fault, no TLB flush), copies back the zap log's pages, and
  protects the used extent again. Any other reset copies the whole start as before. About 2,550 pages copied and
  1,260 zeroed instead of 7,862 copied and the gaps handed back.
- **Hot runs.** A write-protect fault costs 295 to 457 ns on this kernel against 137 to 183 ns to copy a page
  (out/perf/ri/wpbench.c), so faulting on every page the episode writes cost more than the copy saved. The runs the
  last episode wrote (merged across 64-page gaps, up to 256 a env) are not protected again: writes there take no
  fault and every reset copies them back; every 4th reset protects all and the next episode names them anew. Page
  faults over 320 resets: 2.88 M to 2.01 M (lane/cpubase4 1.92 M, mostly the start-up).
- **A whole copy** lifts the protection first (one call; otherwise each page it wrote faulted), and its next episode
  runs unprotected: an env whose starts change, and the brief's bench (one reset at the make), take no fault.

Exact: a verify build (`-DPOOL_RESET_VERIFY` in RL_PICDEF) compares the used extent after every reset with what the
whole copy makes, page by page: the seven digest gates and a stress set, 21,330 delta resets, 0 pages differ. Every
trajectory digest of dig.sh and pgate.sh and the three observation digests are lane/cpubase4's.

## 2026-10-29 What a reset made every episode redo: the start's tick backlog held outside the image and skipped where it did nothing, its packed chunks and its region store's inputs kept with the start; +44% env-steps/s at 200-step episodes, +25% at 500, the brief's bench +9 to 13%, every trajectory and frame the same (lane/resettick)

The brief: training resets (180 s episodes, the milestone archive's many starts), and a reset cost about 400
env-steps of work. After the image copy, an episode's first ticks drained the start's scheduled ticks, packed
chunks and built the region store again. Do once what is the same for every episode from a start, proven equal by
a verify build. Measured on the GPU host, CPU only, placement's pipe0.yaml. Every row is in out/perf/resettick.tsv;
out/report.md has every attempt.

- **Counted first** (a count build, the spawn start gold-g1-s42, 32 envs, 200-step episodes):
  - the pending set holds 154,039 entries at an episode's first tick, all due, and ticks 0 to 153 pop 1,000
    each; later schedules are 14 to 330 a tick; the columns' membership tables resized 16 to 54 times a tick;
  - the set is 9.0 MB of the start's 32.2 MB image (7,862 pages in 457 runs), copied by every reset; the seed
    set's starts hold 104k to 162k entries, 6.1 to 9.5 MB of 26.9 to 41.1 MB;
  - a reset parks 67 chunks at tick 0 and packs 85 at tick 1 (2.5 MB raw); 96% of the blobs were byte-equal to
    one packed before (48% on the seed set, fewer episodes a start);
  - light floods are at most 23 a tick, in ticks 5 to 9;
  - by thread CPU time (128 envs, 16 threads), the server tick was 19.3 s, the drain about 8 s of it (40 ns an
    entry, misses on each entry's chunk and cells), the park 2.5 s (all packing), the region store's build 2.2 to
    2.6 s: 1.6 to 1.9 ms an episode, 0.93 ms of it sorting the seed ticks' index. By the TSC the build took 5.4 to
    23 ms an episode: mapping and unmapping the region cache's 10.9 MB image waits on the address space's lock
    against the other workers' faults and madvises. The build runs inside the drain (a falling block's update
    makes the episode's first chunk load).

Kept. Every trajectory and observation digest equals lane/cpubase4's in all six gates (brute16 512x4, 64x1 and
512x4 with resets every 100 steps, 64x1 at w20, the seed set at 64x2 and 256x4) after every kept change and again
in a fresh worktree. A verify build (ticks.h TICKS_VERIFY: the set as it was kept beside as a shadow, every call
run on both and compared, each skipped tick's cells and each kept blob checked) ran six configurations, 1,280 to
7,680 resets and 69 episodes from saved starts, 0 mismatches.

- **The start's pending set as a shared base** (ticks.c, ticks.h, pool.c). A start's list of 4,096 or more loads
  straight into a `ticks_base` in process memory (ticks_load_all: the loader's dedupe, then the set's order), with
  a membership table and each chunk column's indices and edge strips; the twin's load is checked equal and adopts
  it. An env's set is the base from a cursor plus its columns. Nothing but a pop removes an entry
  (getPendingBlockUpdates(chunk, false) copies), so the base's live part is always a suffix, and the drain's batch
  is a pointer into it. The columns never hold the backlog, so neither does the start's image: the spawn start's
  copy is 5,910 pages in 354 runs where it was 7,862 in 457 (-25%), the seed set's 5,358 to 6,590 where they were
  7,298 to 10,031. pool.c counts references: the start, each env since its reset, each saved start (its parent's).
- **Quiet entries skipped** (servertick.c). servertick_base_quiet marks each base entry by what its tick did on
  the start's world: no updateTick (another block there, or air), or a falling block that cannot fall (it
  publishes World.rand and returns), and each entry's run of quiet entries in its chunk. tick_updates skips a run
  while its chunk's wseq is no later than the start world's (every block and light write stamps the chunk), with
  one wseq test, publishing World.rand where the run's ticks would.
- **The start's packed chunks** (serverreplay.c, world.c chunk_pack_as). The start's overworld chunks are packed
  once, in the twin after the pointer scan, with the world's wseq; the park takes a chunk's blob while the chunk
  is unwritten since. 119,680 parks at 200-step episodes took a kept blob, each equal to chunk_pack's bytes.
- **The region store's inputs kept** (serverreplay.c, regioncache.c). The seed ticks' index by chunk is made once
  in the start's image (389 KB more copy for the spawn start, against a 0.93 ms sort an episode). The first
  episode's region cache hit is offered to the start's slot (an atomic swap) and later builds with the same key
  borrow it, instead of mkdir, open, mmap, parse, munmap and a stats.tsv line each episode.

- **Counted first** (a count build, 64 envs, the first 1,100 steps). An env-step makes 54.6 moves:
  - server livings 17.0, 96% answered by the still-move memo;
  - particles 15.6, the brute's digging, never still;
  - falling gravel 8.5 and its client copies 3.6, the spawn start's cave-in;
  - client living copies 5.6;
  - the players 3.0;
  - items 1.4.

  It makes 37.6 collision queries of 4.3 cells and 0.47 boxes each, and 609 chunk lookups (79% from the near cache;
  the misses mostly chunks not loaded, from the scheduled ticks). A timing build put the move at about 17k cycles an
  env-step: the falling blocks 8.0k at 240 cycles a move, the particles 4.0k, the livings 3.8k. Many small moves,
  none hiding an outsized cost. Only 0.9 queries an env-step met the same cells and stamps as their entity's last,
  too few for a box-list memo.
- **The fire test from the cell pass** (entity.c). World.func_147470_e reads the pass's cells (the same floors,
  when the box's ends + 1 round as the pass's do). A pass that met no callback, with the world's wseq unchanged,
  answers it; a burning cell still needs the fire test's own chunk box loaded. The pass reads metadata only for the
  cauldron, and skips air's empty callback.
- **Water tests from a world memo** (world.h struct water_memo, world.c, player.c, item_entity.c).
  handleMaterialAcceleration's found and the flows' sum depend only on its cells and the cells one around them. They
  are kept with the cells' box, map_ver and the summed wseq of the chunks under them: one slot for the players', four
  by the box's hash for item_entity's water_accelerate (items, orbs, the livings' wet case). The memo is keyed after
  the reads, so a read that loaded a chunk moved map_ver first.
- **The collision scan** (world.c, collide.h). Ids under 32 are inlined from collide_add_boxes_id's switch: a null
  box adds and reads nothing, and a plain id is the cell's integer cube (every plain id under 32 is collidable with
  the full cube's bounds). A column's band is found once for its 16 cells, and an empty band is skipped. add_query
  is inline.
- **Lookups and memo tests inline.** chunk_find_ref's near check is inline in world_chunk, world_chunk_loaded,
  world_check_chunks_exist and the scan, with the probe out of line. A chunk not loaded is remembered in its empty
  near slot until map_ver moves. cell_memo_hold's held case is inline in entity.h, word by word. A first version
  copied the boxes to arrays, which compiled to two rep movsl, 8.6% of entity_move_memo's cycles. The move takes its
  scratch list only when it collides.

  lookups once the kept window skips them).

  ticks), the cells within 15 are 31 x 31 columns of 32 bits; rows outside y 0..255 are 0, as their reads are air.

## 2026-10-30 The native trainer end to end: ntloop with the native actor and learner, the env's own speed, 1.10x fastppo.py (lane/ntwire)

SPEC item 6, a's loop with b's learner (the step before c). `out/runtime/train/ntloop` is the trainer, with no Python
in the loop. `--policy actor` (and any `--run FILE`) launches lane ntactor's nt_actor_step from the loop's policy
launch. Each group has its own workspace and RNG stream on its own stream, and logp and value go into the group's
segment. Lane ntlearn's ntl_update trains each group's segment at the brute recipe (T 64, a group of 128, one
minibatch of 8192, 3 epochs, lr 3e-4, gamma 0.998, lam 0.95, clip 0.2, vf 0.5, ent 0.003, Adam eps 1e-5, grad clip
0.5). It runs one update at a time on its own stream: fastppo's job queue.

- **The refresh order.** fastppo's learner writes its weights into a shadow once the loop has taken the last ones
  (event `taken`), then sets `fresh` after the update has finished on the device. The loop copies the shadow into
  the actor before the next group's ActorStep, and groups in flight keep the old weights. ntloop keeps two actor
  images instead of a copy. A gather kernel on the learner's stream writes the image not in use once every group
  launched so far is done with it, and the first group launched after the refresh has run switches to it.
- **Wrapping actor.h.** actor.h has no reload, so `train/trainer.cu` compiles actor.cu for its private image. The map
  from image slots to the learner's layout is probed once from nt_actor_load_blob (three probe blobs, each weight's
  index in base-256 digits, exact in fp32 and bf16). lane ntwidth owns actor.h; an `nt_actor_reload` there would
  remove the include.
- **The run file and the outputs.** `--run FILE`'s policy part is read in worldconf.c's grammar: ppo, run,
  actions.macros, net.kind, and starts.archive with its items, pool and share (fastppo's --save-starts, which the flag
  also takes). starts.seeds is held to the sim's own seed and starts.window is refused. Checkpoints are net.h .ntw:
  model.ntw with its Adam moments and step at the end, model-MMM.ntw with --save-every, and `--init` from any .ntw,
  for example a fastppo model through `ntref.py export`. iters.jsonl carries fastppo's learner fields (loss, pg, vl,
  ent, kl, clipfrac, ref_kl), its bookkeeping, and own_starts when the archive is on.
- **Gates 1 and 2,** `make -C csrc/runtime train-wire-check` (12 s in a fresh worktree after master, 0c65c070).
  `--check-learn` feeds learn_check's fixture through the loop's path, fp32 and bf16: weights, both Adam moments and
  the books are bit for bit equal to the learner called as learn_check calls it, and the refreshed image is 0 bytes
  from a fresh load. `--check-actor` feeds actor_check's batch through launch(): 0 of 4096 actions differ, loaded and
  refreshed, in fp32 (bf16 44 of 4096, measured, not gated). train-loop-check: the stand-in's digest
  486fdf7386b0ea68 is unchanged, host and device cast, depth 0 and 1. train-learn-check and train-actor-check
  PASS.
- **Gate 3, throughput.** brute16 at 16x16, host cast, 512 envs in 4 groups; gpuq bench windows, 3:45 to 3:49 pm.
  - In one process (`--ab --ab-a loop`, 16 stretches of 100 group steps, both orders, twice), the trainer runs at
    98.5%, 101.8%, 100.9% and 100.8% of ntloop's stand-in (the quads' medians). The learner costs the env nothing
    measurable.
  - As separate processes from one init, interleaved: the trainer 150.1k, 151.2k, 149.9k and 151.2k env-steps/s
    (windows p1 and p3); the stand-in alone 150.3k to 151.3k; fastppo.py --bench 135.3k to 136.5k over six runs.

  (lane/cpubase12's engine: 269k at 512x4). wm 4 and wm 8 are GPU-bound, and the stem nets beat the 64x64 env's 92 to
  107k.
- **What paid** (out/perf/ntwidth.tsv: 12 attempts, each A/B interleaved in one window):
  - The actor's gemm_mma got FM x FN warp tiles, with each variant's tiles from a 24-configuration sweep and nsys per
    layer. At B 128: wm 8 913 to 369 us, wm 4 260 to 131, s2 279 to 186.
  - In the learner's bf16 path the stem runs on the tensor cores from the bytes (lane/ntlearn's conv1 kernels at the
    stem's geometry): s1 57.4 to 46.7 ms.
  - conv1 over the stem became implicit GEMMs, with no 1 GB im2col, no da1 and no col2im. k_stem_mma writes
    relu(x0 + b0) padded, so conv1's A is plain cp.async. k_igemm (cp.async, ldmatrix, mma.sync, with a loader and an
    output functor) runs the forward. k_cwgrad runs the weight gradient over row slices, summed in order. k_c1dx runs
    the input gradient by input parity from a staged dx1 map. Together: s1 to 33.7, s2 74.1 to 62.9.
  - conv2's input gradient by parity (C1 <= 128), and its forward and weight gradient over relu(x1 + b1) padded
    (C2 <= 128): w2 14.2 to 12.8.
  - relu' is read from the padded post-activations (h > 0 exactly where x + b > 0), so the stem nets keep neither x0
    nor x1.
  - k_c1dx went to a sample a block and two tiles a warp.
  - Final: s1 25.8 ms, s2 54.1.
- **What did not:** the weight gradients as row slices (cuBLAS already splits K: slower at every variant). conv2's
  implicit GEMMs at wm 4 and wm 8, where cutlass runs at 74 TFLOPS and k_igemm at 58 to 61: wm 4 lost 7.2% and wm 8
  5.4%, so NTL_IC2 and NTL_IC2X switch them off there. k_igemm's other tiles and a 3- or 4-stage k_igemm3: none
  faster. heads_draw at fewer samples a block: within noise, because every block reads the whole heads matrix.
- **Left:** wm 4 and wm 8 are GPU-bound with their GEMMs near cuBLAS's 82 to 91% of the tensor peak; the waste left
  is conv2's forward im2col and conv3's im2col and col2im (no implicit path for the 3x3 conv yet), which needs an
  implicit GEMM as good as cutlass's. In the stem nets, computing the stem inside conv1's GEMM would remove h0's
  0.3 GB an epoch. The wide actor is launch-bound (six dependent kernels at under a wave each), and a tensor-core
  heads GEMM is its next step. fp32 stays im2col and cuBLAS at every variant (the gate's reference).

## 2026-10-29 The native learner: fastppo's update in CUDA, 4.49 ms in bf16 against PyTorch's captured 9.38, held to it within stated tolerances (lane/ntlearn)

SPEC item 6b. `csrc/runtime/train/learn.{cu,h}` is fastppo.py's Learner for the feed-forward net as a C API over
device buffers: `ntl_gae` (_gae: rewards over the scale, the discounted advantages and returns, the mask of the steps the
policy drove, the advantages normalised over them), `ntl_forward`, `ntl_grad` (one minibatch's forward, _part's loss:
the clipped policy term and the entropy over the masked steps, the value term over all, and its backward into a
gradient buffer, with the books), `ntl_adam` (clip_grad_norm_ 0.5 and torch's fused Adam) and `ntl_update` (GAE, then
3 epochs of each epoch's minibatch order), the whole update one CUDA graph. The parameters are one flat fp32 buffer,
with the three heads as one [97][256] matrix (`ntl_from_ntw`/`ntl_to_ntw` convert net.h's blob). NTL_FP32 is the gate.
NTL_BF16 is fastppo's --amp bf16: activations, their gradients and a weight copy in bf16, every GEMM accumulating in
fp32, and the loss, the weight gradients and Adam in fp32. NTL_TF32 is an option. In bf16 the three convolutions are
hand-written mma.sync m16n8k16 kernels with no im2col or col2im. conv1 reads the observation bytes. conv2 and conv3
read the layer before with bias and relu applied as they load. Their input gradients go by stride parity class, and
their weight gradients are staged through shared memory with block partials summed in a fixed order. fc1, fc2 and the
heads stay on cuBLAS. The loss runs a warp a sample.

- **The reference:** `scripts/ntref.py learner` on mcsr-brute's branch ntlearn (7b1b36d) runs fastppo's own _gae, _part
  and _step in fp32 (autocast and TF32 off, no graph) and writes ~/.cache/netherite-native/learn-a05-070 (23 MB). It
  holds round 10's a05 weights at 70 minutes, a synthetic segment shaped like a real one (64 x 128, actions from the net's
  own logits, noisy actor logp and value so some ratios clip, sparse rewards, dones, masked macro runs), and Adam warmed
  3 steps. It also stores every intermediate through the weights after the whole update, the reference's own spread
  (a second GPU run with cuDNN autotuned, and a CPU run), and fastppo's bf16 learner's error against fp32.
- **The gate**, `make -C csrc/runtime train-learn-check`, about 1 s. fp32: every tensor's max relative error (floor 1e-3
  of its largest entry, 1e-2 for Adam's steps) within 5x the reference's own worst GPU-against-CPU movement for its
  class, and GAE bit for bit. In a fresh worktree after merging master the worst gradient is 1.7e-6 normwise and the
  worst Adam step 7.2e-6: PASS. `--prec bf16`: each tensor's normwise error at most 1.25x fastppo's own bf16 learner's
  on that tensor. The worst gradient is 0.128 against its 0.149, the worst step 0.125 against 0.144 (conv1's weight
  gradient 0.129 against 0.149, conv2's 0.095 against 0.112, conv3's 0.055 against 0.076): PASS. Floating point, so
  never bit-identical.
- **Speed**, the dev host's 3090, one update of the brute recipe (3 epochs of 8192), CUDA events, 20 updates a run.
  fastppo's Learner as a run builds it (compile max, bf16, CUDA graphs; `ntref.py bench`) took 9.38 to 9.78 ms. Ours
  went from 16.2 ms in fp32 (im2col and cuBLAS SGEMMs) to 8.66 in bf16 on the same GEMMs, then 4.487 and 4.485 ms
  (the final head against v12's 4.799 and 4.562, interleaved in one quiet bench window on the 30th, within-run spread
  under 0.5%). That is 5.48M samples trained a second. fp32 is 14.36 ms. Against fastppo it is 2.09x, rough: its
  baseline was measured in an earlier window, and its 38.6 s setup does not fit the 10 s window rule.
- **What paid** (bf16, after/before interleaved; out/perf/ntlearn.tsv has all 20 attempts): every GEMM dimension a
  multiple of 8 (cuBLAS had picked align1 kernels; fc1's weight gradient took 151 us a step), 0.85 to 0.88. conv1 on
  the tensor cores from the bytes, 0.89 to 0.91. conv2's input gradient by parity with its weights padded to 36-word
  rows, 0.91 to 0.94 (unpadded, 8-way bank conflicts made it slower than cuBLAS and col2im). GAE's columns staged in
  shared memory, 0.94 to 0.96 (the walk's 64 dependent loads took 180 us). conv2's forward and weight gradient without
  im2col, 0.78 to 0.84, but only once the weight gradient staged through shared memory: from global memory it ran
  668 us a step and lost. conv3's input-gradient weights in shared memory, 0.93 to 0.98.
- **What did not:** a direct (non-tensor-core) conv1 was 1.15x slower. The loss a warp a sample, conv1's kernels
  through shared memory, and two samples a conv2 input-gradient tile were all inside the noise.
- **Where the time is now** (nsys over the last version, shares only, the 3090 shared with a game in that run): conv2's
  input gradient 24%, its forward 13%, conv3's input gradient 10%, conv2's weight gradient 9%, every cuBLAS GEMM 11.6%.
  conv2 is half the update. At 157k env-steps/s the env takes about 52 ms to make the 8192 samples one update trains
  on, so the learner at 4.49 ms is under a tenth of that.
- Widths: the fp32 path follows net.h. The bf16 convolutions' tiles and paddings are written for 16x16x3 and 32/64/64
  channels, and a static_assert in learn.cu stops a wider net at the build. A later width lane revisits the paddings,
  which follow a rule (a row's words mod 32 = 4).
- Merging master: loop.mk (lane/ntloop) also defines `NTL_OUT`. Included after learn.mk, it moved learn.mk's link
  input to loopcheck/, and a fresh tree failed to link learn_check. learn.mk's internal variables are now `LRN_OUT` and
  `LRN_DIR`.

## 2026-10-29 The actor's forward and sampler as CUDA kernels: 4.2x faster than PyTorch's bf16 actor at B 128, fp32 within 1.6e-5 of the reference (lane/ntactor)

SPEC item 6a, the kernel half. `csrc/runtime/train/actor.h` and `actor.cu` take a group's raw cast bytes
[B][16][16][3] uint8 and its scalars [B][155] on the device, plus a stream. They write the action [B][16], logp,
value and optionally the logits. The noise comes from a device RNG whose counter lives on the device, so a captured
graph replays with fresh noise, or from the caller's uniforms. A call is six kernels: conv1 (with the uint8 decode,
and the scalars copied into fc1's padded row), conv2, conv3, fc1, fc2, then heads_draw (the three heads, the gumbel
sampler and logp). The convolutions are implicit-im2col GEMMs over the batch, with channels-last padded activations.
The fp32 path uses register-tiled FFMA with the k split inside the block and chunks double-buffered in registers. The
bf16 path uses mma.sync m16n8k16, with bf16 activations, the whole K of a tile in one cp.async round, and the weights
reordered at load into fragment order and held in registers. `actor.mk` provides `train-actor`, `train-actor-check`
and `train-actor-bench` (out/runtime/train/), and csrc/runtime/Makefile's `train/*.mk` wildcard includes it.

- **The gate:** `make -C csrc/runtime train-actor-check` runs mcsr-speedrun's ntref.py fixture
  (~/.cache/netherite-native/actor-a05-070, 4096 samples) through the fp32 path. Logits differ by at most 1.53e-5,
  value 8.3e-7, and logp 1e-5; 0 of 4096 actions differ, with 0 near ties under 1e-4. The device RNG's draws pass a
  frequency check (keys z 0.91, camera bins' mean z 0.41) and repeat for a seed. bf16 is measured, not gated: logits
  0.088 / 0.092, value 0.0097, and 1.07% of actions differ. PyTorch's own bf16 actor on the same fixture: 0.131 /
  0.193, 0.0123, 2.27%. The gate takes about 2 s, and a fresh worktree builds in 1.7 s.
- **Speed** (2026-10-30 2:46 pm, one bench window, two runs each interleaved, device time a graph replay, the median
  of 300):

| actor | B 128 (us) | B 512 (us) |
|---|---|---|
| fastppo.py's ActorStep, bf16 CUDA graph | 140.3, 140.3 | 173.1, 173.1 |
| ours fp32 | 51.2, 47.1 | 139.3, 131.1 |
| ours bf16 | 33.8, 33.8 | 78.8, 78.8 |

- What it means (a projection): at 300k env-steps/s in groups of 128, the actor keeps the 3090 busy 7.9% of the time
  in bf16 and 11 to 12% in fp32, where torch's actor needs 33%.
- What did not pay (out/perf/ntactor.tsv has every row):
  - cublasSgemm on the fc shapes: 12.1 and 10.2 us against ours, 8.2 and 5.2.
  - Eleven tile variants for load balance: the best was within the base's 1.2 us spread.
  - The MLP tail fused into one kernel: 58 us against 53, because 830 KB of weights cannot be streamed into one SM
    fast enough.
  - bf16 conv3 and fc1 in one chunk: slower.
  - What did pay: padded channels-last activations (97 to 51 us), the heads fused with the sampler, register
    double-buffering, mma.sync, and the weights in registers (bf16 40 to 34 us).
- Next (not done): the fp32 kernels are bound by latency and L2 traffic, not FMAs. The 123.5 M MAC are 6.9 us of FFMA
  peak inside about 50 us. An outside review (Fable) proposes running conv2 as a direct convolution from a resident
  padded tile, with conv1 folded into conv2's prologue, and splitting K across blocks with a fixed-order reduce for
  conv3 and the fc layers. Its projection is 17 to 20 us fp32. The bf16 layers' K follows net.h. F1K, the fp32 chunks
  and NT_HP are still tuned for today's widths and are held by static_asserts. Lane ntloop's policy launch is where
  `nt_actor_step` plugs in.

## 2026-10-29 The native loop: vec_bench's trajectory digest exactly, the env's speed with the cast on the host, and 3 to 13% faster with the cast on the device pipelined (lane/ntloop)

SPEC item 6a's loop half. `out/runtime/train/ntloop` (csrc/runtime/train/loop.c, loop.cu, loop.h, loop.mk) drives libnwrl's
vector env the way the native trainer will, with no Python. A group gets its own stream when recv returns it. On that
stream: the cast (`nwrl_vec_cast` with engine.raycast device) or the host cast's bytes, and the scalars, copied from
page-locked memory into the group's double-buffered [T] segment. Then the policy is launched (loop.h, a launch over a
group's device buffers: vec_bench's stand-in on the device, or a no-op), the actions are copied back and an event is
recorded. Every group whose event has fired is sent before the next recv, with at most `--depth` groups launched and
unsent. The loop also keeps fastppo.py's reward-scale books (the running return and its Welford spread), the reward,
end and driver of each step in the segment, and episodes.jsonl and iters.jsonl in fastppo.py's format (keys and order
as a fastppo run's rows; the learner's fields are lane ntlearn's).

- **Exact:** with the stand-in, the trajectory digest equals `vec_bench --digest`'s on the same config, envs, groups and
  steps, with the cast on the host and on the device, at depth 0 and 1 (`make -C csrc/runtime train-loop-check`,
  486fdf7386b0ea68, 5.2 s, gpuq.sh check).
- **The comparison is in one process.** Two processes in one bench window measured the same vec_bench at 81.6k and
  118.4k env-steps/s (the first one's cold start). `ntloop --ab R` runs one vector env through 200 group steps a group,
  then alternates vec_bench's own loop (A: its stand-in drawn on the host, each group sent as soon as recv returns it)
  and this loop (B) in stretches of 50 group steps a group, A B B A, six quads. The env's own step cost drifts with the
  game (the workers' 0.11 to 0.18 ms an env-step) and spikes about 900 ticks in (0.34 ms; it follows the slot when the
  order is swapped, so it is the trajectory, likely the integrated server's periodic save). So the gate's figure is the
  median of the quads' ratios, and both orders are run.
- **Same work across configs:** A always draws from the host's xorshift and B from the device's, both seeded as
  vec_bench seeds them. So the host cast in A B B A and the device cast in B A A B play the same draws at the same
  slots; since the two casts are bit-identical, both processes play one trajectory. The save spike lands on the same
  stretches in both, which confirms it.

512 envs, 4 groups, 30 workers, brute16 (16x16 RGB, `--macros 63`), the dev host's 3090, one bench window each,
7:00 to 7:13 pm (out/perf/ntloop.tsv has every row):

| loop | cast | ntloop against vec_bench's loop, the quads' median (both orders' means) | the main thread a group step: own work, waiting on the device |
|---|---|---|---|
| depth 0 | host | 101.4%, 97.0% (99.4%) | 0.052 to 0.056 ms, 0.048 ms (vec_bench's loop 0.032 ms, none) |
| depth 1 | host | 97.6%, 98.6% (97.7%) | 0.055 ms, 0.002 ms |
| depth 0, no-op policy | host | 100.7% | 0.051 ms, 0.044 ms |
| depth 0 | device | 95.8% (fails the gate) | 0.099 ms, 0.567 ms (vec_bench's loop waits 0.625 ms in send) |
| depth 1 | device | 113.1%, 107.8% (108.6%) | 0.11 to 0.12 ms, 0.17 to 0.20 ms |
| depth 2 / 3 | device | 106.6%, 102.9% (103.1%) / 107.4% | 0.11 ms, 0.029 ms (depth 2) |

- With the cast on the host the loop runs at the env's speed: 97.0 to 101.4% of vec_bench's loop, the noise about ±2%.
  Its own work is 0.05 ms of the main thread a group step: 0.018 ms enqueuing the copies (no-op policy), 4 us more for
  the stand-in's launch. At depth 0 it then waits 0.044 to 0.048 ms on the copies' round trip, and depth 1 removes that
  wait. The main thread is busy 7 to 9% of the window (vec_bench's loop 4 to 6%).
- With the cast on the device the loop is what makes the cast pay. vec_bench's loop and the Python trainer wait on it in
  `nwrl_vec_send` (0.625 ms a group step, the main thread 81 to 95% busy). At depth 1 the next group is taken while the
  last one's cast runs: the workers step 27.8 of 30 on average against 24.2. On the same work (12 stretches, one window)
  it ran 104.4% and 112.6% of the host cast with vec_bench's loop: 197.2k and 196.4k against 188.9k and 174.5k (the host
  baseline moved 8% between windows; the device side's did not).
- Depth 2 and 3 and 8 groups of 64 gained nothing (device against device on the same draws, one window, both run
  orders: depth 2 = depth 1, 8 groups about 2% under 4 within the noise; the second run of a window is about 2% faster).
  At 8 groups the main thread waits on the device 61% of the window. What is left is the cast's own latency, about
  0.52 ms a group of 128 (0.567 ms waited at depth 0 less the copies' 0.048), which the loop can only hide by taking other groups meanwhile. recv blocks, so the loop has
  to choose before it calls it.
- Proposals (not done: vecenv.c and rlbind.c are not this lane's): `nwrl_vec_try_recv`, recv without the wait (-2 when no
  group is ready; pipe_poll_some with min 0 already returns at once), so the loop can serve the env and the device as
  either finishes; rcdev_launch's host side (0.04 to 0.05 ms more of the main thread a group than the host cast's staging: packing the records) on the worker
  that synced them (lane rcpipe's area); the ray cast's texture root found as checkpoint_resolve finds the start (the
  library's tree), not the config's directory: the shared ~/.cache/netherite-native/brute16.yaml fails from any tree
  ("no block table or atlas in ~/.cache/netherite-native/out/java/render"), so train/loop.mk copies it beside links
  to the tree's out/assets and out/java/render.

In a fresh worktree of the branch after merging master (out/java and out/assets linked, as the merge trial does):
train-loop-check PASS; train-loop-bench PASS, the host cast at depth 0 97.6%, the device cast at depth 1 112.7%.

Next: lane ntactor's forward and sampler through loop.h (the stand-in's slot), then the learner taking the segments
where loop.c counts them. ntloop's --depth defaults to 0 with the cast on the host and 1 on the device, 4 groups.

SPEC item 6d's second lever asked for `client_player_tick`'s thousand-cell loop (WorldClient.doVoidFogParticles and
Block.randomDisplayTick, 14% of the env's samples, lane/envprof) as a train-fast fidelity switch, licensed by a list of
everything that reads the client world's Random. The list (oracle/src and the engine) says no switch is needed:

  nextInt(11)), which session_client_blocks relights in the client world, whose light the cast reads: it reaches the
  observation, and it is drawn after the last tick's fog loop, so the loop's draw count must stay exact; (2) the fog
  loop (six nextInt(16) a cell, an air cell's nextInt(8), past y three nextFloat); (3) RenderGlobal.doSpawnParticle at
  particleSetting 1 (nextInt(3)); (4) lit redstone ore's func_150186_m (18 nextFloat); (5) sound pitches (drink, burp,
  use, explosions, aux 2002) and witchMagic's colour; (6) the dragon egg's client search, the client item-use and
  activation predictions, the client tile entities. None writes server state or feeds a client packet; only (1)
  reaches the observation.
- The display ticks themselves draw var5, a fresh Det.newRandom each tick (its one seeder long is kept), read the
  client world (no_generate: no load, no write), play sounds (pitched on var5) and spawn particles. At particleSetting
  2 (minimal: the pinned profile's and every training start's; gold-g1-s42 records `particles: 2`)
  doSpawnParticle returns before any FX constructor (RenderGlobal.java 2085 to 2122): no client entity id, no seeder
  or UUID longs, no Math.random. Only lit redstone ore draws the world's Random.

So at minimal the loop's only effect is its draws on WorldClient.rand, and `cp_void_fog_minimal` (player.c) runs just
those: the six coordinate draws of a cell from its start seed at once (the LCG's k steps as s * A[k] + C[k]), the
cells' 27 bands resolved once a tick (chunkscan_block for a chunk not loaded or a band past id 255), the air test, the
roll, lit ore's 18 steps. Rows exact, d.cw, d.cseed and d.cmath included; settings 0 and 1 run the loop as before. The
loop's remaining cost cannot be switched off without moving the cast (lane/fastcast: 0.51% of casts differ), so no
`fidelity.*` key was added.

Measured (gold-g1-s42, test_snapshots --phase-profile, the client tick C2): 24.3 to 26.9 us a tick before, 18.5 and

8e27b5d67bd2de04 on every run. A latency-bound loop's sample share overstates its cost at 30 workers on 16 cores: its

## 2026-10-29 No Python in the training loop: every piece of Python on the path, what it costs, and the native trainer's plan (lane/native)

Elliot: "the point was never to use a Python trainer. The point was to use everything with minimal overhead, with the
custom already fastest kernels, and if none are available then we write them ourselves. Anything here that's using
Python glue needs to be re-evaluated." Decided (SPEC.md Decisions, GOAL.md Constraint): the trainer goes native.

The env with a C loop and no Python (vec_bench, scratch brute16.yaml, 512 envs, 30 workers, `--macros 63`, 180 s
episodes, the dev host idle, 3:39 to 3:46 pm), the cast on the host against the device (out/demo/brute16dev.yaml):

| cast | groups | env-steps/s | the workers' step an env-step | the main thread waiting in recv |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| host | 4 | 157,533; 156,463 | 0.176, 0.177 ms | 97%, 96% |
| device | 4 | 149,341; 149,330 | 0.158, 0.159 ms | 21%, 20% |
| device | 2 | 144,727 | 0.162 ms | 44% |

The device cast takes 10% off the workers' step but nwrl_vec_send launches it and waits, so even a C loop's main
thread is 80% busy and the whole runs 5% slower: the integration is serial, whatever language drives it. The
Python trainer on the same sim ran 130k to 144k (lane/rcab), 8 to 17% under the C loop (rough: separate runs).

Python on the training path today (mcsr-speedrun, branch brute), with the verdict:

- **The loop** (fastppo.py's main thread: recv and send of each 128-env group, the copies, graph replays, rewards,
  returns, episode records): about 0.29 ms of Python a group step at 140k (host 2.2, launch 3.0, sync 0.9, send 1.2,
  tail 2.2 s of each 30 s window); with the cast on the device, 27 of 30 s busy. Native.
- **The actor** (one CUDA graph a group: decode, the forward in bf16, sampling): the GPU's kernels are torch's, but
  for a 0.27M-parameter net they are launch- and occupancy-bound: 17 s of device time a minute at 157k env-steps/s
  for about 0.3 TFLOP/s of work (157k x 1.9 MFLOP a sample). Native, fused kernels.
- **The learner** (a Python thread replaying captured graphs: cuDNN convolutions, torch.compile's Triton GEMMs,
  fused Adam): 9.5 s of device time a minute at 157k, coordinated through Python queues and events. Native, fused
  kernels, cuBLAS where it measures faster.
- **The bindings** (vecenv.py and nwrl.py over ctypes): microseconds a call; gone with the native loop.
- **Setup** (runconf.py's run-file parse, seedset.py's start capture through the oracle, reward tables built in
  Python by default where C has an equal table): once a run, no throughput cost; moves into the native trainer
  (worldconf.c's parser, C's own tables); seed capture is a call to the Java oracle either way.
- **Kept, with the reason:** the analysis and report tools (armstat, curves.py, charts.py, the demo page's builder,
  cmp.py; out of the loop, reading the JSONL files after a run, and outside this repo by its no-Python rule), and
  fastppo.py frozen as the native trainer's reference: its loss, gradients and Adam step on stored batches are what
  the native kernels are held to, as the Java client is for the C engine. It is not run for training.

The plan is SPEC.md's item 6 of "The environment as configuration": the loop and actor (groups pipelined, the
forward and sampling fused, held to vec_bench's env-steps/s), the learner (held to fastppo.py's gradients), end to
end (held to its learning curves on three trainer seeds), then the device cast pipelined and the display ticks.

The trainer's loop, seconds of a 30-second window at minute 3 to 5 (host 1 and 2, device 1 and 2): waiting in recv
for the env 22.6, 22.8 against 14.3, 13.7; sync 0.9, 0.9 against 9.1, 9.7; the loop's tail 2.2, 2.2 against 10.7,
11.3 (host, launch and send unchanged, 6.3 to 6.9). The workers are freed, but the single main thread is then busy
about 27 of 30 seconds, waiting on the device's cast in sync and doing more in its tail. On the GPU host at 32x32
(2026-10-23) the cast was 66% of the workers' cycles and moving it gained 82%; at 16x16 it is 15%, less than the
main thread's new cost. So at 16x16 the env bounds training with the main thread close behind: a faster env needs
the main thread's per-group work cut too (two groups of 256 halve its group steps; lane/rcdev measured +23% from
that at 32x32), which is where the next measurement goes.

## 2026-10-29 Where training time goes on the 3090: the env's CPU, not the policy; a third of it is the observation's cast and the client's display ticks (lane/envprof)

Elliot asked whether training is bound by the policy or the environment, and what in the environment. Measured on the
dev host idle (out/demo/prof.sh; scratch prof/): G3's recipe with the archive from scratch on the 3090 (scratch
brute16.yaml, 512 envs in 4 groups, 30 workers, 180 s episodes, 16x16 RGB ray cast on the host), perf on the whole
process for 60 s from minute 2 at 499 Hz; then vec_bench on the same sim (its stand-in policy, `--macros 63`, 180 s
episodes), perf the same way.

- **The env bounds it.** vec_bench alone: 155,813 env-steps/s, the workers' step 0.1775 ms an env-step (30 workers:
  169k at most). Training: 136k to 140k at minutes 4-5 here, 150k to 168k in xnoarch's later minutes, so 87 to 100%
  of the env alone. xnoarch's loop (60 s windows at 157k): 42.7 s waiting in recv for the env, 23 s of its own work
  (host 4.9, launch 6.6, sync 2.8, send 2.8, tail 5.9); the actor's device time 17.0 s and the learner's 9.5 s, so
  the GPU is busy at most about 40% and the main thread about 35%. perf: 791K samples in 60 s, 26.4 of the 32
  hardware threads busy on average; Python and torch together under 0.5% of them.
- **Inside the env** (% of the training process's samples; vec_bench alone in brackets): the server's game tick 42.0
  (44.9: chunk updates and scheduled ticks, entity movement and collision, mob AI, combat and tracking, world.c's
  chunk lookups); the observation's ray cast 15.2 (20.0; `cast`, 256 rays a step walking cells out to 64 blocks);
  the client's display ticks 14.2 (13.1; `client_player_tick`, player.c's loop over 1,000 random cells within 16
  blocks every tick, vanilla's doVoidFogParticles and randomDisplayTick: six or more serial Java-Random draws a cell,
  kept so the client world's Random stays Java's; 47% of the function's samples are on jrand.h's lines); kernel and
  unresolved 11.5 (8.8); the vector env, macros and the archive's saves 5.9 (2.4; `start_scan` 3.4, making a saved
  start's image); per-tick rows and the replay's bookkeeping 5.5 (5.4; `session_row` 2.2); libc 2.0 (2.8); the
  client's other work 1.8 (1.6).
- Levers, not yet measured here: the cast on the device (`engine.raycast: device`, lane/rcdev: +82% at 32x32 on the
  GPU host, 2026-10-23; the 16x16 configs cast on the host), and the client's display ticks skipped at train-fast
  fidelity if nothing the player sees or the rows check depends on that Random (to be proved against the oracle).
  Together about 29% of the samples: at most 1.4x (a projection). Past that the next walls are the main thread (35%
  busy) and the GPU (40%).
- GOAL.md records Elliot's route (macros generating labelled data, a model cloned down to the raw keyboard and mouse,
  RL on top). The labels for our own data exist already: the vector env records the act each tick became, macros'
  screen clicks included (`acts`; lane/tape writes them as the client's script); the raw action space still lacks the
  hotbar, inventory key and clicks (GOAL item 3), and a model much larger than 0.27M parameters moves the bound to
  the GPU.

## 2026-10-27 A thousand seeds: the mix's starts loaded a window at a time (lane/seedwin)

GOAL item 2 asks for a thousand seeds; lane/seeds loaded every start of the mix at the make, one after another. A seed's
start is about 50 MB resident at train-fast (vec_bench, 32 envs: 99 seeds' starts all loaded peaked at 6.9 GB, 2.5 GB
with at most 16 loaded), so a thousand would be about 50 GB beside the envs, and the 99 took 65 s to load on the GPU
host. Now (API 11):

- `nwrl_vec_opts.start_window` W and `start_stride` S (0: W/2): a group's r-th reset (its round; the make's draws
  round 0) draws from the mix's starts `(r * S + j) mod nstarts`, j < W, the make's start keeping its share, the mix's
  weighted equally (other weights refused). Only the rounds in flight have their starts loaded: the next round's load
  in the background on the pool's workers (`pool_start_load_bg`, a J_LOADBG job made as a save is, `making` until it is
  done; `nwrl_start_load_bg`), and a start no round in flight draws is freed once no env plays from it (lane/evict's
  start_held). An env's draw depends on its own state and its group's round only, so the trajectories are the same at
  any grouping and workers. `nwrl_vec_window` counts the loads, the frees, the starts loaded and the lowest round.
- Without a window the mix's starts now load at once on the workers: 99 in 5.9 s on the dev host (vec_bench, 16
  workers, beside G2; 65 s one at a time on the GPU host, so the ratio is rough).
- The episode record's start is the mix's index as before (1 + k for starts[k], nstarts + 1 a saved one), now kept per
  env (`vec_env.scat`) since a window's binding starts are not the mix's indices.
- Checked: `make -C csrc/runtime rl-window-gate` (32 envs, 99 seeds, ten rounds of 200-step episodes, window 8 stride 4:
  digest 28eecde88f0933ce at 2 and at 4 groups, the 44 starts those rounds name played, 52 loads, at most 16 loaded);
  without a window the lane's digest equals master's (vec_bench, configs/brute.yaml, 32 envs, 2 groups:
  00263017d6b76276 both).
- mcsr-speedrun's brute branch (worktree branch seedwin): `VecEnv(window=(W, S))`, `fastppo --seed-window W[:S]`, the
  run file's `starts.window` and `starts.window_stride`, `nwrl.py` asserts API 11.
- A seed set with an archive needs lane/replayrung's fix (below). Without an archive or milestone weights (the log cap
  only) the 100-seed run collapsed in its first minutes on the GPU host: entropy 8.4 to 0.8 by 5 minutes, the wooden
  pickaxe 24% to 0.4% (one run).

## 2026-10-27 A save's replays read their rung past the rung array's end (lane/replayrung)

Round 3's seed arm (fastppo `--seeds 1-100` with the milestone archive, 512 envs, 28 workers, the GPU host) segfaulted in
libnwrl three runs out of three within its first two rounds: `slab_alloc` (engine/arena.c:423) once, and under gdb
`within_aabb_peer` (engine/item_entity.c:923: a section's item list held a handle to no entity) from a worker's
`step_job` at server tick 3521. The same seeds without the archive ran 5 minutes with no crash, and with the archive
at 20 workers 6 minutes (about six rounds) with none; `start_gate` passes a seed-7 start's saves at vanilla fidelity.

The cause found by reading what a save's replay touches: `reset_job` sets the env's rung from `p->rung[pe->id]`, and a
save's replay env has id n + 2 slot + which (the views are sized for those, pool.h save_slots), past the n entries
`p->rung` holds. The pool allocates `p->envs` right after `p->rung` (pool_make); where the heap puts them side by side,
past the array lie the next chunk's header and `p->envs[0]`'s first fields, and slot 2's second replay (id n + 5)
reads env 0's `state`, whose ENV_DONE is 2, NW_RUNG_STRIPPED. A replay run stripped (spawning off, no mobs, no random
ticks or weather, applied at its reset) beside its twin run exact gives the save two images of different worlds, from
which the start's pointers are named; envs reset to that start run on a damaged image. Whether a given save meets env
0 done is timing, which fits a crash that is frequent but not certain (not the layout itself: not shown). Now the save
records the env's rung when it is made (its image's cfg.rung) and both replays run at it.

- Checked: the crashing run exactly (512 envs, 28 workers, seeds 1-100, the archive, under gdb) on the fix ran 13.9M
  env-steps in 6.3 minutes, about seven rounds, with no crash, where it had crashed three times in three within about
  2.5M; `start_gate walk:1@200+400` passes on seed 42's and seed 7's starts at vanilla fidelity (the gates never build
  `p->rung`, so they never read past it).
- Every run with an archive since lane/ownstarts read the rung this way; seed 42's runs never crashed from it, and a
  save whose replays disagreed may have entered their pools damaged.

## 2026-10-27 One run as one file: configs/brute.yaml, the brute-force goal's default (lane/runfile)

A from-scratch run is now configured as a PufferLib env is, one file: `configs/brute.yaml`, the run-file grammar
(config.yaml's header; `sim` and `policy` parts). Its sim is train-fast.yaml's world, start, fidelity and 32x32 ray
cast with every part of the sim on the CPU (device_mesh 0, the 3090 the learner's), plus the env's shape in its own
keys (`pipeline.worlds` 512, `groups` 4, `episode_seconds` 180, `performance.workers` 30). Its policy is the trainer's,
the 3090 runs' recipe: `actions` (macros, picks), `starts` (seeds, the archive's kind, items, pool and share), `ppo`,
`net`, `run`. The C side reads sim and skips policy (as it does configs/speedrun-grpo.yaml's); mcsr-speedrun's
`fastppo.py --run FILE` (branch brute, `mcsr/fastrun.py`) takes its flags' values from policy and the env's shape from
sim, a flag on its command line winning, an unknown key an error. Checked: a 16-env bench from it (`--n 16 --threads
2` over the file) made the env from the sim part, and the run's args.json holds the file's values (the macros, the
archive's `ms:...:16:0.4`, lr 3e-4, entropy 0.003, horizon 64, 2 hours).

## 2026-10-27 Seeds as the run's configuration: a seed set drawn at each reset, each seed's start captured once (lane/seeds)

GOAL.md item 2. A run names its world seeds in the trainer's config (mcsr-speedrun branch brute, `fastppo.py
--seeds 42`, `--seeds 1-100`, `--seeds 2,7,42`; `mcsr/seedset.py`), not as a `pipeline.seeds` key: every sim key is
also a key of the Java oracle's registry (WorldConf.java), so the key would be an oracle change for a setting the
oracle never reads (SPEC.md "The environment as configuration" item 3). Each seed's start is the oracle's fresh world
of that seed at its first tick, what `netherite play --seed N` records (`make -C oracle script SEED=N
SCRIPT=tests/fresh-play-s1.jsonl`) with the run config's world section, captured once into

## 2026-10-27 A full start archive drops every new level once its starts are all played; it now retires a played one (lane/evict)

lane/srng made every env draw its own saved start, so with a pool far smaller than the envs (16 against 512) every
start in it is being played at every moment. Both eviction paths let go only a start no env plays from, and
`pool_add_level` (lane/msstarts) dropped the new start when none was free ("the new one alone at its level: kept over
the played" broke out of the search with no victim): from the moment the pool filled, the first furnace, ingot or
iron pickaxe start was let go. Random play on master after lane/srng (scratch `randarch.py`: macros 63, the camera 20
± 20, keys 0.5, pool 16, share 0.5, 20 minutes, 27,136 episodes): a furnace at 71 s and nothing after, 1,369 saves
and only levels 1 and 2 in the pool. Before lane/srng the same run reached an iron ingot at 89 s, because each draw
sent a whole group to one start and most of the pool sat unplayed.

Now a full pool lets go the oldest start of its most kept level, never a level's last, an unplayed one first and else
a played one, retired: out of the draws at once, its image freed (`nwrl_start_free`) once no env plays from it and
no save being made replays from it (`retire_sweep` at each receive, `start_held`). The retired list takes what the
address window leaves past the pool, at most 64. The first try freed a retired start while a save still replayed its
env's acts from it: a segfault in the replay's tick (`ticks.c:327`, `heap_push`) after a minute; each save now records
its source start (`pending_src`). The plain own-start path (`save_item` > 0) retires the oldest the same way.

The same random play on it, 15 minutes, 22,016 episodes, 89,497 env-steps/s (the mirror nightly on the host), no
crash: a wooden pickaxe at 21 s, stone pickaxe and furnace at 43 s, an iron ingot at 86 s, and **an iron pickaxe at
886 s, random play's first**; 1,042 saves, every level 1 to 4 in the pool. By the level an episode started at:

## 2026-10-27 The vector env is reproducible at any grouping and workers; vec_bench's digest was not (lane/digest)

lane/picks reported 4 groups on 8 workers giving a new trajectory digest every run. The cause was vec_bench: it ran
`(warm + steps) * groups` receives in total, and recv returns whichever group is ready, so with several groups on
several workers each group got its own number of receives and each env's hash covered its own number of steps. With
`--digest` or `--picks` each group now runs exactly `warm + steps` receives (a group done is not sent again; without
them the bench's loop is as before). 16 envs, 300 steps, configs/tape-gate.yaml: 4 groups on 8 workers twice, 4 on
1 and 1 on 8 all give 5a65798f05bee6fb; 64 envs in 4 groups on 16 workers with random picks over an episode end
(1,300 steps of 60 s episodes) gave 25c5e1ec7b6a38e2 twice, the same 1,514 items crafted both times.

## 2026-10-27 The craft macro as the policy's choice: one masked pick a recipe (lane/picks)

GOAL.md item 3's first step. Until now every macro but the mine lock started on the state (`macro_start`: the craft
macro whenever `craft_plan` had a plan, every 5 steps), so a random policy "crafted" because the environment did.
With `nwrl_vec_opts.picks` 1 (API 10) the craft macro's plans are the policy's, Craftax's way: one pick a recipe
(`NWRL_VEC_PICKS` 20: 0 none, then planks, table, stick, the wooden and stone pickaxes, furnace, smelt, the iron
pickaxe, bucket, flint and steel, the diamond pickaxe, blaze powder, eyes, the bucket's fill and cast, portal, frame,
throw, take; `nwrl_vec_pick_name`). Each step the trainer writes a pick to `bufs.picks`; `bufs.mask` [n][20] says
which the next action may take: `plan_ok`, `craft_plan`'s conditions without its order or its wants (the parts
held, the table or furnace at hand, the plan's macro switch on; a second table, planks past 12 or a worse pickaxe are
the policy's business), only while no macro runs, none always. A pick the mask allowed starts the craft macro on that
plan when no other macro starts first, and that step counts as the policy's (`bufs.chosen` 1, `driver` 0, as the mine
lock's own attack), so the learner credits the pick; the craft macro never starts on its own, and the strip mine
yields to a pick instead of to `craft_plan`. Throw stays the throw key's (never allowed as a pick). Picks off is the
old code path.

- `make -C csrc/runtime rl-picks-gate` (vec_bench, configs/tape-gate.yaml, 32 envs, one 60 s episode each, the base
  macros), PASS in 10.6 s: picks on and none sent, 0 items crafted in 32 episodes; random picks (an allowed one with
  probability 1/8, else a disallowed one with 1/16), 776 items crafted and 4 wooden pickaxes, 215 of 239 allowed
  picks started the craft macro (the rest lost to a macro that starts first) and 0 of 2,443 disallowed ones did.
- Picks off equals master: vec_bench's new `--digest` (an FNV-1a hash an env over every step's reward, driver, kind,
  chosen and scalars) is 5c15a79746aa74f0 on both libraries over 32 episodes (16 envs, 1 group, 8 workers, 2,500
  steps of 60 s episodes, resets included), and 5a65798f05bee6fb on both at 300 steps.
- (Corrected by lane/digest, the next entry: this lane first reported the vector env not reproducible at 4 groups on
  8 workers. It is; the bench's loop was not: it ran a fixed total of receives, so which groups got them, and how many
  steps each env's digest covered, followed the workers' timing.)
- The trainer's side (mcsr-speedrun, branch brute, outside this repo): the small net's camera head grows a third
  41-wide categorical, the pick, its padding and disallowed picks at -1e9 before the draw, logp and entropy, the
  segment keeping each step's mask for the learner; `fastppo.py --picks`. On the 3090, 64 envs: it trains, and

## 2026-10-27 The saved starts went to a whole group at once: every env's start draws seeded only under a mix (lane/srng)

Each env draws its next start (a saved one with the share `save_share`, else the config's) from its own splitmix64
state, `srng`. `nwrl_vec_make` seeded it only inside `if (o->nstarts > 0)`, the `--mix` branch, so without a mix
every env's state stayed 0 and all of them drew the same numbers: at each reset a group's 128 envs all took a saved
start or none did, and all took the same one. Every run with `--save-starts` and no `--mix` had it since
lane/msstarts (2026-10-18): the GPU host's and the dev host's loops, and today's from-scratch run on the 3090 and the archive
measurements of random play. Measured on the episode records (a throwaway script per group end, 128 episodes that
ended together): the 3090 run's 828 group ends were all 0% or 100% from saved starts (mean 43%), the 128 or 512
copies of one start playing out the same where that start was a dead end (at 13.3 minutes 240 of 256 episodes ended
identically, return 0); the same recipe on lane/srng's library (the GPU host): 16 of 16 group ends mixed, 34 to 52% from
saved starts (mean 40%, the configured share), four start levels in every group.

The fix seeds every env (`0x5DEECE66D * (i + 1)`, the mix branch's seed, so a mix run draws exactly as before; a run
with neither a mix nor saved starts never draws). rl-tape-gate PASS (1,200 rows equal). The archive's measurements
of random play and the from-scratch runs are being made again on it.

## 2026-10-27 Run to tape: any vector-env episode from the config's start written as the oracle's script, and the oracle replays it row for row at vanilla fidelity (never at train-fast's) (lane/tape)

GOAL.md's fifth item: a good run found in the sim replays on the Java client. `nwrl_vec_tape(v, id, path)` (vecenv.h)
arms env id: its next episode from the config's start (a Java snapshot; a saved start is not one) is written as the
oracle's script, a Snapshot line and then each world tick's act as the env ran it (the policy's, a macro's, the reset
step's no act: moveact.c's script writer, now `moveact_script_line`), closed at the episode's end. Call it between
recv and send of id's group. No cost unarmed (vec_bench N 64 runs as before).

Gate, `make -C csrc/runtime rl-tape-gate` (vecenv.mk, csrc/runtime/vectape_gate.c, configs/tape-gate.yaml): vec_bench's
seeded stand-in policy drives 8 envs with the macros on, env 0's second episode (60 s) is written with its row
records (`nwrl_rows`), the oracle runs the script on a fresh world of the config's seed (the config's world section
only: the oracle's key registry has no `client.camera raycast`), and test_snapshots' row records of that recording must
equal the episode's. **PASS in 8.8 s: 6 logs, 31 items crafted (the craft macro's clicks through the screens), a
wooden pickaxe, 1,200 rows equal**, the oracle's last row holding the pickaxe. A second run by hand from the scratch
driver (another episode, 0 logs) was equal on all 1,200 rows too.

**At train-fast.yaml's fidelity it fails, as it must**: `TAPE_CONF=configs/train-fast.yaml` (spawning, random ticks and
weather off, which the oracle has no switch for) differs from the first row's server digests, the player's position
from t=179, and the oracle ends with dirt, sticks and a pressure plate where the episode had 5 logs. So every episode
the trainer has played (train-fast.yaml and its copies) is a run of a game the Java client does not play: a run meant
for Java is found at vanilla fidelity, or the oracle gains those switches as documented pins.

## 2026-10-24 fast's cast against full's: it differs on 0.51% of the golden chains' rows, in runs up to 309 whole frames; the gate that measures it (lane/fastcast)

SPEC's ladder item 4 asked for fast's underground cast gate before fast could be trusted for an eval. The masked
pipe gate that "held every frame" under fast (2026-10-24, `MASK="d.cseed,d.cw,d.cmath"`, 41,264 frames) holds the
device's frames to the C renderer of the same env, so it never compared fast with full. New: `pool_gate --fast`
(engine.tick_scope fast), `--mask FIELD,...` (pipe_gate's) and `--raycast-rows DIR` (each row's cast digest a
line), and `csrc/runtime/rcfast.sh` (`make -C csrc/runtime raycast-fast-gate`): every recording replayed full and
fast with the 32x32 ray cast after every row, the rows held to test_snapshots' but for the three declared fields,
and each row's cast held to full's. Over both golden chains (gold-g1 to g30, s1chain-S1 to S23), explore-long-s1 and
six underground recordings (a mineshaft, digging, ore, the client world's light), 60 recordings and 497,217 rows,
93 s a pass on 16 threads: **2,556 casts differ (0.51%), in 22 recordings, the longest run 309 rows**; 14
recordings have a run of 20 or more. The worst, by casts: s1chain-S17 401 (runs to 106), gold-g29-s42 372 (309),
gold-g11-s42 337 (131), gold-g27-s42 332 (82). The six underground recordings alone are clean (0 of 5,011).

What differs, from the raw casts of three of them: in gold-g29-s42 the player turns 118 degrees at row 1963 toward
a torch-lit wall; full's cast shows it (mean 14.9 a channel), fast's is near black (4.5), every one of the 1,024
pixels off by 2 to 59, for 309 rows. Full's client world had rechecked that light; fast's had not. The cause is the
light check fast skips: `cp_world_tick` (player.c) draws the check cell from the client world's Random, and
`session_client_blocks` (session.c) runs `world_check_light_at` there each tick. The torch flicker is not it (the
cast's lightmap reads `tfx` 0). A variant that keeps the check and skips only the 1,000-cell particle loop was
measured and dropped: 2,511 casts differ, in 25 recordings, runs to 376 (s1chain-S16 410, gold-g29 33), since
full's next cell is drawn after that loop's draws, so any other order of checks gives other transient light. Only
the loop's Random draws and block reads (their air test decides the draws) give full's cells, and those are most of
what fast saves (`cp_world_tick` is 78.4% of the client tick's instructions, the loop's Random 26.7% and its block
scan 28.8% of that, DEVLOG 2026-10-24 below). So: the eval stays
`full`; d.cw stays declared. (Corrected 2026-10-25, lane/s0c: this said fast "stays the training configs' choice".
The recipe's `train-fast-32.yaml` sets no tick_scope, so every recipe run is full; only the k configs the 2026-10-24
session wrote in the trainer's `nwroot/configs` ask for fast: `train-32-k10`, `train-32-k2`, `train-16-k2`,
`train-fast-32-k10-scopefast` and `train-fast-32-scopefast`. A run on one of them takes this cost.)

The gate fails on fast today by design (its default, gold-g29-s42, gold-g7-s42 and gold-g8-s42: 470 of 11,849
casts, 3.8 s, the two runs at once) and passes where nothing parts (idx-cwlight-s1, sh-dig-s42,

## 2026-10-24 Checked: no training run had k above 1, fast's +49% was the episode's first minute, and S0 ran without the recipe; fixed the vec env's ticks, fast's particle list and the lanes' PIC builds (lane/vecticks)

A review of the day's claims, each re-measured. Four did not hold and three were fixed here.

**The vec env stepped one tick a decision.** `queue_group` (`vecenv.c`) called `pipe_step(..., 1, 0)` whatever
`client.ticks_per_step` and `client.action_repeat` said, so the trainer never ran k above 1; pipe_bench and the
gates step `obs.ticks`, so the sim's k numbers (the D/T chain) were real. The trainer's only reading of k was its
own `gamma ** ticks_a_step`: B ("k=2") trained at k=1 with gamma 0.996, S0's "k=10" phase at k=1 with 0.980.
`queue_group` now steps `v->ticks` (`nwrl_obs_spec`); every trainer config sets `ticks_per_step: 1`, so k=1 is the
same call. vec_bench, train-fast.yaml and its `action_repeat: 10` twin, N 256, 4 groups, 30 workers: master
85,435 and 85,646 env-steps/s (k ignored), the lane 85,590 at k=1 and **27,864 at k=10 (278,640 world ticks/s)**.
The trainer on the GPU host with the fix (`fastppo.py --bench 20`, the teacher's 0.46M net, 96 workers, card 3 beside the
idle vLLM):

| k | envs, groups | decisions/s | world ticks/s | workers busy | main thread busy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 384, 2 | 245,908 | 245,908 | 38% | 34% |
| 1 | 384, 3 | 280,403 | 280,403 | 42% | 71% |
| 1 | 384, 4 | 268,137 | 268,137 | 38% | 84% |
| 1 | 512, 4 | 288,857 | 288,857 | 48% | 83% |
| 2 | 384, 2 | 218,605 | 437,210 | 47% | 27% |
| 10 | 384, 2 | 91,201 | 912,010 | 61% | 13% |
| 10 | 384, 4 | 138,137 | 1,381,370 | 90% | 34% |

So the trainer is bound in two places. At k=1 it is the main thread's fixed cost a group step (0.63 to 0.79 ms:
the actor 0.17 to 0.23, the loop's tail 0.16 to 0.22, launch, send, sync and host about 0.1 each), whatever the
group's size: two groups leave both the workers and the main thread idle waiting on each other, three bind the
main thread. At k=10 with four groups the workers bind (90%), at 5.6x the world ticks of S0's shape (384, 2,
k=1), and there the per-tick cost is the lever. The "about 300,000 with fast" projection for the trainer at k=1
does not hold: its workers are 38% busy.

**The crash that found the second bug.** The lane's first libnwrl crashed at the first server tick (`chunk_find_ref`
on a null world through `surv.iew`): gdb showed `survival.o`'s `struct run_config` without `rung` beside
`pool.o`'s with it. `make lane` rewrote the copied dependency files' paths in `out/native/obj` only, so in a lane
`out/native/pic` (libnwrl's engine objects), `cg`, `stk` and `cuda/meshing` never rebuilt on a header change. It now
rewrites every `.d` under `out/native`. Master's own libnwrl is older than its source (15:37, before `091740d8`) and
is rebuilt after this landing.

**fast's +49%** (`111cbfe3`, SPEC) was measured at k=20 (`p-16-rgb-fast-k20.yaml`), 30 decisions with `--counters`,
one pair, and labelled k=2. Rounds interleaved (full fast fast full, 64 envs, equal digests) put it by window: +52%
over decisions 10 to 40, +31% over 100 to 200, +1% over 400 to 600, **-13%** over 800 to 1,000; at k=2 over 1,000
decisions +19%. perf over decisions 800 to 1,000: full's `client_player_tick` 21.7% gone in fast, and in its place
`memmove` 10.7% and `fx_add` 3.3%. fast skipped the particle list's tick but not its spawns, so the list filled to
its layer's cap (4,000) and every spawn scanned and shifted all of it. fast now empties
