## 2026-10-24 The ladder's structure settled: three rungs in one engine, the seam at session_tick, and the model demoted to a cost model

The two consults (Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4, read-only, same brief) agreed with each other and against the earlier lean:
no repo forks, no second simulator. Both put every rung inside the one engine, and Gemini would delete
`csrc/runtime/batchtick.c` outright. The decision, with each of their 86 claims marked, is `/tmp/ladder/decision.md`;
what survives into the tree is this: the rung is a per-environment field (`run_config.rung`, applied in `reset_job`
at the pool's start-image copy, read at the top of `session_tick`), the three rungs are `micro` (the client half of
the row with the server world loaded but frozen, which the empty-server client-only mode at `session.c:515` already
proves is a subset of the engine), `stripped` (exact with the `fidelity.*` switches off, all already implemented)
and `exact` (today's, the eval's). `fast` is an axis on every rung, not a rung. `batchtick.c` is not wired as an
env's row: it is the bench and the target a rung-0 tick must beat (152 ns a world tick of movement, 205-242 with
block interactions, 604 the full tick on 32 threads, against the exact tick's 246 us), and
`engine.tick_scope: batched` becomes an alias for `fidelity.rung: micro`.

The k=20 chain says what each rung can buy, and only at large k: measured 189k, 494k, 618k and 707k ticks/s at k =
1, 5, 10 and 20; against those, `stripped` (T' 0.95) is a **projection** of 1.23x and `micro` (T' 0.45) of 2.16x,
with a 6.93x cap at k=20. Next, in order, before any rung-0 code: the k-transfer A/B (20.4 minutes of wall at 768
envs from the teacher, flat k=1 against k=10 then re-initialised at k=1, scored by the fromspawn eval, decided at
the eval's +-0.054), the cross-rung gate (a rung passes only when its first divergent row is the one its tape's
manifest names), then rung 0's row and its plumbing.
## 2026-10-23 The pipeline's new shape in a real 20-minute block: 768 envs in 3 groups of 256, 294,684 env-steps/s against the A/B's 163k

The bench said 253,101 env-steps/s against 192,873 (+31%, alone and interleaved). The same recipe the density A/B used
for its 32x32 arm (T 120, mb 4096, lr 1e-5, --strip, 300-second episodes, 20.4 minutes, grown from
runs/fromspawn-teacher.pt) at 768 envs in 3 groups of 256 with 96 workers: **360,693,504 env-steps in 1224 s =
294,684 env-steps/s**, against arm B's 200,170,240 in 1,224 s (163,540/s): 1.80x, on identical learning work per
step. The learner held its line (its own 5 to 8 s of each 20-s window, 25 to 40%), so the shape's headroom is still
the sim's.

The 64x64 world does not follow: at 768 envs in 3 groups it measures 148,256 against 147,559 at 512/2, its main
thread 77% busy. Its service per group step, not the workers' idleness, is its wall; the shape follows the
observation.

**Addendum, the same night: the shape is a wall-clock saving, not yet a learning gain.** The 20.4-minute block
evaluated at **depth 2.788** (fromspawn, 1,024 worlds, 20 game minutes) against the 512/2 arm's 3.617 +/- 0.054, on
360.7M env-steps. The same shape stopped at the arm's own env-steps, 215.6M in 11.3 minutes, evaluates at **3.609**:
equal learning, in 55% of the wall clock, the error bars overlapping. So the long block's drop is the constant
learning rate over 1.8x the samples (its entropy ended at 12.83 against the arm's 11.59, its policy further from
where the updates were heading), not the shape; the pipeline's own check at three groups is clean (16,629 sends, 0
env actions differing from the segment's). Two ways out, both measured elsewhere: stop the block at the env-step
budget the recipe was tuned for (11.3 minutes for 200M), or retune the lr and step budget to spend 1.8x the
experience.

**The learning-rate sweep, the same night.** Three full 20.4-minute blocks at 768/3 with everything else the A/B's
recipe: **lr 1e-5, 360.7M env-steps, depth 2.788**; **5e-6, 389.9M, 3.017**; **3e-6, 394.6M, 3.346** (fromspawn,
1,024 worlds, 20 game minutes). Lowering the constant rate buys back about 0.28 of the 0.83 that the extra 1.8x of
steps cost, so the 20.4-minute block approaches the 11.3-minute block's 3.609 only below 3e-6 (a projection: 2e-6 is
the next point, and the trend is not guaranteed). The practical reading: the shape is a wall-clock saving at the step
budget the recipe was tuned at, 200M steps in 11.3 minutes at depth 3.609 against the 512/2 arm's 20.4; a longer
block at a constant rate is spent past the depth peak, and banking the 1.8x of experience needs a decay schedule the
trainer does not have yet.

**What the per-env step is made of at the new shape.** `perf stat` over a 60-second bench at 768 worlds in 3
groups, 96 workers (14,684,928 env-steps, 244,747 env-steps/s with the counters on): **1.232M cycles, 615,500
instructions (IPC 0.50), 112,600 branches and 5,437 LLC misses an env-step**. At 100 to 200 cycles a miss that is
0.5 to 1.1M of the 1.232M cycles, so the 0.246 ms step is bound by memory stalls on the world and env state, not by
instruction count (the thread-time per step, 1.23M cycles at 4.2 GHz, is 0.29 ms). The next lane's lever is layout
and locality (a compact per-env working set, prefetching, the arena's chunk data), not fewer instructions.

**The sweep completed, and a real timeline.** A fourth full block at **lr 2e-6: 393,980,672 env-steps, depth
3.614**: the projection held, so 2e-6 banks the whole 1.8x of experience at the 20.4-minute budget (1e-5: 2.788,
5e-6: 3.017, 3e-6: 3.346, 2e-6: 3.614), landing on the 11.3-minute block's 3.609. Two recipes now reach depth 3.61:
200M steps in 11.3 minutes at 1e-5, or 394M in 20.4 minutes at 2e-6.

`nsys profile` over a 20-second bench at 768/3 (4,525,568 env-steps, 226,275/s with the profiler against 294,684
without): the device is 58% busy in kernels (69% counting the copies). **`rc_cast` is 64.6% of the kernel time**
(17,757 launches, 412.8 us average, 1.6 ns a ray); the actor's elementwise family is 31.6% (45,871 launches, 78 us
each, 2.6 a group step, launch-bound on small tensors); the cast's epilogues (`rc_scatter`, `rc_seen_fin`,
`rc_seen_clear`) 2.2%. The bus: **3.17 GB/s host to device** (63.4 GB in the window, 510,040 copies averaging
124 KB: the world's device mirror), 2.4 GB/s device to device (48.5 GB: the frames staged into the rollout buffers),
33 MB/s device to host (the actions). The API: 678,124 `cudaMemcpyAsync` calls, 763 a group step, and
`cudaEventSynchronize` 31% of the window's API time. So the bytes are not the wall (PCIe at 6% of its capacity, the
frames packed at w*h*3 and device-resident since `engine.raycast: device`), and the stream overlap does happen (the
workers step while the cast and the actor run); what is worth about 0.13 ms of the 1.13 ms group step is the copies'
call count (28.7 H2D and 7.5 D2D a group, ~4 us each) and the trainer's event syncs, and the device's own floor at
this shape is the cast's 0.42 ms a group plus the actor's 0.2 ms.

**What a 10x would take, from the measured components.** At 768/3 the rate is 294,684 env-steps/s, and the two
chains are within 6% of each other: the CPU's 0.246 ms a step (615,500 instructions, IPC 0.50, 5,437 LLC misses) over
96 workers, and the device's 1.62 us a step of `rc_cast` (1,024 rays at 1.6 ns) plus 0.79 us of the actor's
elementwise kernels, serial on one stream. Those give the shape's own ceilings: about 400 to 520k env-steps/s on 128
threads ideal, and about 400k on one card's device work. **So inside this architecture the ceiling is ~1.4x, and 10x
(3M) means changing what is simulated or on what.** The levers, by measured leverage and what each trades:

| lever | trade | gain, and its basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the observation: 16x16 semantic cells instead of 32x32 rgb | the pixels the policy sees (a block grid, no textures) | the cast 1,024 rays to 256 (4x) and the actor's encoder 6x smaller: the device's 2.5 us a step to ~0.6 (4x). Measured: 1.6 ns a ray, 412.8 us a 256-env cast |
| a batched fast-mode tick (one thread stepping many worlds in arrays) | bit-exact Java order on the training path (kept as the verification path) | 5-20x on the CPU side (projection): 615k instructions and 5.4k LLC misses a step are the exactness tax (per-tick hash containers, the phases' order, per-chunk strips) |
| four cards | nothing but the CPU's split (4 x 96 workers over 128 threads) | 1.8x net, 4x only if the tick gets 2.5x cheaper; the learner has the headroom (18M samples/s against 3.5M at 4 cards) |
| the pipeline's leftovers: depth 3-4, one mirror upload a group instead of 28.7, the actor's elementwise fused, one staging copy | nothing | 1.2-1.4x (763 `cudaMemcpyAsync` a group, 0.2 ms of elementwise, 0.13 ms of copy overhead) |
| action repeat k=2 | reactivity (a decision every two ticks) | 1.3-1.5x (the cast and actor per decided step) |
| the tick's scope: drop the client-only work the raycast does not need | the HUD, particles, sound and GUI bookkeeping only | 1.5-2x (the profile is flat: 1-3% a function, 50+ functions) |

The device tick as it exists (S6 compiled for the device) is not a speed path: 66 to 136x a CPU thread's time a world
(2026-10-01), and the card's work of about two host threads; it needs the per-world memory cut 15 to 80 times and the
hot phases (entities 43%, S2 22%, S6 9%) rewritten data-parallel over the worlds before it reaches the CPU's class.

## 2026-10-23 The pipeline after the cast moved: 768 envs in 3 groups of 256, and where a group step's 1.34 ms goes

Elliot: "what is the new bottleneck in speed?" then "pursue these now". The trainer's bench on one RTX PRO 6000, the
32x32 world, T 64, 96 workers, 20-second windows, nothing else on the device (the shape matrix was measured in
several sessions and the ones that overlapped another trainer are marked here; the two that decide the shape were
re-run interleaved and alone).

**The shape, measured (env-steps/s).** The wall is not a resource: at the old 512 envs in 2 groups of 256 the
workers are 49% of 96 busy, the main thread 22% (78% of its window waiting in recv) and the learner 21% of one
card. Three groups of 256 with 768 envs, the same group size and the same 96 workers, gives **253,101 against
192,873 (+31%)**, workers 65%, the main thread 55%, the learner 28%: with three groups two are always queued
while the main thread serves one, so the workers stop idling through the service.

| envs, groups | env-steps/s | workers | main thread | learner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512, 2 x 256 | 190,489 / 193,915 / 190,778 / 192,873 | 49% | 22% | 21% |
| 768, 3 x 256 | **253,101 / 253,521** | 65% | 55% | 28% |
| 1024, 4 x 256 | 234,346 | 71% | 62% | 33% |
| 768, 2 x 384 | 135,168 | 42% | 30% | 17% |
| 512, 1 x 512 (depth 0) | 138,569 | 39% | 43% | 16% |
| 384, 2 x 192 | 111,550 | 29% | 38% | 14% |
| 384, 3 x 128 | 84,285 | 23% | 82% | 11% |
| 512, 2 x 256, 128 workers | 177,707 | 40% of 128 | 28% | 20% |

The group size matters more than the group count: at 128 or 192 envs a group the actor's device step does not shrink
(it is 0.207 ms at 256, 0.513 ms at 128, both plus a launch), so small groups pay the same fixed cost for less work.
128 workers lose to 96 (SMT siblings contend). Depth 2 at 4 groups (181,488) loses to depth 1: the extra device
buffer is not what is short.

**One group step (1.34 ms, 256 envs) in pieces**, at 512/2: recv 1.041 ms (of which 0.957 is the C's wait for the
group: the barrier), host 0.068, launch 0.079, and the tail 0.156 (the event sync, the send, the two CUDA events the
loop makes a step). The workers' own compute is 256 env-steps at 0.246 ms each over 96 threads = 0.66 ms, 0.74 with
the ceil to three rounds a thread. So of the 1.34 ms: 0.7 ms computes, 0.3 ms is the group's wake and collect
(96 condvar wakeups and the last env), 0.35 ms is the main thread's service. The workers' capacity at 0.246 ms a step
is 390k env-steps/s; the pipeline delivers 193k of it at 2 groups and 253k at 3, which is 65%.

**The density, in the bench, at the new shape.** The 64x64 world at 512/2 measures 147,559 and the 32x32 world
190-194k: +29%, from the half-size cast and the quarter-size observation the actor reads. (In the real 20-minute
training runs the two densities measured 170k and 163k: the surface's cast is dear and the underground's is not.)

**The shipped ladder, re-measured without `--check`** (the 64x64 world, run round 1, alone): host cast with 4 groups
of 128 and 30 workers 66,050; the same with the cast on the device 118,673; the device cast with 2 groups of 256 and
96 workers 147,559. 2.23x, reproducing the morning's figures.

**Two measurement traps found while doing this.** `--check` copies each group's actions back per send (a device
sync): 148,799 against 190,489 at the same shape, and the four-group shape collapsed to 17,260 with it on. The
"4 groups is pathological" reading was that flag, not the shape. And the shape matrix is only valid alone: a second
trainer on the same card halves the rate (90,555 for a shape that measures 192,873 alone), which contaminated four
runs before they were repeated.

**The instrumentation.** `nwrl_vec_lat` (runtime/vecenv.c) exports the pool's per-env-step latency (its own step,
the queue, the frame, the group's arrival, the trainer's hands) and fastppo prints it as the `pool:` line, beside a
`tail` timer for the loop's own Python. The tail measures 0.156 ms a group step. The pool's own counters read 0 on
the vector env's path, though: `pipe_poll_some` accumulates them only for envs that came through `t_step`, and
`p->lat[0..3]` stay 0 here while the group's wait is plainly in `recv`. Open: set the phase stamps where the vector
env's collection takes an env, or drop the line.

**The wider shape on the 64x64 world buys nothing**: 768 envs in 3 groups of 256 measure 148,256 against 147,559 at
512/2, the main thread 77% busy. The 64x64 world's service per group step, not the workers' idleness, is its wall;
the 32x32 world's is the workers'. So the shape follows the observation: 768/3 for the 32x32 recipe, 512/2 (or the
service made cheaper) for the 64x64 one.

**What is left, measured.** Halving the 0.246 ms env-step doubles the workers' ceiling (390k to 780k); the
pipeline's 0.65 ms of non-compute a group step is the other half. The 4-group point (234,346, and its env make hits
`Too many open files` in the region spill at 1024 envs) is behind 3 groups; the 64x64 net at 253k would put the
learner at its own ceiling (205-236k), so the wider shape suits the 32x32 observation.

## 2026-10-23 The cast's microarchitecture: instruction-bound in the double DDA, not cache or RAM (perf counters and annotate, both CPUs)

Elliot: "point at what the primary bottleneck is, if it is cache-related, RAM-related, compute-related" and whether the
code is shaped for both hosts. Counters on the two CPUS, desktop-3090 (9950X3D, 16 cores, 32 threads, 2 L3 domains of
64 MB) and gpu-workstation (9985WX, 64 cores, 128 threads, 8 L3 domains of 32 MB), 512 worlds in 4 groups, the 64x64 host cast,
the CPU mesh on both for comparability, 1200 steps a window:

| | desktop-3090, 30 workers | gpu-workstation, 30 workers | gpu-workstation, 96 workers |
|---|---|---|---|
| env-steps/s | 41,200 | 45,470 | 45,993 (one window; the same window's ratios are the point) |
| cycles an env-step | 4.45 M | 2.95 M | 3.50 M |
| instructions an env-step | 7.60 M | 6.10 M | 6.27 M |
| IPC | 1.71 | 2.08 | 1.79 |
| L1-dcache load misses | 1.03% | 0.77% | 0.84% |
| L2 hits of the L2's data accesses | 73.6% | 71.5% | 71.4% |
| L2 fills: local CCX / other CCD / DRAM | 65% / 3% / 35% | 52% / 6% / 41% | 51% / 5% / 47% |
| cycles stalled, load not complete | 20.1% | 23.3% | 23.2% |
| cycles the FP divider is busy | 0.02% | 0.03% | 0.02% |
| branch misses | 2.0% | 1.5% | 1.5% |

The cast is 68.55% of the cycles (annotate, the dev host) and 66% (the GPU host, 10-19 and today). Per pixel on the dev host: about 745
cycles and 1,270 instructions, 34 instructions and 20 cycles a cell of the ~22 a ray. The hottest assembly, from
`perf annotate -s cast` on both hosts, is the DDA's double compare chain: `comisd` four times (2.37, 2.30, 1.93,
0.80% of the whole profile on the dev host), then the per-cell `fast`-path test (`test %r11b,0x110(%rsp)`, `and $0x1,%r11d`,
the conditional jumps: about 6% together), the block byte (`movzbl 0x20(%rdi,%rcx,1)`, 1.43%), `cvtsi2sd` (1.16%),
`pxor` (1.20%), and the section pointer setup. walk did not get specialised into two copies, so one body carries
`fast` in a register and tests it at every cell.

So: compute-bound in the DDA's instruction stream, with a 20 to 23% load-latency tail from the per-cell section ->
block-byte chain; not cache-capacity bound (1% L1 misses, 72% L2 hits), not DRAM-bandwidth bound (the DRAM fills are
a third to a half of the L2 fills, and the L2's misses are 6,600 an env-step, about 15% of the cycles at L3 latency),
and the FP divider is idle (0.02%: the per-pixel 1/sqrt costs instructions, not divider time). The TLB is minor: 900
L2-TLB misses an env-step, 0.6% of the cycles.

Two lines of the world file are the dev host's: `workers: 30` (the dev host's 30 of 32 threads; the GPU host has 128) is worth 1.87x
from 96 (measured, the device cast), and the group shape differs (4 groups of 128 on the dev host; 2 groups of 256 on the GPU host,
122,460 to 148,439 with the device cast). `layout: any` is not settled: with the device cast at 96 workers and 2 groups
three rounds gave any 74,803 and 89,127 against pipe 78,997, and with the host cast and the CPU mesh one pair gave
35,559 to 60,320 and another 51,639 to 39,816, so the round-to-round spread (19% at least) swamps the layout on the GPU host.
The locality effect is real but small in throughput: on the dev host the pipe layout cuts the other-CCD's L2 fills 3.8x
(346.6M to 90.7M) for +4% (41,200 to 42,896), and on both hosts the other-CCD fills are only 3 to 6% of the fills.
Treat the layout as unmeasured for the shipping config and keep `any`.

The density lever, measured: the 32x32 cast at the same 30 workers on the dev host is 92,353 env-steps/s against 41,200 at
64x64 (2.24x, the worker's step 0.72 to 0.29 ms), and the 2026-10-19 sweep found no depth loss for the 32x32-class
nets (the teacher 2.83, w1 2.85, s64 2.65 at the same hour). A 2-byte surface+light buffer instead of RGB would also
halve the observation copies the 10-19 profile priced at 9% of the 3090's window.

Projections (not measured): specialising walk on `fast` removes the ~6% test; a float or integer DDA removes the four
comisd and the cvtsi2sd a cell (8 to 10% of the cast); prefetching the next cell could take a part of the 20% load
stall. The next lane: the density (32x32 or 48x48 with the stem) with a depth A/B, then the two walk specialisations
with the cast's bytes gated.

depth 2.49 against w1's 2.85 at the same hour). Not minGRU: no GRU, no parallel scan, a single LSTMCell when enabled;
the family's knobs are wm (width), res (residual blocks), lstm (cell size) and stem.

GPUs (the trainer is one device today, `--dev cuda:0`), and after that the learner's shape (T, minibatch, epochs). The

## 2026-10-23 The wood the next pickaxe needs kept up from a log in view (lane/pick): from-spawn depth 4.98 to 5.30 (2048 worlds an arm, 60 minutes)

Of 512 hour-long from-spawn runs of s64-w2-it55, 179 finish with no stone or iron pickaxe (35%), and the split says
why. One hundred and seven died at least once (21.7% of all runs die, and a death drops the inventory, so they respawn
empty). The other 72 never died: they hold a wooden pickaxe (67 of 72), a median 133 cobblestone, 2 sticks and 1
plank, and 53 of them had reached a stone pickaxe and lost it. The one piece missing for the next stone pickaxe is a
table, 4 planks, and the wood seek that exists (lane/woodseek) wants a log only while a pickaxe is held and a plan's
table or sticks are under 4 or 2 planks: a run whose pickaxe broke at tier 0 never wanted wood at all, and 70% of its
steps ran no macro.

With NWRL_VEC_PICK the want is the wood the next pickaxe needs, at any tier below iron: 3 planks with a table held or
within 4 blocks, 7 without one, 9 when its sticks must be made too. A log in view is walked to and chopped (before
ore; the strip yields to it), the craft plan spends the wood in the order that reaches the pickaxe (log to planks, the
table, sticks, the pickaxe), and the table comes back with the carry macro. A run that breaks its pickaxe deep with a
log in sight makes the table and the stone pickaxe from it, and a run still holding one banks the planks before the
break instead of after it.

The cases: pick-wood (no pickaxe, no wood, a ring of logs 5 to 7 blocks out: the log chopped, a table and a wooden
pickaxe made) and pick-spare (a stone pickaxe, 2 planks, 4 sticks: 6 planks and a table kept up before it breaks).
Both fail with the bit off (no pickaxe, 2 planks held at the end) and pass with it; every other case the bench holds
passes.

## 2026-10-19 The ray cast on the device (lane/rcdev): every frame and seen record the CPU's, the trainer's simulator 4.5x lighter, the 3090 its limit now (orchestrator)

Elliot, 2026-10-19 ~1:45 pm: the trainer waits on the simulator; move the rasterization to the GPU, minding the
correctness gates (not a deep-learning kernel), then find the next bottleneck and say whether it is GPU portable.

Where the time went first (the dev host, the 3090 idle, the w2 arm's flags: fastppo --bench, 160 worlds in 2 groups,
22 workers, the 64x64 cast, PPO updating): 42,166 to 45,438 env-steps/s; the main thread waited on the simulator 92%
of the window, the device 56% busy (the learner's stream 40%, the actor's 22%); perf over the process: libnwrl 89% of
the CPU, raycast.c's cast 59% (its walk 32%), the tick spread thin (client_player_tick 5.5%, start_scan 3.6%, nothing
else over 1.5%). 4 groups of 80 instead of 2: 50,953 and 51,898 (the workers 58% to 78% busy: with 2 groups one group
steps while the other waits for its actions).

What the device cast is (engine.raycast device, libnwrl API 8, mcsr pareto 01b4fd8):
- raycast.c keeps each cast's setup on the env's worker (raycast_head: the camera, the lightmap, sky and fog, the
  entity boxes, rchead.h's plain form) and cuda/raycast/cast.cu runs the rays: walk and its helpers ported line for
  line (generated from raycast.c's text, the fast path's reads swapped for the device copy's), --fmad=false, IEEE
  division and square root, one thread a pixel.
- The device copy of each env's client world (rcmirror.c): a ring of R x R columns (R = 2 (range + 1) / 16 + 2, 10 at
  render distance 4), each column's mask, height map and biomes and its 16 sections' ids, metadata, sky and block
  light. After each step the worker walks the cast's window: a chunk whose wseq moved (any block, metadata or light
  write moves it), or a new chunk, world or reset (pool_epoch, new: a reset puts back memory whose write sequences
  repeat), has each section hashed and the changed ones staged as records; a full stage is copied in from the worker.
  rcmirror_sync was 0.8% of the CPU in training.
- The trainer: nwrl_vec_cast(g, stream) after recv draws the group's frames on the trainer's own stream (the frames
  never leave the device; VecEnv.recv calls it); send waits for the cast and gives each env its seen record before its
  macros run (the seek macro reads it); an episode's last step is cast before its record is kept (its seen steps).

The gates:
- raycast-device-gate (gpu-raycast-check, mirror.tsv RAYCAST): after every tick of raycast-gate's six recordings
  (the speedrun start, swimming, lava, the Nether, the End, a village; resets between 36 episodes) at 32x32, 64x64 and
  48x32, each env's device frame against raycast_ref's and its seen record against raycast_seen's: 47,490 casts equal,
  12 s. The CPU cast's digests equal master's (the setup's move changed no byte).
- Planted: south faces shaded 0.81 for 0.8 fails at row 2982 (one pixel 17 against 18); a section changed in place
  never copied fails all three recordings tried within 19 rows; a gate binary not relinked after a kernel edit passed
  the first plant (the object's rule had no recipe in runtime's make: the gate now builds the object, then links, in
  makes of their own).
- scripts/rcdev_gate.py (mcsr): the model drives the vector env with the host cast and with the device's, actions
  drawn by (group, step): 7,403 group steps of 32 worlds over 3-minute episodes (the strip mine and the seek
  running), every frame, scalar, compiled act, reward, end and driver equal, and 64 episode records. Without the seen
  fold at send it fails (the records' seen steps).

The kernel, a 64x64 cast of 80 worlds (a timing script: the model drives 160 worlds 1,500 group steps, seeded, then
one group cast 30 times, CUDA events, builds interleaved):

| kernel | ms |
|---|---|
| walk ported, doubles (201 registers, 2 blocks an SM) | 1.075 |
| the air loop's steps in float, each decision the float bounds do not settle made in double | 0.786 |
| and the window's ring columns in shared memory (no division a section) | 0.678 |

Each axis' next boundary t is a pure function of the cell index, ((double)(i + (s > 0)) - o) * id, so the air loop
carries the indices and float shadows with a bound (twice u (3 |f| + |o| |id|), the index exact in float, the eye
within 4e6), compares in double only what the bounds leave open, and makes the doubles again from the indices when it
leaves. Tried and dropped: each env's threads taking pixels from a counter (4 blocks an env: 3-4x slower), registers
capped at 168 and 128 (1.21 and 1.29 to 1.50 ms), warps as 8x4 pixel tiles (0.875 against 0.786), pixels ordered by
their last walk's length (0.807 against 0.676). Nsight Compute on one world's cast: 3.1 of 32 lanes active (a warp
waits for its longest ray), 90% of issue slots with no eligible warp; the hot lines the air loop's decisions (25%),
its cell reads (9%) and, before the table, the section lookup (10%).

| env-steps/s | host cast | device cast |
|---|---|---|

The GPU host's updates grew over twelve iterations (lag.py on iters.jsonl; KL the policy's per-update estimate):

|---|---|---|---|
| 118 to 120 | 0.019 to 0.020 | 0.09 | 6.2 to 6.7 |
| 122 to 127 | 0.017 to 0.038 | 0.21 to 0.42 | 10.3 to 13.6 |

Within an iteration KL rises row by row (131: 0.055 to 0.139). The learner's queue is bounded (fastppo --queue), so it
is not the learner falling behind; the drift began with the policy's entropy rising from about 6 to about 13

rows 0.084 to 0.288) and is back at 1e-4 from 133. Open: the cause; the guard is what holds it today.

The reward scale (mcsr fastppo scale(): the running std of the discounted return, divided into every reward): 10 of
the dev host's 48 spawn-lane iterations (sp3 to sp50) had a first logged update with a value loss of 1.5e7 to 7.4e8
(the steady 0.002 to 0.01). A run whose envs all start at spawn pays almost nothing in its first steps, the std came
out near 0 and the first update's returns were scaled by up to 1e4. The scale is now at least 1 (its steady value

save_count (reward.MILESTONES' bits, bit 13 the Nether) its episode gains past what it began with; a save's level is
the mask's milestones then held, the draw takes a level present at random and then one of its starts (the deep ones as
often as the shallow), a full pool lets go the oldest unplayed start of its most kept level, and the record carries
the level (the field was pad3). Two things every saved start now has, in both modes:
- what the macros knew: the table and furnace the env had placed (has_table, has_furnace and their cells) go with the
  start and back to the env that plays it. Without it a start saved after the furnace was placed could not find it.
- a save waits for no macro to run: a macro's own state is not in the start, and one saved mid-smelt left its ore
  in a furnace no plan came back for.

## 2026-10-17 What the agent's camera shows: ore and nether brick counted from the observation's own ray cast (lane/seen, libnwrl API 5) (orchestrator)

The iron start's stall (the iron pickaxe 0 to 23% of episodes, one ingot in 97%) and the nether start's (no blaze
killed) are both about finding what a player would see: iron ore in a cave wall, a fortress's nether brick. Before a
macro that walks to it, a probe counts how often it is on screen at all (the memory's rule: gate a macro by the state
where it helps, counted first).

lane/seen: raycast_seen (raycast.h) is the observation's ray cast with a record of what it drew: for each of four
block ids, the pixels whose colour is that block's opaque cube face (the ray's first, so never through a wall) and
the nearest such cell with its distance from the eye. The bytes are raycast's (one branch where a cube face is
shaded writes a side record): raycast-gate OK, 47,490 rows, 32x32, 64x64 and 48x32 equal to the reference. rlbind's
step hook casts with it and fills nwrl_state's seen_n and seen (NWRL_SEEN 4: iron ore 15, diamond ore 56, nether
brick 112, coal ore 16; NWRL_VERSION 5); the episode record's seen counts the steps each was in view. macro_check
seen (the spawn checkpoint walled in iron ore at 2 to 3 blocks): in view on 60 of 60 steps, and on 0 of 60 without
the wall. All thirteen cases PASS; vecenv_gate PASS; clangcheck ok. Only with the ray cast (train-fast.yaml's
observation); the semantic camera's configs leave seen at zero.

What the fast cast does now (raycast.c; each part the scalar code's own operations): every ray's start 8 pixels at a
time in AVX-512 (rays_v); the air in front of each ray in 8 vector lanes (vwalk), walk's own DDA step in doubles,
each lane's cell read by scalar loads from stored indices in inline asm (this 9950X3D takes 10 to 12 cycles of
throughput for an 8-element gather against about 3 for eight loads: the gather version was the first window's
loser), lanes refilled as they stop, a stopped lane handing walk the step it stopped on; the eye-water surface going
up recorded in the lane and blended by walk later; a ray going up or level ended above the highest block of the
columns its direction can reach (per-cast tops of 256 direction buckets from the columns' block tops): 21% of rays ran
the whole 64-block range at about 98 steps each, 73% of all steps, mostly pointing over 10 degrees up while the cast's
top sat 47 blocks above the eye (15 with the per-ray top); walk_short for a ray stopped on a cube's face or out of
range with nothing in front (76 to 81% of rays) and fin_v for the last layer's fog, overlay and bytes 8 at a time;
snow layers crossed above passed inside walk's fast loop (1e-6 over the top rounded up to a 16th).

Reverted, each measured in a window (out/perf/raycast2.tsv has every row): sending rays back into the vector walk
after each block they pass (1.004), snow passed in the vector lanes (1.062 in the loop, 1.025 at refill: over a snow
field nearly every other cell stops a lane), exact jumps across empty 4x4x4 bricks (1.234, then 1.197: the passes
halved, but the jump sits on the loop's chain before the step), a per-ray top by a walk over the ray's columns (1.008),
section-level column tops (1.017), refilling at 5 to 7 live lanes (1.02 to 1.13), prefetching the hit's metadata and
light (0.997), walk_short taking snow boxes (more instructions).

Where it goes now (2 workers, a window, gold-fast N 32): 67 us a 32x32 cast, the vector walk 30 (about 21 lane
steps a ray at about 6 cycles), the scalar finish 27 (rays over snow fields in walk's fast loop the largest part), ray
start with the bucket tops 8, setup 1.6; 32 workers make it 1.6 times that (SMT). Next would be snow layers in the
lanes from a per-cast snow-cell mask, a finer per-ray top (4x4 column groups), brick jumps with two lane groups

  - the net: 6.9 MFLOPs a sample forward, 0.46M parameters;
  - the bound: the simulator's 30 workers, 93% busy; the main thread is busy 26%;
  - startup: 4.6 s (env 1.2, CUDA graphs 2.2, warm-up 1.0) plus about 1.3 s of imports.
- **How the trainer runs.**
  - The loop runs one group deep: it launches a group's actor step (one CUDA graph) and sends the group it launched
    before.
  - The learner thread replays GAE and each minibatch as CUDA graphs on a lower-priority stream.
  - Weights reach the actor through a shadow copy. Waiting on the learner's own refresh event had held every actor
    step until the whole update finished: 62k became 86.1k on the semantic cast once that was gone.
  - The small net reads the cell's bits as 16 channels-last planes. A learned block embedding's gather and its
    sorting backward were 60% of the update's device time.
- **Learning, semteach_ppo.py's recipe in fastppo against semteach_ppo.py, 3 seeds a side to 6M.**
  - Means at the episode rounds nearest 2M, 4M and 6M: logs 5.41 against 6.65, 19.17 against 18.95, 23.64 against
    24.19; wooden pickaxe share 0.556 against 0.646, 0.914 against 0.939, 0.973 against 0.982.
  - So within 3% at 4M and 6M, and 19% under on logs at 2M, where the reference alone spans 5.05 to 9.23 over its
    seeds.
  - To 6M: 183 to 196 s against 520 to 540 s.
- **How equal learning was reached.** fastppo first had 3.0 to 4.3 logs at 2M. Two causes, each measured:
  - a race: the learner read a segment's bootstrap value before the loop's stream wrote it;
  - staleness: the Teacher's update (57.6 ms a 4096 minibatch) saturated the learner, so the actor ran on old
    weights. semteach_ppo's own trainer on the C env reached 6.14, and fastppo slowed to 10k env-steps/s reached
    6.21.
  The Teacher's conv input and embedding gradients are now two Triton kernels: the input bit-identical, the logits
  identical, 22.3 ms a minibatch (2.6x), and the learner about 55% busy at 32k env-steps/s.
- **Found on the way.** lane/raycast's thread-locals (9.7 KB) made libnwrl.so unloadable from Python; the
  orchestrator fixed it on master (lane/tlsfix).

## 2026-10-15 The device mesher dropped a launch's world copies when every pass in it was shared: stale device worlds at N 256, a sunflower's libm value missing (lane/meshtrig)

A pixel-policy training run (mcsr-speedrun pixdagger.py s32: configs/speedrun-semantic.yaml with camera both, 32x32,
hud off, device_mesh 1, 256 envs of seed 1 from sr-speedrun-s1) stopped after 6.4M env-steps (10 minutes) on
`render: the device mesher could not mesh section 8 4 17 pass 0 (error 1)` (MESHING_ERR_TRIG: kernels.c trig() found
no libm value for a key) and exit(1) in cuda/render mesh_end.

Found from the data, not the callers. The device now records each missing key with the cell whose draw asked for it
(kernels.h struct meshing_miss: fn, a, b, the block, the cell, the kernel, and the cell's id as the table cache, the
band table and the chunk record each hold it), and the renderer prints them. pipe_bench on the run's own config
(out/mt/s32.yaml: the speedrun corpus, N 256, 3,600 steps from the start, an episode) hit it at --env-base 768 in 3 of
4 runs, never at bases 0, 256, 512, 1,024 or 1,280, never at N 64 (the same envs in four runs of 64) and never with
--device-mesh 2: fn 0 (cos), a = 6.0463073783505009e18 (0x1.4fa3321a859ebp+62), the head of a sunflower, 175:8 at
221 64 267, section 13 4 16, drawn by the table mode's list draw and again by mesh_run, and all three of the device's
world sources held 175 there. The request's own list (meshfeed.c, every id-175 cell of its band) had no entry for it:
the device's world held a sunflower the host's band did not. A temporary hash of the centre band (the band the host
read for the request, the feed's shadow of what the device holds, the device's band read back) gave request =
shadow, device different: the host's model was right and the device had not applied some of the feed.

The cause: meshing_count_start (cuda/meshing/host.c) returned at once for a launch with no requests, before run()
uploaded the staging and launched mesh_copy. mesh_begin (cuda/render/host.cu) sends no request for a pass whose key
another env's mesh already serves (render_mesh_share 1, the product's default), so a launch whose every pass is
shared, frequent at N 256 of one start (the speedrun corpus: about 3 passes an env-step served by another env's mesh
against 0.3 meshed), carried its feeds' band and chunk uploads and dropped them, while meshing_add had advanced the
slot's sequence number and the view's shadow recorded the bands as sent. The env's device world then kept those bands
until a later feed happened to send the same granules again: the meshes it made itself were drawn from a stale world (silently, in any
device-meshed run with a launch of shared passes alone since sharing landed, 2026-10-09 c6f9db5d), and a sunflower
head the host no longer had asked for a libm value its request did not list (a liquid cannot: the launch's table
holds every flow sum). --device-mesh 2 and the gates'
play dumps (whose feeds carry no keys) send every pass, so no gate reached it.

Fixed: a launch of copies and no requests runs them (run() with no requests: the upload and mesh_copy) and
meshing_count_wait waits for them before the staging is reused. After it, base 768 three times and bases 0, 256 and
512 once each at N 256: no missing key, no fallback.

The pixels it cost, measured: pipe_bench --frame-digest on that trajectory (N 256, env base 768, one episode) drew
frame digest f3a64478903e4655 twice with the fix (23,234 and 23,616 launches of copies alone: the batching differs,
the frames do not) and 967bb51225e8f50e with the code before it, on the same trajectory digest 601fe90eea9530cc and
with no missing key that run: the old build's frames differed from the C renderer's for the same game states. How
many frames differed was not counted.

The reproduction on stored inputs, 1.0 s: `make -s -C csrc gpu-meshing-check MESH_ARGS="--twin pix-fluid-s1"`
(render_check --twin): one recording's dumps fed to two slots, the second a render behind with its passes withheld
for the first half (render_mesh_withhold, a test switch: as though shared meshes served every pass, so its launches
carry copies and no requests), then both slots every pass; the two slots must end holding the same bands
(meshing_slot_bands) and the second's meshes must equal the host's. Before the fix: bands DIFFER, 655 of 911 device
meshes equal to the host's; after: bands equal, 911 of 911, 22 of 22 frames of slot 0 bit-exact. A mirror quick line.

A pass the device still cannot mesh no longer ends the run: mesh_end meshes it with the C mesher on the host
(meshing_host_mesh: the request's nine chunk records and their bands read back from the device, its flower pots, the
template the device meshes from, rb_mesh_section) and writes it where the device's mesh would go; the first is
printed with its section and its missing keys, and render_stats dmesh_host counts them (pipe_bench prints the count;
pipe_gate fails on any, as it is the device mesher's fault). It is exact when the device's copy of the world is (what
the twin check and the gates hold), not a cover for a stale one. The planted fault (render_mesh_plant, render_check
--plant-trig: no libm value sent at all): `make -s -C csrc gpu-meshing-check MESH_ARGS="--plant-trig pix-fluid-s1
cov-foliage-s1"`: 102 passes meshed on the host, 768 of 768 meshes equal to the host's, 24 of 24 frames bit-exact. A
mirror quick line.

Gates (after the fix): `make -s -C csrc gpu-meshing-check` 36,325 of 36,325 device meshes equal to the host's, 1,798
of 1,798 frames bit-exact over 116 recordings (51 s); every MESHING quick line in mirror.tsv passes (the four
recordings 1,151 of 1,151 and 48 of 48, the stress run, PERF=0, the table mode, --twin, --plant-trig), and the
twin, plant and four-recording lines again from a fresh scratch worktree of the branch; `make -s -C csrc/runtime
pipe-gate PRECS="cov-villagerep-s42 nether-trip-s1 end-dragon-s1"` OK (32,967 rows, 8,252 frames bit-exact), MESH=2
OK (25,845 of 25,845 device meshes equal to the views', 12,335 shared passes equal to their own), MESH=1 OK (14,371
passes meshed on the device, 11,474 shared); `make -s -C csrc clangcheck` ok; no csrc/engine change. One N 256
episode at env base 768 had 13,637 launches of copies and no request (render_stats dmesh_copy_only; 37,068 renders),
each one dropped before. kcab.sh (gold-fast, 3 rounds, equal digests in every window): all three bench windows were

## 2026-10-15 The raster kernel at gold-fast: raster 10 to 13% faster alone, about +1% end to end, under the bar; nothing kept (lane/kcraster)

The kernels goal, the raster kernel (raster<PM> and its pixel functions, raster_launch). 19 rows in
out/perf/kcraster.tsv, the report in the lane's out/report.md. A probe made for it (the lane's out/perf/kcr, not
committed): 24 renders' raster inputs snapshotted from a gold-fast N 128 pipe_bench run and replayed on the idle
device, master's raster against the lane's in one process, 5 rounds alternated, every frame and depth byte compared
(A/A -0.1%, about 2% run to run as the snapshot set changes), its kernels apart by name for Nsight Compute.

What raster's time is (isolated): the record copies about 45%, the pixel calls 33 to 41%, the walk 13% (no pixel
calls: 58.6% of the time; no copies either: 13%). The copies are DRAM misses: records from a hot 2048-triangle set
made raster 37.6% faster, so the records' misses are about 28% of it. In the pipeline (ncu, caches kept) raster reads
2.9 to 3.4 MB of DRAM a frame, the copies alone 3.1 to 3.3 MB at 84% of the bandwidth, without them 0.23 MB; a
frame's records are at most 1.2 to 1.9 MB, each fetched about twice by the tiles that share it. Key order cuts it to
2.1 to 2.5 MB but costs raster 9% (the heaviest tiles start late; end to end -0.9%, and the heavy keys first then key
order -1.1, +0.7, -0.0%): heaviest-first is worth about 15%. A launch is about 50 us plus 4.5 us a frame: the
constant is the heaviest tiles' walk (150 to 260 pairs, 8 to 15 groups a warp). Renders of 1 to 4 frames are 46% of
the pipeline's raster launches. 50 us of spin at the end of every raster launch costs -1.6% end to end. Occupancy is
not the limit (10, 9, 7, 5 blocks an SM: 0, -2, -10, -12%), nor divergence between paths (1.19 a step), the texels
(one atlas for every environment: 1%) or the sky planes (all skipped: 1%).

Measured and not kept (each exact where the code is: every probe frame and depth byte equal, the gates passing):
- 74fb05e8: no L1 prefetch of the batch and records by cp.async.cg (raster -6%), light_sample's division by 255 as
  div255 (q = x fl(1/255) and two fused steps, equal to the division for every float but -0 and the infinities, all
  2^32 checked at render_new by div255_check, which refuses a wrong constant), the cover test after the depth test:
  raster -8.7 to -9.4%; N 64 / 128 +0.7 / +0.7% (3 rounds), +0.2 / +0.4% (5).
- 6dfab313: the first 128 keys in two blocks, a list over 64 pairs drawn by four 8 x 2 warps (renders of 1 to 4
  frames -26% alone, 68.7 to 55.5 us in the pipeline), the records at L2 evict_last: with 74fb05e8 raster -10 to -13%;
  N 128 +0.0% (5 rounds), +2.0% (9), +0.9% (11; round means +1.45% and +1.03%). Reverted (f7a06872) under the 1.5%
  bar; `git diff master -- csrc` is empty.
- Four blocks for the heaviest tiles (small renders -30%, +0.5 / -0.1% end to end), double-buffered groups for long
  lists (+5%), sky planes drawn late (+0.3 to +30%: three inline copies of pixel or an ABI call), a record two lanes

Elliot (2:10 am): 1.7.10, the simpler architecture, is the default version; 1.16.1 stays for speedrunning. In it a run
chooses by configuration the checkpoint it starts from, the sim's fidelity, and what runs on the CPU and what on the

`--start NAME=` take a name from configs/checkpoints.tsv: fresh, spawn, stone, food, iron, diamonds, portal, nether,
nether-return, armor, pearls, pearls-mid, eyes, stronghold-walk, stronghold, end; configs/gold.yaml is the seed-42
world; every gold segment loads and steps 8 envs in 1.0 to 1.8 s).

This lane. Native-only config keys: `WC_NATIVE0` on in csrc/engine/worldconf.c are the runtime's alone. config.yaml
leaves them out, so the oracle's WorldConf.java, its harness hash and every oracle cache are unchanged; the oracle
refuses a file that sets one (it cannot record a reduced game). worldconf_check holds config.yaml to the oracle's keys
and now resolves a checkpoint name to its recording (gold.yaml was skipped as "no ../spawn").

- `fidelity:` (csrc/engine/fidelity.c): spawning (off: the doMobSpawning rule false), spawn_types (the spawner's
  categories), mobs (all, none or EntityList names joined by +: the start's others set dead, any living of another
  kind set dead as it joins the list, an_list_push, and a category no biome fills with a kept kind left out), random_ticks,
  weather (the start's weather stays). The pool applies it to a start's image once after the load, so every env
  copied from it has it. The daylight cycle is world.daylight_cycle, a vanilla rule. pipe_gate, pool_gate and
  start_gate refuse anything but vanilla (pool_config.vanilla_only). pipe_bench takes `--fid KEY=VALUE` and
  `--census` (living mobs by kind at the end).
- `engine.render` (device, none) and `engine.tick` (host; device refused as not implemented) beside the oracle's
  device_mesh, device_generation and device_light.
- `performance:` workers, streams, group, batch, depth, layout, pin, place, tune: pipe_config_file reads them, the
  trainer API (rlbind) keeps them unless its caller passes a nonzero value, pipe_bench's flags override them.
- configs/gold.yaml meshes on the device; configs/gold-fast.yaml is the same world with spawning, random ticks and
  weather off.

## 2026-10-09 Entity models as a graph: box shapes, draws and pose nodes, the corners made on the device; upload 69.0 to 45.9 KB an env-step, env-steps/s +2.6% speedrun, +1.7% village (lane/entgraph)

Elliot, 2026-10-08: "represent many things with one unified structure to connect them together in a
graph sense"; this lane's item, entity models as static model data plus per-frame poses. Measured
first at speedrun.yaml N 128 on master 87722d50: the upload was 69.3 KB an env-step, 37.9 KB of it
entity data, and 34.7 KB of that the model boxes (163.6 an env-step, 1,691 a render, each 208 bytes
with its 8 corners already posed plus 4 of extra-record index); 39 distinct box shapes a render. A
dummy build that uploaded every box record twice (+31.9 KB, same kernels and frames) ran 3.3% slower,
so the bytes were worth cutting. What changed (csrc/engine raster_obs.[ch], raster_mobs.c, raster.c;
csrc/cuda/render/host.cu):

- A box is its shape (the 6 model-space bounds after grow and the mirror's swap, its texture
  rectangle: what no pose changes), its draw (state, tex, matrices, base, light, texture transform,
  flip: shared by every box of an entity's pass) and its pose node, the first of a chain: the box's
  part, its parents, then the entity's tail (model_vertex_tail's stages, draw_box's outer matrix),
  linked by relative NEXT jumps. The recorder keeps each node and shape once a frame by content
  (raster_obs.c rec_node, rec_shape), so a part's boxes share its node and an entity's parts the tail.
  emit_box_xf's boxes (the dragon, the crystal, the knot, the preview) are an XF node and an outer one.
- A node is raster_mobs.c's own float operations (RASTER_EOP_PART: rot_x, rot_y, rot_z and the
  rotation point; ROT, ADD, AXM, BASE, SCALE: model_vertex_tail's statements; XF: xf_point), run by
  one inline interpreter in raster_obs.h (raster_epose_run, __host__ __device__ under nvcc) that the
  live C passes, the C renderer over a frame and the device's ebox kernel all call, so a corner has one
  source. A rotation by zero is left out of PART only when its cosf and sinf bits are 1 and +0, and the
  interpreter turns by exactly those.
- ebox (the device) poses and projects each corner once into shared memory, then a thread a face:
  the first version made 4 corners a face (ebox 13.7 to 25.4 us a launch), this one 16.3.

Exact: a temporary build computed every box's corners both ways (the old model_vertices and
emit_box_xf code beside the nodes) and aborted on any differing bit; the native suite (1,073 jobs ran
the changed code), pipe-gate MESH=2 and the speedrun pipe-gate passed with it, none differed. The
host's frame record does less: 1.355 to 1.261 M user instructions an env-step.

Elliot, 2026-10-08: "where we can represent the same info, or close to the same info, with
significantly fewer bytes ... represent many things with one unified structure"; this lane's items
were 2, quads instead of triangle pairs, and 3, terrain drawn from the mesh quad itself with no

  activity to raster's end) is 2,826 us mean (median 2,514), 2,080 of them gaps behind the other
  streams' work. quads_write takes 109 us a render, and the stream then waits 137 us mean (88
  median) for the side writers (generic_write, equads): in none of 2,268 renders does the write pass
  end on quads_write, so removing it shortens no chain. Launched twice it costs 6.0% of env-steps/s
  (14,023 to 13,178): the device is saturated, and its whole work is what removing it could buy.
  Counters (a temporary build): 84% of the section triangles are in quads with both triangles drawn
  (92.0 M such quads against 34.9 M with one), 15.5 k section triangles a frame, 30.7 k raster group

  speedrun config, -4.2% at village. Registers unchanged; raster's group copy went from 7.5 rounds of
  one path to 13 rounds of up to eight.
- Item 2, g3: every terrain triangle a head and three 48-byte vertex blocks (raster copies 13 uint4s
  a terrain slot, pixel() reads the blocks), the shared vertices stored once, quads_write a thread a
  quad (each vertex made once): -0.8% / -0.1%. quads_write 9.90 to 10.69 us an env-step: half the
  threads at 207 registers in a latency-bound kernel.
- Item 2, g3b: g3 with a thread a triangle: 14,087 against 14,087 at the speedrun config, 13,097
  against 13,108 at village. quads_write 9.90 to 9.20 us an env-step, raster 18.53 to 18.86. The
  same layout without sharing (g3c, every slot 208 bytes) gave quads_write 9.23: the shared
  vertices' 26% fewer record bytes move nothing. Committed (1e55075d) and reverted: the history keeps

## 2026-10-09 The clippers by recorded operations: env-steps/s +1.9% at the speedrun config, +0.8% at village, the generic kernels a quarter less device time, every output the same (lane/cliprep)

Elliot, 2026-10-08: "quantizing things ... decompressing them in shared memory or registers ... bank
conflict resolution or coalescing", one optimization a lane; this lane's was the clippers.
generic_count, generic_write<0> (raster.c clip_triangle: the sky's slots and the section quads the
lean kernel hands over) and generic_write<1> (raster_entities.c clip_and_draw) kept their
Sutherland-Hodgman polygons as arrays of whole vertices in local memory: at the start, on stored dumps
(7 recordings, 314 frames, one render), generic_write<0> stored 270 MB and loaded 179 MB of local
memory, 132 MB of it past L1, with 14.7 warps stalled on long scoreboard an issue. 15 rows in
out/perf/cliprep.tsv. What was kept:

- csrc/cuda/render/rclip.cuh: the clip runs over the clip coordinates alone; the polygon is its vertex
  ids (4 bits each, in a register: 0 to 2 the triangle's, then the made ones), and each vertex a plane
  makes is recorded as its edge's start id, end id and t. Every other attribute is made afterwards by
  replaying those operations in order, start + t * (end - start), the interpolation's own operands and
  operations (--fmad=false), so the same bits; the entity colour without vertex_color is the start's,
  as e_interpolate copies it. The write stores the screen fields from the positions (emit_pos,
  e_tri_pos) and the replayed fields a group at a time (rc_fields, e_rc_fields). A polygon past 6
  made vertices or 9 held still goes to the arrays (0.004% of the speedrun corpus's clipped
  triangles: 140.6 M section-quad triangles clipped, 97.9% by one plane).
- The values by id in shared memory, not registers: the first version picked them with select chains
  and generic_write<0> ran 71% more instructions (FSEL 27%, ISETP 11%); faster alone and on the dumps,
  but in the pipeline its launches (about 10k threads, less than a wave) share the SMs with the other
  streams' kernels and it got 22% slower there. Each thread keeps a column of one 18 KB table a
  kernel (word w at T[w * GBLOCK], a warp's lanes in 32 banks), one load an id.
- The inputs in registers: clip_triangle's inside test by outcodes with constant axes (the indexed
  axis kept the three vertices in local memory), e_clip inlined with its fallback copying the input
  first, a section quad's triangle making its three vertices only.
- The write's environment from the count (the list entry's kind, bits 8 on), not a binary search a
  thread; the write's grid one resident wave (2 SMs: it was 1,312 blocks from an upper bound, 8 waves,
  and in the pipeline 43 of 5,248 warps of an entity write had a triangle) and the count's clipped
  units' 3 SMs.

## 2026-10-09 One device mesh for the section passes of one key across a stream's envs: env-steps/s +2.7% at the speedrun config, +1.3% at village, +8.9% on a reset, the renderer's device memory 37% less an env (lane/meshshare)

Elliot, 2026-10-08: "represent many things with one unified structure to connect them together in a
graph sense ... terrain compression", one optimization a lane; this lane's was content-addressed
section meshes shared by the worlds that hold the same section. 4 rows in out/perf/meshshare.tsv.

- Measured first (a temporary counter in cuda/render's mesh_end, by the views' full mesh key,
  engine/raster_meshkey.h: the section's place, the camera cell when inside it, the bands two
  above and below and the 3x3 chunks' masks, heights and biomes): of the device's section passes
  an env-step, another env held a mesh of the same key then for 0.520 of 0.898 at the speedrun
  config (58%; 0.617 in the whole process), 0.260 of 1.182 at village (22%; 0.296), and 4.728 of
  5.361 on the first 100 steps after a reset (88%; 5.064).
- Kept: the views' feeds carry each request's key beside it (engine/meshfeed.h meshfeed_key, host
  only, never uploaded), and the renderer keeps one reference counted arena block a key and pass
  (cuda/render/host.cu smesh, render_mesh_share). A keyed pass whose key a slot of the stream
  holds, or one a request sent before it in the same work has, is not sent to the mesher: it takes
  that mesh (its count goes back to the view as a meshed one's would). Exact: the key is a hash of
  every input the mesher reads (the view's own reuse of a kept mesh rests on it since lane/remesh),
  and one device mesher meshes every slot with one table set (meshing_context refuses another),
  so one key is one mesh. Proven beside the gates: render_mesh_share 2 (pipe_gate --mesh-check)
  and a frame carrying the host's meshes (device_mesh 2) send every pass anyway and compare its own
  mesh with the shared one it took (count, flags, every drawn vertex's written fields), pipe_gate
  prints and fails on it.
- Not built (measured, step 3): one copy a content of the meshers' world copies. At the end of the
  speedrun corpus the four meshers hold 2,417 MB (18.9 MB an env, not counted in the renderer's
  device memory before; pipe_bench prints it now): per stream about 575 MB of pools, 336 MB of them
  the run kernels' lane buffers and 176 MB band slots. Of 56,064 band slots 28,245 are zero
  (capacity), 27,819 hold 8,685 distinct contents: sharing them would save about 240 MB (1.9 MB an
  env) and 6 KB an env-step of the 8.5 KB of band uploads, through a copy-on-write band protocol in
  meshfeed. Not worth it against the lane buffers.

## 2026-10-09 Palettized textures measured and not built: the texel's bytes are not what raster waits on (lane/texpal)

Elliot, 2026-10-08: "should we be quantizing things from global memory and then dequantizing them
... pack more efficiently", one optimization a lane; this lane's was palettized textures. Measured
first, then probed with value-preserving builds (equal trajectory digests, every dump frame
bit-exact), 9 rows in out/perf/texpal.tsv. No code is kept: csrc is master's.

- The textures do compress: the block atlas (512x256, 512 tiles) has at most 250 colours a 16x16
  tile, 28.8 on average, 297 tiles with 16 or fewer; the item atlas (512x128) at most 75, 18.8 on
  average. Per-tile palettes with 4- or 8-bit indexes: 512 KB to 166 KB and 256 KB to 71 KB.
- Uploads are not the cost: atlas tiles 0.1 KB and textures 2.5 KB of 120.5 KB an env-step at the
  speedrun config (0.2 and 6.9 of 67.4 at village); the entity quads are the rest.
- Reads are not the cost either. In the pipeline's raster launches (Nsight Compute source counters,
  a -lineinfo build) the texel's load is 4.3% of raster's L2 sectors at the speedrun config and 5.1
  to 6.0% at village (the triangle records' cp.async 52%, the pair loads 17%), and the wait on it
  1.6 to 3.0% of the stall samples. Every env reading one atlas (slot 0's) left raster's DRAM bytes a
  block unchanged (9.1 and 9.2 KB): the per-env copies already hit in L2.
- What the texel's bytes cost, measured by doubling them (a second gather a pixel whose value is
  masked off by a run-time zero): raster on the stored dumps (render_check --seq --one-trip over
  pix-zvil-s42, cov-foliage-s1, cov-blkgallery-s1, pix-fluid-s1, 22 launches) 1658.8 to 1678.2 us
  (+1.2%, noise 0.5%), DRAM +1.3%; in the pipeline raster 20.80 to 20.84 us an env-step (nsys, the
  speedrun corpus) and env-steps/s 13,586 to 13,623 (noise). What a palette's extra level costs (one
  more dependent load, an L1 hit, before the texel): 1650.9 to 1684.4 us (+2.0%) on the dumps. A
  palettized fetch adds that level (index, then palette) to save part of bytes whose whole cost is
  1.2% of raster on the dumps and 0.2% in the pipeline, so it was not built.
- The decode in registers instead (attempts 4 and 5): byte / 255.0f as q = x * fl(1/255) and one
  Newton step, q + fma(fma(-q, 255, x), fl(1/255)), equal to the division for all 256 bytes (host
  check; u8f_check held it on the device), in place of u8f_tab's four gathers a pixel (and every
  other table lookup and entity byte division in raster for B). Dumps 1655.4 to 1654.2 and 1653.1
  us, speedrun 13,604 to 13,606 and 13,581, village 12,900 to 12,897 and 12,933 (medians of 3,
  equal digests): neutral, not kept.

Measured under gpubench.sh windows (whole machine) and ncuwrap.sh, on master 87722d50's build; every
probe's trajectory digests equal master's (92ca848bd97af37d speedrun, bd964a706fb0d4b7 village) and
every dump frame bit-exact (60 of 60). Gates: no code kept, so none rerun (git diff master -- csrc
is empty).

## 2026-10-08 The 1.7.10 pipeline's GPU work, third round: env-steps/s +9.8% at the speedrun config, +6.3% at village N 64, every output the same (lane/kernclimb3)

Elliot, 2026-10-08: "Look deeper at the 1.7.10 game and see what the actual kernels are doing and if
there's a faster way to do these while also getting basically perfectly matching outputs". Profiled
first at the training config (speedrun.yaml N 128: nsys of the corpus, each kernel's share of the
device's busy union, Nsight Compute on the pipeline's own launches and on stored dumps, DRAM bytes a
frame, source lines), then one change an attempt, 18 rows in out/perf/kernclimb3.tsv. The finding
that paid: nearly half the section triangles cover no pixel centre (46.6% at the speedrun config,
44.4% at village; 79% of the boxes of up to 8 pixels), and each was written (240 bytes), binned,
sorted and visited by raster for nothing. What was kept:

- quads_count drops a section triangle whose box (up to 32 pixels) has no pixel block_cover's
  terrain test keeps (geom_quads.cu may_draw: the binning's own edge values, without the tie rule,
  a superset of what the pixel draws), so the triangle never reaches the write, the pairs or raster.
  Exact by construction: block_cover would have given every pair of it an empty mask.
- quads_write marks the tiles of a terrain triangle's box a pixel may be in (tile_mask: a warp
  block is out when one edge is below 0 at its four corners, those values monotone in x and y), and
  the binning makes pairs for those tiles alone (pairs_warp takes the k-th set bit): pairs 1.458 G to
  1.154 G over the speedrun corpus, the covering ones unchanged (0.818 G).
- raster cheaper with the same bits: a power-of-two wrap by its low bits, the texel read as one word,
  byte / 255.0f from a compile-time table (u8f_tab; render_new holds it against the device's own
  division and refuses the renderer otherwise, proven with a wrong denominator), the terrain tie
  rule's top-left bits made by the writers into the record's unused aux. Stored dumps: raster 1680 to
  1530 us.

## 2026-10-03 The mesher's spread pass in 8 kernels a launch, not 15: the plan to the sort in one cooperative launch, the vertex copy once (lane/meshfuse)

A spread count launch ran 14 kernels and 2 memsets (copy, class, wsum,
plan, memset, cut, pack, place, keys, sort, draw beside draw_cube, check,
fix, vcopy), and its write pass a 15th (wcopy), most of them a few
microseconds of work behind a launch gap. Two changes, every mesh byte for
byte as before:

- `mesh_mid`: wsum, plan, cut, pack, place, keys and sort in one
  cooperative launch of lcap / 128 blocks (the cut's grid, 164 on the 3090),
  their steps apart by a software grid barrier (an arrival counter and a
  generation word, `L->gbar`). The three one-block steps are gone: every
  block plans the requests in its own shared memory (at most 1024 requests
  a spread launch, `MESHING_MID_MAXN`), the place sums the kept lanes of the
  blocks before it, the sort scans the 256 key counts in every block (counts
  and cursors in two arrays after the perm's ends). Three grid barriers
  where seven launches were; the key counts and the vertex cursor are
  zeroed in its first step (the two memsets).
- `mesh_lcopy`: a spread count pass leaves its vertices in the lanes' pool
  buffers (voff -2) and the write pass copies them straight to their meshes,
  where vcopy copied them into vbuf and wcopy copied them again. The mark
  check moves with it into mapped host memory, read by the next
  `meshing_count_wait` (a planted mark failed render_check loudly, "the
  device mesher failed").

## 2026-10-03 The render's geometry kernels: warp chunks, a triangle a thread, lighter clipper arrays (lane/geomocc)

The section quads' count and write, and the generic kernel's (the sky's
slots, the quads the lean kernel hands to the clipper, the recorded
units), were reshaped for parallelism; every frame stays byte for byte.

- `quads_count` (was `quads<0>`): a warp takes a chunk of 32 quads of one
  draw (`ddraw.chunk0`, found by a warp-uniform search), not a 256-thread
  block a draw that left most lanes idle on small draws. The camera
  offset `make_vertex` made in double for every vertex is made once a draw
  on the host (`ddraw.org`, `draw_org`: the same operations), so the
  kernel has 63 registers where it had 138. Each triangle the write will
  make goes to a list (one atomic a warp, the warp's entries in quad order).
- `quads_write` (was `quads<1>`): a triangle a thread from that list (its
  three vertices again: each vertex's operations are its own), built in
  shared memory and stored by the warp as contiguous uint4s. 14 of 32
  lanes worked on the old write (a quad with no triangle idled its lane).
- `generic_count`: two lanes a unit, a lane a triangle; the units that
  make triangles go to two lists by kind. `generic_write<false>` (sky and
  clipped section quads) and `generic_write<true>` (recorded units) write
  a triangle a thread from those lists on two side streams, replacing the
  two `generic<1>` launches and their warp gather (4.3 active lanes of 32
  on the sky's list).
- `clip_tri`'s Sutherland-Hodgman arrays hold only what the planes read
  (52-byte `pvx` for the write, the 16-byte clip coordinates for the
  count) instead of whole vertices; each fan vertex gets its screen fields
  where its triangle reads it.

Tried and dropped: the polygon as indices into a vertex pool (fewer copies,
but 9.8 KB of stack, 85 to 114 us on the write); a one-plane clip path in
registers (more registers, 77 to 86 us); `__launch_bounds__` minimum
blocks on the writes (the spills cost more than the occupancy gave).

## 2026-10-03 raster: 8x8 tiles and the binning's exact cover masks (lane/rasterbatch)

The device renderer's raster kernel spent most of its time on work the
binning could do once. Each warp computed a cover mask for every triangle
in its 16x16 tile's list. It tested pixels only for boxes of up to 12
pixels and used the whole box beyond that. A per-outcome count over 138
stored frames found that 61% of the terrain pixel-function calls missed
the triangle at the edge test. A clock64 breakdown of the slowest warp
(one frame, 175 us) gave about 30% to those masks, 10% to staging, and the
rest to the walk.

What changed (csrc/cuda/render, frames byte for byte the same):
- Tiles are 8x8, one 64-thread block a tile, two warps of 8x4.
- The binning (`pairs_warp`) writes each pair slot's triangle and both
  warp blocks' cover masks (`pinfo`, 3 words a slot). Each mask tests
  every pixel of the box with the pixel functions' own edge test, on the
  same values. The edge products are made once a column and once a row,
  and the entity path has no branches except FP64 near misses. A pair
  with an empty mask takes the sentinel key. raster reads the masks and
  computes none.
- The binning's warps take 32 pairs each, not 32 triangles: two lanes a
  pair, the first triangle found by a 32-way search of the pair offsets.
  A warp of 32 triangles had held the launch for 66 us on one frame,
  against 18 before the masks.
- raster transposes the batch's masks with five shuffles, picks its
  groups with `__fns`, and stages 16 triangles a group (8 before).
  MINB is 10 (90 registers). Both were measured best on stored village
  frames.
- The arena keeps its size: pairs_cap is arena / 2 / 28 bytes (16 before).

Per kernel, Nsight Compute with `--cache-control none`. The counts are
from render_check --bench over 96 stored village frames (cov-villagerep,
hl-village, struct-village, village-away at the observation), 4 renders,
before / after:

## 2026-10-01 Raw keyboard and mouse to iron ingot, with a pixel-policy clip (lane/iron)

The RL binding now accepts held keys, two mouse buttons, hotbar keys and
41-bin per-axis camera deltas as raw input. An open screen uses those same
deltas for its pointer, with clicks handled by the engine's screen input.
`nwrl_scan` supplies the semantic teacher's local blocks and targets;
`nwrl_layer_auto` draws the open screen over the student's pixel frame at
the frame's size. The run files set four ticks per action, 17 seed starts,
300-second episodes and a one-time ordered reward from log through iron
ingot, bucket, iron pickaxe and flint and steel, with capped item terms and
a death penalty. The teacher sees the 64x36 semantic camera and inventory
numbers. The 181M student sees pixels and sends raw actions. The final
student uses the lean, int8 K/V and FP8 encoder step from lane/polfast.

The semantic teacher's sampled round-11 DAgger checkpoint reached iron
ingot in 36 of 256 teacher-only episodes (14.1%). PPO with saved starts

share fell after updates, even with value-only warmup, a 90% fresh mix or

and is marked invalid in the table. The student was distilled from the

355, stone pickaxe 265, furnace 257, iron ore 116, iron ingot 74 and
bucket 2 times in 2,048 episodes across the 17 seeds; iron came from
seeds 9 and 14. The original imitation policy reached no planks in its
matched 2,048 episodes. `out/perf/iron.tsv` holds each rung's share over
wall time and the final numbers for each seed.

The clip replays the four best student episodes from that evaluation at

## 2026-10-01 A running env saved as a start: two replays of its acts make the image and its twin; a curriculum of milestone starts in GRPO (lane/savestart)

Elliot, 2026-10-01: a curriculum "at different checkpoints of different seeds", the demo target a clip that reaches
iron. A start used to come only from a snapshot the Java oracle recorded. Now pool_start_from_env (pipeline.h
pipe_start_from_env, rlbind.h nwrl_start_save) makes one from a running env, so that an env reset to it continues
exactly as the saved env would have: the same rows and the same frames for the same acts.

Why replays: a reset copies a start's image and rebases its pointers, which a load names by loading the start twice
at two addresses (the twin). A running env has no twin, and telling pointers by value is unsafe (two ints packed in a
word whose high one is near 4,096 + 16 x the slot read as an address in the image window). So with
pool_config.save_slots each env keeps an act log since its reset (process memory, per step the ticks it ran, per tick
the act step_act made: an agent act after the act hook with its hold_only, a tape act or a row's text; about 100 bytes
a tick), and a save copies the log and queues two J_SAVE jobs: each resets a new image to the env's start and runs the
log through step_job itself (replay mode: no tick hook, no profiler, no shared generation cache, which would let one
replay take a chunk the other generates and part their heaps), with a view of its own (spare views n + 2k, n + 2k + 1
of save slot k). The two replays are the start's image and twin: start_scan names the image's pointers as for a load,
plus the words naming the view library's copy. The view (play's statics in its playview.so copy) is saved as its
written pages of the copy's writable segments (less RELRO), the words naming the copy or the image rebased; a reset to
a saved start loads a fresh copy without opening it, writes those pages, rebases, and resumes the view (mesh_resync:
the device forgot the env's meshes). Starts are refcounted with saves on (an env holds its start, a save its parent
until made); the save runs on the workers beside the steps, pool_start_ready/wait report it, a reset to it waits.
Words that differ between the two replays and point at neither are values of each run's own, kept from the first
replay and counted: the view's frame timings (raster_live stats), stack bytes in struct padding; three stale
pointers are cleared in both (the session's hook context, the tile pass's cos_table pointing into its caller's frame,
the shared path search's worker stamp).

The gate, make -C native/runtime rl-start-gate (start_gate.c, startgate.mk): per case env A steps S, is saved (X) and
steps M more; B reset to X, C reset to X then saved again halfway (Y, a save of a saved start), D reset to Y, and A
itself reset to Y: every tick's row record (tests/rowrec.h), every step's result and device frame (and with --draw the
C frame), and the end state must equal A's. Cases: configs/speedrun.yaml at 1 tick a step (walk:1@300+120,
sr-speedrun-s1@400+160) and 4 (walk:2@120+60, sr-speedrun-s1@100+40), device meshing and the HUD; recordings at the
default observation with C frames: chest-chain-s1@20+20 (a chest window open), death-drops-s1@29+40 (the game-over
screen, 73 entities, the drops in flight), cat-recipes-s1@42+30 (the crafting table, its grid filled, 49 entities),
cov-tradelist-s1@3+30 (a trade), fight-zombie-s1@60+40, nether-trip-s1@23+30 (through the portal), @100+40 (in the
Nether), @197+20 (back), end-dragon-s1@50+60: 13 of 13 PASS. Then the binding (mcsr-speedrun mcsr/nwrl_save_gate.py
through libnwrl.so): 100 steps of an env reset to a saved start and 50 of one reset to a save of it equal the saving
env's, every RESULT record field and every frame torch reads: PASS. Per start (start_gate's lines): image 47 to 93 MB
(the env's nonzero pages, 5,855 to 38,281 pointers, 9 into the view), the view's pages 0.18 to 0.45 MB, the region
spill file 0 to 1.7 MB; a save took 0.3 s (60 ticks replayed) to 3.5 s (788 ticks, the Nether), about 1.5 to 4.5 ms a
replayed tick, off the trainer's thread.

mcsr-speedrun (new: mcsr/rl/curriculum.py, mcsr/nwrl_save_gate.py; edited, the originals in data/savestart_backup/:
mcsr/runconf.py, scripts/nw_grpo_async.py): policy.curriculum in the run file (starts fresh|pool, seeds "1-17", fresh,

## 2026-10-01 The semantic camera, a 5.2M teacher trained by PPO on it in 1.5 h, and DAgger into the 181M pixel policy: 24.0 logs and 99.2% wooden pickaxes against the overnight run's 7.0 and 52.3% (lane/semteach)

Elliot, noon: build the fast tier inside v2 and try it on the GPU host. Four parts.

The camera. native/runtime/semcam.[ch]: after each step, per env, a 64x36 grid of rays from the client player's eye
(the renderer's camera: yOffset - 1.62, vertical fov 70, aspect W/H, the axes from MathHelper's sin table) walked cell
by cell through the client world's blocks to 64 blocks; each ray gives block id | meta << 12, the distance in 1/256
blocks, the face entered (or a miss, or the void). Unloaded chunks and missing sections read as air, the eye's own cell
is passed, and with the eye in water or lava the rays see through it. Read only (the chunk lookups fill the world's
near cache, nothing else). Two casts: semcam_cast_ref reads every cell through world_chunk and chunk_get_block,
semcam_cast (the runtime's) keeps the last cell's chunk and band and ends a rising ray once it is above every loaded
section in reach. Run-file keys (C, WorldConf.java, config.yaml): client.camera pixels | semantic | both,
client.semantic 64x36, client.semantic_range 64. semantic makes the pipeline run no view and no renderer (no_view);
both keeps the frames. pool.h gained step_hook (the worker, at a step's end); rlbind's nwrl_semantic exports the
casts as host memory [n][h][w][4] uint16; pipe_bench --semantic (or the config's camera). New configs:
configs/speedrun-semantic.yaml (camera semantic), configs/speedrun-dagger.yaml (both).

Gate: make -C native/runtime semcam-gate (pool_gate --semcam): sr-speedrun-s1, swim-s42, phys-lavaswim-s1,
nether-trip-s1, end-dragon-s1 and cov-villagerep-s42, each run twice, the cast after every tick both ways: 15,830
casts byte-equal, each recording's episodes give one digest, and every row still equals test_snapshots'. Fast cast

## 2026-10-01 The game tick on the device as a throughput path, measured: S6 flat to 48 worlds, the link, a world's 312 MB and 66-136x per world; S1, S2, S4, S5 and SG on the device beside S6 (lane/gputick)

Elliot, noon: "try these out" (v1-class speed at v2 fidelity). The dev host's 3090, every timing under gpubench.sh's
lease, load about 1; numbers by run in out/perf/gputick.tsv (lane), the A/B against master d6872437 interleaved in
one lease from a worktree of master.

Measured as it was (sr-speedrun-s1, S6 alone, a block of one thread a world): the kernel p50 1.29 to 1.36 ms a launch
from 1 to 48 worlds (flat), mean 1.73 to 1.85; explore-long-s1 p50 1.56 to 1.61 (mean 8.6: heavy rows). Kernel-only
26.5k S6 runs/s at 48 worlds; with the round trip 813/s. C's S6 is 23.9 us a tick (9.0% of 2.93 M instructions,
phase-profile over 4,033 rows), 41.8k/s on one thread. 48 worlds is the most that fits: 312.5 MB of device memory a
world (148 real 2 MB granules for 62.9 MB of nonzero image; explore-long-s1 337.6 MB, 82.6 MB). 0.4% of S6 runs come
back to C (a chunk load at the edge). Nsight Compute could not profile the forked device child (it deadlocks in
cuInit under the injection): tick_batch --device-root keeps the device in the process ncu starts, --fn-map names the
device functions for the PCs. One S6 run: 238k warp instructions (C 165 to 342k x86), IPC 0.106 (CPI 9.4: long
scoreboard 37%, fixed-latency waits 30%, issue 11%, instruction fetch 10%, branches 9%), 168 registers (12 world-warps
an SM, 984 resident at most), 67% of L1 sectors local (stack). By function: the chunk loop's random-tick scan 28%, its
prefetch pass (useless on the device) 11%, update_tick 13%, grass 7%, relight 7%; a section's copy-on-write 29% on
the rows that copy, because NVPTX makes every memcpy and memset of 128 bytes or more a byte loop.

The three structural costs: (1) the hybrid's round trip: 5.27 MB down (1,288 pages) and 0.34 MB up a world-row, and
The dev host's 3090 sits on PCIe 3.0 x8: a batched pinned upload of 32 worlds moved 256 MB in 32.5 ms, 7.9 GB/s, the link's
peak, so a hybrid S6 tops out near 1.5k world-rows/s whatever the batch; (2) device memory: 312 MB a world, 48 to 60
worlds on 24 GB, not 1,024; (3) one world a thread: 66x (S6 2.05 ms against 30.8 us), 136x (S4 6.52 ms against 48.0
us) and 21x (S2 0.49 ms against 23.1 us) a CPU thread's time a run, sr-speedrun-s1's first 300 rows.

Kept, every row exact and every row's phase digests equal to C's trace:
- One transfer a launch: every world's pages staged by pinned DMA (the transfer areas' heads registered), one scatter,
  one gather, one dirty reset and three waits a launch, not each a world. Upload 40.0 to 36.3 ms (32 worlds) and 58.6
  to 54.4 (48), download 3.18 to 1.96 and 4.46 to 2.89; with the kernel 739 to 813 S6 runs/s at 48. Link-bound.
- The world tick's other phases on the device: servertick_phase (servertick.c) runs S1, S2, S1T, S4, S5, S6 or SG
  alone, the kernel runs the job's phase, the spawner and the siege's muster are device callbacks; tick_batch --phases,
  gpu-tick-check S6_PHASES (mirror.tsv's TICK quick gate runs S1,S2,S4,S5,S6,SG). 856 functions on the device (358
  before). sr-speedrun-s1 300 rows: S1 0.016, S2 0.493 (233 of 300 runs; the rest load a chunk), S4 6.52, S5 0.032, S6
  2.05, SG 0.006 ms a run; S1T always comes back to C (the sky angle's cos is glibc's: a device port is a follow-up).
  The phases now on the device are 33% of the C tick's instructions (S2 21.7, S6 9.0, S4 2.2), against S6's 9%.
- Wide mem ops: nw-dev hands every memcpy, memmove and memset of 128 bytes or more (702) to dev.c's word copies.
- A write past the mapped margin ends the run before it writes or lists its pages (C redoes it): S4 on the device
  grew a pool there in fight-skeleton-s1 (row 27, a falling block's adoption) and faulted the whole context, then the
  download's gather faulted again (ledger gputick-unmapped-write).
- --pack W: W worlds a thread block, one a thread (dev.h's per-thread state in shared memory). 32 copies of one world in
  one warp: p50 2.23 against 1.34 ms a warp each; 32 different recordings in one warp: p50 55.4 against 25.7 ms (mean
  95.0 against 61.6). A warp of 32 different worlds costs 2.2x its slowest world: 14.8x the worlds an SM.

The plan (projections, from the numbers above): a resident S6 at today's layout, 60 worlds: 33k S6 runs/s. The whole
tick on the device at today's per-world cost (89x C on S2+S4+S6, so about 20 ms a world-tick): 3.0k ticks/s at 60
worlds (312 MB), 12.5k at 250 (a dense layout, 70 MB), 49k at 984 (20 MB a world: terrain shared copy-on-write
between worlds from one start; the register cap at a world a warp), 110k at 4,750 packed 32 a warp (4 MB a world).
The CPU tick's ceiling is 144k on 32 threads (ideal; 60-80k measured loads). So the compiled C on the device reaches the
CPU's class only with the memory a world cut 15 to 80 times; v1-class (1.7M) needs on top the hot phases rewritten
data-parallel over the worlds (S11 entities 43%, S2 22%, S6 9%, S4's scheduled-tick set: its probing is 62% of S4
on the device), checked against the C engine as gpu-tick-check checks the compiled C today.
